# Fast backends in Dart

<p class="dox-top__slogan">Everything your Dart backend needs.</p>

<p class="dox-top__lead">
Build APIs and full web apps in <strong>Dart</strong>, with <strong>batteries included</strong>.
Routing, an ORM, validation, auth and a CLI work from the first command.
One command adds the rest: queues, mail, GraphQL and more.
Your app uses every CPU core and ships as one small native binary.
</p>

The speed comes from the native server. It runs on the isolate's own thread,
so a request never waits for another thread. See
[Performance](digging-deeper/performance.md) for every route and how it was run.

## What you get

<div class="dox-feat" markdown>

-   :material-lightning-bolt: **Fast by default**

    A native HTTP server, one isolate per CPU core and streamed bodies.
    `dox build` makes one native binary. See [Performance](digging-deeper/performance.md).

-   :material-database-outline: **ORM and query builder**

    Models, relations, migrations and transactions for Postgres, MySQL/MariaDB and SQLite.
    Postgres and MySQL use native drivers. See [Database](database/index.md).

-   :material-check-decagram-outline: **Typed validation**

    Write a `@Dto` class. Dox checks the input and gives your controller a typed object.
    See [Validation](the-basic/validation.md).

-   :material-file-document-outline: **OpenAPI**

    OpenAPI 3.1 docs and a Scalar docs page, made from your routes and DTOs.
    See [`dox_openapi`](packages/openapi.md).

-   :material-folder-outline: **File storage**

    Local disk, S3 and Azure Blob Storage behind one API, with signed URLs. See [`dox_storage`](digging-deeper/file-storage.md).

-   :material-cached: **Cache**

    Memory, file and Redis cache with tags and locks. See [`dox_cache`](digging-deeper/cache.md).

-   :material-access-point: **Real time**

    [Socket.IO](packages/socketio.md), with Redis for many servers.

-   :material-shield-lock-outline: **Security**

    JWT [authentication](security/authentication.md), [CORS](security/cors.md),
    [encryption](security/encryption.md) and [hashing](security/hashing.md).

-   :material-console: **CLI**

    Create projects, controllers, models and migrations. Run, build and migrate.
    See [CLI reference](reference/cli.md).

</div>

## One path for every request

<ol class="dox-flow" aria-label="The path of a request" markdown="block">
  <li markdown="span">**[Route](the-basic/routing.md)**<span>match the URL</span></li>
  <li markdown="span">**[Middleware](the-basic/middleware.md)**<span>go on or stop</span></li>
  <li markdown="span">**[DTO](the-basic/dto.md)**<span>check the input</span></li>
  <li markdown="span">**[Controller](the-basic/controller.md)**<span>your code</span></li>
  <li markdown="span">**[View](the-basic/views.md)**<span>render a page</span></li>
  <li markdown="span" class="dox-flow__end">**[Response](the-basic/response.md)**<span>send the answer</span></li>
</ol>

Each card is a page in "The basics". See [How Dox works](concepts/how-dox-works.md) for every step.

## What the code looks like

<div class="dox-sample" markdown>

<div class="dox-sample__code" markdown>

```dart
Route.post('/blogs', (BlogController c) => c.store);

@Inject() // 1
class BlogController {
  BlogController(this.blogs);
  final BlogService blogs;

  Future<Blog> store(CreateBlog input) { // 2
    return blogs.create(input);
  }
}

@Dto() // 3
class CreateBlog {
  @Length(min: 3, max: 100)
  final String title;

  @MinLength(10)
  final String body;
  ...
}
```

</div>

1.  Dox makes the controller and gives it the service it asks for. There is no reflection and no list of classes to keep.
2.  Ask for the DTO as a parameter. Dox reads the JSON body, checks it, and gives you a typed object. Bad input gets a `422` before your code runs.
3.  `@Dto()` marks an input class. The code generator writes the checks from the fields, their types and their rules.

</div>

## Run it in two minutes

You need [Dart](https://dart.dev/get-dart) 3.13 or newer, and nothing else.
The starter project uses SQLite, so there is no database to install.

<div class="dox-start" markdown>

<div markdown>

```bash title="Start the app"
dart pub global activate dox   # install the CLI
dox create my_app              # download the starter project
cd my_app
dart pub get
dox s                          # start the server
```

</div>

<div markdown>

```bash title="In a second terminal, call the first route"
curl localhost:3000/ping
```

```text
pong
```

</div>

</div>

That is a Dox app. Next, follow the [tutorial](tutorial/index.md). It adds a
model, a database table, validation, login and a Docker image, one short step
at a time.

??? note "The CLI is not found?"
    `dart pub global activate` puts `dox` in `$HOME/.pub-cache/bin`.
    Add that folder to your `PATH`. See [Installation](getting-started/installation.md).

# Installation

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/getting-started/installation/

# Installation

This page shows how to install the Dox CLI, make a new project and start the server.

Dox needs Dart 3.13 or newer.

## Install the CLI

The `dox` CLI makes projects, runs the server and makes files. Install it with pub:

```bash
dart pub global activate dox
```

Check that it works:

```bash
dox version
```

If the shell shows "dox: command not found", the pub bin folder is not in your path. Add this line to `~/.bashrc` or `~/.zshrc`, then open a new terminal:

```bash
export PATH="$PATH":"$HOME/.pub-cache/bin"
```

## Create a new project

Give `dox create` the name of your app, then get the packages:

```bash
dox create new_blog
cd new_blog
dart pub get
```

It downloads the newest release of the starter project, [dox-sample](https://github.com/dartondox/dox-sample). Add `--version` with a release tag to get one release. It also makes your `.env` file with a new random app key.

The starter project uses SQLite, so you do not install a database. To use Postgres or MySQL, change `DB_CONNECTION` and the other database keys in `.env`. See [Database](../database/index.md).

## Add Dox to a Dart project

In a Dart project that you have, add the packages with `dart pub add`:

```bash
dart pub add dox_core dox_orm dox_migration
dart pub add dev:dox_builder dev:build_runner
```

## Start the server

Start the server in dev mode:

```bash
dox s
```

It runs `bin/server.dart` and `build_runner watch`. It hot reloads a change in `lib/app/`, and it restarts the server for a change to routes, providers or config. At each start the server runs the new migrations, on the port in `APP_PORT` (default 3000):

```bash
curl localhost:3000/ping
```

```text
pong
```

Add `--ignore-build-runner` to skip the builder, or `--no-reload` to stop hot reload. To start the server with no CLI, run `dart run bin/server.dart`.

For production, build a native binary with `dox build`. See [Deployment](../digging-deeper/deployment.md).

## Start the server with Docker

The starter project has a Docker setup. This starts the app, a queue worker and a Postgres database:

```bash
docker compose up -d --build
```

The app and the worker always use the Postgres service. The database port is open on this machine only.

To run only the database in Docker and the app with `dox s`, run `docker compose up -d postgres`. Then set `DB_CONNECTION=postgres` and `DB_NAME=dox` in `.env`.

## Run the code generator

Dox makes code for models and DTOs with build_runner. `dox s` runs it. To run it alone:

```bash
dox build_runner:watch   # runs again on each file change
dox build_runner:build   # runs one time
```

## AI agents

To give an AI coding agent the real API of each package, run `dart run skills@ get` after `dart pub get`. See [AI agents](ai-agents.md).

## Packages

Dox has many packages, so you add only what you need:

| Package | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `dox` | the CLI |
| `dox_core` | HTTP server, routing, requests, responses, validation |
| `dox_orm` | query builder and models |
| `dox_migration` | database migrations |
| `dox_auth` | Login with access tokens, JWT or sessions |
| `dox_builder`, `dox_annotation` | code generation for models, DTOs and the container |
| `dox_validation` | [typed validation schemas](../packages/validation.md) |
| `dox_openapi` | [OpenAPI docs](../packages/openapi.md) |
| `dox_storage` | [file storage: local, S3, Azure](../digging-deeper/file-storage.md) |
| `dox_cache` | [cache: memory, file, Redis](../digging-deeper/cache.md) |
| `dox_cache_database` | [cache in a database table](../digging-deeper/cache.md#database-store) |
| `dox_socketio` | [Socket.IO server](../packages/socketio.md) |
| `dox_queue` | [background jobs](../digging-deeper/queue.md) |
| `dox_queue_database` | [queue in a database table](../digging-deeper/queue.md#database-driver) |
| `dox_scheduler` | [scheduled tasks](../digging-deeper/scheduler.md) |
| `dox_mailer` | [send email](../digging-deeper/mail.md) |
| `dox_view` | [HTML views](../the-basic/views.md) |
| `dox_inertia` | [Inertia.js pages](../the-basic/inertia.md) |
| `dox_http_native` | [native HTTP server](../digging-deeper/native-server.md) (Rust) |
| `dox_postgres_native`, `dox_mysql_native` | native drivers for [Postgres](../database/postgres-native.md) and [MySQL/MariaDB](../database/mysql-native.md) |

## Next steps

- [Add a package](add-a-package.md): add a feature with one command.
- [CLI](../reference/cli.md): all commands of the CLI.

# AI agents

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/getting-started/ai-agents/

# AI agents

Give your AI coding agent the real Dox API with skills, `AGENTS.md` and the llms files.

Without the real API, an agent guesses class and method names, and the code does not compile. Dox gives two sources:

- **Skills**: short guides that each package ships. The agent reads them while it writes code in your app.
- **llms files**: these docs as plain text, for a chat or a tool with no skills.

## Skills

A skill is a `SKILL.md` file with the real API of one package and the steps for the usual tasks. The agent reads a skill only when your task matches it. A skill comes with the package, so it always agrees with the package version of your app.

These packages ship a skill:

| Package | Skill | Use it for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dox_core` | `dox-core-guide` | routes, controllers, DTOs, serializers, middleware, providers, env config, CLI commands, HTTP tests |
| `dox_orm` | `dox-orm-guide` | models, queries, relations, pagination, transactions, factories, the switch to Postgres or MySQL |
| `dox_migration` | `dox-migration-guide` | migrations, table changes, seeders |
| `dox_validation` | `dox-validation-guide` | DTO rules, custom rules and messages, fluent schemas, database rules |
| `dox_auth` | `dox-auth-guide` | login and logout, JWT, session and access token guards, gates and policies |
| `dox_openapi` | `dox-openapi-guide` | the API docs at `/docs`, annotations for the OpenAPI document |
| `dox_cache` | `dox-cache-guide` | cache stores, `remember`, tags, cache locks, the cache in tests |
| `dox_queue` | `dox-queue-guide` | queue jobs, the worker, the Redis and database drivers, failed jobs, chains and batches |
| `dox_scheduler` | `dox-scheduler-guide` | scheduled tasks, cron frequencies, no double runs on many servers |
| `dox_storage` | `dox-storage-guide` | files and uploads, local, S3, Azure and memory disks, signed URLs |
| `dox_mailer` | `dox-mailer-guide` | mail config, mailables, Markdown mail, queued mail, transports, mail in tests |
| `dox_socketio` | `dox-socketio-guide` | realtime events, rooms, socket login, the Redis adapter, broadcasts |
| `dox_view` | `dox-view-guide` | HTML pages with `.dox.html` templates, layouts, components, forms with CSRF |
| `dox_inertia` | `dox-inertia-guide` | Inertia.js pages with React, Vue or Svelte, shared props, Vite and SSR |
| `dox_mcp` | `dox-mcp-guide` | an MCP server: tools, a route with auth, sessions, OAuth sign-in |
| `dox_grpc` | `dox-grpc-guide` | gRPC services: the `.proto` file, the service class, status codes, deadlines |
| `dox_graphql` | `dox-graphql-guide` | a GraphQL API from annotations and ORM models, auth and limits |
| `ioredis` | `ioredis-guide` | Redis connections, commands, pipelines, transactions, pub/sub |

## Install the skills

The [skills](https://pub.dev/packages/skills) tool copies the skills from your packages into the skills folder of your agent. Run it in the root folder of your app, after `dart pub get`:

```bash
dart run skills@ get
```

It asks which skills to install. Add `--all` to install all of them:

```bash
dart run skills@ get --all
```

### Select your agent

The tool finds your agent from the folders in your project, like `.claude/`. If it finds none, it asks you. To set the agent, use `--agent`:

```bash
dart run skills@ get --all --agent claude
```

| Agent | `--agent` | Skills folder |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Code | `claude` | `.claude/skills/` |
| Codex | `codex` | `.agents/skills/` |
| Cursor | `cursor` | `.cursor/skills/` |
| GitHub Copilot | `copilot` | `.github/skills/` |
| Cline | `cline` | `.cline/skills/` |
| OpenCode | `opencode` | `.opencode/skills/` |
| Antigravity | `antigravity` | `.agents/skills/` |
| Other agents | `generic` | `.agents/skills/` |

The tool does not find GitHub Copilot, so for Copilot always add `--agent copilot`.

### Run it again after a package change

The installed skills are copies. Run the tool again after you add or update a package:

```bash
dart run skills@ get
```

With `--all`, it also removes the skills of packages that you do not use now.

### Packages that come in through another package

The tool reads only the packages in your `pubspec.yaml`. For example, the cache uses ioredis. To get its skill, add it to your app:

```bash
dart pub add ioredis
dart run skills@ get
```

### Make sure that it worked

List the installed skills:

```bash
dart run skills@ list
```

For Claude Code, the core skill is `.claude/skills/dox-core-guide/SKILL.md`. If your tool has no skills, give the `SKILL.md` file to the agent.

## AGENTS.md

The `AGENTS.md` file in the root folder of your app tells the agent how your project is organized. Most coding agents read it before they change code.

The starter project has one. It holds:

- what the project is, and the links to the llms files
- the command that installs the skills, and the list of skills
- the folder layout and the file names
- the `dox` commands that make files
- when to run the code generator, and which files are generated
- the conventions for routes, input, models, migrations, jobs, config and errors
- how to switch the database
- the checks to run before a change is done: `dart format .`, `dart analyze` and `dart test`
- a list of things that the agent must not do

The file is yours. Edit it when your app gets its own rules.

## llms.txt and llms-full.txt

For a chat or a tool with no skills, the docs site has two plain text files in the [llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org) format:

| File | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| [llms.txt](https://dartondox.dev/llms.txt) | A short description of Dox, then one line for each page with its title and its link. |
| [llms-full.txt](https://dartondox.dev/llms-full.txt) | All the docs as one Markdown file, in the order of the menu. |

The docs build makes them again at each change, so they agree with this site.

### Use them

Give the files to an agent in one of these ways:

1. Paste the link `https://dartondox.dev/llms-full.txt` in a chat agent that can open links.
2. Add the link as a docs source in your editor.
3. Download the file, then attach it to the chat:

    ```bash
    curl -o dox-docs.md https://dartondox.dev/llms-full.txt
    ```

If your agent cannot hold the large file, give it `llms.txt`. The agent then opens only the pages that it needs.

## Skills or llms-full.txt

| | Skills | `llms-full.txt` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Use it for | code changes in your app | questions in a chat, or a tool with no skills |
| Size | small, one skill for each package | large, all the docs |
| Version | the package version of your app | the latest Dox version |
| How the agent gets it | automatically, when the task matches | you give it the link or the file |

## Next steps

- [Installation](installation.md): create a project.
- [MCP server](../packages/mcp.md): give AI clients tools from your own app.

# Add a package

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/getting-started/add-a-package/

# Add a package

`dox add` adds a Dox package to your app and sets it up.

## Adding a package

Give the short name of the package. The full name, like `dox_orm`, also works:

```bash
dox add orm
```

It runs `dart pub add dox_orm`, then `dart pub get`, then the setup command of the package (here `dox orm:install`). The setup command writes the config files, adds the keys to `.env` and `.env.example`, and runs build_runner if necessary. At the end it shows what it did and the next steps.

A package with no setup command is only added.

## Options

Words after the name go to the setup command, for example to pick a driver:

```bash
dox add orm --driver=postgres
```

Add `--dev` to add the package as a dev dependency.

## Running it again

The setup command never overwrites a file or a `.env` key. So you can run `dox add` again, and it adds only what is missing.

## Packages with a setup command

| Command | What it sets up |
| --- | --- |
| `dox add orm [--driver=sqlite\|postgres\|mysql]` | The ORM and migrations. See [Database](../database/index.md). |
| `dox add queue [--driver=database\|redis\|sync]` | Queued jobs and `bin/queue.dart`. `database` is the default and needs `dox add orm` first. See [Queue](../digging-deeper/queue.md). |
| `dox add scheduler` | Scheduled tasks and `bin/schedule.dart`. See [Scheduler](../digging-deeper/scheduler.md). |
| `dox add mailer [--transport=log\|smtp\|resend\|mailgun\|postmark\|ses]` | Mail. `log` is the default. See [Mail](../digging-deeper/mail.md). |
| `dox add cache [--store=file\|redis\|memory\|database]` | Cache stores. `database` needs `dox add orm` first. See [Cache](../digging-deeper/cache.md). |
| `dox add auth` | Access token auth. Needs `dox add orm` and a `User` model first. See [Authentication](../security/authentication.md). |
| `dox add storage [--disk=local\|s3\|azure]` | File storage. See [File storage](../digging-deeper/file-storage.md). |
| `dox add socketio [--broadcasting]` | Socket.IO, and broadcasting with the flag. See [Socket.IO](../packages/socketio.md). |
| `dox add view` | Views and `resources/views/`. See [Views](../the-basic/views.md). |
| `dox add inertia` | The server side of Inertia. It prints the Vite steps. See [Inertia](../the-basic/inertia.md). |
| `dox add mcp` | An MCP server with a sample tool. See [MCP](../packages/mcp.md). |
| `dox add grpc` | gRPC: a sample `.proto` file, a router with the health service and `APP_HTTP2` in `.env`. See [gRPC](../digging-deeper/grpc.md). |

The first `dox add orm` can download or build the Postgres and MySQL drivers one time. After that, `pubspec.yaml` skips the drivers that you do not use.

## Next steps

- [Package commands](../digging-deeper/package-commands.md#ship-an-install-command): add a setup command to your own package.
- [CLI](../reference/cli.md): all commands of the CLI.

# Build a blog API

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/tutorial/

# Build a blog API

This tutorial takes you from an empty folder to a small blog API that runs as one native binary.

Each step has the full code and a `curl` command to check your work. The finished project is on GitHub: [examples/blog-api](https://github.com/dartondox/dox/tree/main/examples/blog-api). CI builds it and runs its tests on each push.

## What you will build

A JSON API for blog posts. Anyone can read posts. Only a logged in user can write them:

| Method | Path | Who | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/api/posts` | anyone | list all posts |
| `GET` | `/api/posts/{id}` | anyone | one post, or 404 |
| `POST` | `/api/posts` | logged in user | make a post (201, or 422 on bad input) |
| `PUT` | `/api/posts/{id}` | logged in user | change a post |
| `POST` | `/api/auth/register` | anyone | make an account, get a token |
| `POST` | `/api/auth/login` | anyone | log in, get a token |
| `GET` | `/api/auth/user` | logged in user | the user of the token |

## What you need

- Dart 3.13 or newer. Check it with `dart --version`.
- curl, to call the API.
- Approximately 15 minutes.

You do not need Docker or a database server. The app uses SQLite, which keeps the database in one file in your project.

## The steps

1. [Create the project](01-create-project.md)
2. [Model and migration](02-model-and-migration.md)
3. [Routes and controller](03-routes-and-controller.md)
4. [Validation](04-validation.md)
5. [Authentication](05-auth.md)
6. [Test](06-test.md)
7. [Build and deploy](07-build-and-deploy.md)

## The finished project

This is the project at the end. A `*` marks the files that you make or change. The template has more files, but this tree shows only the files of this tutorial.

```text
blog/
├── bin/
│   ├── migrate.dart              runs the dox migration:* commands
│   ├── server.dart               runs the migrations, starts the server
│   └── queue.dart, schedule.dart, seed.dart
├── db/migration/
│   ├── ..._create_posts_table.dart   *
│   ├── ..._create_users_table.dart
│   └── migrations.dart           the list of migrations (Dox writes it)
├── lib/
│   ├── app/http/controllers/
│   │   ├── auth.controller.dart  *
│   │   └── post.controller.dart  *
│   ├── app/dtos/
│   │   ├── login_user/login_user.dto.dart   *
│   │   ├── register_user/register_user.dto.dart *
│   │   └── save_post/save_post.dto.dart    *
│   ├── app/models/
│   │   ├── post/post.model.dart  *
│   │   └── user/user.model.dart
│   ├── config/
│   │   ├── app.dart              * adds the DTO list
│   │   ├── database.dart
│   │   └── env.dart              the .env keys, typed
│   ├── routes/api.dart           *
│   ├── providers/
│   │   ├── auth_provider.dart    *
│   │   └── orm_provider.dart
│   └── generated/
│       ├── container.g.dart      * generated
│       └── dtos.g.dart           * generated
├── test/http_test.dart           *
├── .env                          made by dox create
├── Dockerfile
└── pubspec.yaml                  * adds dox_auth
```

# Step 1: Create the project

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/tutorial/01-create-project/

# Step 1: Create the project

In this step you make a new Dox project, start the dev server and call the first route.

## 1. Make the project

Install the `dox` command line tool, then make a project with the name blog:

```bash
dart pub global activate dox
dox create blog
cd blog
dart pub get
```

The package name is blog, so each import in this tutorial starts with `package:blog/`.

## 2. Look at the database settings

You do not change anything here. `dox create` made a `.env` file with a new random app key, and the template uses SQLite:

```ini title=".env"
APP_PORT=3000
APP_KEY=<your new random key>

DB_CONNECTION=sqlite
DB_NAME=db/dox.sqlite
```

Dox makes the database file at the first start, but not its folder. If you set a path in a new folder, make the folder first. See [Environment variables](../digging-deeper/env.md).

## 3. Start the server

Start the dev server:

```bash
dox s
```

It runs the code generator and the server. It hot reloads your code in `lib/app/`, and it restarts the server when you change routes or config.

The first start is slower, because it compiles the SQLite library and runs the migrations of the template. At the end you see this log line:

```text
[server] Server started at http://[::]:3000 with 8 isolate (native)
```

The number of isolates is the number of CPU cores on your machine.

## Check it

Call the ping route from a second terminal:

```bash
curl -i http://localhost:3000/api/ping
```

You see:

```text
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: text/plain; charset=utf-8
...

pong
```

The route is in `lib/routes/api.dart`. Its router has the prefix api, so `/ping` is at `/api/ping`.

## Next steps

- [Step 2: Model and migration](02-model-and-migration.md): make the posts table and its model.

# Step 2: Model and migration

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/tutorial/02-model-and-migration/

# Step 2: Model and migration

In this step you make the posts table with a migration, and a `Post` model to read and write it.

## 1. Make the model and the migration

Stop `dox s` first with Ctrl+C. The server runs new migrations when it starts, so it would run the migration before you add the columns.

Make the model and its migration:

```bash
dox make:model Post -m
```

This makes two files and updates one:

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `lib/app/models/post/post.model.dart` | the model (new) |
| `db/migration/<date>_create_posts_table.dart` | the migration (new) |
| `db/migration/migrations.dart` | the list of all Dart migrations. Dox writes it. Do not edit it. |

## 2. Add the columns to the migration

Open the new file in `db/migration` and add a title and a body:

```dart title="db/migration/2026_10_22_205345_create_posts_table.dart"
// ignore_for_file: file_names
import 'package:dox_migration/dox_migration.dart';

class CreatePostsTable extends Migration {
  @override
  Future<void> up(Schema schema) async {
    await schema.create('posts', (Table table) {
      table.id();
      table.string('title');
      table.text('body');
      table.timestamps();
    });
  }

  @override
  Future<void> down(Schema schema) async {
    await schema.dropIfExists('posts');
  }
}
```

`table.id()` makes an auto increment primary key. `table.timestamps()` makes the created_at and updated_at columns, and the model fills them.

## 3. Add the fields to the model

Add one field for each new column:

```dart title="lib/app/models/post/post.model.dart"
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';

part 'post.model.g.dart';

@DoxModel(table: 'posts')
class Post extends PostGenerator {
  @override
  List<String> get hidden => <String>[];

  @Column()
  String? title;

  @Column()
  String? body;
}
```

Each field is nullable, because a new `Post()` has no values. The id and the timestamps come from `PostGenerator`.

## 4. See how migrations run

You do not change anything here. The template's `bin/server.dart` runs the migrations before the server starts:

```dart title="bin/server.dart"
import '../db/migration/migrations.dart';

void main() async {
  Dox().initialize(appConfig);

  await Migrator(
    migrations: migrations,
    config: databaseConfig.getConnectionConfig(),
  ).migrate();

  await Dox().startServer();
}
```

This also works in the native binary of [step 7](07-build-and-deploy.md).

## 5. Run the migration and the generator

Run the new migration:

```bash
dox migration:run
```

```text
Migrating: 2026_10_22_205345_create_posts_table
Migrated: 2026_10_22_205345_create_posts_table
```

If `dox s` was still on, the table can exist without the new columns. Then run `dox migration:rollback` and `dox migration:run` again.

The model also needs its generated file. `dox s` makes it, so if the server is off, run the generator one time:

```bash
dart run build_runner build
```

## Check it

See which migrations ran:

```bash
dox migration:status
```

You see:

```text
Migration                                 Batch  Status
2023_07_16_131937700_create_users_table   1      Ran
2026_10_25_000000000_create_queue_tables  1      Ran
2026_10_22_205345_create_posts_table      2      Ran
```

The first two come with the template. The server ran them in step 1.

Start the server again with `dox s`.

## Next steps

- [Step 3: Routes and controller](03-routes-and-controller.md): add the post routes.

# Step 3: Routes and controller

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/tutorial/03-routes-and-controller/

# Step 3: Routes and controller

In this step you add a controller and the routes to list, create and show posts.

## 1. Make the controller

A controller holds the code that answers a request. Make one for posts:

```bash
dox make:controller Post -r
```

The `-r` flag makes a resource controller with seven methods. You need three now, so replace the file with this:

```dart title="lib/app/http/controllers/post.controller.dart"
import 'package:blog/app/models/post/post.model.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

@Inject()
class PostController {
  /// GET /api/posts
  Future<List<Post>> index(DoxRequest req) async {
    return Post().all();
  }

  /// POST /api/posts
  Future<DoxResponse> store(DoxRequest req) async {
    Post post = Post()
      ..title = req.input('title')
      ..body = req.input('body');
    await post.save();
    return response(post).statusCode(201);
  }

  /// GET /api/posts/{id}
  Future<Post> show(int id) async {
    Post? post = await Post().find(id);
    if (post == null) {
      throw NotFoundHttpException();
    }
    return post;
  }
}
```

What the code does:

- `@Inject()` puts the controller in the container. The code generator adds it to `lib/generated/container.g.dart`, and a new project uses that file.
- A model or a list of models goes back as JSON.
- `statusCode` sets the status code.
- `show(int id)` gets the id from the URL. A path like `/api/posts/abc` gets 404, because abc is not an integer.
- `input` reads the input with no check. You add checks in [step 4](04-validation.md).

## 2. Add the routes

Open `lib/routes/api.dart` and add `Route.resource`:

```dart title="lib/routes/api.dart"
import 'package:blog/app/http/controllers/api.controller.dart';
import 'package:blog/app/http/controllers/post.controller.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

class ApiRouter extends Router {
  @override
  String get prefix => 'api';

  @override
  List<dynamic> get middleware => <dynamic>[];

  @override
  void register() {
    Route.get('/ping', (ApiController c) => c.pong);

    Route.resource('posts', PostController);
  }
}
```

It makes one route for each method of the controller:

| Method | Path | Controller method |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/api/posts` | `index` |
| `POST` | `/api/posts` | `store` |
| `GET` | `/api/posts/{id}` | `show` |

Dox finds each router class, so you do not register it.

## 3. Start the server

If the server is off, start it:

```bash
dox s
```

If it is on, it restarts when you save a file.

## Check it

Make a post:

```bash
curl -i -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/posts \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"title":"Hello Dox","body":"My first post."}'
```

You get 201 and the new post:

```text
HTTP/1.1 201 Created
content-type: application/json; charset=utf-8
...

{"id":1,"title":"Hello Dox","body":"My first post.","created_at":"2026-10-22T13:58:14.062215Z","updated_at":"2026-10-22T13:58:14.062215Z"}
```

List the posts:

```bash
curl http://localhost:3000/api/posts
```

```json
[{"id":1,"title":"Hello Dox","body":"My first post.","created_at":"2026-10-22T13:58:14.062215Z","updated_at":"2026-10-22T13:58:14.062215Z"}]
```

Show one post:

```bash
curl http://localhost:3000/api/posts/1
```

```json
{"id":1,"title":"Hello Dox","body":"My first post.","created_at":"2026-10-22T13:58:14.062215Z","updated_at":"2026-10-22T13:58:14.062215Z"}
```

Ask for a post that does not exist. You get 404:

```bash
curl -i http://localhost:3000/api/posts/99
```

```text
HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
...

{"code":"not_found","message":"Not Found"}
```

# Step 4: Validation

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/tutorial/04-validation/

# Step 4: Validation

In this step you check the input of create and update with a DTO class, so bad input gets a 422 answer.

## 1. Make the DTO

A [DTO](../the-basic/dto.md) is a class for the input that you expect, with a rule on each field. Make one:

```bash
dox make:dto SavePost
```

Create and update use the same fields, so one class is sufficient. Replace the file with this:

```dart title="lib/app/dtos/save_post/save_post.dto.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

part 'save_post.dto.g.dart';

/// Typed, checked input. Run `dox build_runner:build` after a change.
@Dto()
class SavePost {
  @Trim()
  @Length(min: 3, max: 100)
  final String title;

  @Trim()
  @MinLength(10)
  final String body;

  const SavePost({required this.title, required this.body});

  static const DtoSchema<SavePost> schema = $SavePostDto;
}
```

A field that is not nullable and has no default is required. The rules run from top to bottom, so after `@Trim()` an empty string counts as missing. See [Validation](../the-basic/validation.md) for all rules.

## 2. Give the DTO list to the app

The code generator writes a list of all DTOs to `lib/generated/dtos.g.dart`. Add two lines to `lib/config/app.dart`:

```dart title="lib/config/app.dart"
import 'package:blog/generated/dtos.g.dart';

AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  /// DTOs (generated list in lib/generated/dtos.g.dart)
  dtos: dtos,

  // ... the rest stays the same
);
```

## 3. Use the DTO in the controller

Ask for `SavePost` as a parameter of the controller method. Dox checks the body and gives you a typed object. This version also adds `update`:

```dart title="lib/app/http/controllers/post.controller.dart"
import 'package:blog/app/dtos/save_post/save_post.dto.dart';
import 'package:blog/app/models/post/post.model.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

@Inject()
class PostController {
  /// GET /api/posts
  Future<List<Post>> index(DoxRequest req) async {
    return Post().all();
  }

  /// POST /api/posts
  Future<DoxResponse> store(SavePost body) async {
    Post post = Post()
      ..title = body.title
      ..body = body.body;
    await post.save();
    return response(post).statusCode(201);
  }

  /// GET /api/posts/{id}
  Future<Post> show(int id) async {
    return _find(id);
  }

  /// PUT /api/posts/{id}
  Future<Post> update(int id, SavePost body) async {
    Post post = await _find(id);
    post
      ..title = body.title
      ..body = body.body;
    await post.save();
    return post;
  }

  Future<Post> _find(int id) async {
    Post? post = await Post().find(id);
    if (post == null) {
      throw NotFoundHttpException();
    }
    return post;
  }
}
```

The routes stay the same. The resource route finds the new method and adds PUT and PATCH for `/api/posts/{id}`.

## 4. Run the generator

`dox s` runs the generator. If the server is off, run it one time:

```bash
dart run build_runner build
```

It writes `save_post.dto.g.dart` and `lib/generated/dtos.g.dart`.

## Check it

Send a title and a body that are too short:

```bash
curl -i -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/posts \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"title":"Hi","body":"Short"}'
```

You get 422 with one message for each field:

```text
HTTP/1.1 422 Unprocessable Entity
content-type: application/json; charset=utf-8
...

{"title":"The title must be between 3 and 100 characters","body":"The body must be at least 10 characters"}
```

Send an empty body:

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/posts \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}'
```

```json
{"title":"The title is required","body":"The body is required"}
```

Good input gives 201:

```bash
curl -i -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/posts \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"title":"Second post","body":"Validation works now."}'
```

```text
HTTP/1.1 201 Created
```

Update the first post:

```bash
curl -X PUT http://localhost:3000/api/posts/1 \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"title":"Hello Dox (edited)","body":"My first post, edited."}'
```

```json
{"id":1,"title":"Hello Dox (edited)","body":"My first post, edited.","created_at":"2026-10-22T13:58:14.062215Z","updated_at":"2026-10-22T13:59:13.539886Z"}
```

# Step 5: Authentication

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/tutorial/05-auth/

# Step 5: Authentication

In this step you add register and login with a JWT token, so only a logged in user can create or change posts.

## 1. Add the package

The `dox_auth` package does the login and the tokens. Add it:

```bash
dart pub add dox_auth
```

## 2. Look at the users table

The template has a user model and a users table. This is the `User` model:

```dart title="lib/app/models/user/user.model.dart"
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';

part 'user.model.g.dart';

@DoxModel(table: 'users', softDelete: true)
class User extends UserGenerator {
  @override
  List<String> get hidden => <String>['password'];

  @Column()
  String? name;

  @Column()
  String? email;

  @Column()
  String? password;
}
```

The password is in `hidden`, so it is never in the JSON. This is important, because the token holds the user as JSON and anyone can read a JWT.

The server ran this migration at the first start in [step 1](01-create-project.md):

```dart title="db/migration/2023_07_16_131937700_create_users_table.dart"
class CreateUsersTable extends Migration {
  @override
  Future<void> up(Schema schema) async {
    await schema.create('users', (Table table) {
      table.id();
      table.string('name');
      table.string('email').unique();
      table.string('password');
      table.softDeletes();
      table.timestamps();
    });
  }
  // ...
}
```

`softDeletes()` makes the deleted_at column for the soft delete. The email is unique, so a second register with the same email fails.

## 3. Make the DTOs

Register and login have different input, so make two DTOs:

```bash
dox make:dto RegisterUser
dox make:dto LoginUser
```

Replace the register DTO with this:

```dart title="lib/app/dtos/register_user/register_user.dto.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart' hide Schema;

part 'register_user.dto.g.dart';

@Dto()
class RegisterUser {
  @Trim()
  @Length(min: 2, max: 50)
  final String name;

  @Trim()
  @Lowercase()
  @Email()
  @Unique('users', column: 'email')
  final String email;

  @MinLength(8)
  final String password;

  const RegisterUser({
    required this.name,
    required this.email,
    required this.password,
  });

  static const DtoSchema<RegisterUser> schema = $RegisterUserDto;
}
```

`@Unique` comes from `dox_orm` and reads the database, so it runs after the other rules. The ORM also has a class with the name `Schema`, so the import hides it.

Replace the login DTO with this:

```dart title="lib/app/dtos/login_user/login_user.dto.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

part 'login_user.dto.g.dart';

@Dto()
class LoginUser {
  @Trim()
  @Lowercase()
  @Email()
  final String email;

  final String password;

  const LoginUser({required this.email, required this.password});

  static const DtoSchema<LoginUser> schema = $LoginUserDto;
}
```

## 4. Set up the auth provider

A provider tells the auth package which model to use and how to sign tokens. It runs one time in each isolate at start. Make this file:

```dart title="lib/providers/auth_provider.dart"
import 'package:blog/app/models/user/user.model.dart';
import 'package:blog/config/env.dart';
import 'package:dox_auth/dox_auth.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

/// Auth provider
/// --------------------------
/// Sets up JWT login with the User model.
/// Tokens are signed with APP_KEY and last 7 days.
class AppAuthProvider extends DoxProvider {
  @override
  void setup() {
    Auth.initialize(
      AuthConfig(
        defaultGuard: 'api',
        guards: <String, AuthGuard>{
          'api': AuthGuard(
            driver: JwtAuthDriver(
              secret: SecretKey(env.appKey),
              expiresIn: const Duration(days: 7),
            ),
            provider: AuthProvider(model: () => User()),
          ),
        },
      ),
    );
  }
}
```

Dox finds the provider, and the code generator adds it to `lib/generated/container.g.dart`.

## 5. Write the auth controller

This controller has the register, login and "who am I" routes:

```dart title="lib/app/http/controllers/auth.controller.dart"
import 'package:blog/app/dtos/login_user/login_user.dto.dart';
import 'package:blog/app/dtos/register_user/register_user.dto.dart';
import 'package:blog/app/models/user/user.model.dart';
import 'package:dox_auth/dox_auth.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

@Inject()
class AuthController {
  /// POST /api/auth/register
  Future<DoxResponse> register(RegisterUser body) async {
    User user = User()
      ..name = body.name
      ..email = body.email
      ..password = await Hash.makeAsync(body.password);
    await user.save();

    String? token = Auth().login(user);
    return response(<String, dynamic>{
      'token': token,
      'user': user,
    }).statusCode(201);
  }

  /// POST /api/auth/login
  Future<Map<String, dynamic>> login(LoginUser body) async {
    Auth auth = Auth();
    String? token = await auth.attempt(<String, dynamic>{
      'email': body.email,
      'password': body.password,
    });
    if (token == null) {
      throw UnAuthorizedException(message: 'Wrong email or password');
    }
    return <String, dynamic>{'token': token, 'user': auth.user<User>()};
  }

  /// GET /api/auth/user
  User? user(DoxRequest req) {
    return req.auth?.user<User>();
  }
}
```

- `Hash.makeAsync()` makes a bcrypt hash of the password on another isolate. Never save a plain password.
- `attempt()` finds the user by email and checks the password. It gives a token, or null.
- `login(user)` gives a token with no password check. Register uses it for the new user.

## 6. Protect the write routes

Read routes stay public, and write routes need a login. Replace the resource route with single routes, and put the write routes in `Route.middleware`:

```dart title="lib/routes/api.dart"
import 'package:blog/app/http/controllers/api.controller.dart';
import 'package:blog/app/http/controllers/auth.controller.dart';
import 'package:blog/app/http/controllers/post.controller.dart';
import 'package:dox_auth/dox_auth.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

class ApiRouter extends Router {
  @override
  String get prefix => 'api';

  @override
  List<dynamic> get middleware => <dynamic>[];

  @override
  void register() {
    Route.get('/ping', (ApiController c) => c.pong);

    // Anyone can read posts.
    Route.get('/posts', (PostController c) => c.index);
    Route.get('/posts/{id}', (PostController c) => c.show);

    // Register and log in.
    Route.post('/auth/register', (AuthController c) => c.register);
    Route.post('/auth/login', (AuthController c) => c.login);

    // Only a logged in user can write posts.
    Route.middleware(<dynamic>[AuthMiddleware()], () {
      Route.get('/auth/user', (AuthController c) => c.user);
      Route.post('/posts', (PostController c) => c.store);
      Route.put('/posts/{id}', (PostController c) => c.update);
    });
  }
}
```

`AuthMiddleware` reads the bearer token in the Authorization header and loads the user. A missing or wrong token gets 401. For a public route that still knows the user, use `AuthMiddleware(optional: true)`.

## 7. Run the generator

`dox s` runs the generator. If the server is off, run it one time:

```bash
dart run build_runner build
```

## Check it

Register a user. You get 201 with a token:

```bash
curl -i -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/auth/register \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"Ann","email":"ann@example.com","password":"secret123"}'
```

```text
HTTP/1.1 201 Created
content-type: application/json; charset=utf-8
...

{"token":"eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIs...","user":{"id":1,"name":"Ann","email":"ann@example.com","created_at":"2026-10-22T14:01:07.827769Z","updated_at":"2026-10-22T14:01:07.827769Z"}}
```

Register with the same email again. You get 422:

```json
{"email":"The email has already been taken"}
```

Log in with a wrong password. You get 401:

```bash
curl -i -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/auth/login \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"ann@example.com","password":"wrong"}'
```

```text
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
...

{"code":"unauthorized","message":"Wrong email or password"}
```

Log in with the right password, and keep the token in a shell variable:

```bash
TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/auth/login \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"ann@example.com","password":"secret123"}' \
  | sed -E 's/.*"token":"([^"]+)".*/\1/')
echo $TOKEN
```

Make a post with no token. You get 401:

```bash
curl -i -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/posts \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"title":"Third post","body":"Written with a token."}'
```

```text
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
...

{"code":"unauthorized","message":"Authentication failed"}
```

Send the same post with the token:

```bash
curl -i -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/posts \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"title":"Third post","body":"Written with a token."}'
```

```text
HTTP/1.1 201 Created
...

{"id":3,"title":"Third post","body":"Written with a token.","created_at":"2026-10-22T14:01:08.094211Z","updated_at":"2026-10-22T14:01:08.094211Z"}
```

Ask who you are:

```bash
curl http://localhost:3000/api/auth/user \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

```json
{"id":1,"name":"Ann","email":"ann@example.com","created_at":"2026-10-22T14:01:07.827769Z","updated_at":"2026-10-22T14:01:07.827769Z"}
```

The answer has no password, because it is hidden.

# Step 6: Test

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/tutorial/06-test/

# Step 6: Test

In this step you write one HTTP test for the list route and run it.

## 1. Write the test

A test calls your routes like a real client. Replace the template's `test/http_test.dart` with this:

```dart title="test/http_test.dart"
import 'package:blog/config/app.dart';
import 'package:blog/config/database.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/testing.dart';
import 'package:dox_migration/dox_migration.dart';
import 'package:test/test.dart';

import '../db/migration/migrations.dart';

void main() {
  late DoxTestClient client;

  setUpAll(() async {
    await Migrator(
      migrations: migrations,
      config: databaseConfig.getConnectionConfig(),
    ).migrate();
    client = await DoxTestClient.start(appConfig);
  });

  tearDownAll(() async {
    await client.close();
  });

  test('GET /api/posts gives a list', () async {
    TestResponse res = await client.get('/api/posts');
    res.expectStatus(200).expectJson(isA<List<dynamic>>());
  });
}
```

`DoxTestClient.start` runs the app in the test on a free port. The test runs the migrations first, so it also works on an empty database.

## Check it

Run the test:

```bash
dart test test/http_test.dart
```

You see:

```text
00:01 +1: All tests passed!
```

The test reads `.env`, so it uses your dev database. To use another database, make a `.env.testing` file with `DB_NAME=test.sqlite`. The test reads it on top of `.env`.

# Step 7: Build and deploy

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/tutorial/07-build-and-deploy/

# Step 7: Build and deploy

In this step you compile the app to one native binary, run it, and run it in Docker.

!!! warning "Use a native binary in production"
    `dox s` and `dart run` use the JIT compiler. It uses approximately 25 times more memory and starts slower.

## 1. Build the binary

Build the app:

```bash
dox build
```

```text
Built with build_runner/aot in 1s; wrote 0 outputs.
Running build hooks...Running link hooks...
Generated: /.../blog/build/bundle/bin/server
[Dox] Built build/bundle. Run it with: cd build/bundle && ./bin/server
```

It runs the code generator, then `dart build cli`. The `build/bundle` folder has all that the app needs:

| Path | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `bin/server` | the binary, approximately 10 MB. It needs no Dart SDK. |
| `bin/queue` | the [queue worker](../digging-deeper/queue.md). Run it as its own process. |
| `bin/schedule` | the [scheduler](../digging-deeper/scheduler.md). Run it as its own process. |
| `lib/` | native libraries from build hooks, like `libsqlite3`. Keep it next to `bin/`. |
| `db/` | your migrations. Your local SQLite file is not copied. |
| `.env.example` | a copy of the example env file. |

## 2. Run the binary

The binary reads `.env` from the folder where you start it, so copy your file there:

```bash
cd build/bundle
cp ../../.env .env
./bin/server
```

```text
Migrating: 2023_07_16_131937700_create_users_table
Migrated: 2023_07_16_131937700_create_users_table
Migrating: 2026_10_25_000000000_create_queue_tables
Migrated: 2026_10_25_000000000_create_queue_tables
Migrating: 2026_10_22_205345_create_posts_table
Migrated: 2026_10_22_205345_create_posts_table
... "message":"Server started at http://[::]:3000 with 8 isolate (native)" ...
```

The migrations run again, because the bundle has a new database file. The binary has the migration list in it.

On a server you can set real environment variables in place of `.env`. They win over `.env`.

## Check it

Call the binary from a second terminal:

```bash
curl http://localhost:3000/api/ping
curl http://localhost:3000/api/posts
```

```text
pong
[]
```

The list is empty, because the database file is new. Stop the server with Ctrl+C.

## 3. Docker

The project has a `Dockerfile`. It builds the same bundle and copies it into an empty scratch image:

```dockerfile title="Dockerfile"
FROM dart:stable AS build

# Resolve dependencies first, so this layer is cached.
WORKDIR /app
COPY pubspec.* ./
RUN dart pub get

COPY . .
RUN dart pub get --offline

# The dox CLI. `dox build` runs build_runner, then AOT-compiles
# bin/server.dart, bin/queue.dart and bin/schedule.dart with
# `dart build cli`. It puts all of them in build/bundle/bin, the native
# libraries in build/bundle/lib and the migrations in build/bundle/db.
# The queue worker and the scheduler run as their own processes:
# `/app/bin/queue work` and `/app/bin/schedule work`.
RUN dart pub global activate dox
RUN /root/.pub-cache/bin/dox build

# Lay out the final file tree:
# /app/bin/server, /app/bin/queue, /app/bin/schedule, /app/lib (native
# libraries), /app/db/migration, /app/storage and a writable /tmp
# (uploads bigger than 1 MB are streamed to a temp file).
RUN mkdir -p /out/app/storage /out/tmp \
  && chmod 1777 /out/tmp \
  && cp -r build/bundle/. /out/app/

# Minimal serving image: the AOT runtime files from the dart image
# (`/runtime/`) plus our bundle. No Dart SDK, no source code.
FROM scratch
COPY --from=build /runtime/ /
COPY --from=build /out/ /
WORKDIR /app

# Config comes from env variables. The image has no .env file,
# so secrets stay out of it.
EXPOSE 3000
CMD ["/app/bin/server"]
```

Build and run the image. The image has no `.env` file, so give the config as environment variables. The app key must have exactly 32 characters, or the app does not start:

```bash
docker build -t blog .
docker run -p 3000:3000 \
  -e APP_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16) \
  -e DB_CONNECTION=sqlite \
  -e DB_NAME=storage/blog.sqlite \
  blog
```

!!! warning "SQLite in Docker"
    The database file is in the container, so you lose it when you remove the container. Mount a volume for it: `-v blog-data:/app/storage`. For a busy app, use Postgres or MySQL. See [Database](../database/index.md).

# How Dox works

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/concepts/how-dox-works/

# How Dox works

This page shows the path of a request, how isolates work and what each folder of an app is for.

## The life of a request

Each request takes the same path. The pages in "The basics" follow this order:

<ol class="dox-flow" aria-label="The path of a request" markdown="block">
  <li markdown="span">**[Route](../the-basic/routing.md)**<span>match the URL</span></li>
  <li markdown="span">**[Middleware](../the-basic/middleware.md)**<span>go on or stop</span></li>
  <li markdown="span">**[DTO](../the-basic/dto.md)**<span>check the input</span></li>
  <li markdown="span">**[Controller](../the-basic/controller.md)**<span>your code</span></li>
  <li markdown="span">**[View](../the-basic/views.md)**<span>render a page</span></li>
  <li markdown="span" class="dox-flow__end">**[Response](../the-basic/response.md)**<span>send the answer</span></li>
</ol>

Dox has two parts. The native server (`dox_http_native`) owns the sockets and parses HTTP. Your Dart app runs the routes, middleware, DTOs, controllers and the ORM.

A request goes through these steps:

1. The native server parses the request. A broken request gets 400, headers over 16 KB get 431, and a body over the size limit gets 413.
2. The native server gives the requests to Dart in a batch.
3. Dart finds the route by the method, the host and the path. No match gets 404. A CORS preflight gets 204.
4. Dart adds the CORS headers of the route.
5. Dart reads the body, if the request has a content type.
6. Dart runs the middleware in this order: global, router, group, route. If a middleware returns a value that is not the request, Dart sends that value as the response.
7. Dart fills the controller parameters. A path param that does not fit its type gets 404. Bad DTO input gets 422, a body that is not JSON gets 400, and an unknown content type gets 415.
8. The controller runs and returns a value.
9. The `responseHandler` of `AppConfig` runs, if you set one.
10. Dox makes the response: a string is text, a map or model is JSON, and a file is streamed.
11. Dart gives the answers of the batch back to the native server, which writes them to the socket.

If a step throws, Dox catches the error. An `IHttpException` gives its own status. Any other error gives 500 and goes to the `report` method of your `ExceptionHandler`.

<div class="dox-seq" style="--lanes:5" role="group" aria-label="The steps of a request, from the client to the controller and back">
  <div class="dox-seq__head"><strong>Client</strong><strong>Native server</strong><strong>Dart isolate</strong><strong>Middleware</strong><strong>Controller</strong></div>
  <ol>
    <li style="--a:1;--b:2">TCP connection, HTTP request</li>
    <li style="--a:2" class="dox-seq__self">parse request, check size limits</li>
    <li style="--a:2;--b:3">batch of requests (one message)</li>
    <li style="--a:3" class="dox-seq__self">router: method, host, path</li>
    <li style="--a:3" class="dox-seq__self">CORS headers, read body</li>
    <li style="--a:3;--b:4">global, router, group, route middleware</li>
    <li style="--a:3;--b:4" class="dox-seq__back dox-seq__reply">request (go on) or a response</li>
    <li style="--a:3" class="dox-seq__self">path params, DTO check</li>
    <li style="--a:3;--b:5">call with typed parameters</li>
    <li style="--a:3;--b:5" class="dox-seq__back dox-seq__reply">return value</li>
    <li style="--a:3" class="dox-seq__self">response handler, build the response</li>
    <li style="--a:2;--b:3" class="dox-seq__back">batch of answers (one call)</li>
    <li style="--a:1;--b:2" class="dox-seq__back">bytes</li>
  </ol>
</div>

Dox uses no reflection. DTOs come from a generated list, so `dox build` can make a native binary.

### Where things are decided

| Step | Code | What it decides |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Route match | `lib/routes/*.dart`, `Route.get(...)` | which controller runs |
| Middleware | `AppConfig(globalMiddleware:)`, `Router.middleware`, `Route.middleware(...)`, the route list | go on, or answer early |
| Input | a `@Dto` class in `lib/app/dtos/<name>/` | what the controller gets, or 422 |
| Output | the return value, `response(...)`, `responseHandler` | status, headers, body |
| Errors | `IHttpException`, `AppConfig(exceptionHandler:)` | the error response, logging |

## Isolates

An **isolate** is like a thread with its own memory. Dox starts one isolate for each CPU that the process can use, also in a container, and each isolate runs the full app.

### One port, many isolates

Each isolate runs its own HTTP server on the same port:

| System | Native server |
| --- | --- |
| Linux | one socket per isolate (`SO_REUSEPORT`) |
| macOS | the isolates share one socket |
| Windows | only one isolate serves HTTP |

See [Native server](../digging-deeper/native-server.md#how-it-works).

### What each isolate gets

Dox copies the `AppConfig`, the providers, and the routes and binders that you added before `startServer()` to each isolate. Then each isolate does these steps one time:

1. It runs `setup()` of each provider, in list order.
2. It registers the routes of your routers.
3. It reads the parameter types of each controller.
4. It starts its HTTP server.

The config and the providers are copied, so they must not hold open sockets or pools. Open them in `setup()`. See [Providers](../digging-deeper/providers.md).

### Each isolate has its own memory

Isolates do not share memory:

- A static value or a singleton exists one time in each isolate.
- The memory cache store is per isolate. Use the Redis store to share cache data.
- To share data, use the database, Redis or files.

`Dox().isolateId` gives the isolate that runs the code. The first one is 1.

### When an isolate crashes

- An error in a request gets 500, and the isolate continues.
- An async error outside a request goes to the `ExceptionHandler`, and the isolate continues.
- If a worker isolate stops, Dox starts a new one after 1 second.
- If the main isolate stops, the process exits with an error code. In production, use a supervisor to start it again, like Docker `restart:` or systemd `Restart=always`.

### How many isolates

Set `totalIsolate` in `AppConfig` or `APP_TOTAL_ISOLATE` in `.env`. `Dox().totalIsolate(2)` before `startServer()` wins over the config. See [Isolate](../digging-deeper/isolate.md).

## Where the database pools live

Each isolate runs `setup()` of the ORM provider, so each isolate asks for a pool. The native drivers give isolates with the same settings the same pool:

| Driver | Per isolate | Per process |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Postgres native (`dox_postgres_native`) | nothing | one pool of `maxConnectionCount` connections per settings |
| MySQL native (`dox_mysql_native`) | nothing | one pool of `maxConnectionCount` connections per settings |
| SQLite | one connection | nothing shared |

So for Postgres and MySQL, the app opens at most `maxConnectionCount` connections for all isolates. Set it below the max_connections of the database. See [Native Postgres driver](../database/postgres-native.md#options).

## The layout of a Dox app

`dox create my_app` copies the [dox-sample](https://github.com/dartondox/dox-sample) template:

```text
my_app/
├── bin/
│   ├── server.dart          # starts the app
│   ├── migrate.dart         # runs the migrations (dox migration:*)
│   ├── seed.dart            # runs the seeders (dox db:seed)
│   ├── queue.dart           # the queue worker (dox queue:*)
│   └── schedule.dart        # the scheduler (dox schedule:*)
├── db/
│   ├── factories/           # model factories, *.factory.dart
│   ├── migration/           # migrations (.dart with a registry, or .sql)
│   └── seeders/             # seeders, *.seeder.dart
├── lib/
│   ├── app/
│   │   ├── http/
│   │   │   └── controllers/     # *.controller.dart
│   │   ├── jobs/                # queue jobs, *.job.dart
│   │   └── models/              # one folder per model, *.model.dart
│   ├── config/
│   │   ├── app.dart             # AppConfig: port, isolates, middleware
│   │   ├── cache.dart           # cache stores
│   │   ├── cors.dart
│   │   ├── database.dart        # DatabaseConfig: connections
│   │   ├── env.dart             # typed env class (@DoxEnv)
│   │   ├── logger.dart
│   │   ├── queue.dart           # QueueConfig
│   │   ├── schedule.dart        # ScheduleConfig and your tasks
│   │   └── storage.dart         # storage disks
│   ├── routes/
│   │   ├── api.dart             # ApiRouter, prefix `api`
│   │   └── web.dart             # WebRouter
│   ├── providers/               # one DoxProvider per file
│   │   ├── orm_provider.dart        # opens the database
│   │   ├── queue_provider.dart
│   │   ├── schedule_provider.dart
│   │   └── storage_provider.dart
│   └── generated/               # made by build_runner, do not edit
│       ├── container.g.dart     # @Inject classes, routers, providers
│       ├── jobs.g.dart          # the list of queue jobs
│       └── openapi.g.dart       # the OpenAPI docs
├── test/
├── .env                         # local settings, not in git
├── .env.example
├── Dockerfile
├── docker-compose.yml
└── pubspec.yaml
```

The `dox make:*` commands add more folders when you need them, like `lib/app/dtos/`, `lib/app/http/middleware/` and `lib/app/serializers/`. The app makes `storage/` when it first writes files.

| Folder | What goes there |
| --- | --- |
| `bin/` | `server.dart` calls `Dox().initialize(appConfig)`, runs the migrations, then `Dox().startServer()`. The other files are the entry points of the `dox migration:*`, `db:seed`, `queue:*` and `schedule:*` commands. |
| `db/` | Your migrations, factories and seeders. The CLI writes the list of Dart migrations in `db/migration/migrations.dart`. |
| `lib/app/http/` | Controllers and middleware. |
| `lib/app/serializers/` | Serializers. MCP and WebSocket code also use them. |
| `lib/app/dtos/` | One folder per DTO: typed and checked input. |
| `lib/app/jobs/` | Queue jobs. |
| `lib/app/models/` | One folder per model, with its generated file. |
| `lib/config/` | One file per config object. `app.dart` puts them together in `AppConfig`. |
| `lib/routes/` | One `Router` class per file. Dox finds each router. |
| `lib/providers/` | Classes that extend `DoxProvider`. Their `setup()` runs in each isolate. Dox finds each provider. |
| `lib/generated/` | Generated files. Run `dox build_runner:build` to make them again. |
| `storage/` | Files the app writes: uploads, the file cache, SQLite files. |

- [Providers](../digging-deeper/providers.md): code that runs when the app starts.
