# Middleware

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/the-basic/middleware/

# Middleware

Middleware is code that runs before the controller, and if you want, after it too.

## Making a middleware

Make a middleware with the CLI:

```bash
dox make:middleware Logger
```

It writes `lib/app/http/middleware/logger.middleware.dart`. Write your code in `handle`:

```dart title="lib/app/http/middleware/logger.middleware.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

class LoggerMiddleware implements IDoxMiddleware {
  @override
  dynamic handle(IDoxRequest req) {
    print('${req.method} ${req.uri.path}');
    return req; // go on to the next middleware
  }
}
```

`handle` can be async. Return the request to go on. Return any other value to send it as the response, or throw an exception to send an error. Then the controller does not run.

!!! warning
    Do not forget `return req`. A middleware that returns null ends the request with an empty 200.

### Function middleware

A function that takes a `DoxRequest` also works as middleware:

```dart title="lib/app/http/middleware/api_key.middleware.dart"
dynamic apiKeyMiddleware(DoxRequest req) {
  String apiKey = Env.get<String>('API_KEY');
  String given = req.header('X-Api-Key') ?? '';
  if (apiKey.isEmpty || !Hash.equals(given, apiKey)) {
    return response(<String, String>{'message': 'Unauthorized'})
        .statusCode(401);
  }
  return req;
}
```

Compare secrets with `Hash.equals`, not `==`, so the time does not tell an attacker how much of the key was right.

## Registering middleware

### On a route

Put the middleware in a list before the controller. They run from left to right:

```dart
Route.get('/ping', <dynamic>[
  LoggerMiddleware(),
  apiKeyMiddleware,
  (WebController c) => c.pong, // the controller is always last
]);
```

### On a group of routes

Run a middleware for many routes:

```dart
Route.middleware(<dynamic>[LoggerMiddleware()], () {
  Route.get('/me', (AuthController c) => c.me);
  Route.post('/logout', (AuthController c) => c.logout);
});
```

### On a router

Run a middleware for all routes of one router:

```dart title="lib/routes/api.dart"
class ApiRouter extends Router {
  @override
  List<dynamic> get middleware => <dynamic>[LoggerMiddleware()];

  @override
  void register() {
    // every route here runs LoggerMiddleware
  }
}
```

### Global middleware

Run a middleware for all routes:

```dart title="lib/config/app.dart"
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  globalMiddleware: <dynamic>[
    LogMiddleware(enabled: env.appEnv != 'production'),
  ],
);
```

### Global middleware from a package

A package adds a global middleware in the `setup()` of its provider. It runs before the global middleware of the app:

```dart
class AuditProvider extends DoxProvider {
  @override
  Future<void> setup() async {
    Dox().addGlobalMiddleware(AuditMiddleware());
  }
}
```

A second add of the same middleware is skipped, so use a top-level function or a const instance.

### Skip a middleware on one route

Take every middleware of a type out of one route, also a global one:

```dart
Route.post('/events', (EventController c) => c.stream)
    .withoutMiddleware<RequestTimeout>();
```

It also takes out the subtypes of the type, so use a specific type.

### The order

Middleware runs in this order. If one returns a value or throws, the rest do not run:

<ol class="dox-flow" aria-label="The order of middleware">
  <li><strong>Package</strong><span>from a provider</span></li>
  <li><strong>Global</strong><span>all routes</span></li>
  <li><strong>Router</strong><span>one router</span></li>
  <li><strong>Group</strong><span>a route group</span></li>
  <li><strong>Route</strong><span>one route</span></li>
  <li class="dox-flow__end"><strong>Controller</strong><span>handles the request</span></li>
</ol>

## Run code after the controller

Implement `IDoxNextMiddleware` to change the response. `await next()` runs the rest of the middleware and the controller:

```dart title="lib/app/http/middleware/see_other.middleware.dart"
class SeeOtherMiddleware implements IDoxNextMiddleware {
  @override
  Future<DoxResponse> handle(DoxRequest req, Next next) async {
    DoxResponse res = await next();
    if (res.status == 302 && req.httpRequest.method != 'GET') {
      res.statusCode(303);
    }
    return res;
  }
}
```

If the controller throws, `next()` gives the error response from the [ExceptionHandler](errors.md), so the code after it always runs.

A function works too:

```dart
Future<DoxResponse> timerMiddleware(DoxRequest req, Next next) async {
  Stopwatch watch = Stopwatch()..start();
  DoxResponse res = await next();
  return res.header('X-Time', '${watch.elapsedMilliseconds}ms');
}
```

## Run code after the answer is sent

Implement `IDoxTerminableMiddleware` for work that must not make the client wait, like logs or metrics:

```dart title="lib/app/http/middleware/metrics.middleware.dart"
class MetricsMiddleware
    implements IDoxMiddleware, IDoxTerminableMiddleware {
  @override
  dynamic handle(IDoxRequest req) => req;

  @override
  void terminate(DoxRequest req, DoxResponse res) {
    print('${req.method} ${req.uri.path} ${res.status}');
  }
}
```

An error in `terminate` goes to `ExceptionHandler.report`. It never changes the answer.

### From any code

`AfterResponse` adds work after the answer from a controller, a service or a package. Turn it on in the `setup()` of a provider:

```dart title="lib/providers/app_provider.dart"
@override
void setup() {
  AfterResponse.enable();
}
```

Then add work anywhere in the request. The work runs in the order you add it:

```dart
AfterResponse.run(() => mailer.sendWelcome(user));
```

Work that did not run yet is lost when the server stops. For work that must run, use a [queue](../digging-deeper/queue.md#dispatching-jobs).

`AfterResponse.disable()` turns it off again, for tests. `AfterResponse.enabled` tells if it is on.

## Built-in middleware

### Request id

`RequestId` gives each request an id. It is sent in the `X-Request-Id` header, and you read it as `req.requestId`:

```dart title="lib/config/app.dart"
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  globalMiddleware: <dynamic>[
    const RequestId(),
    LogMiddleware(),
  ],
);
```

Put it before `LogMiddleware`, so each log line gets the id. Dox keeps a safe id from the client. `RequestId(trustClient: false)` always makes a new one.

To make an id yourself, call `RequestId.make()`. It gives 32 hex characters.

### ETag and 304 Not Modified

`ETag` answers 304 with no body when the client already has the same data:

```dart
Route.get('/posts',
    <dynamic>[const ETag(), (PostController c) => c.index]);
```

It works on 200 answers with a body in memory. The controller still runs, so it saves bandwidth, not server time.

To make a weak ETag yourself, use `ETag.of(bytes)`. `ETag.matches(ifNoneMatch, tag)` tells if the header of the client has the tag.

### Request timeout

Answer 503 when the route takes too long:

```dart
Route.get('/report', (ReportController c) => c.show)
    .timeout(Duration(seconds: 30));
```

For every route, add the `RequestTimeout` middleware to `globalMiddleware`:

```dart
RequestTimeout(Duration(seconds: 30))
```

Dart can not stop a running Future, so the controller keeps running and its late result is dropped. A global timeout also ends long streams. See [Skip a middleware on one route](#skip-a-middleware-on-one-route).

### Server timing

`ServerTiming` adds a `Server-Timing` header. The browser dev tools show it in the Network tab:

```dart title="lib/config/app.dart"
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  globalMiddleware: <dynamic>[
    if (Env.get<String>('APP_ENV') == 'development') const ServerTiming(),
  ],
);
```

!!! warning "Development or trusted clients only"
    The header tells every client how long your code takes. An attacker can use it, for example to guess if an email has an account.

It sends the time in the controller as `handler` and the full time as `total`. Add your own time to the current request:

```dart
ServerTiming.add('db', Duration(milliseconds: 4));
```

Run a function and add the time it took:

```dart
String html = await ServerTiming.measure('render', () => view.render());
```

The header then looks like this. A name you add again adds up, with a count:

```
Server-Timing: db;dur=4.10;desc="3 calls", handler;dur=12.34, total;dur=13.02
```

#### Timing database queries

Add the time of every query in the `setup()` of a provider:

```dart title="lib/providers/query_timing_provider.dart"
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';

void onQuery(QueryEvent event) {
  ServerTiming.add('db', event.time);
}

class QueryTimingProvider extends DoxProvider {
  @override
  void setup() {
    SqlQueryBuilder().listen(onQuery);
  }
}
```

See [Listen to queries](../database/index.md#listen-to-queries).

### Log requests

`LogMiddleware` logs one line for each request. It follows the logger config. These are its options:

| Option | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `enabled` | false turns the request logs off. Not set: follow the logger. |
| `withHeader` | true also logs the headers. |
| `redact` | Fields and headers whose name has one of these words are logged as `[REDACTED]`. Default: `LogMiddleware.defaultRedact` (password, secret, token, cookie and more). |
| `filter` | A function that changes the line before it is logged. |

```dart
LogMiddleware(withHeader: true, redact: <String>['password', 'pin'])
```

### More middleware

Other pages have more middleware:

- `AuthMiddleware` and `GuestMiddleware` check the login. See [Authentication](../security/authentication.md).
- `RateLimit` answers 429 for too many requests. See [Rate limiting](../security/rate-limiting.md).
- `SecurityHeaders` adds safe headers. See [Security headers](../security/security-headers.md).
- `SessionMiddleware` gives each request a session. See [Session](session.md).
- `CsrfMiddleware` stops cross site request forgery. See [CSRF protection](../security/csrf.md).
- `ValidateSignature` checks signed URLs. See [Signed URLs](../security/signed-urls.md).
- `MethodOverride` lets HTML forms send PUT, PATCH and DELETE. See [Routing](routing.md#forms-with-put-patch-and-delete).

## Next steps

- [Routing](routing.md): add middleware to routes and groups.
- [Rate limiting](../security/rate-limiting.md): limit the requests of a client.
- [CORS](../security/cors.md): let other origins call your API.

# Session

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/the-basic/session/

# Session

A session keeps data for one browser across many requests, like the logged in user or a shopping cart.

Dox gives every browser a session cookie and keeps the data for that cookie. Web pages with forms and logins need a session. An API with tokens does not.

## Setup

Add `SessionMiddleware` to `globalMiddleware`. Session forms also need [CSRF protection](../security/csrf.md), so add `CsrfMiddleware` after it:

```dart title="lib/config/app.dart"
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  globalMiddleware: <dynamic>[
    const SessionMiddleware(),
    const CsrfMiddleware(except: <String>['/api/*']),
  ],
);
```

Now every request has `req.session`. On a route with no session middleware, `req.session` throws.

### Configuration

Set `session` in the app config. Set only the options you want to change:

```dart title="lib/config/app.dart"
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  session: const SessionConfig(
    driver: 'cache',
    store: 'redis',
    lifetime: Duration(hours: 2),
  ),
);
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `driver` | cookie | cookie or cache. See [Drivers](#drivers). |
| `store` | null | The cache store for the cache driver, like redis. null uses the default store. |
| `cookie` | `dox_session` | The name of the session cookie. |
| `lifetime` | 2 hours | The session ends after this time with no use. |
| `path` | `/` | The path of the cookie. |
| `domain` | null | The domain of the cookie. null means only the host that set it. |
| `httpOnly` | true | Page scripts can not read the cookie. |
| `secure` | null | null sets `Secure` when the request came over https. |
| `sameSite` | lax | The `SameSite` of the cookie. |

To give one middleware its own config, use `SessionMiddleware(SessionConfig(...))`.

### Drivers

The **driver** decides where the data is kept:

- cookie: all data is in the cookie, encrypted with your `APP_KEY`. A cookie holds about 4 KB, so store an id, not a full object. An old copy of the cookie works until the lifetime ends, also after logout.
- cache: the cookie holds only a session id, and the data is in a [cache store](../digging-deeper/cache.md). On logout the data is deleted.

For more than one server, use the cache driver with a shared store like redis or [database](../digging-deeper/cache.md#database-store). The memory store is shared by the isolates of one server only, and it is lost when the server stops.

## Retrieving data

Read a value. The second argument is the default for a missing key:

```dart
String? name = req.session.get('name');
List<dynamic> cart = req.session.get('cart', <int>[]);
```

### Retrieving all data

Get a copy of all session data:

```dart
Map<String, dynamic> data = req.session.all();
```

### Checking if a value exists

`has` gives true when the key is in the session and its value is not null:

```dart
if (req.session.has('cart')) {
  // ...
}
```

## Storing data

Store a value. It must be a JSON type: a map, a list, a string, a number, a bool or null:

```dart
req.session.put('cart', <int>[1, 2]);
```

### Retrieving and deleting a value

Read a value and remove it in one step:

```dart
dynamic cart = req.session.pull('cart');
```

## Flash data

**Flash data** stays for the current request and the next one, like a "saved" message after a redirect:

```dart
req.session.flash('message', 'The post is saved');
return redirect('/posts');
```

On the next page, `req.session.get('message')` gives the text.

### Keeping flash data

Keep all flash data for one more request, or only some keys:

```dart
req.session.reflash();
req.session.keep(<String>['message']);
```

## Deleting data

Remove one value, or all data:

```dart
req.session.forget('cart');
req.session.flush();
```

## Regenerating the session ID

Give the user a new session id at login. This stops a [session fixation](https://owasp.org/www-community/attacks/Session_fixation) attack. It also gives a new CSRF token and keeps the data:

```dart
req.session.regenerate();
```

`regenerate(keepToken: true)` keeps the CSRF token, for forms in other tabs. Do not use it at login.

At logout, remove all data and get a new id:

```dart
req.session.invalidate();
```

[Session login](../security/authentication.md#session-login-for-web-pages) from `dox_auth` does both for you.

## CSRF token

Read the CSRF token of the session. It is made on first use:

```dart
String token = req.session.token;
```

See [CSRF protection](../security/csrf.md).

## Validation errors and old input

When a form post fails [validation](validation.md), Dox redirects back to the form. It flashes the errors and the old input. Password fields and files are never kept:

```dart
Route.get('/register', (DoxRequest req) {
  Map<String, dynamic> errors = req.session.errors; // empty when none
  String? email = req.session.old('email');
  // ...
});
```

A request that wants JSON gets a 422 JSON answer instead.

### Flash errors yourself

Flash errors and input, then go back to the page the request came from:

```dart
req.session.flashErrors(<String, String>{'email': 'The email is taken'},
    input: req.all());
return back(req);
```

## Session without a request {#other-cases}

Code with no request, like a Socket.IO login, loads the session from the raw cookie value. Changes to it are not saved:

```dart
Session session = await SessionMiddleware().fromCookie(value);
session.get('auth_web');
```

## Testing

`client.withSession()` gives a test client that keeps cookies like a browser. It also sends the CSRF token:

```dart
DoxTestClient browser = client.withSession();
await browser.get('/cart/add?id=1');
(await browser.get('/cart')).expectJson(isNotEmpty);
```

See [Testing: keep a session](../digging-deeper/testing.md#keep-a-session-cookies-and-csrf).

## Next steps

- [Cache](../digging-deeper/cache.md): the stores a session can use.
- [CSRF protection](../security/csrf.md): protect forms that use the session.
- [Authentication](../security/authentication.md): session login.

# Request

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/the-basic/request/

# Request

The request gives you the input, files, headers and cookies that the client sent.

## Typed input

Ask for a [DTO](dto.md) in your controller. Dox reads the body (or the query for GET, HEAD and DELETE), checks it, and gives you a typed object:

```dart
Route.put('/users/{id}', (UserController c) => c.update);

@Inject()
class UserController {
  Future<User?> update(int id, UpdateUser input) async {
    User? user = await User().find(id);
    user?.name = input.name;
    await user?.save();
    return user;
  }
}
```

Bad input gets 422 before your method runs. See [Validation](validation.md).

### Checking in the controller

To check the input at a later point, call `validate` with the DTO type:

```dart
CreateUser data = await req.validate<CreateUser>();
```

For input you know only at runtime, use a fluent schema. See [Fluent schemas](../packages/validation.md#fluent-schemas-for-dynamic-input):

```dart
Map<String, dynamic> data = await req.validateSchema(v.object(
    <String, Schema<Object?>>{'email': v.string().email()}));
```

## Raw input

Add a `DoxRequest` parameter to read the raw values. Dox does not check these values.

### Retrieving an input value

Read one value from the query string or the body. The body wins when both have the key:

```dart
String? name = req.input('name');
String name = req.input('name', 'guest'); // default for a missing key
```

Use a dot key to read inside a map or a list:

```dart
req.input('user.name');
req.input('items.0.id'); // the id of the first item
```

A key that is in the input as it is, like `'a.b'`, wins over a dot key.

### Retrieving all input

Get all values of the query string and the body:

```dart
Map<String, dynamic> data = req.all();
```

Get only the body or only the query string:

```dart
req.body;  // JSON or form data
req.query; // the query string
```

### Retrieving a part of the input

Get some keys, or all keys but some:

```dart
req.only(<String>['name', 'email']);
req.except(<String>['password']);
```

### Checking if a value exists

`filled` gives true when the key is there and not empty. Only spaces, an empty list and an empty map count as empty:

```dart
if (req.filled('name')) {
  // ...
}
```

`exists` gives true for a key with any value, also an empty string or null. `missing` is the opposite:

```dart
req.exists('name');
req.missing('name');
```

`has` gives true when the key is there and not empty. It does not read dot keys.

### Reading booleans and numbers

`boolean` gives true for true, 1, on and yes, so it works for checkboxes:

```dart
bool remember = req.boolean('remember');
```

`integer` gives the default when the key is missing or not a number:

```dart
int page = req.integer('page', 1);
```

### Adding input

Add one value, or a map of values, for example in a middleware:

```dart
req.add('key', value);
req.merge(<String, dynamic>{'key': value});
```

### Lists and maps in forms

Form and query keys with brackets give lists and maps:

| Input | `req.input(...)` gives |
| --- | --- |
| `tags[]=a&tags[]=b` | `req.input('tags')` is `['a', 'b']` |
| `address[city]=Yangon` | `req.input('address')` is `{'city': 'Yangon'}` |
| `items[0][name]=x` | `req.input('items')` is `[{'name': 'x'}]` |
| `name=a&name=b` (no brackets) | `req.input('name')` is `'b'`, the last value |

## Route params

Ask for a path param as a typed parameter, like `int id` above. See [Controller: parameters](controller.md#parameters).

The URL-decoded text values are also in `req.param`:

```dart
String? id = req.param['id'];
Map<String, String> params = req.pathParams; // {'id': '5'}
```

A value from [route model binding](routing.md#route-model-binding) comes from `bound`:

```dart
User user = req.bound<User>('user');
```

## Form data (File)

An uploaded file is a `RequestFile`. The request must be `multipart/form-data`. Put the file in a DTO, so Dox checks its type and size:

```dart title="lib/app/dtos/upload_image/upload_image.dto.dart"
@Dto()
class UploadImage {
  @Image()
  @MaxSize('5MB')
  final RequestFile image;

  const UploadImage({required this.image});

  static const DtoSchema<UploadImage> schema = $UploadImageDto;
}
```

Then store it. `store` comes from the [`dox_storage`](../digging-deeper/file-storage.md) package:

```dart
Future<Map<String, String>> uploadImage(UploadImage input) async {
  String path = await input.image.store('images');
  return <String, String>{'filename': path};
}
```

!!! warning "Save the file before you return"
    Dox deletes the temp file of a big upload when the response is sent.
    Call `store`, `moveTo` or `stream` before your controller returns.

### Files without a DTO

Get a file, or null when the field is not a file. Dox does not check it:

```dart
RequestFile? image = req.file('image');
```

`hasFile` gives true when the field holds a file or a list of files. For a field with many files, use `req.input('images')`:

```dart
if (req.hasFile('image')) {
  // ...
}
```

### Reading and saving a file {#requestfile}

A `RequestFile` tells you about the file:

```dart
file.filename;  // name from the client
file.filetype;  // content type, like video/mp4
file.extension; // mp4
file.length;    // size in bytes
await file.size; // size in KB
file.head;      // the first bytes, to find the real file type
```

Save it to storage, or move it:

```dart
await file.store('videos');              // gives the path
await file.moveTo('/data/videos/1.mp4'); // gives the new File
```

Read it in chunks with `stream`. `bytes` loads the full file in memory, so do not use it for big files:

```dart
file.stream();
await file.bytes;
```

`file.file` is the temp file on disk, or null when the upload is in memory. An upload up to 1 MB stays in memory.

### Size limits

A body that is too big gets 413. Change the limits in `AppConfig`:

```dart title="lib/config/app.dart"
AppConfig(
  maxBodySize: 10 * 1024 * 1024,       // JSON and urlencoded, default 10 MB
  maxMultipartSize: 100 * 1024 * 1024, // uploads, default 100 MB
);
```

Set the same limit in your proxy, like `client_max_body_size` in nginx.

## Headers

Read one header, or all of them. A repeated header is joined with `', '`:

```dart
String? token = req.header('X-Token');
Map<String, dynamic> all = req.headers;
```

There are short methods for common headers:

```dart
req.userAgent();   // User-Agent header
req.host();        // Host header
req.origin();      // Origin header, or null
req.referer();     // Referer header, or null
req.locale;        // first language of Accept-Language, like 'th', or null
req.bearerToken(); // the token of 'Authorization: Bearer <token>', or null
```

### Body type

Check the body type, or if the client wants a JSON answer:

```dart
req.isJson();      // true for a JSON body
req.isFormData();  // true for multipart/form-data
req.expectsJson(); // true for a JSON Accept header, JSON body or XHR
```

## Method, path and URL

Read the method and the URL of the request:

```dart
req.method;          // 'GET'
req.path();          // '/admin/users/5'
req.fullUrl();       // 'https://example.com/admin/users/5?tab=info'
req.uri;             // the Uri
req.protocolVersion; // '1.1', or '2.0' for HTTP/2
```

Check where the request goes. `*` matches any text, and a route with no name never matches `routeIs`:

```dart
req.pathIs('admin/*');        // a path pattern
req.routeIs('admin.users.*'); // a route name
```

## Cookies

Read a cookie. Dox encrypts cookies by default, so you get the decrypted value:

```dart
String? token = req.cookie('token');
String? raw = req.cookie('theme', decrypt: false); // value as sent
```

See [Response](response.md#cookie) to set a cookie.

## Client IP and scheme

```dart
req.ip();       // client IP
req.scheme();   // http or https
req.isSecure(); // true for https
```

Behind a proxy, set `trustedProxies` in `AppConfig`, or `req.ip()` gives the proxy. See [Deployment](../digging-deeper/deployment.md#https-put-a-proxy-in-front).

## Other request data

These come from middleware:

```dart
req.requestId; // from RequestId, see Middleware
req.session;   // from SessionMiddleware, see Session
req.hasSession; // true when the route has a session
req.auth;      // the logged in user, see Authentication
```

See [Middleware](middleware.md#request-id), [Session](session.md) and [Authentication](../security/authentication.md).

## Send the response yourself

Write the response on `req.httpRequest.response`. After `takeOverResponse`, Dox sends nothing more for the request:

```dart
Future<void> handle(DoxRequest req) async {
  req.takeOverResponse();
  HttpResponse res = req.httpRequest.response;
  res.write('done');
  await res.close();
}
```

Your code must close the response. `req.responseTakenOver` gives true after the call.

## Next steps

- [DTO](dto.md): typed and checked input.
- [Validation](validation.md): the rules for input.
- [Response](response.md): send an answer.


---

# DTOs

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/the-basic/dto/

# DTOs

A DTO is a typed Dart class that describes the input of a request, so your controller gets checked data instead of a raw map.

A **DTO** (data transfer object) is a class with `@Dto()`. Each field has a Dart type and some [rules](validation.md#rules). When the input is wrong, the client gets 422, and your method does not run.

## Creating a DTO

Make a DTO with the CLI. It writes `lib/app/dtos/<name>/<name>.dto.dart`:

```bash
dox make:dto CreateUser
```

Then run the generator. It writes a `.dto.g.dart` file next to the DTO. `dox serve` and `dox build_runner:watch` run it on every save:

```bash
dox build_runner:build
```

## Defining fields

Each field is a final field and a parameter of the constructor. Put rules on a field as annotations:

```dart title="lib/app/dtos/create_user/create_user.dto.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

part 'create_user.dto.g.dart';

@Dto()
class CreateUser {
  @Trim()
  @Length(min: 3, max: 50)
  final String name;

  @Email()
  final String email;

  @Min(18)
  final int? age; // nullable, so optional

  const CreateUser({required this.name, required this.email, this.age});

  static const DtoSchema<CreateUser> schema = $CreateUserDto;
}
```

Keep the `part` line and the `schema` line. They connect the class to its generated code.

A field that is not nullable and has no default is required. See [Required and optional fields](validation.md#required-and-optional-fields).

### Field types

These field types work:

| Dart type | JSON | Query and form data |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `String`, `int`, `double`, `num`, `bool` | the same JSON type | text, converted |
| `DateTime` | an ISO 8601 string | the same |
| an `enum` | the name, like `"admin"` | the same |
| `RequestFile` | not allowed | a file part |
| a `@Dto` class | an object | bracket keys: `address[city]` |
| `List<T>` | an array | `tags=a&tags=b` or `tags[]=a` |
| `Map<String, T>` | an object | bracket keys: `meta[color]` |

JSON is strict: "18" is not an integer. See [Types in detail](validation-rules.md#types-in-detail).

### Numbers as text in JSON

Read numbers and bools that a client sends as text in JSON:

```dart
@Dto(coerce: true)
class UpdateStock {
  final int count; // {"count": "18"} gives 18
  final bool active; // {"active": 1} gives true

  const UpdateStock({required this.count, required this.active});
}
```

### Nested objects and lists

A field can be another `@Dto` class, or a list of them:

```dart
@Dto()
class CreateOrder {
  final Address address;

  @MinItems(1)
  final List<OrderItem> items;

  const CreateOrder({required this.address, required this.items});

  static const DtoSchema<CreateOrder> schema = $CreateOrderDto;
}
```

An error in a nested value has a path key, like `items.1.quantity`.

### Input keys

The input key is the field name in snake case, so `firstName` reads `first_name`. Use `@Name` to pick another key:

```dart
final String firstName; // key: first_name

@Name('emailAddress')
final String email; // key: emailAddress
```

`@Dto(keyCase: KeyCase.field)` uses the field names as they are. Unknown keys are dropped, and `@Dto(strict: true)` makes them an error. All options are in [Keys and DTO options](validation-rules.md#keys-and-dto-options).

## Registering DTOs

The generator writes the list of all DTOs to `lib/generated/dtos.g.dart`. Give it to the app config one time. A new app already has this line:

```dart title="lib/config/app.dart"
import 'package:my_app/generated/dtos.g.dart';

AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  dtos: dtos,
);
```

## Using a DTO in a controller

Add a parameter with the DTO type. Dox checks the request before your method runs:

```dart
@Inject()
class UserController {
  Future<User> store(CreateUser body) async {
    User user = User()
      ..name = body.name
      ..email = body.email;
    await user.save();
    return user;
  }
}
```

A method can have one DTO parameter, next to others like `DoxRequest` and path params. See [Controller: parameters](controller.md#parameters).

### Validating inside the method

Check the input later in the method. It gives the object, or throws the 422 error:

```dart
CreateUser data = await req.validate<CreateUser>();
```

### Body and query string

Dox reads one source. It never mixes the query and the body:

| Request | Dox reads |
| --- | --- |
| GET, HEAD, DELETE | the query string |
| POST, PUT, PATCH | the body (JSON, form or multipart) |

Set `source` to pick the source, on the DTO or on one call:

```dart
@Dto(source: Source.query) // on the DTO
class SearchUsers { ... }

await req.validate<SearchUsers>(source: Source.query); // for one call
```

Path params are not part of a DTO. See the [Pagination](../guides/pagination.md) guide for a full query DTO.

### Uploaded files

A `RequestFile` field reads a file from a multipart request. Add [file rules](validation-rules.md#files) to check its type and size:

```dart
@Image()
@MaxSize('2MB')
final RequestFile avatar;

@Mimes(<String>['pdf', 'docx'])
final List<RequestFile> documents;
```

Dox checks the real file type from its first bytes. To save the file, see [Request: form data](request.md#form-data-file).

## When validation fails

Dox answers 422 with one message for each field:

```json
{
  "email": "The email is not a valid email"
}
```

On a form post with a [session](session.md#validation-errors-and-old-input), Dox redirects back with the errors. To change the messages, see [Validation](validation.md).

## Converting a DTO

Build a DTO from trusted data with no checks, or turn it into a map with the input keys:

```dart
CreateUser user = CreateUser.schema.fromMap(<String, dynamic>{
  'name': 'Ann',
  'email': 'ann@dox.dev',
});
Map<String, dynamic> map = CreateUser.schema.toMap(user);
```

Get the JSON Schema of the DTO:

```dart
Map<String, dynamic> json = CreateUser.schema.toJsonSchema();
```

## Using a DTO in other places

- [OpenAPI docs](../guides/api-docs-with-openapi.md#5-see-how-a-dto-becomes-a-schema): each DTO becomes a schema. A `///` comment or `@Describe('...')` on a field becomes its description.
- [MCP tools](../packages/mcp.md#tools-that-take-a-dto): extend `McpDtoTool<T>` to get the checked object.
- [Flutter](../guides/share-code-with-flutter.md): import `dox_validation` in a shared package, and check a form before you send it.

## Testing

Make a DTO directly to skip the checks:

```dart
CreateUser input = const CreateUser(name: 'Ann', email: 'ann@dox.dev');
```

Test the checks with `safeValidateMap`. It never throws:

```dart
ParseResult<CreateUser> result =
    await CreateUser.schema.safeValidateMap(<String, dynamic>{
  'name': 'A',
  'email': 'not-an-email',
});

expect(result.success, isFalse);
expect(result.errors['email'], 'The email is not a valid email');
```

`validateMap` gives the object or throws. Pass `source: Source.query` to read the map like a query string, and `params:` to give path params. `@Unique` and `@Exists` need a test database.

- [Validation](validation.md): rules, messages and custom checks.
- [Validation rules](validation-rules.md): every rule and option.
- [Request](request.md): raw input and files.

# Validation

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/the-basic/validation/

# Validation

Validation checks the request input with a typed [DTO](dto.md) class, so your controller only gets good data.

Put rules on the fields of a DTO, then ask for it in your controller. When the input is wrong, Dox answers 422 with the errors:

```dart title="lib/app/dtos/create_user/create_user.dto.dart"
@Dto()
class CreateUser {
  @Trim()
  @Length(min: 3, max: 50)
  final String name;

  @Email()
  final String email;

  @MinLength(8)
  final String password;

  const CreateUser({
    required this.name,
    required this.email,
    required this.password,
  });

  static const DtoSchema<CreateUser> schema = $CreateUserDto;
}
```

```dart title="lib/app/http/controllers/user.controller.dart"
Future<User> store(CreateUser body) async {
  // body is already checked
  User user = User()
    ..name = body.name
    ..email = body.email
    ..password = await Hash.makeAsync(body.password);
  await user.save();
  return user;
}
```

To make and register a DTO, see [DTOs](dto.md).

## Required and optional fields

The Dart type decides if a field is required:

| Field | Key missing | Value null |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `final String name;` | error `required` | error `required` |
| `final int? age;` | null | null |
| `final Role role;` with `this.role = Role.user` | `Role.user` | error `required` |

Rules on an optional field run only when it has a value. The rules do not check a default value.

### Empty strings and spaces

An empty string counts as missing, so a required string rejects "". Add `@AllowEmpty()` to keep it:

```dart
@AllowEmpty()
final String note;
```

Spaces are kept, so "   " passes, unless the field has `@Trim()`. To trim all text fields, set it on the DTO:

```dart
@Dto(trim: true) // trim every text field
class CreatePost { ... }
```

`@Dto(emptyStringsToNull: true)` makes "" null.

### Using the default for bad values

Turn a bad value into the default, with no error. The field needs a default, a nullable type or a `Maybe` type:

```dart
@OrDefault()
@NotIn(<int>[0])
final int page; // with this.page = 1, page=abc and page=0 give 1
```

### Missing or null (for PATCH)

A `T?` field gives null for a missing key and for null. Use `Maybe<T>` to know the difference:

```dart
@Length(max: 500)
final Maybe<String?> bio; // default: const Maybe.missing()

// in the controller
if (body.bio.isPresent) {
  user.bio = body.bio.value; // can be null: the client cleared it
}
```

## Rules

Rules run from top to bottom, and the first rule that fails gives the error:

```dart
@Trim()
@Lowercase()
@Email()
@MaxLength(255)
final String email;
```

A rule on a list checks each item. Only the list rules check the list itself. Every rule, with its error code and message, is in [Validation rules](validation-rules.md):

| Kind | Annotations |
| --- | --- |
| Text | `@Length`, `@MinLength`, `@MaxLength`, `@Email`, `@Url`, `@Uuid`, `@Ulid`, `@Ip`, `@Regex`, `@In`, `@NotIn`, `@StartsWith`, `@EndsWith`, `@Alpha`, `@AlphaNumeric`, `@AlphaDash` |
| Change text | `@Trim`, `@Lowercase`, `@Uppercase`, `@AllowEmpty` |
| Numbers | `@Min`, `@Max`, `@Range`, `@Positive`, `@GreaterThan`, `@LessThan`, `@In`, `@NotIn` |
| Lists | `@MinItems`, `@MaxItems`, `@UniqueItems` |
| Dates | `@After`, `@Before`, `@AfterOrEqual`, `@BeforeOrEqual` |
| Other fields | `@Same`, `@Confirmed`, `@Different`, `@GreaterThanField`, `@GreaterThanOrEqualField`, `@LessThanField`, `@LessThanOrEqualField`, `@ProhibitedIf` |
| Present or missing | `@RequiredIf`, `@RequiredUnless`, `@RequiredWith`, `@RequiredWithout`, `@RequiredWithoutAll`, `@Filled`, `@Present`, `@Prohibited`, `@Accepted`, `@Declined` |
| Skip a field | `@ExcludeIf`, `@ExcludeUnless` |
| Files | `@MaxSize`, `@MinSize`, `@Mimes`, `@MimeTypes`, `@Image`, `@Dimensions` |
| Database | `@Unique`, `@Exists` |

## Checks across fields

Add a `validate` method to the DTO. Dox calls it after all field rules pass:

```dart
void validate(DtoErrors errors) {
  if (password != passwordConfirmation) {
    errors.add('password_confirmation', 'The passwords do not match');
  }
}
```

The key is the input key. Use `_root` for an error about the full body. `errors.has(key)` tells if a key already has an error. The method can be async.

## Database rules: `@Unique` and `@Exists`

Check the database, for example that an email is not taken. Import `package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart` in the DTO file:

```dart
@Unique('users', column: 'email')
final String email;

@Exists('teams') // column defaults to id
final int teamId;
```

For an update, skip the row of the route param:

```dart
// PUT /users/{id}
@Unique('users', column: 'email', ignoreParam: 'id')
final String email;
```

These rules run last. See [Validation rules: database](validation-rules.md#database).

## The error response

Dox answers 422 with one message for each field. The key is the path to the value:

```json
{
  "email": "The email is not a valid email",
  "tags.0": "The tags may not be greater than 20 characters",
  "items.1.quantity": "The quantity must be greater than 0"
}
```

On a form post with a [session](session.md#validation-errors-and-old-input), Dox redirects back with the errors. The `laravelErrors` flag sends `{"message": "...", "errors": {"field": ["..."]}}`. See [Core flags](../reference/app-config.md#core-flags).

For another shape, read `error.issues` of the `ValidationException` in your [ExceptionHandler](errors.md). Each issue has `dottedPath`, `code`, `message` and `params`.

## Messages

Set your own error text. There are three places, and the first one wins.

On the rule:

```dart
@Email(message: 'Please check your email')
final String email;
```

On the DTO, by code or by `key.code`. Use `*` for list items, like `'tags.*.required'`:

```dart
@Dto(messages: <String, String>{
  'email.required': 'We need your email',
  'integer': 'The {field} must be a number',
})
```

For the full app, with a `MessageResolver`:

```dart
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  validationMessages: MessageResolver(
    messages: <String, String>{'required': 'Please fill in {field}'},
  ),
);
```

A message can use `{field}` (the last key), `{value}`, and rule values like `{min}` and `{max}`.

### Messages in other languages

Extend `MessageResolver` and override `resolve`. `request.locale` comes from Accept-Language:

```dart
class AppMessages extends MessageResolver {
  static const Map<String, Map<String, String>> _texts =
      <String, Map<String, String>>{
    'th': <String, String>{'required': 'กรุณากรอก {field}'},
  };

  @override
  String resolve(MessageRequest request) {
    String? template = _texts[request.locale]?[request.code];
    if (template == null) {
      return super.resolve(request);
    }
    return format(template, request.params);
  }
}
```

`setMessages` adds messages to a resolver at a later time.

### Names for `{field}`

Show a nice name in place of the key, on the DTO:

```dart
@Dto(attributes: <String, String>{'first_name': 'first name'})
class CreateUser { ... }
// The first name is required
```

Or for the full app, also for fluent schemas:

```dart
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  validationMessages: MessageResolver(
    attributes: <String, String>{'first_name': 'first name'},
  ),
);
```

The key in the error response stays the same. `setAttributes` adds names later, and a custom resolver can override `attributeName(path)`.

### Short rule names in message keys

With the `laravelMessageKeys` flag, a message key can use a short name. So `'name.min'` gives the message for the `min_length` error of `name`. Set it in the `setup()` of a provider, like the [other flags](../packages/validation.md#opt-in-flags):

```dart
Validator.flags = const ValidationFlags(laravelMessageKeys: true);
```

The full code wins over the short name. The error code in the response stays `min_length`:

| Dox code | Short name |
| --- | --- |
| `min_length` | `min` |
| `max_length` | `max` |
| `length` | `size` |
| `length_between` | `between` |
| `start_with` | `starts_with` |
| `end_with` | `ends_with` |
| `alpha_numeric` | `alpha_num` |
| `greater_than` | `gt` |
| `less_than` | `lt` |
| `min_items` | `min` |
| `max_items` | `max` |
| `unique_items` | `distinct` |
| `min_size` | `min` |
| `max_size` | `max` |
| `mime_types` | `mimetypes` |
| `datetime` | `date` |

## Custom rules

Extend `Rule<T>`. `T` is the field type, or the item type for a list:

```dart
class Slug extends Rule<String> {
  const Slug({super.message});

  @override
  String get name => 'slug'; // the error code

  @override
  String get defaultMessage => 'The {field} must be a slug';

  @override
  bool check(String value, RuleContext context) {
    return _pattern.hasMatch(value);
  }

  static final RegExp _pattern = RegExp(r'^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$');
}
```

Then use it like any rule:

```dart
@Slug()
final String slug;
```

- Override `params` to give values to the message, like `{'min': 3}`.
- Override `toJsonSchema` to add JSON Schema keys, like `{'format': 'slug'}`.
- `context.lookup('other.key')` reads another input value, and `context.sibling('key')` reads a field next to this one. Both give `undefined` for a missing value.
- `context.value`, `context.field` and `context.root` give the value, the field name and the full input.

### Rules that read the database

Extend `AsyncRule<T>` and write `checkAsync`:

```dart
class FreeName extends AsyncRule<String> {
  const FreeName({super.message});

  @override
  String get name => 'free_name';

  @override
  String get defaultMessage => 'The {field} is taken';

  @override
  Future<bool> checkAsync(String value, RuleContext context) async {
    return await nameIsFree(value); // your database check
  }
}
```

For a list field, override `failedItems` to check all items in one query. It gives the indexes of the bad items.

## Dynamic input

For input you know only at runtime, like form fields from the database, use a fluent schema:

```dart
Map<String, dynamic> data = await req.validateSchema(v.object(fields));
```

See [Fluent schemas](../packages/validation.md#fluent-schemas-for-dynamic-input).

## Testing

Test the checks of a DTO with `safeValidateMap`. See [DTOs: testing](dto.md#testing).

- [DTOs](dto.md): the typed class that holds the input.
- [Validation rules](validation-rules.md): every rule.
- [Validation package](../packages/validation.md): opt-in flags, fluent schemas and use without Dox.

# Validation rules

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/the-basic/validation-rules/

# Validation rules

This page lists every annotation you can put on a `@Dto` field, with its error code and default message.

To learn how DTOs work, read [Validation](validation.md) first. How to read the tables:

- Code is the error code. Use it in `@Dto(messages: ...)` and in a `MessageResolver`.
- Message is the default English text. `{field}` is the last key of the path.
- Every annotation also takes `message:`. It wins over every other message.
- All limits include the limit itself, unless the table says "exclusive".
- On a list field, a value rule checks each item. Only the list rules check the list itself.

## Type errors

You get these errors when a value does not fit the field type. They have no annotation.

| Code | When | Message |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `required` | a required field is missing, null, or "" | `The {field} is required` |
| `string` | not a string | `The {field} must be a string` |
| `integer` | not a whole number | `The {field} must be an integer` |
| `numeric` | not a number (`double`, `num`) | `The {field} must be a number` |
| `boolean` | not a bool | `The {field} must be a boolean` |
| `date` | not an ISO 8601 date | `The {field} must be a date` |
| `in` | not a name of the enum | `The selected {field} is invalid. Valid options are {values}` |
| `array` | not a list | `The {field} must be an array` |
| `object` | not an object (nested DTO, `Map`) | `The {field} must be an object` |
| `file` | not a file | `The {field} must be a file` |
| `unrecognized_keys` | unknown key, with `@Dto(strict: true)` | `The {field} field is not allowed` |

## Text

Use these rules on string fields and string list items:

| Annotation | Code | Message | JSON Schema |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@Length(min: 3, max: 50)` | `length_between` | `The {field} must be between {min} and {max} characters` | `minLength`, `maxLength` |
| `@Length(min: 6, max: 6)` | `length` | `The {field} must be exactly {length} characters` | `minLength`, `maxLength` |
| `@MinLength(3)` | `min_length` | `The {field} must be at least {min} characters` | `minLength` |
| `@MaxLength(50)` | `max_length` | `The {field} may not be greater than {max} characters` | `maxLength` |
| `@Email()` | `email` | `The {field} is not a valid email` | `format: email` |
| `@Url()` | `url` | `The {field} must be a url` | `format: uri` |
| `@Uuid()` | `uuid` | `The {field} is invalid uuid` | `format: uuid` |
| `@Ulid()` | `ulid` | `The {field} must be a valid ULID` | `pattern` |
| `@Ip()` | `ip` | `The {field} must be an ip address` | `anyOf` `ipv4` / `ipv6` |
| `@Regex(r'[a-z]+')` | `regex` | `The {field} format is invalid` | `pattern` |
| `@In(['a', 'b'])` | `in` | `The selected {field} is invalid. Valid options are {values}` | `enum` |
| `@NotIn(['root'])` | `not_in` | `The {field} field cannot be {value}` | `not: {enum}` |
| `@StartsWith('dox')` | `start_with` | `The {field} must start with {prefix}` | `pattern` |
| `@EndsWith('.dev')` | `end_with` | `The {field} must end with {suffix}` | `pattern` |
| `@Alpha()` | `alpha` | `The {field} must be an alphabetic` | `pattern` |
| `@AlphaNumeric()` | `alpha_numeric` | `The {field} must be only alphabetic and number` | `pattern` |
| `@AlphaDash()` | `alpha_dash` | `The {field} must be only alphabetic, number, dash and underscore` | `pattern` |

- `@Length` needs `min:`, `max:` or both. With one of them, it acts like `@MinLength` or `@MaxLength`.
- Length counts characters (Unicode code points), so é counts as 1.
- `@Url()` needs http or https and a host.
- `@Uuid()` takes any version, in upper or lower case.
- `@Ulid()` takes 26 Crockford base32 characters, in upper or lower case. The first one is 0 to 7.
- `@Regex` must match the full value, so you do not need `^` and `$`. A bad regex stops the build.
- The alpha rules use the ASCII letters a-z and A-Z. `@AlphaDash()` also allows the digits 0-9, `-` and `_`.
- `@In` and `@NotIn` compare exactly, and case matters.

## More text rules

These are also for string fields:

| Annotation | Code | Message | JSON Schema |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@Json()` | `json` | `The {field} is not a valid json` | `contentMediaType: application/json` |
| `@Digits(6)` | `digits` | `The {field} must be {digits} digits` | `pattern` |
| `@DigitsBetween(4, 6)` | `digits_between` | `The {field} must be between {min} and {max} digits` | `pattern` |
| `@DateFormatted('Y-m-d')` | `date_format` | `The {field} must match the format {format}` | |
| `@HexColor()`, `@HexColor(short: true)` | `hex_color` | `The {field} must be a hex color like #1a2b3c` | `pattern` |
| `@Password(min: 8, ...)` | `password` | `The {field} must have {rules}` | `minLength` |

- `@HexColor()` takes # and 6 hex digits, in any case. With `short: true` it also takes 3 digits, like #abc.
- `@Digits` and `@DigitsBetween` take only 0-9, with no sign and no dot. Use a string field, so leading zeros stay.
- `@DateFormatted` uses these letters:
  day `d`, `j`, `D` (Mon), `l` (Monday), `N`, `w`, `S` (st), `z`;
  month `m`, `n`, `M` (Jan), `F` (January), `t`;
  year `Y`, `y`, `L`;
  time `a`, `A`, `g`, `h`, `G`, `H`, `i`, `s`, `v`, `u`;
  time zone `e`, `T`, `P`, `p`, `O`, `Z`, `I`;
  full `U`, `c`, `r`.
  Put `\` before a letter to use it as text, like `Y-m-d\TH:i`. Any other letter stops the build. Other characters must be there as they are.
  `j`, `n`, `g`, `G`, `z` and `U` take no leading zero, so `j/n/Y` rejects 01/02/2024.
  The date must exist, so 2023-02-29 fails. Names need the case shown (Jan, not jan), and a day name must fit the date. The field stays a string. Use a `DateTime` field for ISO 8601 dates.
- `@Password` options: `min` (default 8), `letters`, `mixedCase` (one upper and one lower case letter), `numbers` and `symbols`. The others are off by default. Letters, numbers and symbols are Unicode. `{rules}` lists the options you set, like "at least 8 characters and one number".

## Other fields

These rules read another key of the same object, like a password and its confirmation. Give the input key, like `account_type`, not the Dart name. A Dart name stops the build.

| Annotation | Code | Message |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@Confirmed()` | `confirmed` | `The {field} confirmation does not match` |
| `@Same('email')` | `same` | `The {field} must match {other}` |
| `@RequiredIf('type', 'company')` | `required_if` | `The {field} is required when {other} is {values}` |
| `@RequiredWith(['phone'])` | `required_with` | `The {field} is required when {others} is present` |
| `@RequiredUnless('type', 'guest')` | `required_unless` | `The {field} is required unless {other} is {values}` |
| `@RequiredWithout(['email'])` | `required_without` | `The {field} is required when {others} is not present` |
| `@RequiredWithoutAll(['email', 'phone'])` | `required_without_all` | `The {field} is required when none of {others} are present` |
| `@Different('old_password')` | `different` | `The {field} and {other} must be different` |
| `@ProhibitedIf('type', 'guest')` | `prohibited_if` | `The {field} is prohibited when {other} is {values}` |
| `@GreaterThanField('min_price')` | `greater_than` | `The {field} must be greater than {min}` |
| `@GreaterThanOrEqualField('min_price')` | `min` | `The {field} must be greater than or equal {min}` |
| `@LessThanField('max_price')` | `less_than` | `The {field} must be less than {max}` |
| `@LessThanOrEqualField('max_price')` | `max` | `The {field} must be less than or equal {max}` |

- `@Confirmed()` on `password` needs the key `password_confirmation` with the same value. The error is on `password`. Use `@Confirmed(other: 'password_again')` for another key. The DTO needs no field for the confirmation key.
- `@Confirmed`, `@Same` and `@Different` compare the raw input of both keys, so `@Trim` does not change the compare. A missing other key passes `@Different`.
- Text and numbers match by text, so 1234 matches "1234".
- The required rules work on a nullable field, a `Maybe` field or a field with a default. On an always-required field the build stops.
- `@RequiredIf` and `@RequiredUnless` also take a list of values, like `@RequiredIf('type', ['company', 'shop'])`. An enum value matches its name: `@RequiredIf('role', Role.admin)` matches "admin".
- `@RequiredWith`: the field is required when any of the keys has a value. `@RequiredWithout`: when any of the keys is missing. `@RequiredWithoutAll`: when all of them are missing.
- `@RequiredUnless`: a missing other key counts as null, so the field is required then.
- `@ProhibitedIf`: when the other key matches, the field must be missing or empty. 0 and false fail.
- The field compare rules (`@GreaterThanField` and the others) are for number fields. A missing other key, or one that is not a number, fails. `{min}` and `{max}` in the message are the other key.
- On a list field, `@Different` checks the full list. The field compare rules do not fit a list.
- Missing means: not there, null, blank text, an empty list or an empty map.

## Present or missing

These rules check if a key is sent and has a value:

| Annotation | Code | Message |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@Filled()` | `filled` | `The {field} must have a value` |
| `@Present()` | `present` | `The {field} must be present` |
| `@Prohibited()` | `prohibited` | `The {field} is prohibited` |
| `@Accepted()` | `accepted` | `The {field} must be accepted` |
| `@Declined()` | `declined` | `The {field} must be declined` |

- `@Filled()`: a missing key passes. A sent key must have a value: not null, not blank text, not an empty list.
- `@Present()`: the key must be sent. Its value can be null or empty.
- `@Prohibited()`: the key must be missing, or blank text. Any other value fails, also null, `[]`, `{}`, 0 and false.
- `@Filled`, `@Present` and `@Prohibited` are for a nullable, `Maybe` or default field.
- `@Accepted()` takes true, 1, "1", "true", "yes" and "on". `@Declined()` takes false, 0, "0", "false", "no" and "off". The text is case sensitive. Use them on a bool field with no default. In a JSON body a bool field takes only true and false, unless the DTO has `@Dto(coerce: true)`.

```dart
@Accepted()
final bool terms;

@Present()
final String? note; // the key must be there, null is fine
```

## Skip a field

These rules skip a field for some input, like a VAT number that is only for a company:

| Annotation | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `@ExcludeIf('type', 'person')` | when `type` is person, the field is skipped |
| `@ExcludeUnless('type', 'company')` | unless `type` is company, the field is skipped |

- A skipped field gets its default, null or `Maybe.missing()`, as if it was not sent.
- They match like `@RequiredIf`, also with a list of values.
- `@ExcludeIf`: a missing other key does not skip. `@ExcludeUnless`: a missing other key counts as null, so the field is skipped.
- They are for a nullable, `Maybe` or default field.
- Fluent schemas have `.excludeIf()` and `.excludeUnless()`. See [Skip a field](../packages/validation.md#skip-a-field).

```dart
final String type;

@ExcludeIf('type', 'person')
@MinLength(5)
final String? vatNumber; // not checked for a person
```

## Change text

These change the value before the rules run. They always run in this order: `@Trim`, then `@Lowercase` or `@Uppercase`, then the "empty string is missing" check.

| Annotation | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `@Trim()` | removes spaces at the start and the end |
| `@Lowercase()` | makes the text lower case |
| `@Uppercase()` | makes the text upper case |
| `@AllowEmpty()` | keeps "" as a value. Without it, "" counts as missing. |

`@Lowercase()` and `@Uppercase()` together stop the build.

## Bad value to default

| Annotation | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `@OrDefault()` | a bad value gives the default of the field (or null, or `Maybe.missing()`), not an error. |

- It drops type errors and the errors of the normal rules of the field.
- Errors from async rules and from `validate()` still give 422.
- The field needs a default, a nullable type or a `Maybe` type.

## Numbers

Use these rules on `int`, `double` and `num` fields and list items:

| Annotation | Code | Message | JSON Schema |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@Min(18)` | `min` | `The {field} must be greater than or equal {min}` | `minimum` |
| `@Max(100)` | `max` | `The {field} must be less than or equal {max}` | `maximum` |
| `@Range(1, 10)` | `between` | `The {field} must be between {min} and {max}` | `minimum`, `maximum` |
| `@Positive()` | `greater_than` | `The {field} must be greater than 0` | `exclusiveMinimum: 0` |
| `@GreaterThan(0.5)` | `greater_than` | `The {field} must be greater than {min}` (exclusive) | `exclusiveMinimum` |
| `@LessThan(100)` | `less_than` | `The {field} must be less than {max}` (exclusive) | `exclusiveMaximum` |
| `@In([1, 2, 3])` | `in` | `The selected {field} is invalid. Valid options are {values}` | `enum` |
| `@NotIn([0])` | `not_in` | `The {field} field cannot be {value}` | `not: {enum}` |

`@Min(1.5)` on an `int` field stops the build.

## Lists

Use these rules on list fields. They check the list, not the items:

| Annotation | Code | Message | JSON Schema |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@MinItems(1)` | `min_items` | `The {field} must have at least {min} items` | `minItems` |
| `@MaxItems(5)` | `max_items` | `The {field} may not have more than {max} items` | `maxItems` |
| `@UniqueItems()` | `unique_items` | `The {field} must not have duplicate items` | `uniqueItems: true` |

`@UniqueItems()` works for strings, numbers, bools, enums and dates. On a list of DTOs it stops the build.

## Dates

Use these rules on `DateTime` fields:

| Annotation | Code | Message | JSON Schema |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@After('2000-01-01')` | `after` | `The {field} must be a date after {date}` | `format: date-time` |
| `@Before('now')` | `before` | `The {field} must be a date before {date}` | `format: date-time` |
| `@AfterOrEqual('today')` | `after_or_equal` | `The {field} must be a date after or equal to {date}` | `format: date-time` |
| `@BeforeOrEqual('end_date')` | `before_or_equal` | `The {field} must be a date before or equal to {date}` | `format: date-time` |

- The value is one of these:
    - an ISO 8601 date, like '2000-01-01',
    - a word: 'now' (the time of the request), 'today', 'tomorrow' or 'yesterday'. These are in UTC, and 'today' is the start of the day,
    - the input key of another date field of the same DTO, like 'start_date'. When that field has no value, the check passes.
- `@After` and `@Before` are exclusive. `@AfterOrEqual` and `@BeforeOrEqual` accept the same time.

```dart
final DateTime startDate;

@After('start_date')
@BeforeOrEqual('tomorrow')
final DateTime endDate;
```

## Files

Use these rules on `RequestFile` and `List<RequestFile>` fields:

| Annotation | Code | Message | JSON Schema |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@MaxSize('2MB')` | `max_size` | `The {field} may not be larger than {max}` | `maxLength` (bytes) |
| `@Mimes(['pdf', 'png'])` | `mimes` | `The {field} must be a file of type: {types}` | `contentMediaType` |
| `@Image()` | `image` | `The {field} must be an image` | `contentMediaType: image/*` |
| `@MinSize('10KB')` | `min_size` | `The {field} must be at least {min}` | `minLength` (bytes) |
| `@MimeTypes(['image/png', 'image/*'])` | `mime_types` | `The {field} must be a file of type: {types}` | `contentMediaType` |
| `@Dimensions(minWidth: 100, ratio: 3 / 2)` | `dimensions` | `The {field} has invalid image dimensions` | `contentMediaType: image/*` |

- Size units are B, KB, MB and GB. 1KB is 1024 bytes.
- `@Mimes` takes file extensions. Dox finds the real type from the first bytes of the file. The file name extension must not name another type, or a type a browser runs (like html or svg). For zip types (like docx), the extension must match too. For types with no byte signature (like txt or csv), Dox uses the extension.
- `@Image()` is `@Mimes(['jpg', 'jpeg', 'png', 'gif', 'webp', 'bmp'])`, with no svg.
- `@MimeTypes` takes MIME types and checks the real bytes like `@Mimes`. `image/*` means jpg, jpeg, png, gif, webp, bmp, tif, tiff, ico, heic, heif, avif and psd. Browsers can not show most of these, so for web images use `@Image()`. Write `image/jpeg`: `image/jpg` never matches.
- `@Dimensions` limits: `width`, `height` (exact), `minWidth`, `maxWidth`, `minHeight`, `maxHeight` and `ratio` (width / height). It reads the header of PNG, GIF, WebP and JPEG files. Any other file fails. A ratio passes when it is off by less than one pixel.

With fluent schemas, use `v.file()`. Sizes there are in bytes:

```dart
v.file()
    .maxSize(2 * 1024 * 1024) // 2 MB
    .mimeTypes(<String>['image/jpeg', 'image/png'])
    .dimensions(minWidth: 100, maxWidth: 2000);
```

The fluent methods are `maxSize`, `minSize`, `mimes`, `mimeTypes`, `dimensions`, `image` and `extensions`.

## Database

These rules come from `dox_orm`. They run after all other checks pass:

| Annotation | Code | Message |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@Unique(table, {column, ignoreParam, ignoreColumn, connection})` | `unique` | `The {field} has already been taken` |
| `@Exists(table, {column, connection})` | `exists` | `The selected {field} is invalid` |

- The default column of `@Unique` is the input key. The default column of `@Exists` is id.
- They read the table, not the model, so soft-deleted rows count too.
- `ignoreParam: 'id'` skips the row where `ignoreColumn` (default id) equals the path param `{id}`.

See [Database rules](validation.md#database-rules-unique-and-exists). In a fluent schema, use `v.string().unique('users', column: 'email')` and `v.int().exists('teams')`. See [Fluent schemas](../packages/validation.md#more-rules).

## Keys and DTO options

These options change how the full DTO reads its input:

| Annotation | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `@Name('emailAddress')` | the input key for this field. Default: the field name in snake case. |
| `@Dto()` | marks the class. |
| `@Dto(source: Source.query)` | where to read: `Source.auto` (default), `Source.query`, `Source.body`. |
| `@Dto(keyCase: KeyCase.field)` | keys: `KeyCase.snake` (default) or `KeyCase.field` (the Dart name as it is). |
| `@Dto(strict: true)` | unknown keys are errors. Default false: they are dropped. |
| `@Dto(emptyStringsToNull: true)` | "" is read as null, not as missing. Default false. |
| `@Dto(trim: true)` | trims every string field and text item, like `@Trim()` on each. Default false. |
| `@Dto(coerce: true)` | a JSON body can send text for numbers and bools, like a form. Default false. |
| `@Dto(messages: {...})` | messages by code or `key.code`. A dotted path like `address.city.required` or `tags.*.required` works too. See [Short rule names](validation.md#short-rule-names-in-message-keys). |
| `@Dto(attributes: {...})` | the names shown for `{field}`, by key. See [Names for field](validation.md#names-for-field). |
| `@Describe('...')` | on a field: the description of the field in the JSON Schema. |

A nested DTO uses its own `trim` and `coerce`. A `///` doc comment on a field also becomes its description. `@Describe` wins over it. The OpenAPI docs and MCP tools show it:

```dart
@Describe('Category ID (see list_categories).')
final int categoryId;
```

## Types in detail

This is how each field type reads input. The short table is in [Field types](dto.md#field-types).

- JSON is strict. In a JSON body, "18" is not an integer, and you get the error `integer`. With `@Dto(coerce: true)`, JSON is read like form text for numbers and bools, and a bool also takes 1 and 0.
- Query and form data are text. Dox changes the text into the field type first.
- `int` takes 18 or 18.0, never a fraction.
- `bool` in text takes true, 1, yes, on and false, 0, no, off, in any case.
- `DateTime` takes 2024-01-31 or 2024-01-31T10:00:00Z. A value with no time zone is read as UTC, and the result is always UTC. A timestamp number is not allowed.
- An enum matches the Dart name exactly, so "Admin" does not match `Role.admin`.
- `Object?` and `dynamic` take any value, with no check.
- `Map<String, dynamic>` must be an object. Its values are not checked.
- In query and form data, one value for a list field gives a list with one item. Bracket indexes are sorted and packed, so `items[3]` alone gives a list with one item.
- In query and form data, a list can have at most 1000 items, and keys can nest at most 10 levels. More gives 422 with the key `_root`.

## Body types

The content type of the body decides how Dox reads it:

| Body | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `application/json` (or any `+json` type) | read with strict JSON types |
| `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, `multipart/form-data` | read as text, then converted |
| any other content type | 415 Unsupported Media Type |
| JSON that is not valid | 400 Bad Request |
| JSON that is not an object (like `[1, 2]`) | 422 with the key `_root` |

## The order of checks

Dox checks the input in four steps:

1. Read the input and convert types. Change text (`@Trim`, `@Lowercase`, `@Uppercase`). Find missing required fields and run the rules that read other keys, except `@Confirmed` and `@Same`.
2. The field rules, top to bottom. The first rule that fails stops the other rules of that field. A fluent schema runs all rules, unless you add `.bail()`. See [Stop at the first error](../packages/validation.md#stop-at-the-first-error).
3. The `validate()` method, nested DTOs first.
4. Async rules (`@Unique`, `@Exists`, your `AsyncRule`), one at a time, in field order.

Each step runs only when the step before it had no errors, so the database never gets input that is already wrong. Inside one step, Dox collects the errors of all fields.

## What the generator checks

The build stops with a clear error when:

- a field is not final, or is not a parameter of the unnamed constructor,
- a field type is not supported (see [Field types](dto.md#field-types)),
- a rule does not fit the field type (like `@Email()` on an `int`),
- a `Maybe<T>` field has no `const Maybe.missing()` default,
- a required, present, prohibited or exclude rule, or `@OrDefault()`, is on a field that is always required,
- a rule that reads another key names a Dart field (like `accountType`) instead of its input key (`account_type`),
- a date rule has a text that is not a date, a word or another date field,
- `@DateFormatted` has a letter it does not know,
- `@Regex` has a bad pattern, or a size text is bad,
- two `@Dto` classes in the app have the same name,
- the class is generic, or extends another class (other than `Object`).

## Next steps

- [Validation](validation.md): messages, custom rules and checks across fields.
- [DTOs](dto.md): make and use a DTO.
- [Validation package](../packages/validation.md): fluent schemas.

# Controller

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/the-basic/controller/

# Controller

A controller holds the code that answers a route, so your route files stay short.

## Writing controllers

### Basic controllers

Make a controller with the CLI. It writes `lib/app/http/controllers/blog.controller.dart` with an empty `index` method:

```bash
dox make:controller Blog
```

Fill in the method:

```dart title="lib/app/http/controllers/blog.controller.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

@Inject()
class BlogController {
  String index(DoxRequest req) {
    return 'all blogs';
  }
}
```

Then point a route to it:

```dart title="lib/routes/api.dart"
Route.get('/blogs', (BlogController c) => c.index);
```

`@Inject()` puts the controller in the container, so its constructor can ask for services. Run `dart run build_runner build` after you add one. See [Dependency injection](dependency-injection.md).

### Static methods

A static method works when the controller needs nothing from the container:

```dart
class AppController {
  static String ping(DoxRequest req) {
    return 'pong';
  }
}

Route.get('/ping', AppController.ping);
```

### Plain functions

A plain function works too:

```dart
String listBlog(DoxRequest req) {
  return 'all blogs';
}

Route.get('/blogs', listBlog);
```

## Resource controllers

A **resource controller** has the 7 methods that `Route.resource` uses. Make one with `-r`:

```bash
dox make:controller Blog -r
```

```dart title="lib/app/http/controllers/blog.controller.dart"
/// Route: Route.resource('path', BlogController);
@Inject()
class BlogController {
  /// GET /resource
  Future<dynamic> index(DoxRequest req) async {}

  /// GET /resource/create
  Future<dynamic> create(DoxRequest req) async {}

  /// POST /resource
  Future<dynamic> store(DoxRequest req) async {}

  /// GET /resource/{id}
  Future<dynamic> show(DoxRequest req, int id) async {}

  /// GET /resource/{id}/edit
  Future<dynamic> edit(DoxRequest req, int id) async {}

  /// PUT|PATCH /resource/{id}
  Future<dynamic> update(DoxRequest req, int id) async {}

  /// DELETE /resource/{id}
  Future<dynamic> destroy(DoxRequest req, int id) async {}
}
```

Register it with one route. `Route.resource` skips the methods you delete:

```dart title="lib/routes/api.dart"
Route.resource('blogs', BlogController);
```

See [Routing: resource routes](routing.md#resource-routes).

### API resource controllers

Make a resource controller with no `create` and `edit`, for an API with no form pages:

```bash
dox make:controller Blog --api
```

### Resource controllers for a model

Fill the methods with code for one model:

```bash
dox make:controller Blog --model=Blog
```

```dart title="lib/app/http/controllers/blog.controller.dart"
@Inject()
class BlogController {
  Future<dynamic> index(DoxRequest req) async {
    return Blog().all();
  }

  Future<dynamic> store(DoxRequest req) async {
    return Blog().create(req.body);
  }

  Future<dynamic> show(DoxRequest req, Blog blog) async {
    return blog;
  }

  Future<dynamic> update(DoxRequest req, Blog blog) async {
    await blog.update(req.body);
    return blog;
  }

  Future<dynamic> destroy(DoxRequest req, Blog blog) async {
    await blog.delete();
  }

  // ... create and edit
}
```

[Route model binding](dependency-injection.md#route-model-binding) loads the model by the `{id}`, and no row answers 404. `create()` and `update()` take only the columns in the `fillable` list of the model, so add your columns there first.

You can use `--api` and `--model` together. `dox make:model Blog -r` makes the model and this controller in one step.

## Parameters

A controller method asks for what it needs by type, and Dox fills each parameter:

```dart
Route.put('/teams/{teamId}/users/{id}', (UserController c) => c.update);

@Inject()
class UserController {
  Future<User> update(int teamId, int id, UpdateUser body) async { ... }
}
```

These types work:

| Parameter type | Dox gives |
| --- | --- |
| `DoxRequest` | the request |
| a `@Dto` class | the checked body or query. See [Validation](validation.md). |
| `String`, `int`, `double`, `num`, `bool` | the path params, in the order of the route |
| the same types with `?` | an optional path param (`{id?}`). null when it is not in the URL. |
| a `@DoxModel` class | the model, loaded by the route param. See [route model binding](dependency-injection.md#route-model-binding). |
| an `@Inject()` class | the instance from the [container](dependency-injection.md#handler-parameters) |

The parameters can be in any order. The first path param parameter gets the first `{...}` in the route. These rules apply:

- At most one `@Dto` parameter.
- Only positional parameters.
- A catch-all `{path*}` param is a string.
- The same rules work for static methods and plain functions.

The server does not start when a parameter type is not in the list, or when the method has more path params than the route.

### Path param types

Dox changes the text from the URL into the type. Text that does not fit gets 404:

- `int`: "42" is 42. "abc" or "4.5" gives 404.
- `double`, `num`: "4.5" is 4.5.
- `bool`: true or 1 is true. false or 0 is false. Any other text gives 404.

Dox checks path params before the DTO.

## Next steps

- [Response](response.md): return a string, a map, a model, a file and more.
- [Dependency injection](dependency-injection.md): give services to a controller.
- [Request](request.md): read the input.

# Dependency injection

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/the-basic/dependency-injection/

# Dependency injection

The Dox container makes your classes and gives each constructor what it needs, so you never wire classes by hand.

Put `@Inject()` above a class, and `dox_builder` adds it to the **container**. Then any class can ask for it in its constructor.

## Setup

The builder writes `lib/generated/container.g.dart`. Give it to the app one time:

```dart title="lib/config/app.dart"
import 'package:my_app/generated/container.g.dart';

AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  container: registerContainer,
);
```

Run the builder again after you add a class:

```bash
dart run build_runner build
```

Do not edit the generated file. Dox finds classes in `lib/` only.

## A full example

A repository reads the database, a service holds the business logic, and a controller answers the route. Each one asks for the one below it:

```dart title="lib/app/repositories/user.repository.dart"
@Inject()
class UserRepository {
  Future<User?> find(int id) => User().find(id);
}
```

```dart title="lib/app/services/user.service.dart"
@Inject()
class UserService {
  UserService(this.users);

  final UserRepository users;

  Future<User> show(int id) async {
    User? user = await users.find(id);
    if (user == null) throw NotFoundHttpException();
    return user;
  }
}
```

```dart title="lib/app/http/controllers/user.controller.dart"
@Inject()
class UserController {
  UserController(this.service);

  final UserService service;

  Future<User> show(int id) => service.show(id);
}
```

```dart title="lib/routes/api.dart"
Route.get('/users/{id}', (UserController c) => c.show);
```

GET /api/users/5 makes the repository, the service and the controller, and calls `show(5)`.

## Lifetime

`@Inject()` makes one instance for each isolate, on first use. For a new instance each time, use `singleton: false`:

```dart
@Inject(singleton: false)
class ReportBuilder {}
```

Isolates do not share objects. Keep state that all isolates must see in the cache or the database.

## Constructor parameters

Dox finds each constructor parameter by its type. Positional and named parameters both work. If the type is not in the container, an optional parameter keeps its default, and a nullable parameter gets null.

### Abstract types

A parameter of an abstract type gets the one container class that implements it:

```dart
abstract class Mailer {}

@Inject()
class SmtpMailer implements Mailer {}

@Inject()
class SignupService {
  SignupService(this.mailer); // gets the SmtpMailer

  final Mailer mailer;
}
```

This works for constructor parameters only. `get<Mailer>()` and handler parameters need the class itself.

## Routes to controller methods

Pass a function that picks the method. Dox finds the controller by the parameter type, one time for each isolate at start:

```dart
Route.get('/posts', (PostController c) => c.index);
Route.resource('posts', PostController);
```

See [Controller: parameters](controller.md#parameters).

## Handler parameters

A controller method or a route function can ask for any class of the container:

```dart
Route.get('/stats', (StatsService stats) => stats.today());
```

Dox reads a singleton one time, at start, and makes a `singleton: false` class on each request.

## Route model binding

Every `@DoxModel` class gets a binder. A handler parameter of a model type gets the model, loaded by its primary key:

```dart
Route.get('/posts/{post}', (PostController c) => c.show);

@Inject()
class PostController {
  Post show(Post post) => post;
}
```

Dox uses the route param with the name of the model, like `{post}` for `Post` or `{blogPost}` for `BlogPost`. Else it uses the next route param, like `{id}`. A missing row gives 404.

A binder from `Route.bind` wins. See [Routing: route model binding](routing.md#route-model-binding).

## Routers and providers

Dox finds every class that extends `Router` or `DoxProvider`, with no `@Inject()`. It registers the routes and runs `setup()` of each provider at start, in every isolate. Their constructors also get parameters from the container.

They run in the order of their file path. To pick the order, list them in `AppConfig`. The others follow:

```dart
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  container: registerContainer,
  providers: <DoxProvider>[ORMProvider()], // runs first
  routers: <Router>[ApiRouter()],          // registered first
);
```

A provider can add global middleware. See [Middleware](middleware.md#global-middleware).

## Using the container in code

`Dox().ioc` is the container of the current isolate. Get a class:

```dart
UserService users = Dox().ioc.get<UserService>();
```

`get` throws when the class is not in the container. Check first with `has`:

```dart
if (Dox().ioc.has<UserService>()) {
  // ...
}
```

### Adding classes by hand

`singleton` makes one instance on first use, `factory` makes a new one on each `get`, and `instance` uses the value you give:

```dart
Dox().ioc.singleton<Clock>((IocContainer c) => Clock());
Dox().ioc.factory<Report>((IocContainer c) => Report());
Dox().ioc.instance<MailConfig>(mailConfig);
```

## Testing

Put a fake in place of a real class with `override`, before the app starts. Remove it with `clearOverrides`:

```dart
setUpAll(() async {
  Dox().ioc.override<UserRepository>(FakeUserRepository());
  client = await DoxTestClient.start(appConfig);
});

tearDownAll(() async {
  await client.close();
  Dox().ioc.clearOverrides();
});
```

## Build errors

The build stops with the file and line when:

- a required parameter has a type that is not in the container,
- two or more container classes implement the abstract type of a parameter,
- classes need each other in a circle, like `A -> B -> C -> A`,
- `@Inject()` is on an abstract class or a generic class,
- a class has no unnamed constructor.

A private class (like `_AdminRouter`) is not put in the container, and the build shows a warning. Two classes with the same name can not be handler parameters.

## Next steps

- [Controller](controller.md): get services in a controller.
- [Providers](../digging-deeper/providers.md): run code when the app starts.
