# Views

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/the-basic/views/

# Views

Views are HTML templates that Dox fills with your data and sends as the response.

The `dox_view` package has the template engine. Templates are `.dox.html` files in `resources/views`.

## Setup

Add the package with the CLI. It adds the package, the provider, the `resources/views` folder and a sample view:

```bash
dox add view
```

### Set it up by hand

Add the package:

```bash
dart pub add dox_view
```

Add the provider in `lib/`, so every isolate sets up the engine:

```dart title="lib/providers/view_provider.dart"
import 'package:dox_view/dox_view.dart';

class AppViewProvider extends ViewProvider {
  AppViewProvider() : super(const ViewConfig());
}
```

To make a view file, run `dox make:view emails/welcome`. See [`dox make:view`](../reference/cli.md#dox-makeview).

### Config

Set the options in `ViewConfig`:

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | `resources/views` | the folder of the templates |
| `extension` | `.dox.html` | the file extension |
| `cache` | on, but off when `APP_ENV` is development or local | keep parsed templates in memory. With the cache off, a changed template shows on the next request. |
| `globals` | empty | variables for every template. See [Globals](#globals). |
| `directives` | empty | your own tags, by name. See [Your own tags](#your-own-tags). |
| `strictVariables` | false | a variable that does not exist throws. See [Strict options](#strict-options). |
| `stringZeroIsFalse` | false | the text '0' is false in a condition |
| `bladeOutput` | false | print true as 1, false as nothing and 10.0 as 10 |
| `bladeWarnings` | true | warn about tag names of other template engines. See [Unknown tag warnings](#unknown-tag-warnings). |

To set up the engine with no provider, call `View.configure(config)`.

## Rendering views

Render a template and send it as HTML. Leave out the `.dox.html` extension:

```dart
DoxResponse show(DoxRequest req) {
  return view(req, 'users/show', <String, dynamic>{
    'user': user,
    'posts': posts,
  });
}
```

This renders `resources/views/users/show.dox.html`:

```html
<h1>{{ user.name }}</h1>
```

### Rendering to a string

Get the HTML as a string, for example for an email:

```dart
String html =
    View.render('emails/welcome', <String, dynamic>{'name': 'Ann'});
```

`View.engine.exists('emails/welcome')` tells if a template is there.

## Displaying data

`{{ }}` prints a value. It escapes HTML, so a user can not add a script tag to your page:

```html
<p>Hello {{ user.name }}</p>
```

`{{{ }}}` prints a value with no escape. Use it only for HTML you trust:

```html
<article>{{{ post.html }}}</article>
```

A null value and a variable that does not exist print nothing.

### Comments

A comment is not in the output:

```html
{{-- only you see this --}}
```

To print `{{` or a tag as text, put `@` before it: `@{{ name }}` prints `{{ name }}`, and `@@if` prints `@if`.

### Stay safe

`{{ }}` escapes HTML, but that does not make every place in a page safe:

- Always quote attributes. Write `href="{{ url }}"`, not `href={{ url }}`.
- Check URLs from users. `href="{{ url }}"` does not block a `javascript:` URL, so allow only http and https URLs.
- Do not print user data inside a script or style tag with `{{ }}`. Use [`@json`](#json-for-javascript), or a quoted `data-` attribute.

```html
<div id="app" data-user-name="{{ user.name }}"></div>
<script>
  const name = document.getElementById('app').dataset.userName;
</script>
```

## Expressions

Use these expressions inside `{{ }}` and tags:

| What | Example |
| --- | --- |
| Values | `'text'`, `"text"`, `42`, `1.5`, `true`, `false`, `null` |
| Lists and maps | `[1, 2]`, `{ name: 'Ann', 'full name': 'Ann Lee' }` |
| Fields | `user.name`, `user?.name`, `items[0]`, `map['key']` |
| Math | `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, `%`, `~/` |
| Compare | `==`, `!=`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=` (`===` and `!==` work too) |
| Logic | `&&`, `\|\|`, `!`, `a ?? b`, `a ? b : c` |
| Functions | `route('users.show', { id: 5 })`, `name.toUpperCase()` |

`+` joins text. Fields work on maps, and on objects with a `toJson()` method, like Dox models. These methods work too:

- Lists, maps and text: `length`, `isEmpty`, `isNotEmpty`.
- Lists: `first`, `last`, `contains()`, `join()`, `indexOf()`.
- Text: `toUpperCase()`, `toLowerCase()`, `trim()`, `contains()`, `startsWith()`, `endsWith()`, `split()`, `replaceAll()`, `substring()`, `indexOf()`.
- Numbers: `toStringAsFixed()`, `round()`, `floor()`, `ceil()`, `abs()`.

In a condition, these values are false: null, false, 0, an empty string, an empty list and an empty map.

## Conditions

Show a part only in some cases. Close it with `@end`:

```html
@if(user.isAdmin)
  <a href="/admin">Admin</a>
@elseif(user.isEditor)
  <a href="/posts">Posts</a>
@else
  <p>Welcome</p>
@end
```

`@unless(x)` is `@if(!x)`. A tag alone on its line leaves no empty line in the output.

A tag right after a letter or a digit stays text, so `me@mail.com` is safe. Put a space before the tag, or use `{{ on ? 'active' : '' }}`.

## Loops

Print a list. The `@else` part shows when the list is empty:

```html
<ul>
  @each(user in users)
    <li>{{ user.name }}</li>
  @else
    <li>No users yet</li>
  @end
</ul>
```

Use two names to get the index, or the key of a map:

```html
@each((user, index) in users)
  {{ index + 1 }}. {{ user.name }}
@end

@each((value, key) in settings)
  {{ key }}: {{ value }}
@end
```

### The loop variable

`$loop` tells you where the loop is:

```html
@each(tag in tags)
  {{ tag }}{{ $loop.last ? '' : ', ' }}
@end
```

| Field | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `$loop.index` | the round, from 0 |
| `$loop.iteration` | the round, from 1 |
| `$loop.first` | true in the first round |
| `$loop.last` | true in the last round |
| `$loop.count` | the number of items. `$loop.length` is the same. |
| `$loop.remaining` | the rounds left after this one |
| `$loop.even` | true in the 2nd, 4th, ... round |
| `$loop.odd` | true in the 1st, 3rd, ... round |
| `$loop.depth` | 1 for a loop, 2 for a loop inside a loop |
| `$loop.parent` | the `$loop` of the outer loop, or null |

## Variables

Make a variable with `@let`, and change it with `@assign`:

```html
@let(total = 0)
@each(item in cart)
  @assign(total = total + item.price)
@end
Total: {{ total }}
```

## Partials

Put another template in this one. It sees the same variables:

```html
@include('partials/nav')
```

Pass a map to give it more variables, only for this include:

```html
@include('partials/card', { title: 'Profile', user: post.author })
```

Include a template only when a condition is true. `@includeIf` and `@includeWhen` are the same:

```html
@includeIf(user, 'partials/account')
@includeWhen(user.isAdmin, 'partials/admin', { level: 2 })
```

## More tags

Close a block tag with `@end`. `@else` works in all of them, but not in `@once` and `@verbatim`:

| Tag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `@isset(user.phone) ... @end` | shows when the value is not null |
| `@empty(items) ... @end` | shows when the value is false |
| `@auth ... @end` | shows when the user is logged in (`req.auth`) |
| `@guest ... @end` | shows when the user is not logged in |
| `@env('local') ... @end` | shows when `APP_ENV` is this value. A list works too: `@env(['local', 'staging'])`. |
| `@production ... @end` | shows when `APP_ENV` is production |
| `@once ... @end` | shows only the first time in one render, for example a script in a component |
| `@verbatim ... @end` | prints the text as it is, for JavaScript frameworks that also use `{{ }}`. The text can not have `@end`. |
| `@extends('layouts/app')` | the layout of the page. See [Layouts with sections](#layouts-with-sections). |
| `@section('name') ... @end` | fills a section. Short form: `@section('title', 'Home')`. |
| `@yield('name')` | prints a section. `@yield('title', 'My app')` has a default. |
| `@stack('scripts')` | prints every push of the stack. See [Stacks](#stacks). |
| `@push('scripts') ... @end` | adds to the end of a stack |
| `@prepend('scripts') ... @end` | adds to the start of a stack |
| `@csrf` | the hidden `_token` field. See [Forms](#forms). |
| `@method('PUT')` | the hidden `_method` field |
| `@error('email') ... @end` | shows when the field has a validation error |
| `@json(value)` | the value as JSON. See [JSON for JavaScript](#json-for-javascript). |

Put `@auth`, `@guest`, `@production`, `@once` and `@verbatim` alone on their line. In `View.render` there is no request, so `@guest` shows.

### Attributes from conditions

Print an HTML attribute when a condition is true:

```html
<a @class(['link', { active: isActive, muted: !isActive }])>Home</a>
<input type="checkbox" name="news" @checked(user.news)>
<option value="en" @selected(lang == 'en')>English</option>
<button @disabled(saving)>Save</button>
```

`@class` takes text, a map of class name to a condition, or a list of these.

## Layouts and components

A **component** is a template with its own props and slots. Use one for the page layout:

```html title="resources/views/layouts/main.dox.html"
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
  <head>
    <title>{{ title ?? 'My app' }}</title>
  </head>
  <body>
    <header>{{ $slots.header }}</header>
    <main>{{ $slots.main }}</main>
  </body>
</html>
```

A page puts its content in the component:

```html title="resources/views/home.dox.html"
@component('layouts/main', { title: 'Home' })
  @slot('header')
    <h1>Welcome</h1>
  @end

  <p>Hello {{ user.name }}</p>
@end
```

- The second argument is the props. In the component they are variables, and also `$props.title`.
- `@slot('name') ... @end` fills a named slot. All other content goes into `$slots.main`, which is also `$slot`.
- A component does not see the variables of the page. It sees its props, the slots, `$attributes`, the globals and the [form helpers](#forms).

`@!component(...)` is a component with no body and no `@end`.

### Components as tags

A template in `resources/views/components/` is also a tag with its name. A `.` in the tag is a folder:

```html title="resources/views/components/button.dox.html"
<button class="btn btn-{{ type ?? 'primary' }}">{{ $slots.main }}</button>
```

```html
@button({ type: 'danger' })
  Delete
@end

@!form.input({ name: 'email' })   {{-- components/form/input.dox.html --}}
```

### Attributes

`{{ $attributes }}` prints the props as escaped HTML attributes, like `id="save" title="Save"`. `merge` adds defaults. A prop wins, but `class` is joined:

```html
<button {{ $attributes.merge({ class: 'btn', type: 'button' }) }}>
  {{ $slot }}
</button>
```

```html
@button({ class: 'btn-big', type: 'submit' })
  Save
@end
```

This prints `<button class="btn btn-big" type="submit">`.

Leave out props that are only for the logic of the component with `except`. It can go before `merge`:

```html
<button {{ $attributes.except(['variant']).merge({ class: 'btn' }) }}>
```

Only text, numbers and true are attributes, and true prints the name alone. `$attributes` keeps any attribute name, like `onclick`, so do not pass a map from the user as props.

## Layouts with sections

A page can name its layout with `@extends`. The page fills sections, and the layout prints them with `@yield`:

```html title="resources/views/layouts/app.dox.html"
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
  <head>
    <title>@yield('title', 'My app')</title>
  </head>
  <body>
    <main>@yield('content')</main>
  </body>
</html>
```

```html title="resources/views/home.dox.html"
@extends('layouts/app')

@section('title', 'Home')

@section('content')
  <p>Hello {{ user.name }}</p>
@end
```

- `@extends` must be the first thing in the template.
- Only the sections reach the layout. Text outside a section is not printed.
- A layout can extend another layout. When both fill the same section, the page wins.

Use `@extends` for the page layout. Use a component when you need props or more than one copy on a page.

## Stacks

A **stack** collects HTML from many templates and prints it in one place, like scripts in the head. The layout prints it:

```html
<head>
  @stack('styles')
</head>
<body>
  @yield('content')
  @stack('scripts')
</body>
```

A page, an include or a component adds to it:

```html
@push('scripts')
  <script src="/js/chart.js"></script>
@end
```

`@prepend` adds to the start. Put `@once` inside `@push` in a component, so the script is added one time only.

## Forms

With `SessionMiddleware`, `view()` adds these to every template, also to components and layouts:

| Name | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `csrfField()` | the hidden `_token` field for `CsrfMiddleware`. `@csrf` prints the same. |
| `csrfToken()` | the CSRF token |
| `errors` | the flashed validation errors, like `errors.email` |
| `old('email')` | the input of the request before |
| `session('key')` | a value from the session |
| `request.path`, `request.method`, `request.query` | the current request (also with no session) |

```html
<form method="POST" action="/register">
  @csrf
  <input name="email" value="{{ old('email') }}">
  @error('email')
    <p class="error">{{ message }}</p>
  @end
  <button>Register</button>
</form>
```

With no session, `@csrf` throws a `ViewException`.

### Validation errors

`@error('field')` shows its body when the field has an error. Inside it, `message` is the error. A dotted name, like `@error('user.email')`, works for nested fields, and the name can be a variable.

### Method fields

For a PUT, PATCH or DELETE route, send a POST with `@method`. The [`MethodOverride`](routing.md#forms-with-put-patch-and-delete) middleware reads it:

```html
<form method="POST" action="/posts/{{ post.id }}">
  @csrf
  @method('PUT')
  <input name="title" value="{{ post.title }}">
  <button>Save</button>
</form>
```

## Globals

A **global** is a variable or a function that every template can use. `route()` is there by default:

```dart
const ViewConfig(globals: <String, Object?>{'appName': 'My app'});

View.global('year', DateTime.now().year);
View.global('money', (num cents) => (cents / 100).toStringAsFixed(2));
```

```html
<footer>{{ appName }} {{ year }}</footer>
<p>{{ money(order.total) }}</p>
```

Each isolate has its own engine, so add globals in your provider, after `super.setup()`:

```dart title="lib/providers/view_provider.dart"
class AppViewProvider extends ViewProvider {
  AppViewProvider() : super(const ViewConfig());

  @override
  void setup() {
    super.setup();
    View.global('year', DateTime.now().year);
  }
}
```

A global that holds HTML must be a `SafeString`, so it is printed with no escape:

```dart
View.global('logo', const SafeString('<img src="/logo.svg" alt="Logo">'));
```

To escape text yourself in Dart, use `escapeHtml(text)`.

## JSON for JavaScript

Print a value as JSON. The output is safe in a script block and in an attribute in single quotes:

```html
<script>
  const user = @json(user);
</script>

<div data-tags='@json(tags)'></div>
```

Do not use it in an attribute in double quotes, because the JSON has `"` in it. A value that can not be JSON, like a `DateTime`, throws a `ViewException`.

`json(value)` does the same in an expression, and `SafeString.json(value)` does it in Dart:

```html
@!chart({ points: json(points) })
```

## Your own tags

A **directive** is a tag that your app adds. Its `render` method gets the values between the brackets, and gives the text to print:

```dart
class DateTimeDirective implements ViewDirective {
  @override
  Object? render(List<Object?> args, Scope scope) {
    Object? value = args[0];
    DateTime time = value is DateTime ? value : DateTime.parse('$value');
    return '${time.day}/${time.month}/${time.year}';
  }
}

View.directive('datetime', DateTimeDirective());
```

```html
<time>@datetime(post.createdAt)</time>
```

The text is escaped. Give a `SafeString` to print HTML. `scope.lookup('name')` reads a variable, and `scope.has('name')` tells if it is there. Add directives in your provider like globals, or in `ViewConfig(directives: ...)`.

## Strict options

These three options are off by default. Turn them on in `ViewConfig`:

```dart
const ViewConfig(
  strictVariables: true,
  stringZeroIsFalse: true,
  bladeOutput: true,
);
```

- `strictVariables`: a variable that does not exist throws a `ViewException` with the name, the template and the line. So a typo like `{{ titel }}` shows as an error.
- `stringZeroIsFalse`: the text '0' is false in a condition. Other text, like '00', is still true.
- `bladeOutput`: `{{ }}` prints true as 1, false as nothing, and 10.0 as 10.

With `strictVariables`, these ways to read a variable that may not exist never throw:

| Code | What it gives when `user` does not exist |
| --- | --- |
| `@isset(user) ... @end` | the body is not printed |
| `@empty(user) ... @end` | the body is printed |
| `{{ user ?? 'Guest' }}` | Guest |
| `{{ user?.name }}` | nothing |

`{{ user.name ?? 'Guest' }}` still throws when `user` does not exist. Write `{{ user?.name ?? 'Guest' }}`.

## Unknown tag warnings

Some tag names of other template engines, like `@foreach`, are not Dox tags. Dox prints them as text, and writes one warning to stderr:

```
dox_view: warning: posts/index:12 "@foreach" is not a Dox tag. Use "@each(item in items) ... @end".
```

| Other name | Dox |
| --- | --- |
| `{!! html !!}` | `{{{ html }}}` |
| `@foreach`, `@forelse`, `@for` | `@each(item in items) ... @else ... @end` |
| `@endif`, `@endforeach`, `@endsection` and the other `@end...` names, `@stop` | `@end` |
| `@switch` | `@if ... @elseif ... @else ... @end` |
| `@php`, `@endphp` | `@let(name = value)` |
| `@show` | `@end`, then `@yield('name')` |
| `@parent` | not there. Use `@stack` and `@push` to add content. |

`ViewConfig(bladeWarnings: false)` turns the warnings off.

## Errors

A syntax error, or an error in an expression, throws a `ViewException` with the template name and the line:

```
ViewException: expected ")" but found the end (in "users/show", line 12)
```

## Prettier

Prettier does not know the `@` tags. Add this line to `.prettierignore`:

```
*.dox.html
```

## Testing

Render templates from a map, with no files:

```dart
ViewEngine engine = ViewEngine(MemoryTemplateLoader(<String, String>{
  'hello': 'Hello {{ name }}',
}));

engine.render('hello', <String, Object?>{'name': 'Ann'}); // Hello Ann
```

- [Mail](../digging-deeper/mail.md): use a view as a mail template.

# Inertia

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/the-basic/inertia/

# Inertia

Inertia lets you build a single page app with React, Vue or Svelte, and keep routes and controllers in Dox.

A controller gives a page name and its props, and Inertia shows the page in the browser. The first visit gets a full HTML page. After that, links and forms get only JSON. The `dox_inertia` package is the server side. Use it with Vite and the Inertia 3 client (`@inertiajs/react`, `@inertiajs/vue3` or `@inertiajs/svelte`).

## Setup

Add the package with the CLI. It does steps 1 to 3 below, and prints the steps you do yourself:

```bash
dox add inertia
```

### Set it up by hand

Add the package:

```bash
dart pub add dox_inertia
```

### 1. Root view

The **root view** is the HTML page of the first visit. Dox puts the script and style tags in place of `@vite`, and the page in place of `@inertia`:

```html title="resources/views/app.html"
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8">
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
    <title>My app</title>
    @vite
  </head>
  <body>
    @inertia
  </body>
</html>
```

### 2. Config

Tell Dox where your Vite files are:

```dart title="lib/config/inertia.dart"
import 'package:dox_inertia/dox_inertia.dart';

InertiaConfig inertiaConfig = InertiaConfig(
  entryPoints: <String>['resources/js/app.jsx'],
  devServerUrl: 'http://localhost:5173',
  reactRefresh: true,
);
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rootView` | `resources/views/app.html` | the HTML page of the first visit |
| `entryPoints` | `['resources/js/app.js']` | the Vite entry files |
| `publicPath` | `public` | the folder of public files |
| `buildDirectory` | `build` | the folder in `publicPath` where `vite build` writes its files |
| `devServerUrl` | null | the URL of the Vite dev server. See [Vite](#vite). |
| `reactRefresh` | false | add the React Fast Refresh code in dev mode |
| `version` | hash of the manifest | the asset version. See [Asset version](#asset-version). |
| `encryptHistory` | false | encrypt the browser history of every page. See [History encryption](#history-encryption). |
| `ssr` | null | server side rendering. See [SSR](#server-side-rendering-ssr). |

Paths are from the project root.

### 3. Provider

The provider sets up Inertia in every isolate. Put it in `lib/`:

```dart title="lib/providers/inertia_provider.dart"
import 'package:dox_inertia/dox_inertia.dart';

import '../config/inertia.dart';

class AppInertiaProvider extends InertiaProvider {
  AppInertiaProvider() : super(inertiaConfig);
}
```

With no provider, Dox uses the defaults. `Inertia.configure(config)` sets the config with no provider, and `Inertia.config` reads it.

### 4. Vite

Set up Vite so it writes a manifest into `public/build`:

```js title="vite.config.js"
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'
import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react'

export default defineConfig(({ command }) => ({
  plugins: [react()],
  // public/ holds the Dox public files, so Vite must not copy it
  publicDir: false,
  base: command === 'build' ? '/build/' : '/',
  server: { origin: 'http://localhost:5173' },
  build: {
    manifest: true,
    outDir: 'public/build',
    rollupOptions: { input: 'resources/js/app.jsx' },
  },
}))
```

Then start the Inertia app in your entry file:

```jsx title="resources/js/app.jsx"
import { createInertiaApp } from '@inertiajs/react'
import { createRoot } from 'react-dom/client'

createInertiaApp({
  resolve: (name) => {
    const pages = import.meta.glob('./Pages/**/*.jsx', { eager: true })
    return pages[`./Pages/${name}.jsx`]
  },
  setup({ el, App, props }) {
    createRoot(el).render(<App {...props} />)
  },
})
```

### 5. Serve the built files

In production the browser loads `/build/assets/...`. Add a route for them, or let your proxy serve `public/build`:

```dart title="lib/routes/web.dart"
Route.get('/build/{path*}', (String path) {
  if (path.contains('..')) throw NotFoundHttpException();
  // the file names have a hash, so the browser can keep them for a year
  return response(File('public/build/$path'))
      .cache(const Duration(days: 365));
});
```

### 6. Middleware

Add three middleware to `globalMiddleware`, in this order:

```dart title="lib/config/app.dart"
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  globalMiddleware: <dynamic>[
    const SessionMiddleware(),
    const CsrfMiddleware(),
    HandleInertiaRequests(),
  ],
);
```

- `SessionMiddleware` keeps the validation errors and the flash data. See [Session](session.md).
- `CsrfMiddleware` sets the `XSRF-TOKEN` cookie, and the Inertia client sends it back. See [CSRF](../security/csrf.md#axios-and-inertia).
- `HandleInertiaRequests` is your `InertiaMiddleware`. See [Shared props](#shared-props). With no props to share, use `const InertiaMiddleware()`.

You can also add them to a router, in the same order.

## Rendering pages

Give the request, the page name and the props. The page name is the file in `resources/js/Pages`, with no extension:

```dart title="lib/app/http/controllers/user.controller.dart"
@Inject()
class UserController {
  Future<DoxResponse> index(DoxRequest req) {
    return inertia(req, 'Users/Index', <String, dynamic>{
      'title': 'Users',
      'users': () => User().query().all(),
    });
  }
}
```

A function prop, like `users`, runs only when the prop is sent. It can give a Future. Props become JSON, so a model works. `Inertia.render(req, ...)` is the same as `inertia(req, ...)`.

A Dart integer above 2^53 loses precision in JavaScript, so send such a number as a string.

### Is it an Inertia request

Check if the request came from the Inertia client:

```dart
if (Inertia.isInertia(req)) {
  // ...
}
```

## Shared props

Share props with every page, like the signed in user. Extend `InertiaMiddleware` and return them from `share`. It can be async:

```dart title="lib/app/http/middleware/handle_inertia_requests.dart"
class HandleInertiaRequests extends InertiaMiddleware {
  @override
  Map<String, dynamic> share(DoxRequest req) {
    return <String, dynamic>{
      'appName': 'My app',
      'auth': () => req.auth?.toJson(),
    };
  }
}
```

A page prop with the same name wins. Share from any middleware or controller with `Inertia.share(req, {...})`, and read all shared props with `Inertia.shared(req)`.

### Global values

Share one value with the full app. Call it in the `setup()` of your provider:

```dart
@override
void setup() {
  super.setup();
  Inertia.shareGlobal('appName', 'Dox');
}
```

!!! warning
    All users get a global value. Put data of one user, like the signed in user, in `share`.

## Partial reloads

The client can ask for some props only, with `router.reload({ only: ['users'] })`. Dox then sends only those props. Ask for a top level prop, like `auth`, not `auth.user`.

These helpers change when a prop is sent:

| Helper | First visit | Partial reload |
| --- | --- | --- |
| plain value or function | sent | sent when asked |
| `Inertia.optional` | not sent | sent when asked |
| `Inertia.always` | sent | always sent |
| `Inertia.defer` | not sent, loaded right after | sent when asked |
| `Inertia.merge` | sent | sent when asked |

### Optional props

Send the prop only when a partial reload asks for it. `Inertia.lazy` is the same:

```dart
'stats': Inertia.optional(() => Stats.load()),
```

### Always props

Send the prop on every request:

```dart
'notices': Inertia.always(notices),
```

### Deferred props

Leave a slow prop out of the first visit. The page loads it right after. Props of the same `group` load in one request:

```dart
'comments': Inertia.defer(() => Comment().query().all()),
'likes': Inertia.defer(() => Like().query().count(), group: 'side'),
```

### Merging props

Add the new items to the old ones, for infinite scroll:

```dart
'posts': Inertia.merge(posts),
'feed': Inertia.defer(() => Post().query().all()).merge(),
```

## Forms and validation errors

A form post needs no extra code for errors. When validation fails, Dox flashes the errors and redirects back. The page gets them in the `errors` prop:

```dart
Future<DoxResponse> store(DoxRequest req) async {
  await req.validateSchema(
    v.object(<String, Schema<Object?>>{
      'name': v.string().min(2),
      'email': v.string().email(),
    }),
  );
  // ... save the user
  return redirect('/users');
}
```

```jsx
const { data, setData, post, errors } = useForm({ name: '', email: '' })
// errors.email holds the message, or is undefined
```

### Error bags

Keep the errors of two forms on one page apart. Pass `errorBag` in the post, and the errors are under the bag name, like `errors.login.email`:

```jsx
router.post(url, data, { errorBag: 'login' })
```

## Redirects

Redirect with `redirect(url)` or `back(req)`. After PUT, PATCH or DELETE, `InertiaMiddleware` changes a 302 into 303, so the browser follows with GET:

```dart
return redirect('/users');
```

A controller that returns nothing to an Inertia request sends the browser back, like `back(req)`.

### External redirects

Go to an outside site, or a page that is not an Inertia page, with a full page load:

```dart
return Inertia.location(req, 'https://checkout.example.com/pay/1');
```

## Flash data

Give the next page a short message, like "User saved". It needs `SessionMiddleware`:

```dart
Inertia.flash(req, 'message', 'User saved');
return redirect('/users');
```

The next page gets it in `page.flash`, one time:

```jsx
const { flash } = usePage()
// flash.message is 'User saved'
```

## Vite

In dev mode, `@vite` loads the entry files from the Vite dev server, with hot reload. In production, Dox reads `public/build/.vite/manifest.json`.

Dox is in dev mode when `devServerUrl` is set, or when `public/hot` exists. So set `devServerUrl` from the env:

```dart title="lib/config/inertia.dart"
InertiaConfig inertiaConfig = InertiaConfig(
  entryPoints: <String>['resources/js/app.jsx'],
  devServerUrl: Env.get<String>('APP_ENV') == 'development'
      ? 'http://localhost:5173'
      : null,
);
```

When `APP_ENV` is production, Dox ignores `public/hot` and prints a warning.

## Asset version

When the asset version changes, the next link click loads the full page again, with the new files. The default is a hash of the Vite manifest, read one time for each isolate. So restart the server after `vite build`.

Set your own version, for example the git commit:

```dart
InertiaConfig(version: Env.get<String>('GIT_SHA'));
```

`Inertia.version` gives the current version.

## Root view data

Give the root view a value, like the title. Write `{{ key }}` in the root view:

```html
<head>
  <meta name="csrf-token" content="{{ csrfToken }}">
  <title>{{ title }}</title>
  @vite
</head>
```

Set the values in a controller or a middleware. More calls merge the data:

```dart
Inertia.withViewData(req, <String, Object?>{'title': 'Users'});
return inertia(req, 'Users/Index');
```

- Dox fills `{{ csrfToken }}` with the CSRF token of the session.
- A key that you did not set stays as it is, so set every key of the root view.
- Each value is HTML escaped. Put it only in text or in a quoted attribute.
- Later visits do not load the root view again. So set the title in the `<Head>` component of the client too.

### Another root view for some pages

Use another HTML file for one request, like an admin area:

```dart
Inertia.setRootView(req, 'resources/views/admin.html');
return inertia(req, 'Admin/Dashboard');
```

For every page of a router, use `RootViewMiddleware`:

```dart
@override
List<dynamic> get middleware => <dynamic>[
  const RootViewMiddleware('resources/views/admin.html'),
];
```

!!! warning
    Use a fixed path. A path from the request could show any file of the server.

## History encryption

The browser keeps the props of each page in its history. After a logout, the back button can show private data. With history encryption, the browser encrypts the page data, and a cleared history can not be read. It works only on HTTPS and on localhost.

Turn it on for all pages:

```dart title="lib/config/inertia.dart"
InertiaConfig inertiaConfig = InertiaConfig(encryptHistory: true);
```

Or for one page. Pass false to turn it off for one page:

```dart
Inertia.encryptHistory(req);
return inertia(req, 'Account/Show', props);
```

Or for all pages of a router:

```dart
@override
List<dynamic> get middleware => <dynamic>[const EncryptHistoryMiddleware()];
```

Clear the history, for example at logout. It needs `SessionMiddleware`:

```dart
Inertia.clearHistory(req);
return redirect('/login');
```

## Server side rendering (SSR)

With SSR, the first visit gets the full HTML of the page, so search engines can read it. The Inertia SSR server renders it. It is a Bun or Node process next to your Dox app. Links and forms never use it.

### 1. The SSR entry file

`dox inertia:install --ssr` writes the entry file and adds a `build:ssr` script to `package.json`:

```json title="package.json"
{
  "scripts": {
    "build:ssr": "vite build && vite build --ssr resources/js/ssr.jsx --outDir bootstrap/ssr"
  }
}
```

The entry file looks like this:

```jsx title="resources/js/ssr.jsx"
import { createInertiaApp } from '@inertiajs/react'
import createServer from '@inertiajs/react/server'
import ReactDOMServer from 'react-dom/server'

createServer(
  (page) =>
    createInertiaApp({
      page,
      render: ReactDOMServer.renderToString,
      resolve: (name) => {
        const pages = import.meta.glob('./Pages/**/*.jsx', { eager: true })
        return pages[`./Pages/${name}.jsx`]
      },
      setup: ({ App, props }) => <App {...props} />,
    }),
  { host: '127.0.0.1' },
)
```

Vue and Svelte have the same `createServer`, in `@inertiajs/vue3/server` and `@inertiajs/svelte/server`. Keep `host` at 127.0.0.1, so only your own machine can reach the server.

### 2. Hydrate in the browser

Reuse the HTML from the server. Change `setup` in your app file:

```jsx title="resources/js/app.jsx"
setup({ el, App, props }) {
  if (el.hasAttribute('data-server-rendered')) {
    hydrateRoot(el, <App {...props} />)
  } else {
    createRoot(el).render(<App {...props} />)
  }
},
```

### 3. Build and run

Build the files, then start the SSR server with Bun. Add `--node` for Node:

```bash
bun run build:ssr
dox inertia:start-ssr
```

It runs `bootstrap/ssr/ssr.js` (or `ssr.mjs`) in the foreground. Run it under Docker, pm2 or systemd, and keep `node_modules` on the server.

### 4. Turn it on

Set `ssr` in the config:

```dart title="lib/config/inertia.dart"
InertiaConfig inertiaConfig = InertiaConfig(
  entryPoints: <String>['resources/js/app.jsx'],
  ssr: Env.get<String>('APP_ENV') == 'production' ? InertiaSsr() : null,
);
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `url` | `http://127.0.0.1:13714/render` | the render URL of the SSR server |
| `timeout` | 2 seconds | how long Dox waits for the answer |

The head tags of the page go before `</head>`. So when your pages set a title with `<Head>`, remove the title from the root view.

When the SSR server is down or slow, the visitor gets the normal page, and Dox prints one warning.

## Next steps

- [Views](views.md): server templates with no front-end framework.
- [Session](session.md): errors and flash data.
- [Static files and SPA](../guides/static-files.md): serve the built front-end files.

# Serializer

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/the-basic/serializer/

# Serializer

A serializer sets the JSON shape of a response: which keys the client gets, their names and their values.

It works with any Dart type: a model, a plain class or a map. A controller can also return a model, a map or a list as it is. See [Response](response.md#return-a-value). To only hide some model fields, use [`hidden`](../database/model/index.md#hide-fields).

## Create a serializer

Make a serializer with the CLI. It writes `lib/app/serializers/blog.serializer.dart`, for the model with the same name:

```bash
dox make:serializer Blog
```

## Writing a serializer

Extend `Serializer<T>` and write `convert`. It gets one value and gives one JSON object:

```dart title="lib/app/serializers/blog.serializer.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

import 'package:my_app/app/models/blog/blog.model.dart';

class BlogSerializer extends Serializer<Blog> {
  BlogSerializer(super.data);

  @override
  Map<String, dynamic> convert(Blog m) {
    return <String, dynamic>{
      'uid': m.id,
      'title_en': m.title,
    };
  }
}
```

Return the serializer from a controller, with one model or a list:

```dart title="lib/app/http/controllers/blog.controller.dart"
class BlogController {
  Future<BlogSerializer> index(DoxRequest req) async {
    List<Blog> blogs = await Blog().all();
    return BlogSerializer(blogs); // a list
  }

  Future<BlogSerializer> show(DoxRequest req, String id) async {
    Blog? blog = await Blog().find(id);
    return BlogSerializer(blog); // one model
  }
}
```

The response of `show`:

```json
{
  "uid": 1,
  "title_en": "This is title"
}
```

This is what the client gets for each input:

| You give | The client gets |
| --- | --- |
| one value of type `T` | one JSON object |
| a `List<T>` | a JSON list (`[]` when the list is empty) |
| null, or any other type | null |

A `List<dynamic>`, like a list from `jsonDecode`, gives null. Call `.cast<T>()` first. See [JSON from another API](#json-from-another-api).

### Getting the JSON

`toJson()` gives the map, the list or null, for use in other code:

```dart
dynamic json = BlogSerializer(blogs).toJson();
```

## Examples with models

### Change values

Format dates, join fields and add new keys:

```dart title="lib/app/serializers/user.serializer.dart"
class UserSerializer extends Serializer<User> {
  UserSerializer(super.data);

  @override
  Map<String, dynamic> convert(User m) {
    return <String, dynamic>{
      'id': m.id,
      'name': '${m.firstName} ${m.lastName}',
      'is_active': m.status == 'active',
      'joined_at': m.createdAt?.toIso8601String(),
    };
  }
}
```

### A serializer inside a serializer

Use the serializer of a relation inside the other one:

```dart title="lib/app/serializers/comment.serializer.dart"
class CommentSerializer extends Serializer<Comment> {
  CommentSerializer(super.data);

  @override
  Map<String, dynamic> convert(Comment m) {
    return <String, dynamic>{
      'id': m.id,
      'content': m.content,
      'user': UserSerializer(m.user).toJson(), // null when there is no user
    };
  }
}
```

Load the relation first, with [`preload`](../database/model/relationship/belongs-to.md#loading-the-relation):

```dart
Future<CommentSerializer> index(DoxRequest req) async {
  List<Comment> comments = await Comment().preload('user').all();
  return CommentSerializer(comments);
}
```

### With pagination

Put the serializer output in place of `data` of the page:

```dart
Future<Map<String, dynamic>> index(ListUsers query) async {
  Pagination<User> page = await User()
      .orderBy('id', 'desc')
      .paginate(currentPage: query.page, perPage: query.perPage);
  return <String, dynamic>{
    ...page.toJson(),
    'data': UserSerializer(page.data).toJson(),
  };
}
```

See [Pagination](../guides/pagination.md).

## Examples without models

### A plain Dart class

A serializer for a plain class works the same way:

```dart title="lib/app/serializers/weather.serializer.dart"
class Weather {
  final String city;
  final double celsius;

  Weather(this.city, this.celsius);
}

class WeatherSerializer extends Serializer<Weather> {
  WeatherSerializer(super.data);

  @override
  Map<String, dynamic> convert(Weather m) {
    return <String, dynamic>{
      'city': m.city,
      'celsius': m.celsius,
      'fahrenheit': m.celsius * 9 / 5 + 32,
    };
  }
}
```

### Rows from the query builder

`QueryBuilder.table(...)` gives rows as maps. Use `Serializer<Map<String, dynamic>>` to pick and rename the keys:

```dart title="lib/app/serializers/sales_report.serializer.dart"
class SalesReportSerializer extends Serializer<Map<String, dynamic>> {
  SalesReportSerializer(super.data);

  @override
  Map<String, dynamic> convert(Map<String, dynamic> m) {
    return <String, dynamic>{
      'product': m['name'],
      'sold': m['total'],
    };
  }
}
```

```dart
Future<SalesReportSerializer> report(DoxRequest req) async {
  List<Map<String, dynamic>> rows = await QueryBuilder.table('orders')
      .selectRaw('name, count(*) as total')
      .groupBy('name')
      .get();
  return SalesReportSerializer(rows);
}
```

### JSON from another API

Cast the list to the type of the serializer first:

```dart
Future<SalesReportSerializer> remote(DoxRequest req) async {
  String body = await fetchReport(); // your HTTP call
  List<dynamic> rows = jsonDecode(body);
  return SalesReportSerializer(rows.cast<Map<String, dynamic>>());
}
```

## Next steps

- [Response](response.md): other values a controller can return.
- [CLI: `dox make:serializer`](../reference/cli.md#dox-makeserializer): the make command.

# Response

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/the-basic/response/

# Response

A controller returns a value, and Dox turns it into the response for the client.

## Return a value

Return the value from your controller. Dox sends a string as text, and a map or a model as JSON:

```dart
Map<String, String> hello(DoxRequest req) {
  return <String, String>{'message': 'hello world!'};
}

Future<Blog?> show(int id) async {
  return Blog().find(id);
}
```

This is what the client gets for each type:

| You return | The client gets |
| --- | --- |
| a `String` | the text |
| a `Map` or a `List` | JSON |
| a model, a list of models, a [serializer](serializer.md) | JSON (from `toJson()`) |
| a `DateTime` | the ISO 8601 text |
| an `IHttpException`, like `NotFoundHttpException()` | its status code and JSON: `{"code": ..., "message": ...}` |
| a `File` (from `dart:io`) | the file, streamed |
| a `Stream<List<int>>` | the bytes, streamed |
| a `StreamFile` or a `DownloadableFile` | the file, streamed |
| `response(...)` | full control: status, headers, cookies |

The `htmlStrings` flag sends a string as HTML. See [Core flags](../reference/app-config.md#core-flags).

## Errors

Throw or return an exception to answer with an error:

```dart
throw NotFoundHttpException(message: 'Blog not found');
```

The client gets 404 with `{"code":"not_found","message":"Blog not found"}`. Each exception takes `message:` and `errorCode:`. A map message is sent as it is.

| Exception | Status |
| --- | --- |
| `BadRequestException()` | 400 |
| `ForbiddenHttpException()` | 403 |
| `NotFoundHttpException()` | 404 |
| `MethodNotAllowedHttpException(allow)` | 405 |
| `PayloadTooLargeException()` | 413 |
| `UnsupportedMediaTypeException()` | 415 |
| `TokenMismatchException()` | 419 |
| `ValidationException()` | 422 |
| `TooManyRequestsException()` | 429 |
| `InternalErrorException()` | 500 |
| `QueryException()` | 500 |

See [HTTP exceptions](../reference/http-exceptions.md) for all of them.

### Any status

Stop the request with any status, an optional message and headers:

```dart
if (post.userId != req.auth?.id()) abort(403);
throw HttpStatusException(503,
    headers: <String, String>{'retry-after': '60'});
```

### Your own exception

Extend `IHttpException`:

```dart
class PaymentRequiredException extends IHttpException {
  PaymentRequiredException({String message = 'Payment required'}) {
    super.code = HttpStatus.paymentRequired;
    super.errorCode = 'payment_required';
    super.message = message;
  }
}
```

Any other error gets 500, and goes to the [exception handler](errors.md).

## Files and big responses

Return a `File` or a `Stream<List<int>>` to send a file. Dox sends it in chunks:

```dart
Route.get('/video', (DoxRequest req) => File('storage/video.mp4'));
```

A file gets the right `Content-Type` and `Content-Length`. It also answers Range requests with 206, so video players can seek and downloads can resume.

### A stream with a type

Send a stream with its content type, or as a download with a file name:

```dart
return StreamFile(ContentType.parse('image/png'), bytes, length: size);
return DownloadableFile(ContentType.binary, bytes, 'report.pdf');
```

### Files from storage

Make the browser save a file from [File Storage](../digging-deeper/file-storage.md):

```dart
Future<DownloadableFile> download(DoxRequest req) async {
  return Storage().download('report.pdf');
}
```

Show the file in the browser:

```dart
Future<StreamFile> show(DoxRequest req) async {
  return Storage().stream('photo.jpg');
}
```

## The `response()` helper

Set the status, headers or cookies. All methods return the response, so you can chain them:

```dart
DoxResponse store(DoxRequest req) {
  return response(<String, String>{'status': 'created'})
      .statusCode(201)
      .header('X-Request-Id', 'abc')
      .contentType(ContentType.json);
}
```

### Setting the status

Set the status code. The default is 200:

```dart
response(data).statusCode(201);
```

### Setting headers

Set one header. If a middleware already set it, the new value is added. Pass `replace: true` to replace it:

```dart
response(data).header('X-Key', 'value');
response(data).header('X-Key', 'value', replace: true);
```

The `replaceHeaders` flag makes `header` replace by default. See [Core flags](../reference/app-config.md#core-flags).

Set many headers. Each key replaces the header with the same name:

```dart
response(data).withHeaders(<String, String>{'X-One': '1', 'X-Two': '2'});
```

Set the content type. `ContentType` is from `dart:io`:

```dart
response(html).contentType(ContentType.html);
```

### Caching

Set `Cache-Control`. `Duration(minutes: 5)` sends `max-age=300`:

```dart
response(data).cache(Duration(minutes: 5));
```

### Changing the body

Change the body, or send a byte stream as the body:

```dart
response('').content(value);
response('').stream(byteStream);
```

### Reading the response

Read the body, the status and the headers, for example in a [middleware](middleware.md#run-code-after-the-controller). A null status means 200:

```dart
res.getContent();
res.status;
res.headers;
```

## Redirect

Send the browser to another page. The status is 302 by default:

```dart
return redirect('/login');
return redirect('/posts', status: 301);
```

Send the browser back to the page of the Referer header, for example after a form post. With no Referer, or one of another host, it goes to the fallback:

```dart
return back(req);
return back(req, fallback: '/home');
```

See [Session](session.md#flash-data) for flash messages with a redirect.

## Cookie

Make a `DoxCookie` and add it to the response:

```dart
DoxCookie cookie = DoxCookie('theme', 'dark');
return response('ok').cookie(cookie);
```

Set the cookie options:

```dart
DoxCookie token = DoxCookie(
  'token',
  'value',
  maxAge: Duration(days: 7), // default 1 hour
  httpOnly: true, // default true: page scripts can not read it
  secure: true,   // default: only when the request came over https
  path: '/',
  sameSite: SameSite.lax, // from dart:io. default: none sent
);
return response('ok').cookie(token);
```

Delete a cookie:

```dart
return response('ok').cookie(DoxCookie('token', ''), setExpire: true);
```

Dox encrypts the cookie value with `APP_KEY`. If the browser or another app must read it, use `DoxCookie(key, value, encrypt: false)`, and read it with `req.cookie(key, decrypt: false)`. See [Request: cookies](request.md#cookies).

To decrypt a raw cookie value with no request, use `DoxCookie.decrypt(name, value)`.

## Send the response yourself

Write the raw response, for example a stream with trailers. See [Request: send the response yourself](request.md#send-the-response-yourself).

## Change every response

Change every response in one place, for example to add a header. Set a `responseHandler` in `AppConfig`:

```dart title="lib/app/http/handler.dart"
class ResponseHandler extends ResponseHandlerInterface {
  @override
  DoxResponse handle(DoxResponse res) {
    return res.header('X-Powered-By', 'Dox');
  }
}
```

```dart title="lib/config/app.dart"
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  responseHandler: ResponseHandler(),
);
```

## Next steps

- [Serializer](serializer.md): set the JSON shape of a response.
- [Error handling](errors.md): report and render errors.
- [Request](request.md): read the input.

# Error handling

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/the-basic/errors/

# Error handling

Every error that a route throws goes to one exception handler, which logs it and sends an answer to the client.

The handler has two methods. `report(error, stackTrace)` logs the error, and `render(error, req)` decides what the client gets. The default handler works with no setup.

## The default answer

This is what the client gets with the default handler:

| Error | Status | Body |
| --- | --- | --- |
| an `IHttpException`, like `NotFoundHttpException` | its `code` | `{"code": "not_found", "message": "Not Found"}` |
| a `ValidationException` (bad input) | 422 | the field errors, like `{"name": "The name is required"}` |
| a `ValidationException` on a form post with a [session](session.md#validation-errors-and-old-input) | 302 | a redirect back, with the errors and the old input in the session |
| a URL with no route | 404 | `{"code": "not_found", "message": "GET /x not found"}` |
| any other error | 500 | `{"code": "server_error", "message": "Server Error"}` |

For a 500, the client gets the error text only when `APP_ENV` is development or local. See [HTTP exceptions](../reference/http-exceptions.md) for the exception classes.

`report` runs for every error, except an `IHttpException` with a 4xx code. It also runs for errors outside a request, like a future that nobody awaits.

## An HTML error page

Send browsers an HTML page in place of JSON. A JSON client and a validation error get the same answer as before:

```dart title="lib/config/app.dart"
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  htmlErrors: true,
);
```

The page shows the status and its title, like "404 Not Found". In development or local, it also shows the error text and the stack trace.

### Your own error page

Set `errorPage`. `debug` is true when `APP_ENV` is development or local:

```dart title="lib/config/app.dart"
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  htmlErrors: true,
  errorPage: (int status, Object error, StackTrace stack, bool debug) =>
      '<h1>Sorry, error $status</h1>',
);
```

!!! warning
    Escape every value you put in the page.

Call `defaultErrorPage` with the same arguments for the statuses you do not handle.

## Your own handler

Extend `ExceptionHandler`, for example to send errors to an error tracker. Override one method or both:

```dart title="lib/app/exception_handler.dart"
class PaymentRequiredException implements Exception {}

class AppExceptionHandler extends ExceptionHandler {
  const AppExceptionHandler();

  @override
  void report(Object error, StackTrace stackTrace) {
    print('ERROR $error\n$stackTrace'); // send it to your error tracker
  }

  @override
  dynamic render(Object error, HttpRequest req) {
    if (error is PaymentRequiredException) {
      return response(<String, String>{'message': 'Please pay'})
          .statusCode(402);
    }
    return super.render(error, req); // the default answer
  }
}
```

Then set it in `AppConfig`:

```dart title="lib/config/app.dart"
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  exceptionHandler: const AppExceptionHandler(),
);
```

`render` can return anything a controller can return. Return the error itself for the default answer. `req` is the raw `HttpRequest`, so read headers with `req.headers.value('accept')`. See [Custom errors](../guides/custom-errors.md).

### The request id in a report

Read the id from [`RequestId`](middleware.md#request-id) at the start of `report`, before any await:

```dart
sentry.captureException(error, hint: ExceptionHandler.requestId);
```

## Errors of one route

Send the errors of one route to your own function, for example for gRPC. It also gets the errors of the middleware and of the body:

```dart
DoxResponse? rpcError(Object error, DoxRequest req) {
  return response(<String, String>{'error': 'failed'}).statusCode(500);
}

Route.post('/rpc', (RpcController c) => c.call)
    .renderErrorsWith(rpcError);
```

Return null to get the answer of your `ExceptionHandler`. The error is still reported. The function must be a top-level or static function, because Dox sends routes to every isolate.

## Show error text only in development

Decide if the client can see the error text in an answer you send yourself. It is true when `APP_ENV` is development or local:

```dart
String message = showErrors() ? '$error' : 'Server Error';
```

## Next steps

- [HTTP exceptions](../reference/http-exceptions.md): the exception classes and their status codes.
- [Custom errors](../guides/custom-errors.md): your own exceptions and one JSON shape.
- [Error index](../reference/errors.md): every message Dox prints or throws.

# Cache

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/digging-deeper/cache/

# Cache

`Cache()` keeps data that is slow to make, so the next request can read it fast.

A **driver** is the place where the data is kept, like files, memory or Redis. A **store** is a driver with a name and its settings.

The cache is in the `dox_cache` package, which is built into `dox_core`. You can also use it [without Dox](#without-dox).

## Setup

A new project already has `lib/config/cache.dart`, with a file store and a memory store. The `CACHE_STORE` key in `.env` picks the default store.

### Install

In an app that has no cache config, run this command:

```bash
dox add cache
```

To pick another default store, add `--store=redis` (or `memory`, `database`). The database option needs `dox add orm` first.

### Drivers

A store uses one driver:

| Driver | Where the data is | Shared between isolates |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `file` | files in a folder (default `storage/cache`) | yes, on the same machine |
| `memory` | a map inside the isolate | no |
| `redis` | a Redis server | yes, also between machines |
| `database` | a table in your database. See [Database store](#database-store) | yes, also between machines |
| `null` | nowhere. It stores nothing | - |

Each isolate has its own memory store. If all isolates and servers must see the same data, use Redis or the database.

Use the memory store for local development and tests only. In production, use the file store on one server, or use Redis or the database.

### Adding a Redis store

Add a store in the config file. This example adds a Redis store:

```dart title="lib/config/cache.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

CacheConfig cache = CacheConfig(
  defaultStore: env.cacheStore,
  stores: <String, Map<String, dynamic>>{
    'file': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'file', 'path': 'storage/cache'},
    'memory': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'memory', 'max_size': 10000},
    'redis': <String, dynamic>{
      'driver': 'redis',
      'host': env.redisHost,
      'port': env.redisPort,
      'prefix': 'app_cache:',
    },
  },
);
```

Add the two env keys to `lib/config/env.dart`, then run `dart run build_runner build`:

```dart title="lib/config/env.dart"
  String get redisHost => '127.0.0.1';

  int get redisPort => 6379;
```

### Store options

| Driver | Options |
| --- | --- |
| `file` | `path` (default `storage/cache`), `prefix`, `encrypt`, `prune_every` and `fsync`. See [Pruning the file store](#pruning-the-file-store) |
| `memory` | `max_size`: the most items. When it is full, the item used least recently is removed. No limit by default. Also `prefix`. |
| `redis` | `host` (default `127.0.0.1`), `port` (default `6379`), `username`, `password`, `db` (default `0`), `tls`, `pool_size` (default 10), `max_value_bytes` (no limit by default), `prefix`, `encrypt` |
| `database` | `table`, `connection`, `prefix`, `encrypt`, `prune_interval`. See [Database store](#database-store) |

A Redis store with no prefix gets `<app name>_cache:` from `APP_NAME`. The other drivers use `dox_cache:`.

### Redis options

To set another Redis option, like a command timeout, give the store a `RedisOptions`:

```dart title="lib/config/cache.dart"
'redis': <String, dynamic>{
  'driver': 'redis',
  'options': RedisOptions(
    host: env.redisHost,
    port: env.redisPort,
    commandTimeout: const Duration(seconds: 2),
  ),
},
```

Do not set `host`, `port`, `username`, `password`, `db`, `tls` or `pool_size` next to it. That throws an `ArgumentError`.

Sessions and the [rate limit](../security/rate-limiting.md) use the same store, so they get these options too.

## Retrieving items

Read a value with `get`. The second argument is the default for a missing key:

```dart
await Cache().get('foo');            // 'bar', or null when missing
await Cache().get('foo', 'default'); // 'default' when missing
```

### Checking if an item exists

Check if a key is in the cache:

```dart
if (await Cache().has('foo')) {
  // ...
}
```

### Retrieving many items

Read many keys at once:

```dart
await Cache().many(<String>['a', 'b', 'c']); // {a: 1, b: 2, c: null}
```

### Retrieve and store

Read a value, or make it and store it when it is missing:

```dart
List<dynamic> posts = await Cache().remember(
  'posts',
  Duration(minutes: 5),
  () async => (await Post().all()).map((Post p) => p.toJson()).toList(),
);
```

The value is stored as JSON, so return maps, lists, strings and numbers, not models. For no expiry, use `rememberForever`.

`remember` has two options:

- `decode` turns the stored JSON back into your type, like `decode: (j) => (j as List).cast<String>()`.
- `lock: true` lets only one caller, on all isolates and servers, run the function. The others wait for its value.

### Serving stale values

Serve an old value while a new one is made in the background. The `flexible` method takes two durations:

- For the first duration, the value is **fresh**. Callers get it as it is.
- For the second duration, the value is **stale**. Callers still get it at once, and the function runs one time in the background.

```dart
Map<String, dynamic> stats = await Cache().flexible(
  'stats', Duration(minutes: 1), Duration(minutes: 5), loadStats,
);
```

Pass null as the second duration to keep the old value until a refresh replaces it:

```dart
Map<String, dynamic> rates = await Cache().flexible(
  'rates', Duration(minutes: 10), null, fetchRates,
);
```

### Retrieve and delete

Read a value and remove it in one step:

```dart
dynamic code = await Cache().pull('login_code');
```

### Retrieving raw JSON

Get the stored JSON text as it is, to send it back with no decode:

```dart
String? json = await Cache().getRaw('posts');
if (json != null) {
  return response(json).contentType(ContentType.json);
}
```

## Storing items

Store a value with `put`. With no duration, the value stays forever:

```dart
await Cache().put('foo', 'bar', duration: Duration(minutes: 10));

await Cache().put('foo', 'bar');
```

A value must be a JSON type. For a model, store `model.toJson()`.

### Storing an item forever

Store a value with no expiry:

```dart
await Cache().forever('settings', <String, dynamic>{'theme': 'dark'});
```

### Storing if not present

Store a value only when the key is missing. It returns true when the value was stored:

```dart
bool stored = await Cache()
    .add('foo', 'bar', duration: Duration(minutes: 10));
```

### Storing many items

Store many values at once:

```dart
await Cache().putMany(<String, Object?>{'a': 1, 'b': 2});
```

### Incrementing and decrementing

Change an integer. A missing key starts at 0:

```dart
await Cache().increment('visits');
await Cache().decrement('stock', 5);
```

### Changing the expiry

Give a key a new expiry:

```dart
await Cache().touch('foo', duration: Duration(hours: 1));
```

## Removing items

Remove one key with `forget`, or all items of the store with `flush`:

```dart
await Cache().forget('foo');

await Cache().flush();
```

On Redis, `flush` deletes only the keys with the store prefix.

## Using another store

`Cache()` uses the default store. Call `store` to use another one:

```dart
await Cache().store('redis').put('foo', 'bar');
```

## Cache tags

A **tag** puts items in a group, so you can remove only that group:

```dart
await Cache().tag('users').put('u1', 'Ann');
await Cache().tag('users').flush(); // removes only the items of this tag
```

For many tags, call `tags(['a', 'b'])`.

## Atomic locks

A **lock** lets only one request, or one server, run some code at a time:

```dart
CacheLock lock = Cache().store('redis')
    .lock('report', Duration(seconds: 30));
if (await lock.get()) {
  try {
    await buildReport();
  } finally {
    await lock.release();
  }
}
```

The lock is freed after its time, 30 seconds here, also when you never call `release()`.

A memory lock works in one isolate only, and a file lock on one machine only. For many servers, use Redis or the database.

### Waiting for a lock

Wait for a lock with `block`. It gives false when the time is over:

```dart
if (await lock.block(Duration(seconds: 5))) {
  // ...
}
```

Pass a callback, and `block` runs it with the lock and then frees the lock. It throws a `LockTimeoutException` when the time is over:

```dart
await lock.block(Duration(seconds: 5), buildReport);
```

To free a lock that another owner holds, use `forceRelease()`.

## Encrypting the cache

By default the cache keeps plain JSON. To hide the values, add `'encrypt': true` to a file or Redis store:

```dart
'file': {'driver': 'file', 'path': 'storage/cache', 'encrypt': true},
```

The values are encrypted with your app key. When the key changes, old entries read as a miss.

Cache keys and tag names are not encrypted. Someone who can write to the store can copy an encrypted value to another key.

## Database store

The `dox_cache_database` package keeps the cache in a table of your database, so all servers share it with no Redis.

Install it and make the table:

```bash
dart pub add dox_cache_database
dox cache:table
dox migrate
```

Give `--table=<name>` to `cache:table` for another table name.

Register the driver when the app starts:

```dart
import 'package:dox_cache_database/dox_cache_database.dart';

Dox().cache.extend(
  'database',
  DatabaseCacheDriverFactory(Dox().cache.config.encrypter),
);
```

Then add a store to the config file:

```dart
'database': <String, dynamic>{
  'driver': 'database',
  'table': 'cache', // optional, default `cache`
  'connection': 'cache', // optional, default the default connection
  'prefix': 'app:', // optional
  'encrypt': true, // optional
},
```

Cache calls inside a transaction on the same connection roll back with it. To avoid this, give the store its own connection.

### Deleting expired rows

Expired rows stay in the table. To delete them in the background, set `prune_interval` on the store, in seconds:

```dart
'database': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'database', 'prune_interval': 3600},
```

Or call `prune()` yourself, for example in a schedule:

```dart
int deleted = await (store.driver as DatabaseCacheDriver).prune();
```

## Pruning the file store

The file store deletes expired files by itself, one time per hour at most.

To clean up more often, call `prune()` yourself, for example in a schedule:

```dart
int deleted = await (store.driver as FileDriver).prune();
```

Or set `prune_every` on the store to prune one time in that many writes:

```dart
'file': <String, dynamic>{
  'driver': 'file',
  'path': 'storage/cache',
  'prune_every': 1000,
},
```

### Faster writes

Each write syncs the file to the disk, which is slow. Turn the sync off with `fsync`:

```dart
'file': <String, dynamic>{
  'driver': 'file',
  'path': 'storage/cache',
  'fsync': false,
},
```

With the sync off, a power cut can lose the last writes. Keep it on for a store that holds sessions.

## Testing

To use a memory store in tests, see [Testing](testing.md#test-the-cache).

## Without Dox

`dox_cache` also works on its own:

```bash
dart pub add dox_cache
```

Make a `CacheManager` with your stores:

```dart
import 'package:dox_cache/dox_cache.dart';

CacheManager cache = CacheManager(CacheConfig(
  defaultStore: 'redis',
  stores: <String, Map<String, dynamic>>{
    'memory': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'memory', 'max_size': 1000},
    'file': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'file', 'path': 'storage/cache'},
    'redis': <String, dynamic>{
      'driver': 'redis',
      'host': '127.0.0.1',
      'prefix': 'app:',
    },
  },
));

CacheStore store = cache.store();     // the default store
await cache.store('file').get('a');   // a named store
```

A `CacheStore` has the same methods as `Cache()`, but the duration is a normal argument:

```dart
await store.put('a', 1, Duration(minutes: 5));
```

### Encryption without Dox

A `CacheManager` you build yourself needs an encrypter for stores with `'encrypt': true`:

```dart
class MyEncrypter implements CacheEncrypter {
  @override
  String encrypt(String text) => myEncrypt(text);

  @override
  String decrypt(String text) => myDecrypt(text); // throw on bad input
}

CacheConfig(defaultStore: 'file', stores: stores, encrypter: MyEncrypter());
```

### Your own driver

Write a factory and register it with `extend`. Or add a ready driver with `addStore`:

```dart
class MyDriverFactory implements CacheDriverFactory {
  @override
  CacheDriver create(Map<String, dynamic> options) {
    return MyDriver(options);
  }
}

cache.extend('mine', MyDriverFactory()); // config: {'driver': 'mine'}
cache.addStore('ready', MemoryDriver());
```

Your driver extends `CacheDriver`. It must implement `prefix`, `get`, `put`, `add`, `increment`, `forget` and `flush`. Override `lock` to support locks.

### Closing the cache

Call `cache.close()` to close the connections of every store, like the Redis connections.

## Next steps

- [Session](../the-basic/session.md): keep sessions in a cache store.
- [Rate limiting](../security/rate-limiting.md): the counts live in the default cache store.
- [Testing](testing.md#test-the-cache): a memory store for each test.
