# Native MySQL driver

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/database/mysql-native/

# Native MySQL driver

`dox_mysql_native` is the MySQL and MariaDB driver of the Dox ORM, written in Rust.

You use it through your models and queries. Rust ([mysql_async](https://docs.rs/mysql_async)) owns the connections and the pool, and each connection keeps its prepared statements. It works with MySQL 8.4 and MariaDB 11.

## Setup

`dox_orm` already depends on `dox_mysql_native`. Add it yourself only to use `MysqlNativePool` without the ORM:

```bash
dart pub add dox_mysql_native
```

The build hook downloads a ready library for your system, so you do not need Rust. The package has its own repo: [dartondox/dox-mysql-native](https://github.com/dartondox/dox-mysql-native).

### Options

The driver reads `host`, `port`, `user`, `password`, `database` and `useSSL` of the `ConnectionConfig`, and these keys from `extra`:

| Key | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `maxConnectionCount` | 10 | Most connections in the pool, for the whole process. |
| `requestTimeout` | 300 s | The longest time for one request. |
| `maxConnectionAge` | 12 hours | Close a connection older than this, when it has no query. |
| `idleTimeout` | 12 hours | Close a connection with no traffic for this long. |
| `serverKill` | true | Stop a cancelled or timed out query on the server with `KILL QUERY`. |
| `preparedStatementCacheSize` | 100 | Prepared statements kept per connection. |
| `verifyCertificate` | true | With `useSSL`, check the server certificate. Set false only for a self-signed certificate in development. |

See [Pool settings](index.md#pool-settings). The connection uses utf8mb4. A login with sha256_password does not work. The default caching_sha2_password and mysql_native_password work.

### Behind a proxy

A cancelled query gets a `KILL QUERY` on a new connection. Behind a proxy with its own connection ids, like ProxySQL, that connection can reach another server. Turn it off there:

```dart
extra: <String, dynamic>{'serverKill': false},
```

Then a cancelled query fails in Dart at once, but it runs to its end on the server. In `DATABASE_URL`, use `?serverKill=false`.

## When the library does not load

If the native library does not load, `SqlQueryBuilder.initializeWithDatabaseConfig` throws an `UnsupportedError`:

```text
dox_mysql_native did not load: <reason>.
Dox needs it to talk to MySQL. Fix: run the app with `dart run` or `dart build cli`. ...
```

To fix it:

- Run the app with `dart run`, `dart test` or `dart build cli`, because they run the build hook. `dart compile exe` does not.
- Or install [Rust](https://rustup.rs). The build hook then builds the library from source.
- If you set `lib_path` in `pubspec.yaml`, check that the file is there and fits your system.

`MysqlNativePool.isAvailable` tells you if the library loaded, and `MysqlNativePool.loadError` gives the reason.

## Types

Rows come back with these Dart types:

| MySQL, MariaDB | Dart |
|---|---|
| TINYINT(1) (`boolean()`) | `bool` |
| TINYINT, SMALLINT, INT, BIGINT, YEAR | `int` |
| FLOAT, DOUBLE, DECIMAL | `double` |
| CHAR, VARCHAR, TEXT, ENUM | `String` |
| DATE, DATETIME, TIMESTAMP | `DateTime` in UTC |
| TIME | `String`, like 12:34:56 |
| JSON | the decoded JSON value |
| BLOB, BINARY, VARBINARY | `Uint8List` |
| NULL | null |

MariaDB keeps JSON columns as LONGTEXT. So on MariaDB, TEXT that holds a JSON object or array comes back decoded.

## Handling errors

Every error throws a `MysqlException`. For a server error, `code` is the MySQL error number, like 1062 for a duplicate key:

```dart
try {
  await QueryBuilder.table('users')
      .insert(<String, dynamic>{'email': email});
} on MysqlException catch (error) {
  if (error.code == 1062) print('taken');
}
```

`sqlState` is the 5 letter SQLSTATE. For other errors, like a down server, both are null. A cancelled query throws a `MysqlQueryCancelledException`. They come from `package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart`.

## Without Dox

### Opening a pool

`MysqlNativePool.open` opens a pool. `query` returns a `MysqlNativeResult` with `columns` and `rows`:

```dart
MysqlNativePool pool = MysqlNativePool.open(
  host: 'localhost',
  user: 'root',
  password: 'password',
  database: 'app',
);

MysqlNativeResult result = await pool.query(
  'SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id = ?',
  parameters: <Object?>[1],
);
print(result.rows); // [{id: 1, name: Ada}]
```

`parameters` is a list for `?`, or a map for `@name`. A write also gives the new id and the changed row count:

```dart
MysqlNativeResult insert = await pool.query(
  'INSERT INTO users (name) VALUES (@name)',
  parameters: <String, dynamic>{'name': 'Bob'},
);
print(insert.insertId);     // the new AUTO_INCREMENT id
print(insert.affectedRows); // 1
```

### Pool settings

`open` also takes `port` (3306), `maxConnections` (10), `secure` (TLS), `verifyCertificate`, `sslRootCert`, `statementCacheSize` (32), `requestTimeout`, `maxConnectionAge`, `idleTimeout` and `serverKill`:

```dart
MysqlNativePool pool = MysqlNativePool.open(
  host: 'localhost',
  user: 'root',
  password: 'password',
  database: 'app',
  secure: true,
  sslRootCert: '/etc/ssl/certs/db-ca.pem',
  requestTimeout: const Duration(seconds: 30),
);
```

A host that starts with `/` is a Unix socket file. Here `maxConnectionAge` has no limit by default.

### Pool from a url

`MysqlNativePool.fromUrl` takes a url with the mysql_async options, like `?pool_max=20`. The kill option there is `server_kill`:

```dart
MysqlNativePool pool =
    MysqlNativePool.fromUrl('mysql://root:password@localhost:3306/app');
```

### Transactions

`begin` gives a transaction id. `execute` is like `query`, but it sends no rows back:

```dart
int tx = await pool.begin();
await pool.execute('UPDATE users SET name = ?',
    parameters: <Object?>['Cy'], transaction: tx);
await pool.commit(tx); // or pool.rollback(tx)
```

### Cancelling a query

Pass a `MysqlCancelToken` to `query`, `execute` or `stream`, and call `cancel()`. `isCancelled` is true after it:

```dart
MysqlCancelToken token = MysqlCancelToken();
Future<MysqlNativeResult> slow =
    pool.query('SELECT SLEEP(10)', cancelToken: token);
token.cancel(); // slow fails with MysqlQueryCancelledException
```

In the ORM, use [`cancelWith()`](query-builder.md#cancelling-a-query).

### Streaming rows

`stream` gives the rows in chunks of up to `chunkSize` rows. Rust reads at most 2 chunks ahead:

```dart
await for (MysqlNativeResult chunk
    in pool.stream('SELECT * FROM logs', chunkSize: 1000)) {
  print(chunk.rows.length);
}
```

Stop the loop with `break` to stop the query. Do not pause a stream for longer than the `net_write_timeout` of the server (60 s by default). In the ORM, use [`cursor()`](query-builder.md#streaming-results).

### Sharing and closing a pool

`pool.handle` works in every isolate of the process. Open the same pool there with `MysqlNativePool.fromHandle(handle)`. `close()` gives back one open, and the last close closes the pool:

```dart
MysqlNativePool other = MysqlNativePool.fromHandle(pool.handle);
pool.close();
```

- [Native Postgres driver](postgres-native.md): the Postgres driver.
- [Performance: database drivers](../digging-deeper/performance.md#database-drivers): driver speed.

# Model

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/database/model/

# Model

A model is a Dart class for one database table, used to read, create, change and delete its rows.

Each object of the model is one row. A model also has all the [query builder](../query-builder.md) methods, so you can query the table through it.

## Setup

Use `make:model` to make a new model. The `-m` option also makes a migration for the table:

```bash
dox make:model Blog      # only the model
dox make:model Blog -m   # the model and a migration for the table blogs
dox make:model Blog -a   # also a migration, factory, seeder, controller
```

This makes `lib/app/models/blog/blog.model.dart`. For the other options, see the [CLI reference](../../reference/cli.md#dox-makemodel).

A model uses a generated class, so run the generator after you make or change a model. Use `watch` in place of `build` to run it on each save:

```bash
dart run build_runner build
```

### Model options

All options go in `@DoxModel(...)`:

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `table` | class name in snake_case | The table name. |
| `primaryKey` | `'id'` | The primary key column. |
| `primaryKeyType` | `int` | The Dart type of the primary key, like `String` for a UUID. |
| `createdAt` | `'created_at'` | The column that keeps the create time. null turns it off. |
| `updatedAt` | `'updated_at'` | The column that keeps the last update time. null turns it off. |
| `timestamps` | `true` | false turns off `createdAt` and `updatedAt`. |
| `softDelete` | `false` | `delete()` sets `deleted_at` and keeps the row. |

## Defining models

A model is a class with `@DoxModel()`. Each `@Column()` field is one column of the table:

```dart title="lib/app/models/blog/blog.model.dart"
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';

part 'blog.model.g.dart'; // (1)!

@DoxModel() // (2)!
class Blog extends BlogGenerator { // (3)!
  @Column() // (4)!
  String? title;

  @Column(name: 'body') // (5)!
  String? description;

  @Column(name: 'user_id')
  int? userId;
}
```

1.  `build_runner` writes this file. It holds the generated `BlogGenerator` class.
2.  Marks the class as a model. See [Model options](#model-options).
3.  The generated class gives the model `id`, `createdAt` and `updatedAt`, and the query builder methods.
4.  The column name is the field name in snake_case.
5.  Use `name` when the column name is not the snake_case of the field.

Make every column field nullable, because a new model has no values yet.

### Table names

The default table name is the class name in snake_case: `BlogPost` uses `blog_post`. Set `table` for another name:

```dart
@DoxModel(table: 'blogs')
class Blog extends BlogGenerator {}
```

`dox make:model Blog` sets `table: 'blogs'` for you. With the [`pluralTableNames` flag](../index.md#orm-flags), the default name is plural.

### Primary keys

Set `primaryKey` for a key with another name, and `primaryKeyType` for a key that is not an integer:

```dart
@DoxModel(primaryKey: 'uuid', primaryKeyType: String)
class Device extends DeviceGenerator {}
```

The field name is the key in camelCase. `save()` inserts a new model, also when you set the key yourself.

### Timestamps

`save()` sets `created_at` and `updated_at` to the current UTC time. Set other column names, or turn them off:

```dart
@DoxModel(createdAt: 'created', updatedAt: 'modified')
class Blog extends BlogGenerator {}

@DoxModel(timestamps: false)
class Setting extends SettingGenerator {}
```

### Column types

The field type tells Dox how to read the value:

| Field type | Column |
|---|---|
| `String?` | text, varchar |
| `int?` | integer types |
| `double?` | float, double. MySQL also gives decimal as a double. Postgres gives numeric as a string. |
| `bool?` | boolean, or a number like tinyint (0 is false) |
| `DateTime?` | date, datetime, timestamp |
| `Map<String, dynamic>?` or `List<dynamic>?` | JSON |
| an enum, like `Status?` | text with the enum name |

For other types, use a [cast](casts.md).

### Changing values on save and read

`beforeSave` and `beforeGet` take a static function of the model. The function gets a map of the values and returns the new value:

```dart
@Column(beforeSave: makeSlug)
String? slug;

@Column(beforeGet: readStatus)
String? status;

static String? makeSlug(Map<String, dynamic> map) {
  return map['title']?.toString().toLowerCase().replaceAll(' ', '-');
}

static String? readStatus(Map<String, dynamic> map) {
  return map['status'] as String? ?? 'draft';
}
```

`beforeSave` gets the model values by column name. `beforeGet` gets the row from the database.

### Using another connection

Use a named connection for the query, and for the save and delete of its models:

```dart
Blog blog = Blog()..withConnection('mysql');
await blog.save();
```

## Retrieving models

Use the [query builder](../query-builder.md) methods to read rows:

```dart
Blog? found = await Blog().find(1);
List<Blog> drafts = await Blog().where('status', 'draft').get();
```

### Starting a new query

A model object keeps the parts of its query. `query()` gives a new, empty model to start another query:

```dart
Blog blog = Blog();
List<Blog> active = await blog.where('status', 'active').get();
List<Blog> deleted = await blog.query().where('status', 'deleted').get();
```

### Refreshing models

`refresh()` reads the row again into this model, with its relations. `fresh()` gives a new model and keeps this one as it is:

```dart
await blog.refresh();
Blog? now = await blog.fresh(); // null when the row is gone
```

Both read the row by its primary key. They also find a soft deleted row.

### Reloading relations

`reload()` loads the relations of the model again, for example after a save:

```dart
await blog.save();
await blog.reload();
```

## Inserting and updating models

### Inserts

Make a new model, set its fields and call `save()`:

```dart
Blog blog = Blog();
blog.title = 'My first blog';
await blog.save();
print(blog.id); // the new id
```

Null fields are not sent, so the database default is used.

### Updates

`save()` on a model from the table updates it. It sends only the fields that changed:

```dart
Blog? found = await Blog().find(1);
found?.title = 'New title';
await found?.save();
```

To clear a column, set the field to null and save. A map or list field is always sent, because it can change in place.

`save()` returns false when a [model event](events.md) cancels it. `saveQuietly()` saves with no events.

### Checking if a row exists

`exists` is true when the model is in the table. `wasRecentlyCreated` is true after a save inserted the row:

```dart
User user = await User().firstOrCreate(<String, dynamic>{'email': email});
if (user.wasRecentlyCreated) await sendWelcomeMail(user);
```

### Creating from a map

`create()` makes a new row from a map and returns the model. The model needs `fillable`, see [Mass assignment](#mass-assignment):

```dart
Blog created = await Blog().create(<String, dynamic>{
  'title': 'My first blog',
  'status': 'draft',
});
```

It works like `save()` on a new model, with the events. A null key is not sent, unless the [`createWritesNull` flag](../index.md#orm-flags) is on. `insert()` on a model does the same as `create()`.

### Updating from a map

`update()` on a model from the table changes only that row and sets `updated_at`. It fires no model events:

```dart
await blog.update(<String, dynamic>{'status': 'live'});
```

### Mass assignment

`create()`, `insert()`, `update()`, `upsert()` and the find or create methods take their keys from a map. So a model is guarded by default. List the keys that may come from a map:

```dart
@DoxModel()
class User extends UserGenerator {
  // only these keys are taken from a map
  @override
  List<String> get fillable => <String>['name', 'email'];

  // or: every key but these is taken from a map
  @override
  List<String> get guarded => <String>['is_admin'];
}
```

With `fillable`, other keys are dropped. A model with no `fillable` and the default `guarded` throws a `MassAssignmentException` for a map with keys. Fields you set in code are always saved.

To take every key, set `guarded` to an empty list. This is not safe with user input:

```dart
@override
List<String> get guarded => const <String>[];
```

#### Skip the fillable check

These methods ignore `fillable` and `guarded`. Never pass user input, like `req.body`, to them:

```dart
await User().forceCreate(
    <String, dynamic>{'name': 'Ann', 'is_admin': true});
await User().where('id', 1)
    .forceUpdate(<String, dynamic>{'is_admin': true});
await user.forceFill(<String, dynamic>{'is_admin': true}).save();
```

`forceFill()` sets the fields and does not save. Model events that fire inside `forceCreate()` and `forceUpdate()` also skip the check.

`Model.unguarded()` turns the check off for everything inside the callback. Await all work inside it, because work that ends later also runs with the check off:

```dart
await Model.unguarded(() async {
  await User().create(<String, dynamic>{'name': 'Bob', 'is_admin': true});
});
```

`Model.isUnguarded` is true inside the callback.

### Find or create

These methods find a row by the first map. When there is no row, they use both maps:

```dart
User user = await User().firstOrCreate(
  <String, dynamic>{'email': 'ann@example.com'},
  <String, dynamic>{'name': 'Ann'},
);

User other = await User().firstOrNew(
    <String, dynamic>{'email': 'bob@example.com'});

User updated = await User().updateOrCreate(
  <String, dynamic>{'email': 'ann@example.com'},
  <String, dynamic>{'name': 'Ann Lee'},
);
```

`firstOrNew()` does not save the new model. See the [query builder](../query-builder.md#finding-or-creating-a-row).

### Incrementing and decrementing

Add to or take from a number column in one query. The field gets the new value too:

```dart
await blog.increment('views');      // views + 1
await blog.increment('views', 5);   // views + 5
await blog.decrement('views');      // views - 1
await blog.increment('views', 1, <String, dynamic>{'status': 'hot'});
```

The third argument sets other columns. They fire no model events and do not set `updated_at`, unless the [`incrementFiresEvents` flag](../index.md#orm-flags) is on.

### Touch and replicate

`touch()` sets `updated_at`, or the column you give, to now. It fires the save events. `touchQuietly()` fires none:

```dart
await blog.touch();               // updated_at = now
await blog.touch('published_at'); // published_at = now
```

`replicate()` makes an unsaved copy with no primary key and no timestamps. List the columns to leave out:

```dart
Blog copy = blog.replicate(<String>['slug'])..title = 'Copy';
await copy.save();
```

Relations are not copied. The copy of a soft deleted model is soft deleted too.

### Checking changed columns

These methods tell you what changed before or after a save. The names are column names, like `user_id`:

```dart
blog.title = 'New title';

blog.isDirty();             // true
blog.isDirty('title');      // true
blog.isClean('body');       // true
blog.getDirty();            // {title: New title}
blog.getOriginal('title');  // the old title

await blog.save();
blog.wasChanged('title');   // true
blog.getChanges();          // {title: New title, updated_at: ...}
```

`isDirty()`, `isClean()` and `wasChanged()` also take a list of names.

## Deleting models

`delete()` deletes the row of the model. It returns 1, or 0 when the row was not there or a [model event](events.md) cancelled it:

```dart
int count = await blog.delete();
```

A model with no primary key value throws a `StateError`, so `Blog().delete()` can not delete every row. To delete the rows of a query, add a `where`. A [global scope](scopes.md#global-scopes) counts as a `where`. See [writing every row](../query-builder.md#writing-every-row).

### Soft deleting

A **soft delete** keeps the row and sets its `deleted_at`. Turn it on with `softDelete`:

```dart
@DoxModel(softDelete: true)
class Blog extends BlogGenerator {}
```

The table needs a nullable `deleted_at` column. In a migration, add `table.softDeletes();`. Queries then leave out soft deleted rows.

### Reading soft deleted rows

`withTrash()` also gets the soft deleted rows. `onlyTrashed()` gets only them:

```dart
List<Blog> all = await Blog().withTrash().get();
List<Blog> trashed = await Blog().onlyTrashed().get();
```

### Restoring soft deleted models

`trashed()` tells you if a model is soft deleted. `restore()` brings it back:

```dart
Blog? blog = await Blog().withTrash().find(1);
if (blog!.trashed()) await blog.restore();
```

### Deleting for good

`forceDelete()` deletes the row, also on a soft delete model:

```dart
await blog.forceDelete();
```

## Converting to a map or JSON

`toMap()` gives all columns and computed values. `toJson()` gives the same without hidden fields:

```dart
Map<String, dynamic> map = blog.toMap();
Map<String, dynamic> json = blog.toJson();
Map<String, dynamic> row = blog.toMap(original: true); // the raw row
```

`jsonEncode(blog)` uses `toJson()`, so a controller can return a model or a list of models.

### Hide fields

Put fields like a password in `hidden`, and `toJson()` leaves them out. Use the column names:

```dart
@override
List<String> get hidden => <String>['password', 'remember_token'];
```

To keep only some fields, list them in `visibleFields`:

```dart
@override
List<String> get visibleFields => const <String>['id', 'name'];
```

For one model or a list of models, use `makeHidden()` and `makeVisible()`:

```dart
return user.makeVisible(<String>['email']).toJson();
return users.makeHidden(<String>['phone']);
```

### Computed values

A **computed value** is a getter in the JSON that is not a column. Add `@Computed()`, then run the generator:

```dart
@Computed() // json key: full_name
String get fullName => '$firstName $lastName';

@Computed(name: 'initials') // custom json key
String get shortName => '${firstName?[0]}${lastName?[0]}';
```

The getter runs each time `toJson()` or `toMap()` runs, so keep it fast. `hidden` hides it by its json key.

## Relationships

A model can load related models. See [HasOne](relationship/has-one.md), [HasMany](relationship/has-many.md), [BelongsTo](relationship/belongs-to.md), [ManyToMany](relationship/many-to-many.md), [HasManyThrough](relationship/through.md) and [Polymorphic](relationship/polymorphic.md).

### Preloading relations

`preload()` loads a relation for all rows of a query. A dot path also loads the relations of the loaded rows:

```dart
Blog? blog = await Blog().preload('comments').find(1);
List<User> users = await User().preload('posts.comments').get();
```

### Filtering a preload

Give a callback to load only some related rows. With a dot path, it is for the last relation:

```dart
await User().preload('posts', (QueryBuilder<dynamic> q) {
  q.where('published', true);
}).get();
```

### Loading a relation on a model

`$getRelation()` loads a relation into its field. `related()` gives a query for the related rows:

```dart
await blog.$getRelation('comments');
List<Comment> recent = await blog
        .related<Comment>('comments')
        ?.orderBy('id', 'desc')
        .get() ??
    <Comment>[];
```

### Saving through a relation

These methods save a related model and set the foreign key. They work with `@HasMany`, `@HasOne`, `@MorphMany` and `@MorphOne`:

```dart
Comment c = await blog.createRelated<Comment>('comments',
    <String, dynamic>{'body': 'hi'});
await blog.saveRelated('comments', Comment()..body = 'hi');
await blog.saveManyRelated('comments', <Comment>[c1, c2]);
```

`createRelated()` uses `create()`, but the foreign key does not need to be in `fillable`. For a `@BelongsTo`, use `associate()` and `dissociate()`. See [BelongsTo](relationship/belongs-to.md#saving-related-models).

## Debugging queries

`debug(true)` prints the SQL of the model in the terminal:

```dart
Blog blog = Blog()..debug(true);
blog.title = 'John Wick';
await blog.save();
```

# Model events

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/database/model/events/

# Model events

A model fires events when you save, delete or restore it, so you can run your own code at these moments.

There are two ways to listen. A **hook** is a method in the model class. An **observer** is a separate class, for code that needs other services, like a mailer.

Events fire only on one model object. A query write, like `Post().where('draft', true).update({...})`, runs one query and fires no events.

## Defining hooks

Override an `on...` method in the model class, then run `dart run build_runner build`:

```dart title="lib/app/models/post/post.model.dart"
@DoxModel()
class Post extends PostGenerator {
  @Column()
  String? title;

  @Column()
  String? slug;

  @override
  Future<void> onSaving() async {
    slug = title?.trim().toLowerCase().replaceAll(' ', '-');
  }
}
```

A before hook runs before the query, so it can change values or [cancel the operation](#cancelling-an-operation). An after hook runs when the row is written:

| Before hook | After hook | Runs on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `onSaving` | `onSaved` | every `save()` |
| `onCreating` | `onCreated` | `save()` or `create()` on a new model |
| `onUpdating` | `onUpdated` | `save()` on a model from the table |
| `onDeleting` | `onDeleted` | `delete()` |
| `onForceDeleting` | `onForceDeleted` | `forceDelete()` |
| `onRestoring` | `onRestored` | `restore()` |

`onTrashed` runs after `onDeleted` when a soft delete changed the row. `touch()`, `firstOrCreate()` and `updateOrCreate()` fire the save events too.

### Order of events

The model hook runs first. Then the observers run, in the order you added them:

| Call | Events, in order |
|------|------------------|
| `save()` on a new model | saving, creating, INSERT, created, saved |
| `save()` on a model from the table | saving, updating, UPDATE, updated, saved |
| `delete()` | deleting, DELETE, deleted, then trashed after a soft delete |
| `forceDelete()` | forceDeleting, deleting, DELETE, deleted, forceDeleted |
| `restore()` | restoring, UPDATE, restored |

A save with no changes runs no UPDATE, but it fires the same events. With the [`skipCleanUpdateEvents` flag](../index.md#orm-flags), it fires only saving and saved.

### Setting a value only on create

Use `onCreating` for a value that you set one time, on a new row:

```dart
@override
Future<void> onCreating() async {
  status ??= 'draft';
}
```

### Doing something after a change

Use an after hook for side effects, because the row is already in the database:

```dart
@override
Future<void> onSaved() async {
  await Cache().forget('post:$id');
}
```

## Cancelling an operation

Throw `CancelModelEvent` in a before hook, and the query does not run:

```dart title="lib/app/models/post/post.model.dart"
@override
Future<void> onDeleting() async {
  if (status == 'published') {
    throw CancelModelEvent('unpublish the post first');
  }
}
```

`save()` and `restore()` then return false, and `delete()` and `forceDelete()` return 0. `create()` returns the unsaved model, with a null `id`.

## Observers

Extend `ModelObserver<T>` and override only the methods you need. They have the names of the hooks, and each one gets the model:

```dart title="lib/app/observers/user.observer.dart"
class UserObserver extends ModelObserver<User> {
  final Mailer mailer;

  UserObserver(this.mailer);

  @override
  Future<void> onCreated(User model) async {
    await mailer.sendWelcome(model.email!);
  }
}
```

A before method can also throw `CancelModelEvent`.

### Registering observers

Add the observer with `Model.observe()` in the `setup()` of a [provider](../../digging-deeper/providers.md). The provider runs it in every isolate:

```dart title="lib/providers/observer_provider.dart"
class ObserverProvider extends DoxProvider {
  @override
  void setup() {
    Model.observe<User>(UserObserver(Mailer()));
  }
}
```

A model can have more than one observer.

### Removing observers

`Model.forgetObservers()` removes the observers of one model, or of all models:

```dart
Model.forgetObservers<User>();
Model.forgetObservers();
```

### Listening to soft deletes

Add the `TrashedObserver` mixin and override `onTrashed`:

```dart
class PostObserver extends ModelObserver<Post> with TrashedObserver<Post> {
  @override
  void onTrashed(Post post) => print('trashed ${post.id}');
}
```

## Saving without events

`saveQuietly()` saves one model with no events, and `touchQuietly()` touches it with no events:

```dart
await user.saveQuietly();
```

`Model.withoutEvents()` turns off events for everything inside the callback:

```dart
await Model.withoutEvents(() async {
  await user.save();
  await post.delete();
});
```

## Events and transactions

`save()` does not start a transaction, so the row stays written when an after hook throws. To undo it, use a [transaction](../transactions.md):

```dart
await QueryBuilder.transaction(() async {
  await user.save(); // if onCreated() throws, the INSERT is rolled back
});
```

## Next steps

- [Model](index.md): save and delete models.
- [Providers](../../digging-deeper/providers.md): register observers.
- [Transactions](../transactions.md): undo a write when a hook fails.

# Query scopes

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/database/model/scopes/

# Query scopes

A scope is a query part that you use again and again, like "only active users", written once in the model and called like a query method.

## Local scopes

Add a static method with `@Scope()` to the model. It takes the query first and returns the query. Then run `dart run build_runner build`:

```dart
@DoxModel()
class User extends UserGenerator {
  @Scope()
  static QueryBuilder<User> isActive(QueryBuilder<User> q) {
    return q.where('active', true);
  }

  @Scope()
  static QueryBuilder<User> olderThan(QueryBuilder<User> q, int age) {
    return q.where('age', '>', age);
  }
}
```

Call each scope as a method on the query, without the query argument:

```dart
List<User> adults = await User().isActive().olderThan(18).get();
```

The scope name must not be the name of a field, a method of the model or a query method. So name a scope `isActive`, not `active`, next to an `active` field.

## Global scopes

A **global scope** adds a condition to every query of the model. Use `@Scope(global: true)`:

```dart
@DoxModel()
class Post extends PostGenerator {
  @Scope(global: true)
  static QueryBuilder<Post> notArchived(QueryBuilder<Post> q) {
    return q.where('archived', false);
  }
}

await Post().get(); // ... WHERE ("archived" = false)
```

It applies to reads, counts, query updates and deletes, and relation queries. So `Post().delete()` deletes only the rows in the scope.

### Removing global scopes

Remove one scope by its method name, or remove all of them:

```dart
await Post().withoutGlobalScope('notArchived').get();
await Post().withoutGlobalScopes().find(1);
```

A query write with `withoutGlobalScopes()` and no `where` throws a `StateError`.

## Next steps

- [Query Builder](../query-builder.md): the methods you can use in a scope.
- [Model](index.md): the model basics.

# Attribute casts

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/database/model/casts/

# Attribute casts

A cast changes a column value between the database and Dart, for example to read JSON text as a map or to save an enum by its name.

A cast runs when a row is read, when the model is saved, and in `toJson()`. Casts work the same on Postgres, MySQL, MariaDB and SQLite.

## Defining casts

Set a cast with `cast` on `@Column()`, then run `dart run build_runner build`:

```dart
@DoxModel()
class Item extends ItemGenerator {
  @Column(cast: JsonCast())
  Map<String, dynamic>? meta;

  @Column(cast: ListCast<String>())
  List<String>? tags;

  @Column(cast: EnumCast<Level>(Level.values, byIndex: true))
  Level? level;
}
```

A bool field gets `BoolCast()` and an enum field gets `EnumCast(values)` by itself. A column with `beforeGet` does not use its cast.

A cast does not change a `where()` value, so use the database value there:

```dart
where('status', Status.live.name)
```

## Built-in casts

| Cast | Dart value | Database value |
|---|---|---|
| `JsonCast()` | a map or a list | JSON, or JSON in a text column |
| `ListCast<E>()` | a typed list, like `List<String>` | JSON, or JSON in a text column |
| `BoolCast()` | a bool | boolean, a number (0 is false), or the text 1, 0, true, false, t, f |
| `EnumCast<E>(E.values)` | an enum | text with the enum name |
| `EnumCast<E>(E.values, byIndex: true)` | an enum | a number, the enum index |

## Unknown enum values

A stored value that the enum does not have reads as null, with one warning in the log. Give `unknown` to read it as a value of your own:

```dart
@Column(cast: EnumCast(Status.values, unknown: Status.draft))
Status status = Status.draft;
```

A field that can not be null and has no `unknown` throws a `StateError`. A save does not overwrite the stored value, unless you set a real enum value.

## Custom casts

Extend `Cast<T>`. `get()` changes the database value to the Dart value, and `set()` changes it back. The class needs a const constructor:

```dart
class MoneyCast extends Cast<Money> {
  const MoneyCast();

  @override
  Money? get(dynamic value) => value == null ? null : Money(value as int);

  @override
  dynamic set(Money? value) => value?.cents;
}

@DoxModel()
class Product extends ProductGenerator {
  @Column(cast: MoneyCast())
  Money? price;
}
```

The generator copies the `cast` code into the generated file, so import the names it uses in the model file.

## Next steps

- [Model](index.md): the column types of a model.
- [Serializer](../../the-basic/serializer.md): set the JSON shape of a model.

# Counting relations

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/database/model/counting-relations/

# Counting relations

`withCount()` adds the number of related rows to each model, without loading the rows.

It adds a subquery to the select, so you get the counts with the same query. Use the relation name, which is the field name.

## Counting related rows

Read the count with `countOf()`. In JSON, the key is the relation name in snake_case with `_count`:

```dart
List<User> users = await User().withCount('posts').get();

users.first.countOf('posts'); // 3
users.first.toJson();         // {..., "posts_count": 3}
```

It works with every relation but `@BelongsTo` and `@MorphTo`, which throw an `UnsupportedError`. The global scopes and soft deletes of the related model apply.

### Counting only some rows

Give a function with conditions, and use `as` to give the count its own key. Read a custom key with `aggregate()`:

```dart
List<User> users = await User()
    .withCount('posts as published_count', (QueryBuilder<dynamic> q) {
      q.where('published', true);
    })
    .get();

users.first.aggregate('published_count');
```

### Counting and loading together

`withCount()` works with the other query methods and with `preload()`:

```dart
User? user = await User().preload('posts').withCount('posts').find(1);
```

## Sum, average, min and max

`withSum()`, `withAvg()`, `withMin()` and `withMax()` work like `withCount()` on one column. The value is null when there is no related row:

```dart
User? user = await User()
    .withSum('posts', 'views')
    .withAvg('posts', 'views')
    .withMin('posts', 'views')
    .withMax('posts', 'views')
    .find(1);

user?.aggregate('posts_sum_views');
```

The keys are `posts_sum_views`, `posts_avg_views`, `posts_min_views` and `posts_max_views`.

## Checking if related rows exist

`withExists()` adds `<relation>_exists`, which is true when there is a related row. It takes a function and `as`, like `withCount()`:

```dart
User? user = await User().withExists('posts').find(1);
user?.aggregate('posts_exists'); // true or false
```

## Next steps

- [Query by relations](relation-queries.md): keep only the rows that have related rows.
- [HasMany](relationship/has-many.md): define a relation.

# Query by relations

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/database/model/relation-queries/

# Query by relations

`whereHas()`, `whereDoesntHave()` and `has()` keep the rows of a query by their related rows.

They add a subquery to the `where` part and do not load the related rows. To load them, use [`preload()`](index.md#preloading-relations). Use the relation name (the field name), and start the query with a model, like `User()`.

## Rows that have a relation

`whereHas()` keeps the rows that have a related row. A function adds conditions to the related rows:

```dart
List<User> users = await User().whereHas('posts').get();

List<User> writers = await User().whereHas('posts',
    (QueryBuilder<dynamic> q) {
  q.where('published', true);
}).get();
```

Soft deleted related rows do not count. The global scopes and the `onQuery` function of the relation apply.

## Rows that do not have a relation

`whereDoesntHave()` keeps the rows that have no related row. It also takes a function:

```dart
List<User> users = await User().whereDoesntHave('posts').get();
```

## Joining with or

`orWhereHas()` and `orWhereDoesntHave()` join the condition with OR:

```dart
List<User> users = await User()
    .where('name', 'Ann')
    .orWhereHas('posts')
    .get();

await User().where('name', 'Ann').orWhereDoesntHave('posts').get();
```

## Counting related rows

`has()` takes an operator and a number. The default is at least one related row:

```dart
await User().has('posts', '>=', 3).get();
await User().has('posts', '=', 0).get();

await User().has('posts', '>', 1, (QueryBuilder<dynamic> q) {
  q.where('published', true);
}).get();
```

The operator is one of `=`, `!=`, `<>`, `<`, `>`, `<=` or `>=`.

## Relations of relations

Use a dot path. The function is for the last relation:

```dart
await User().whereHas('posts.comments', (QueryBuilder<dynamic> q) {
  q.where('user_id', 1);
}).get();
```

With `has()`, the count is for the last relation of one row. So `has('posts.comments', '>=', 2)` keeps the users that have a post with two comments or more.

## A relation to the same table

It works for a relation to the same table, like a category and its parent:

```dart
List<Category> books = await Category()
    .whereHas('parent', (QueryBuilder<dynamic> q) {
      q.where('name', 'Books');
    })
    .get();
```

In the function, write the column without the table name: `name`, not `categories.name`.

## Next steps

- [Counting relations](counting-relations.md): count the related rows.
- [HasMany](relationship/has-many.md): define a relation.

# HasOne

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/database/model/relationship/has-one/

# HasOne

Use `HasOne` when one row of this table has one row in another table.

For example, a user has one user info row. The other table keeps the foreign key: `user_info.user_id`.

## Setup

Add a nullable field with `@HasOne()` to the model. The related model has the foreign key column:

```dart title="lib/app/models/user/user.model.dart"
@DoxModel()
class User extends UserGenerator {
  @HasOne(UserInfo)
  UserInfo? userInfo;
}

@DoxModel()
class UserInfo extends UserInfoGenerator {
  @Column()
  int? userId; // column user_id

  @Column()
  String? address;
}
```

Run `dart run build_runner build` after you add a relation.

### Options

Set the keys when your columns have other names:

```dart
@HasOne(UserInfo, foreignKey: 'owner_id', localKey: 'id')
UserInfo? userInfo;
```

| Option | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `foreignKey` | `{this model}_id`, like `user_id` | The column in the related table that points to this model. |
| `localKey` | the primary key of this model | The column in this table that `foreignKey` points to. |
| `onQuery` | none | A static function that changes the query. |
| `eager` | `false` | Load the relation on every query. |

The default foreign key comes from the class name, also when the table is `users`.

## Loading the relation

The relation is not loaded by default. Use the field name, `'userInfo'`, as the relation name.

### Preloading

`preload()` loads the relation for all models of a query, with one more query:

```dart
User? user = await User().preload('userInfo').find(1);
print(user?.userInfo?.address);
```

The relation is then in `toJson()`, with the field name in snake_case as the key.

### Loading on a model you have

`$getRelation()` loads the relation into the field:

```dart
await user.$getRelation('userInfo');
```

### Querying the relation

`related()` gives a query for the related row. It does not set the field:

```dart
UserInfo? info = await user
    .related<UserInfo>('userInfo')
    ?.where('address', '!=', '')
    .getFirst();
```

### Always loading the relation

Set `eager: true` to load the relation on every query of the model:

```dart
@HasOne(UserInfo, eager: true)
UserInfo? userInfo;
```

## Saving related models

`createRelated()` and `saveRelated()` save the related model and set its foreign key:

```dart
await user.createRelated<UserInfo>('userInfo',
    <String, dynamic>{'address': 'Paris'});
await user.saveRelated('userInfo', UserInfo()..address = 'Paris');
```

Save the user first, because a model with no key throws a `StateError`.

## Filtering by the relation

`whereHas()` keeps the users that have a user info row. `whereDoesntHave()` keeps the users without one:

```dart
List<User> inParis = await User().whereHas('userInfo',
    (QueryBuilder<dynamic> q) {
  q.where('address', 'Paris');
}).get();

List<User> noInfo = await User().whereDoesntHave('userInfo').get();
```

See [Query by relations](../relation-queries.md).

## Changing the relation query

Give `onQuery` a static function of the model. It gets the query of the related model and returns it:

```dart
@HasOne(UserInfo, onQuery: byId)
UserInfo? userInfo;

static QueryBuilder<UserInfo> byId(UserInfo q) {
  return q.orderBy('id');
}
```

When there are many related rows, the relation keeps the last row of the query. So this example keeps the row with the highest id.

## Next steps

- [HasMany](has-many.md): one row with many related rows.
- [BelongsTo](belongs-to.md): the other side of the relation.
- [Counting relations](../counting-relations.md): count the related rows.


---

# HasMany

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/database/model/relationship/has-many/

# HasMany

Use `HasMany` when one row of this table has many rows in another table.

For example, a user has many posts. The other table keeps the foreign key: `post.user_id`.

## Setup

Add a list field with `@HasMany()` to the model, and start it as an empty list. The related model has the foreign key column:

```dart title="lib/app/models/user/user.model.dart"
@DoxModel()
class User extends UserGenerator {
  @HasMany(Post)
  List<Post> posts = <Post>[];
}

@DoxModel()
class Post extends PostGenerator {
  @Column()
  int? userId; // column user_id

  @Column()
  String? title;
}
```

Run `dart run build_runner build` after you add a relation.

### Options

Set the keys when your columns have other names:

```dart
@HasMany(Book, foreignKey: 'author_code', localKey: 'code')
List<Book> books = <Book>[];
```

| Option | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `foreignKey` | `{this model}_id`, like `user_id` | The column in the related table that points to this model. |
| `localKey` | the primary key of this model | The column in this table that `foreignKey` points to. |
| `onQuery` | none | A static function that changes the query. |
| `eager` | `false` | Load the relation on every query. |

The default foreign key comes from the class name, also when the table is `users`.

## Loading the relation

The relation is not loaded by default. Use the field name, `'posts'`, as the relation name.

### Preloading

`preload()` loads the relation for all models of a query, with one more query. A user with no posts gets an empty list:

```dart
List<User> users = await User().preload('posts').get();
print(users.first.posts.length);
```

The relation is then in `toJson()`, with the field name in snake_case as the key.

### Loading on a model you have

`$getRelation()` loads the relation into the field:

```dart
await user.$getRelation('posts');
```

### Querying the relation

`related()` gives a query for the related rows. It does not set the field:

```dart
List<Post> drafts = await user
        .related<Post>('posts')
        ?.where('status', 'draft')
        .get() ??
    <Post>[];
```

### Always loading the relation

Set `eager: true` to load the relation on every query of the model:

```dart
@HasMany(Post, eager: true)
List<Post> posts = <Post>[];
```

## Saving related models

`createRelated()`, `saveRelated()` and `saveManyRelated()` save related models and set their foreign key:

```dart
Post post = await user.createRelated<Post>('posts',
    <String, dynamic>{'title': 'Hello'});
await user.saveRelated('posts', Post()..title = 'Hello');
await user.saveManyRelated('posts', <Post>[first, second]);
```

Save the user first, because a model with no key throws a `StateError`.

## Filtering by the relation

`whereHas()` keeps the users that have a post. `whereDoesntHave()` keeps the users with no post, and `has()` counts the posts:

```dart
List<User> writers = await User().whereHas('posts').get();
List<User> noPosts = await User().whereDoesntHave('posts').get();
List<User> busy = await User().has('posts', '>=', 10).get();
```

See [Query by relations](../relation-queries.md).

## Changing the relation query

Give `onQuery` a static function of the model. It gets the query of the related model and returns it. Two fields can use the same model with other queries:

```dart
@HasMany(Post)
List<Post> posts = <Post>[];

@HasMany(Post, onQuery: onlyActive)
List<Post> activePosts = <Post>[];

static QueryBuilder<Post> onlyActive(Post q) {
  return q.where('status', 'active').orderBy('id', 'desc');
}
```

## Next steps

- [BelongsTo](belongs-to.md): the other side of the relation.
- [Counting relations](../counting-relations.md): count the related rows.
- [Query by relations](../relation-queries.md): filter by the related rows.


---

# BelongsTo

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/database/model/relationship/belongs-to/

# BelongsTo

Use `BelongsTo` when this table keeps the foreign key to another table.

For example, a comment belongs to a user, so the comment table has the column `user_id`. It is the other side of [HasOne](has-one.md) and [HasMany](has-many.md).

## Setup

Add a nullable field with `@BelongsTo()` to the model that has the foreign key column:

```dart title="lib/app/models/comment/comment.model.dart"
@DoxModel()
class Comment extends CommentGenerator {
  @Column()
  int? userId; // column user_id

  @Column()
  String? content;

  @BelongsTo(User)
  User? user;
}
```

Run `dart run build_runner build` after you add a relation.

### Options

The default foreign key comes from the class name of the related model, not from the field name. So a field `author` still uses `user_id`. Set the key for another name:

```dart
@BelongsTo(User, foreignKey: 'author_id', localKey: 'id')
User? author;
```

| Option | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `foreignKey` | `{related model}_id`, like `user_id` | The column in this table that points to the related model. |
| `localKey` | the primary key of the related model | The column in the related table that `foreignKey` points to. |
| `onQuery` | none | A static function that changes the query. |
| `eager` | `false` | Load the relation on every query. |

With the [`belongsToKeyFromRelation` flag](../../index.md#orm-flags), the default comes from the field name: `author` gives `author_id`.

## Loading the relation

The relation is not loaded by default. Use the field name, `'user'`, as the relation name.

### Preloading

`preload()` loads the relation for all models of a query, with one more query. Comments of the same user get the same `User` object:

```dart
List<Comment> comments = await Comment().preload('user').all();
print(comments.first.user?.name);
```

The relation is then in `toJson()`, with the field name in snake_case as the key.

### Loading on a model you have

`$getRelation()` loads the relation into the field. It runs one query each time, so use `preload()` for a list:

```dart
await comment.$getRelation('user');
```

### Querying the relation

`related()` gives a query for the related row. It does not set the field:

```dart
User? activeUser = await comment
    .related<User>('user')
    ?.where('status', 'active')
    .getFirst();
```

### Always loading the relation

Set `eager: true` to load the relation on every query of the model:

```dart
@BelongsTo(User, eager: true)
User? user;
```

## Saving related models

`associate()` sets the foreign key to the key of a saved model. `dissociate()` sets it to null. Call `save()` after them:

```dart
await comment.associate('user', user).save();
await comment.dissociate('user').save();
```

The relation field does not change.

## Filtering by the relation

`whereHas()` keeps the comments of a user that matches:

```dart
List<Comment> comments = await Comment().whereHas('user',
    (QueryBuilder<dynamic> q) {
  q.where('name', 'Ann');
}).get();
```

See [Query by relations](../relation-queries.md).

## Changing the relation query

Give `onQuery` a static function of the model. It gets the query of the related model and returns it:

```dart
@BelongsTo(User, onQuery: onlyActive)
User? activeUser;

static QueryBuilder<User> onlyActive(User q) {
  return q.where('status', 'active');
}
```

## Next steps

- [HasMany](has-many.md): the other side of the relation.
- [Serializer](../../../the-basic/serializer.md): set the JSON shape of a model.
- [Query by relations](../relation-queries.md): filter by the related rows.


---

# ManyToMany

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/database/model/relationship/many-to-many/

# ManyToMany

Use `ManyToMany` when rows on both sides can have many rows on the other side.

For example, an artist has many songs, and a song has many artists. A third table, the **pivot table**, keeps the links. It has one foreign key to each side.

## Setup

### Tables

| Table | Columns |
|---|---|
| `artist` | `id`, `name` |
| `song` | `id`, `title` |
| `artist_song` (pivot) | `id`, `artist_id`, `song_id` |

The default pivot table name is the two class names in snake_case, in A-Z order, joined with `_`. A migration for it:

```dart
await schema.create('artist_song', (Table table) {
  table.id();
  table.foreignId('artist_id').constrained('artist').cascadeOnDelete();
  table.foreignId('song_id').constrained('song').cascadeOnDelete();
});
```

### Defining the relation

Add a list field with `@ManyToMany()` to each model that needs it, and start it as an empty list:

```dart title="lib/app/models/artist/artist.model.dart"
@DoxModel()
class Artist extends ArtistGenerator {
  @ManyToMany(Song)
  List<Song> songs = <Song>[];
}

@DoxModel()
class Song extends SongGenerator {
  @ManyToMany(Artist)
  List<Artist> artists = <Artist>[];
}
```

Run `dart run build_runner build` after you add a relation.

### Options

Set the names when your pivot table or columns have other names:

```dart
@ManyToMany(
  Song,
  pivotTable: 'artist_song',
  pivotForeignKey: 'artist_id',
  pivotRelatedForeignKey: 'song_id',
)
List<Song> songs = <Song>[];
```

The examples are for `@ManyToMany(Song)` in the `Artist` model:

| Option | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `pivotTable` | the two class names in A-Z order, like `artist_song` | The pivot table. |
| `pivotForeignKey` | `{this model}_id`, like `artist_id` | The pivot column that points to this model. |
| `pivotRelatedForeignKey` | `{related model}_id`, like `song_id` | The pivot column that points to the related model. |
| `localKey` | the primary key of this model | The column in `artist` that `pivotForeignKey` points to. |
| `relatedKey` | the primary key of the related model | The column in `song` that `pivotRelatedForeignKey` points to. |
| `withPivot` | none | More pivot columns to read, like `['role']`. |
| `withTimestamps` | `false` | Read and set `created_at` and `updated_at` in the pivot table. |
| `onQuery` | none | A static function that changes the query. |
| `eager` | `false` | Load the relation on every query. |

## Loading the relation

The relation is not loaded by default. Use the field name, `'songs'`, as the relation name.

### Preloading

`preload()` loads the relation for all models of a query, with one more query. A model with no links gets an empty list:

```dart
Artist? artist = await Artist().preload('songs').find(1);
print(artist?.songs.length);
```

The relation is then in `toJson()`, with the field name in snake_case as the key.

### Loading on a model you have

`$getRelation()` loads the relation into the field:

```dart
await artist.$getRelation('songs');
```

### Querying the relation

`related()` gives a query for the related rows. It does not set the field. The query joins the pivot table, so write `table.column`:

```dart
List<Song> songs = await artist
        .related<Song>('songs')
        ?.orderBy('song.title')
        .get() ??
    <Song>[];
```

### Always loading the relation

Set `eager: true` to load the relation on every query of the model. Do not set it on both sides, because each side then loads the other side again and again:

```dart
@ManyToMany(Song, eager: true)
List<Song> songs = <Song>[];
```

### Reading pivot columns

List the pivot columns in `withPivot`, then read them with `pivot` on each related model:

```dart
@ManyToMany(Song, withPivot: <String>['role'])
List<Song> songs = <Song>[];

for (Song song in artist.songs) {
  print(song.pivot['role']);
}
```

`pivot` is empty on a model that the relation did not load. `toJson()` has a `pivot` key. Put `'pivot'` in `hidden` to leave it out.

## Saving related models

These methods add and remove pivot rows. Save the model first, because a model with no key throws a `StateError`.

The ids can be one id, a model, a list of ids or models, or a map of `id => pivot values`. Each id is used once.

### Attaching

`attach()` adds a pivot row for each id. The third argument has the pivot values for each new row:

```dart
await artist.attach('songs', 1);
await artist.attach('songs', <int>[2, 3],
    <String, dynamic>{'role': 'singer'});
await artist.attach('songs', <int, Map<String, dynamic>>{
  4: <String, dynamic>{'role': 'writer'},
});
```

`attach()` does not check for a row that is already there. Use `sync()` or `syncWithoutDetaching()` when it can be there.

### Detaching

`detach()` deletes the pivot rows of the ids and returns the number of deleted rows. With no ids, it deletes every pivot row of the model:

```dart
await artist.detach('songs', <int>[1, 2]);
await artist.detach('songs');
```

### Syncing

`sync()` makes the pivot rows match the ids. It returns a `PivotSyncResult` with the ids of each change:

```dart
PivotSyncResult result = await artist.sync('songs', <int>[1, 2, 3]);
print(result.attached); // ids that got a new row
print(result.detached); // ids whose row was deleted
print(result.updated);  // ids whose pivot values changed
```

A null id or an unsaved model in the list makes `sync()` throw an `ArgumentError`, because it would delete every other link. A null list deletes every link.

`syncWithoutDetaching()` adds links and never deletes:

```dart
await artist.syncWithoutDetaching('songs', <int>[4]);
```

### Toggling

`toggle()` adds a row for each id that has none, and deletes the row of each id that has one:

```dart
await artist.toggle('songs', <int>[1, 2]);
```

### Updating pivot values

`updateExistingPivot()` sets pivot values on the rows of one id or a list of ids. It returns the number of changed rows:

```dart
await artist.updateExistingPivot('songs', 1,
    <String, dynamic>{'role': 'writer'});
```

With `withTimestamps`, `attach()`, `sync()` and `toggle()` set the pivot timestamps, and `updateExistingPivot()` sets `updated_at`.

## Filtering by the relation

`whereHas()` keeps the artists that have a song. It checks the pivot table for you:

```dart
List<Artist> artists = await Artist().whereHas('songs',
    (QueryBuilder<dynamic> q) {
  q.where('title', 'Yesterday');
}).get();

List<Artist> noSongs = await Artist().whereDoesntHave('songs').get();
```

See [Query by relations](../relation-queries.md).

## Changing the relation query

Give `onQuery` a static function of the model. It gets the query of the related model and returns it. Write `table.column`, because the query joins the pivot table:

```dart
@ManyToMany(Song, onQuery: onlyPublished)
List<Song> songs = <Song>[];

static QueryBuilder<Song> onlyPublished(Song q) {
  return q.where('song.status', 'published');
}
```

## Next steps

- [HasMany](has-many.md): a relation with no pivot table.
- [Schema](../../schema.md): make the pivot table.
- [Counting relations](../counting-relations.md): count the related rows.


---

# HasManyThrough

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/database/model/relationship/through/

# HasManyThrough

Use `HasManyThrough` to read rows that are two steps away, through a model in the middle. `HasOneThrough` is the same, but it gives one row.

For example, a country has many users, and a user has many posts. So a country has many posts through its users.

## Setup

### Tables

| Table | Columns |
|---|---|
| `country` | `id`, `name` |
| `user` | `id`, `country_id` |
| `post` | `id`, `user_id`, `title` |

### Defining the relation

Add the field to the first model. The `through` option is the model in the middle:

```dart title="lib/app/models/country/country.model.dart"
@DoxModel()
class Country extends CountryGenerator {
  @HasManyThrough(Post, through: User)
  List<Post> posts = <Post>[];

  @HasOneThrough(Post, through: User)
  Post? post;
}
```

Run `dart run build_runner build` after you add a relation.

### Options

Set the four keys when your columns have other names:

```dart
@HasManyThrough(
  Post,
  through: User,
  foreignKey: 'home_country_id', // on user, points to the country
  localKey: 'id', // on country
  throughForeignKey: 'author_id', // on post, points to the user
  throughLocalKey: 'id', // on user
)
List<Post> posts = <Post>[];
```

| Option | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `through` | required | The model in the middle. |
| `foreignKey` | `{this model}_id`, like `country_id` | The column in the middle table that points to this model. |
| `localKey` | the primary key of this model | The column in this table that `foreignKey` points to. |
| `throughForeignKey` | `{middle model}_id`, like `user_id` | The column in the far table that points to the middle model. |
| `throughLocalKey` | the primary key of the middle model | The column in the middle table that `throughForeignKey` points to. |
| `onQuery` | none | A static function that changes the query. |
| `eager` | `false` | Load the relation on every query. |

## Loading the relation

The relation is not loaded by default. Use the field name, `'posts'`, as the relation name. Soft deleted rows of the middle and the far table are left out.

### Preloading

`preload()` loads the relation for all models of a query, with one more query:

```dart
Country? country = await Country().preload('posts').find(1);
print(country?.posts.length);
```

The relation is then in `toJson()`, with the field name in snake_case as the key.

### Loading on a model you have

`$getRelation()` loads the relation into the field:

```dart
await country.$getRelation('posts');
```

### Querying the relation

`related()` gives a query for the far rows. It does not set the field:

```dart
List<Post> posts = await country
        .related<Post>('posts')
        ?.where('post.title', 'Hello')
        .get() ??
    <Post>[];
```

### Always loading the relation

Set `eager: true` to load the relation on every query of the model:

```dart
@HasManyThrough(Post, through: User, eager: true)
List<Post> posts = <Post>[];
```

## Saving related models

A through relation only reads. Save the middle and the far models with their own relations, like [HasMany](has-many.md#saving-related-models).

## Filtering by the relation

`whereHas()`, `whereDoesntHave()`, `has()` and `withCount()` work too. The query joins two tables, so write the table in front of the column:

```dart
List<Country> countries = await Country().whereHas('posts',
    (QueryBuilder<dynamic> q) {
  q.where('post.title', 'Hello');
}).get();
```

See [Query by relations](../relation-queries.md) and [Counting relations](../counting-relations.md).

## Changing the relation query

Give `onQuery` a static function of the model. Write the table in front of the column:

```dart
@HasOneThrough(Post, through: User, onQuery: newest)
Post? latestPost;

static Model<Post> newest(Post q) {
  q.orderBy('post.id');
  return q;
}
```

With `HasOneThrough`, the last row of the query wins. So this example keeps the post with the highest id.

## Next steps

- [HasMany](has-many.md): the direct relation.
- [ManyToMany](many-to-many.md): a relation with a pivot table.


---

# Polymorphic

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/database/model/relationship/polymorphic/

# Polymorphic

Use a polymorphic relation when one model can belong to more than one other model.

For example, a comment can belong to a photo or to a video. The `comment` table keeps the id in `commentable_id` and the type, like `photo`, in `commentable_type`. `commentable` is the **morph name**, and you pick it.

## Setup

### Tables

| Table | Columns |
|---|---|
| `photo` | `id`, `title` |
| `video` | `id`, `title` |
| `comment` | `id`, `body`, `commentable_id`, `commentable_type` |

`morphs()` adds both columns and an index:

```dart
await schema.create('comment', (Table table) {
  table.id();
  table.string('body');
  table.morphs('commentable');
});
```

### The morph map

The **morph map** gives each model the type name that goes in the type column. Set it in the `setup()` of a [provider](../../../digging-deeper/providers.md), so it runs in every isolate:

```dart
class MorphMapProvider extends DoxProvider {
  @override
  void setup() {
    Model.morphMap(<String, Model<dynamic> Function()>{
      'photo': Photo.new,
      'video': Video.new,
    });
  }
}
```

`@MorphTo` throws without the map. Without it, the other relations store the class name, which changes when you rename the class or build with `--obfuscate`. Do not change a type name later, because then the old rows do not match.

A queue worker or a CLI command that reads these relations must set the map too. `merge: false` removes the names you set before.

### Defining the relation

A photo has many comments. Use `@MorphMany`, with the morph name as the second argument:

```dart title="lib/app/models/photo/photo.model.dart"
@DoxModel()
class Photo extends PhotoGenerator {
  @MorphMany(Comment, 'commentable')
  List<Comment> comments = <Comment>[];
}
```

For one row, use `@MorphOne`. When there are many rows, it keeps the last row of the query:

```dart
@MorphOne(Image, 'imageable')
Image? cover;
```

A comment belongs to a photo or a video. Use `@MorphTo` on a `Model<dynamic>?` field. The id and type columns must be `@Column` fields:

```dart title="lib/app/models/comment/comment.model.dart"
@DoxModel()
class Comment extends CommentGenerator {
  @Column()
  int? commentableId;

  @Column()
  String? commentableType;

  @MorphTo()
  Model<dynamic>? commentable;
}
```

Run `dart run build_runner build` after you add a relation.

### Options

The examples are for `@MorphMany(Comment, 'commentable')` in the `Photo` model. `@MorphOne` has the same options:

| Option | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `name` (2nd argument) | required | The morph name, like `commentable`. |
| `typeColumn` | `{name}_type` | The type column in `comment`. |
| `idColumn` | `{name}_id` | The id column in `comment`. |
| `localKey` | the primary key of this model | The column in `photo` that `idColumn` points to. |
| `onQuery` | none | A static function that changes the query. |
| `eager` | `false` | Load the relation on every query. |

The options of `@MorphTo`:

| Option | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | the field name in snake_case | The morph name. |
| `typeColumn` | `{name}_type` | The type column in this table. |
| `idColumn` | `{name}_id` | The id column in this table. |
| `ownerKey` | the primary key of the related model | The column in the related table that `idColumn` points to. |
| `onQuery` | none | A static function that changes the query of each type. |
| `eager` | `false` | Load the relation on every query. |

## Loading the relation

The relation is not loaded by default. Use the field name, like `'comments'` or `'commentable'`, as the relation name.

### Preloading

`preload()` loads the relation for all models of a query. A `@MorphTo` runs one query for each type:

```dart
List<Comment> comments = await Comment().preload('commentable').get();
for (Comment c in comments) {
  if (c.commentable is Photo) print((c.commentable as Photo).title);
}
```

A type that is not in the morph map throws a `StateError`. No type, or an empty type, gives null.

### Loading on a model you have

`$getRelation()` loads the relation into the field:

```dart
await photo.$getRelation('comments');
```

### Querying the relation

`related()` gives a query for the related rows. It does not set the field:

```dart
List<Comment> recent = await photo
        .related<Comment>('comments')
        ?.orderBy('id', 'desc')
        .get() ??
    <Comment>[];
```

### Always loading the relation

Set `eager: true` to load the relation on every query of the model:

```dart
@MorphMany(Comment, 'commentable', eager: true)
List<Comment> comments = <Comment>[];
```

## Saving related models

`createRelated()`, `saveRelated()` and `saveManyRelated()` work with `@MorphMany` and `@MorphOne`. They set the id and the type column:

```dart
await photo.createRelated<Comment>('comments',
    <String, dynamic>{'body': 'Nice'});
```

A `@MorphTo` has no `associate()`. Set the two columns yourself, and get the type with `Model.morphTypeOf()`:

```dart
Comment comment = Comment()
  ..body = 'Nice'
  ..commentableId = photo.id
  ..commentableType = Model.morphTypeOf(photo);
await comment.save();
```

`Model.morphModel('video')` gives a new model of a type name.

## Filtering by the relation

`whereHas()`, `whereDoesntHave()` and `withCount()` work with `@MorphMany` and `@MorphOne`. A `@MorphTo` throws an `UnsupportedError`:

```dart
List<Photo> photos = await Photo().whereHas('comments').get();
List<Video> videos = await Video().withCount('comments').get();
```

See [Query by relations](../relation-queries.md).

## Changing the relation query

Give `onQuery` a static function of the model. For `@MorphTo`, it runs for the query of each type, so it takes and returns `Model<dynamic>`:

```dart
@MorphTo(onQuery: notHidden)
Model<dynamic>? commentable;

static Model<dynamic> notHidden(Model<dynamic> q) {
  q.whereNull('hidden_at');
  return q;
}
```

## Next steps

- [HasMany](has-many.md): a relation to one model.
- [Providers](../../../digging-deeper/providers.md): set the morph map.
