# Signed URLs

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/security/signed-urls/

# Signed URLs

A signed URL has a `signature` in its query, so nobody can change the URL without your `APP_KEY`.

Use it for links in emails, like "unsubscribe" or "download your file", when the user is not logged in.

## Creating signed URLs

Give the route a name and add the `ValidateSignature` middleware:

```dart title="lib/routes/web.dart"
Route.get('/unsubscribe/{user}', <dynamic>[
  const ValidateSignature(),
  (UserController c) => c.unsubscribe,
]).name('unsubscribe');
```

Then make the URL with `Route.signedUrl`:

```dart
String url = Route.signedUrl(
  'unsubscribe',
  params: <String, Object>{'user': 5},
);
// https://example.com/unsubscribe/5?signature=3f9a...
```

A URL with no signature, a wrong signature, or a changed path or query gets 403. URLs made with a key in `AppConfig.previousKeys` still work.

### Adding a query

Give `query` to add query params. They are signed too. `signature` is a reserved name:

```dart
String url = Route.signedUrl(
  'unsubscribe',
  params: <String, Object>{'user': 5},
  query: <String, Object>{'list': 'news'},
);
```

### URLs that expire

Give `expires` to make a link that works only for a time. After that time it gets 403:

```dart
String url = Route.signedUrl(
  'download',
  params: <String, Object>{'file': 12},
  expires: Duration(hours: 1),
);
```

## Relative URLs

By default Dox puts `APP_URL` in front, and signs the scheme and host too. Give `baseUrl` to use another one. The scheme, host and port of the request must match it.

To sign only the path and the query, use `absolute: false`, and check it with `ValidateSignature(absolute: false)`:

```dart
Route.get('/files/{id}', <dynamic>[
  const ValidateSignature(absolute: false),
  (FileController c) => c.show,
]).name('files.show');

String url = Route.signedUrl(
  'files.show',
  params: <String, Object>{'id': 3},
  absolute: false,
);
// /files/3?signature=...
```

Behind a proxy that ends TLS, add the proxy to `AppConfig.trustedProxies`, so Dox sees the https scheme.

## Checking in a controller

To answer a bad link in your own way, use `ValidateSignature.hasValidSignature(req)`:

```dart
if (!ValidateSignature.hasValidSignature(req)) {
  return redirect('/link-expired');
}
```

For a relative URL, give `absolute: false`.

## Next steps

- [File Storage](../digging-deeper/file-storage.md): signed URLs for files.
- [Encryption](encryption.md): the app key that signs the URL.

# Validation

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/packages/validation/

# Validation

`dox_validation` checks input and gives you typed Dart objects.

It has two parts. A **DTO** is a class with `@Dto()` and rule annotations, and a generator writes its checks. Use it for almost all input, see [DTOs](../the-basic/dto.md). A **fluent schema** like `v.object(...)` is for input whose shape you know only at runtime. Both give all errors at once, and both give a JSON Schema for [OpenAPI](openapi.md).

## Setup

`dox_core` exports `dox_validation`, so you install nothing. Import `package:dox_core/dox_core.dart`.

1. Make a DTO with `dox make:dto CreateUser`. It writes `lib/app/dtos/create_user/create_user.dto.dart`.
2. Run the generator: `dox build_runner:build`.
3. Give the list of DTOs to the app:

    ```dart title="lib/config/app.dart"
    import 'package:my_app/generated/dtos.g.dart';

    AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
      // ...
      dtos: dtos, // from lib/generated/dtos.g.dart
    );
    ```

Then ask for the DTO in a controller. Dox checks the body before the method runs, and bad input gets 422 with the errors:

```dart title="lib/app/http/controllers/user.controller.dart"
class UserController {
  Future<Map<String, dynamic>> store(CreateUser body) async {
    // body is already checked and typed
    return <String, dynamic>{'name': body.name};
  }
}
```

The full guide is [Validation](../the-basic/validation.md), and every rule is in the [rules reference](../the-basic/validation-rules.md). This page is about the package.

## Defining a DTO

Give each field its rules as annotations:

```dart
import 'package:dox_validation/dox_validation.dart';

part 'create_user.dto.g.dart';

@Dto()
class CreateUser {
  @Length(min: 3, max: 50)
  @Trim()
  final String name;

  @Email()
  final String email;

  const CreateUser({required this.name, required this.email});

  static const DtoSchema<CreateUser> schema = $CreateUserDto;
}
```

The generator writes a `DtoSchema<CreateUser>` named `$CreateUserDto`, with the checks, the converter and the JSON Schema. The `schema` line lets you use it as `CreateUser.schema`. The generator also writes `lib/generated/dtos.g.dart`, with the list `dtos` of every DTO in `lib/`.

## Validating a map

A `DtoSchema` is also a normal `Schema`. You can use it inside `v.object(...)` and `v.list(...)`, and with OpenAPI.

### Validating and throwing

`validateMap` runs all checks and gives the object. Bad input throws a `ValidationException` with the errors:

```dart
CreateUser user = await CreateUser.schema.validateMap(input);
```

In a controller, this answers 422. `dox_core` has its own `ValidationException` and does not export the one of `dox_validation`.

### Validating without throwing

`safeValidateMap` gives a `ParseResult`, and never throws for bad input:

```dart
ParseResult<CreateUser> result =
    await CreateUser.schema.safeValidateMap(input);
if (!result.success) {
  print(result.errors); // {'email': 'The email is not a valid email'}
}
```

A `ParseResult` has:

- `success`: true when there are no errors.
- `value`: the result, or null when `success` is false.
- `errors`: the first message for each field, like `{'user.email': '...'}`.
- `fieldErrors`: all messages for each field.
- `issues`: the full list of `ValidationIssue` objects, with code and path.

Both methods take these options:

- `source: Source.query` reads the map like a query string, so text is converted to the field type.
- `params` are the path params, for `@Unique(ignoreParam: ...)`.
- `messages` and `locale` change the error text for this call. See [Messages](#messages).

`parse`, `safeParse`, `parseAsync` and `safeParseAsync` also work on a `DtoSchema`. `parse` throws a `StateError` when the DTO has async rules.

### Building an object with no checks

`fromMap` builds the object with no checks. It reads the keys, converts JSON types and fills in defaults. Use it only for data you trust, because a wrong type throws a `TypeError`:

```dart
CreateUser user = CreateUser.schema.fromMap(trustedData);
```

### Turning an object back into a map

`toMap` gives the object as a map with the input keys. A `DateTime` becomes an ISO 8601 string, and an enum becomes its name:

```dart
Map<String, dynamic> data = CreateUser.schema.toMap(user);
```

### Getting the JSON Schema

`toJsonSchema` gives the JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) of the DTO:

```dart
CreateUser.schema.toJsonSchema();
```

For a `CreateUser` with `age` and `role` fields, you get:

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "CreateUser",
  "properties": {
    "name": { "type": "string", "minLength": 3, "maxLength": 50 },
    "email": { "type": "string", "format": "email" },
    "age": { "type": ["integer", "null"], "minimum": 18 },
    "role": { "type": "string", "enum": ["admin", "user"], "default": "user" }
  },
  "required": ["name", "email"]
}
```

A `///` doc comment on a field becomes its `description`. `@Describe('...')` also sets it, and wins over the comment. A nested DTO goes in `$defs` with a `$ref`, and `@Dto(strict: true)` adds `"additionalProperties": false`.

## Fluent schemas (for dynamic input)

When you know the fields only at runtime, use a fluent schema. The output is a map, not a class:

```dart
final ObjectSchema createUser = v.object(<String, Schema<Object?>>{
  'name': v.string().trim().min(3).max(50),
  'email': v.string().email(),
  'age': v.coerce.int().min(18).optional(),
  'role': v.enumOf<String>(<String>['admin', 'user']).defaultTo('user'),
  'tags': v.list(v.string()).max(5),
  'address': Address.schema, // a DTO inside a fluent schema
});
```

`parse` gives the data, and throws a `ValidationException` for bad input. `safeParse` gives a `ParseResult`:

```dart
Map<String, dynamic> data = createUser.parse(input);

ParseResult<Map<String, dynamic>> result = createUser.safeParse(input);
```

In a controller, use `req.validateSchema`:

```dart
Map<String, dynamic> data = await req.validateSchema(createUser);
```

Fluent schemas do not use the DTO defaults:

- A key is required, unless you add `optional()`.
- An empty string is a value, not "missing".
- Text is not converted to numbers or booleans, unless you use `v.coerce`.

### Available schemas

| Schema | Checks |
| --- | --- |
| `v.string()` | `min`, `max`, `length`, `nonEmpty`, `email`, `url`, `uuid`, `ulid`, `ip`, `datetime`, `regex`, `startsWith`, `endsWith`, `includes`, `alpha`, `alphaDash`, `alphaNumeric`, `json`, `digits`, `digitsBetween`, `dateFormat`, `hexColor`, `password`, `exists`, `unique`, `trim`, `toLowerCase`, `toUpperCase` |
| `v.int()`, `v.num()` | `min`, `max`, `between`, `gt`, `lt`, `positive`, `nonNegative`, `multipleOf`, `gtField`, `gteField`, `ltField`, `lteField`, `exists`, `unique` |
| `v.bool()` | |
| `v.date()` | `DateTime` only. `min`, `max` |
| `v.enumOf([...])`, `v.literal(x)` | |
| `v.list(item)` | `min`, `max`, `nonEmpty` |
| `v.object({...})` | `strict`, `passthrough`, `strip`, `pick`, `omit`, `extend`, `partial` |
| `v.map(values, keys: ...)` | any keys |
| `v.union([...])` | the first match wins |
| `v.any()`, `v.file()` | `file()` has `maxSize`, `minSize`, `mimes`, `mimeTypes`, `dimensions`, `image` and `extensions` |

`gtField`, `gteField`, `ltField` and `lteField` fail when the other key is missing.

### Optional and nullable values

Every schema has these methods:

- `optional()`: the key can be missing. Null is still an error.
- `nullable()`: the value can be null, but the key must be there.
- `nullish()`: both.
- `defaultTo(x)`: the value when the key is missing.

```dart
v.string().optional();
v.int().defaultTo(0);
```

Every schema also has `transform`, `refine`, `superRefine`, `use(rule)`, `same(other)`, `different(other)`, `confirmed()`, `accepted()`, `declined()`, and `describe(text)` and `example(x)` for the JSON Schema.

### Converting text

Query strings and form data are always text. `v.coerce` turns the text into the type first:

```dart
v.coerce.int().parse('42');       // 42
v.coerce.num().parse('4.5');      // 4.5
v.coerce.bool().parse('on');      // true (true/1/yes/on, false/0/no/off)
v.coerce.date().parse('2024-01-31');
v.coerce.string().parse(5);       // '5'
```

### Checking across fields

For a rule on two fields, use `refine` on the object. `path` sets the field that gets the error:

```dart
final ObjectSchema signUp = v.object(<String, Schema<Object?>>{
  'password': v.string().min(8),
  'confirm': v.string(),
}).refine((Map<String, dynamic> data) {
  return data['password'] == data['confirm'];
}, message: 'Passwords do not match', path: <Object>['confirm']);
```

### More rules

Fluent schemas have the same rules as the DTO annotations, with the same codes and messages:

```dart
final ObjectSchema signUp = v.object(<String, Schema<Object?>>{
  // needs password_confirmation with the same value
  'password': v.string()
      .password(min: 8, mixedCase: true, numbers: true)
      .confirmed(),
  'email': v.string().email().unique('users', column: 'email'),
  'team_id': v.int().exists('teams'),
  'type': v.enumOf<String>(<String>['person', 'company']),
  'company': v.string().optional().requiredIf('type', 'company'),
  'phone': v.string().digitsBetween(8, 12).optional(),
  'country_code': v.string().optional().requiredWith(<String>['phone']),
  'birthday': v.string().dateFormat('Y-m-d').optional(),
  'settings': v.string().json().optional(),
  'age': v.int().between(18, 120).optional(),
});

Map<String, dynamic> data = await signUp.parseAsync(input);
```

There are more presence and compare rules:

```dart
final ObjectSchema order = v.object(<String, Schema<Object?>>{
  'type': v.string(),
  'email': v.string().optional().requiredWithout(<String>['phone']),
  'phone': v.string().optional(),
  'fax': v.string().optional()
      .requiredWithoutAll(<String>['email', 'phone']),
  'company': v.string().optional().requiredUnless('type', 'person'),
  'nick': v.string().optional().filled(),
  'note': v.string().optional().present().nullable(),
  'coupon': v.string().optional().prohibitedIf('type', 'guest'),
  'debug': v.any().optional().prohibited(),
  'terms': v.coerce.bool().accepted(),
  'new_password': v.string().different('old_password'),
  'id': v.string().ulid(),
  'min_price': v.int(),
  'max_price': v.int().gtField('min_price'),
});
```

Each rule is in the [rules reference](../the-basic/validation-rules.md#present-or-missing). Keep these points in mind:

- The `required...`, `prohibited...`, `filled` and `present` rules come after `optional()` (or `nullish()`).
- `exists` and `unique` ask the database, so they are async. Use `parseAsync()` or `safeParseAsync()`.
- `exists(table, column: 'id')`: the column default is `id`. Use `v.int().exists('teams')` for a number id, so text like `abc` fails before a query.
- `unique(table, column: 'email', ignore: id)`: `column` is required. `ignore` skips the row with this id, for updates.
- A table or column name can have letters, digits, `_` and `$`, with `.` between parts. Other names throw an `ArgumentError`.
- The database decides if two values match. On MySQL, `TAKEN@dox.dev` is taken when `taken@dox.dev` is there.
- `accepted()` on `v.bool()` takes only true. For form words like `yes` and `on`, use `v.coerce.bool().accepted()`.

### Stop at the first error

A fluent schema gives one error for each failed rule of a value. Add `.bail()` to get only the first error. A DTO always does this:

```dart
v.string().min(8).email().bail().safeParse('ab');
// one error: min_length. Without bail(): min_length and email.
```

Put `.bail()` before `.optional()`, `.nullable()` or `.transform()`, because rules after them belong to the wrapper. Async rules after a failed rule do not run.

### Skip a field

`excludeIf(other, value)` and `excludeUnless(other, value)` skip a field of `v.object()`. When they match, the field is not checked and its key is not in the output:

```dart
final ObjectSchema account = v.object(<String, Schema<Object?>>{
  'type': v.string(),
  'vat_number': v.string().min(5).excludeIf('type', 'person'),
  'company': v.string().excludeUnless('type', 'company'),
});

account.parse(<String, dynamic>{'type': 'person', 'vat_number': 'x'});
// {type: person}
```

`other` must be a key of the same object. A skipped field never gets its default. When `other` is missing, `excludeIf` does not skip, and `excludeUnless` skips.

### Async checks

For a check that needs the database, use `refineAsync`, or `superRefineAsync` in place of `superRefine`. Then call `parseAsync()` or `safeParseAsync()`, because `parse()` throws a `StateError`:

```dart
v.string().refineAsync(isFreeName, message: 'The name is taken');
```

### Custom rules

A `Rule<T>` class works as an annotation on a DTO, and with `use()` in a fluent schema:

```dart
v.string().min(3).use(const Slug());
```

See [Custom rules](../the-basic/validation.md#custom-rules) to write one.

### Standard Schema

Every schema and every `DtoSchema` implements the [Standard Schema](https://standardschema.dev) interface. Code that only validates can take any `StandardSchema` and call `validate`:

```dart
StandardResult<Object?> result = await schema.validate(input);
```

## Messages

Each error has a code, like `required` or `min_length`. A message can use placeholders: `{field}`, `{value}`, and rule values like `{min}` and `{max}`.

To change messages for the whole app, set `MessageResolver.global`. In a Dox app, use `AppConfig(validationMessages: ...)`:

```dart
MessageResolver.global = MessageResolver(messages: <String, String>{
  'required': 'Please fill in {field}',
});
```

To add messages to a resolver later, use `setMessages`:

```dart
MessageResolver.global.setMessages(<String, String>{
  'email.required': 'We need your email',
});
```

To change messages for one call, give `messages`. It replaces the global resolver for that call, and falls back to the built-in text:

```dart
createUser.safeParse(input,
    messages: MessageResolver(messages: <String, String>{
      'email.required': 'We need your email',
    }));
```

To show a name for `{field}` in place of the key, give `attributes`, or call `setAttributes`:

```dart
MessageResolver.global = MessageResolver(
  attributes: <String, String>{'first_name': 'first name'},
);
// The first name is required
```

A DTO can give its own names with `@Dto(attributes:)`. For other languages, extend `MessageResolver` and override `resolve()`. See [Messages](../the-basic/validation.md#messages).

## Opt-in flags

`ValidationFlags` turns on behavior that is off by default. Set it in `Validator.flags`:

```dart
// turn on one flag
Validator.flags = const ValidationFlags(unicodeAlpha: true);

// turn on every flag
Validator.flags = const ValidationFlags.all();
```

Each isolate has its own `Validator.flags`. In a Dox app, set it in the `setup()` of a provider, which runs in every isolate:

```dart
class ValidationProvider extends DoxProvider {
  @override
  void setup() {
    Validator.flags = const ValidationFlags.all();
  }
}
```

| Flag | What it does when on |
| --- | --- |
| `emptyStringsToNull` | Fluent schemas change each empty string to null before the check, also in nested maps and lists. For a DTO, use `@Dto(emptyStringsToNull: true)`. |
| `unicodeAlpha` | `alpha`, `alphaNumeric` and `alphaDash` accept Unicode letters, like `José`. |
| `shortInMessage` | The default `in` message is `The selected {field} is invalid`, with no list of allowed values. |
| `dtoAllErrors` | A DTO runs the rules of every field with the right type, also when another field is missing or wrong. |
| `dtoRejectEmptyList` | A required `List` field of a DTO fails `required` on `[]`. |
| `dtoMaybeRejectsEmpty` | A `Maybe<T>` field of a DTO fails `required` when the key has an empty value, like `""`. |
| `laravelMessageKeys` | A custom message key can also use the short rule name, like `name.min` for the `min_length` error. See the [list of names](../the-basic/validation.md#short-rule-names-in-message-keys). |

After you turn on a `dto...` flag, run `dart run build_runner build` one time.

## Without Dox

`dox_validation` works in any Dart program. Add the package, and the builder for DTOs:

```bash
dart pub add dox_validation
dart pub add dev:dox_builder dev:build_runner
```

```dart
import 'package:dox_validation/dox_validation.dart';
```

Run the DTO generator with `dart run build_runner build`.

### Database rules

`exists` and `unique` ask a `PresenceVerifier`. In a Dox app, `dox_orm` sets one when the database starts. `@Unique` and `@Exists` for DTOs are in `dox_orm`.

With another database layer, write your own. Each isolate has its own value, so set it in code that runs in every isolate:

```dart
class MyVerifier extends PresenceVerifier {
  @override
  Future<Set<String>> found(
    String table,
    String column,
    List<Object?> values, {
    String? exceptColumn,
    Object? exceptValue,
    String? connection,
  }) async {
    // Return the values that are in the column, as text.
    // Bind the values as query parameters, never put them into the SQL.
    return <String>{};
  }
}

class VerifierProvider extends DoxProvider {
  @override
  void setup() {
    PresenceVerifier.instance = MyVerifier();
  }
}
```

- [Validation rules](../the-basic/validation-rules.md): every rule.

# OpenAPI

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/packages/openapi/

# OpenAPI

Dox makes OpenAPI 3.1 docs for your API from your routes, controllers and request classes.

You get three URLs: `/docs`, a [Scalar](https://github.com/scalar/scalar) page with every route and "Try it" buttons, `/openapi.json` and `/openapi.yaml`. The docs come from the routes, the `@Dto` request classes and the controller methods, so you write little by hand.

## Setup

A new app already serves `/docs` in development, but each route shows only its path and method. Do these steps to get the full docs:

1. Write the config, with the generated `openApiRegistry`:

    ```dart title="lib/config/openapi.dart"
    import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
    import 'package:my_app/generated/openapi.g.dart';

    OpenApiConfig openApi = OpenApiConfig(
      info: Info(title: 'Blog API', version: '1.0.0'),
      registry: openApiRegistry,
    );
    ```

    The import shows an error until the builder runs in step 3.

2. Add it to `AppConfig`:

    ```dart title="lib/config/app.dart"
    import 'package:my_app/config/openapi.dart';

    AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
      openApi: openApi,
      // ...
    );
    ```

3. Run the builder. It writes `lib/generated/openapi.g.dart`. Run it again after you change routes, controllers, request classes or models, or use `dox build_runner:watch`:

    ```bash
    dart run build_runner build      # or: dox build_runner:build
    ```

4. Start the app with `APP_ENV=development` in `.env`, and open `http://localhost:3000/docs`.

The docs are on only when `APP_ENV` is `development` or `local`. With no `APP_ENV`, the app is in production, and `/docs` gives 404.

### Configuration

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | none | true or false turns the docs on or off. With none, they are on only when `APP_ENV` is `development` or `local` |
| `info` | `Info(title: 'Dox API', version: '1.0.0')` | title and version of the API |
| `servers` | `[]` | base URLs, like `[Server('https://api.my.app')]` |
| `registry` | empty | `openApiRegistry` from `lib/generated/openapi.g.dart` |
| `securitySchemes`, `securityByMiddleware` | `{}` | see [Login schemes](#login-schemes) |
| `ui` | `DocsUi.scalar` | the docs page: `DocsUi.scalar` or `DocsUi.swagger` |
| `scalar` | `ScalarOptions()` | see [Changing the docs page](#changing-the-docs-page) |
| `pageTitle` | `info.title` | title of the `/docs` page |
| `include` | `[]` (all routes) | only these paths go in the docs, like `['/api/*']` |
| `exclude` | `[]` | these paths are left out, like `['/api/internal/*']` |

`openApi.isEnabled` tells you if the live docs are on.

## Describe a route

A normal controller already gets docs, see [What Dox fills in for you](#what-dox-fills-in-for-you). For better text, put annotations from `dox_core` on the controller method. Each annotation also has a lower case name, like `@summary('Log in')`, except `@Response`.

### Adding a summary and tags

`@Summary` is the short title, `@Description` is the longer text, and `@Tags` puts the route in a group. `@Tags` also works on the class:

```dart
class BlogController {
  @Summary('Get one blog')
  @Description('Deleted blogs are not found.')
  @Tags(<String>['Blogs'])
  Future<Blog?> show(DoxRequest req, String id) async {
    return Blog().find(id);
  }
}
```

For `GET /blogs/{id}` with `AuthMiddleware` on the route, you get:

```yaml
get:
  tags: [Blogs]
  summary: Get one blog
  description: Deleted blogs are not found.
  operationId: BlogController.show
  parameters:
    - {name: id, in: path, required: true, schema: {type: string}}
  responses:
    "200":
      content:
        application/json:
          schema: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/Blog"}
    "401": {description: Not logged in}
    "404": {description: Not found}
    "500": {description: Server error}
  security:
    - bearerAuth: []
```

For a class that is not in a `Route.get(...)` call, set its tag with `@DoxController(tag: 'Users')`.

### Using doc comments

A `///` comment on a method also sets the summary (the first line) and the description (the rest). An annotation wins over the comment:

```dart
/// Get one blog
///
/// Deleted blogs are not found.
Future<Blog?> show(DoxRequest req, String id) async {
  return Blog().find(id);
}
```

### Adding responses

`@Response` describes one answer. Add one for each status code:

```dart
@Summary('Log in')
@Request(LoginUser)
@Response(200, LoginResult)
@Response(401, null, description: 'Wrong email or password')
Future<dynamic> login(DoxRequest req) async { ... }
```

The type can be a model, `List<User>`, a `@Dto`, a `Serializer` or a basic type like `String`. With a 2xx `@Response`, the return type of the method is not used.

### Hiding a route

`@ApiIgnore()` leaves a method, or a full class, out of the docs. To leave out routes by path, use `include` and `exclude` in the [config](#configuration):

```dart
@ApiIgnore()
Future<void> internal(DoxRequest req) async { ... }
```

### Marking a route as deprecated

Use `@ApiDeprecated()` or the Dart `@Deprecated`:

```dart
@ApiDeprecated()
Future<List<Blog>> oldIndex() async { ... }
```

## Describing the request

The builder finds the request class of a method in this order:

1. `@Body(T)`, `@Query(T)` or `@Request(T)` on the method.
2. An argument whose type is a `@Dto` class, like `store(CreateBlog body)`.
3. A `req.validate<T>()` call in the method, where `T` is a `@Dto` class.

For POST, PUT and PATCH, the request is the JSON body. For other methods, each field is a query param. `@Body`, `@Query` and `@Dto(source: Source.query)` set the place. The route `body` option wins over all of them.

```dart
@Dto()
class CreateBlog {
  @Length(min: 3, max: 200)
  final String title;

  /// Text of the blog.
  final String? description;   // nullable: optional

  final int views;             // default: optional, `default: 0`

  final Status status;         // enum: only `draft` or `published`

  final List<Tag> tags;        // a list of another @Dto class

  const CreateBlog({required this.title, this.description, this.views = 0,
      required this.status, required this.tags});
}
```

The keys are the keys the DTO reads: snake_case, or `@Name('key')`. `@Dto(keyCase: KeyCase.field)` keeps the field names. Each rule adds its JSON Schema keys, see the [rules reference](../the-basic/validation-rules.md).

## Describing the response

The return type of the method gives the 200 answer. `Future<T>` counts as `T`.

| Return type | Schema |
| --- | --- |
| a model (`@DoxModel`) | `$ref` to the model. Keys in `hidden` are left out |
| `List<Model>` | an array of the model |
| a `@Dto` class | `$ref` to the class |
| a `Serializer<Model>` | the map that `convert()` returns, else the model |
| `Pagination` | `total`, `per_page`, `last_page`, `current_page`, `data` |
| `String`, `int`, `bool`, `Map`, `List` | the basic JSON type |
| `dynamic` | the types of the `return` values. A map literal gives its keys |
| `DoxResponse`, `void` | no schema |

A model schema has the primary key, the `@Column` fields, `created_at`, `updated_at`, the relations (only when they are loaded) and the `@Computed` getters. It goes in `components/schemas`:

```yaml
Blog:
  type: object
  properties:
    id: {type: integer}
    title: {type: [string, "null"]}
    user: {anyOf: [{$ref: "#/components/schemas/User"}, {type: "null"}]}
    created_at: {type: [string, "null"], format: date-time}
```

## Login schemes

"Try it" must know how a route is protected to send a token. Put `@Security` on a middleware class, and every route with this middleware gets the scheme:

```dart
/// `Authorization: Bearer <api key>`. Not a JWT.
@Security.bearer(format: 'API key')
class ApiKeyAuthMiddleware implements IDoxMiddleware { ... }
```

`@Security.bearer()` gives `type: http, scheme: bearer`, and `format` becomes `bearerFormat`. For a key in a header, use `@Security.apiKey`. The default header is `X-API-Key`:

```dart
@Security.apiKey(header: 'X-API-Key')
class HeaderKeyMiddleware implements IDoxMiddleware { ... }
```

Run `dart run build_runner build` after you add it. The scheme name is the class name without `Middleware`, with a small first letter: `ApiKeyAuthMiddleware` gives `apiKeyAuth`. Give `scheme: 'myName'` for another name.

A middleware with no `@Security` whose class name ends with `AuthMiddleware` gets `bearerAuth`.

### Setting schemes in the config

For a key in the query or a cookie, set the scheme in the config. The config wins over `@Security`:

```dart
OpenApiConfig(
  registry: openApiRegistry,
  securitySchemes: <String, SecurityScheme>{
    'apiKey': SecurityScheme.apiKey(name: 'key', location: 'query'),
  },
  securityByMiddleware: <String, List<Map<String, List<String>>>>{
    'ApiKeyMiddleware': <Map<String, List<String>>>[
      <String, List<String>>{'apiKey': <String>[]},
    ],
  },
);
```

`SecurityScheme.bearer(bearerFormat: 'JWT')` makes a bearer scheme, and `SecurityScheme.raw(map)` takes a raw OpenAPI map.

## What Dox fills in for you

A controller with no annotations gets docs. Annotations only change the result.

| Part of the docs | Where it comes from |
| --- | --- |
| path, method | the route table |
| path param types | the controller arguments after the first one, in order. `int id` gives `integer` |
| tags | the class name without `Controller` (`BlogController` gives `Blog`) |
| operationId | `Class.method`, like `BlogController.show` |
| summary, description | the annotations, else the `///` comment |
| request | see [Describing the request](#describing-the-request) |
| 200 answer | the return type, see [Describing the response](#describing-the-response) |
| 401 and a login scheme | see [Login schemes](#login-schemes) |
| 401 and 403 | the `Can` middleware, or a `req.authorize(...)` call in the method |
| 403 | the `GuestMiddleware` or `ValidateSignature` middleware, or a `Gate.authorize(...)` call in the method |
| 404 | the path has a `{param}` |
| 422 | the route has a request class, or the method calls `req.validate<T>()` or `req.validateSchema(...)` |
| 500 | every route |

- A `@Response` with the same status wins over an automatic answer. `GuestMiddleware(redirectTo: ...)` shows 403, but the app sends a redirect, so add a `@Response(403, ...)`.
- An optional param gives two paths: `/blog/{id?}` gives `/blog/{id}` and `/blog`. The short path gets no 404.
- Dox matches a route to its docs by method name, HTTP method and the end of the path. When two controllers have a method with the same name, name the class in the route, like `(LinkController c) => c.index`.

## Changing the docs page

Change the look of the Scalar page with `scalar`:

```dart
OpenApiConfig(
  registry: openApiRegistry,
  pageTitle: 'Blog API docs',
  scalar: ScalarOptions(theme: ScalarTheme.purple, darkMode: true),
);
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `theme` | `ScalarTheme.default_` | color theme, like `moon`, `purple`, `deepSpace`, `saturn`, `kepler` or `mars` |
| `darkMode` | false | start in dark mode |
| `showDownloadButton` | true | show the button that downloads the document |
| `proxyUrl` | none | send "Try it" requests through this proxy. Without it, requests go from the browser to your API |

To use Swagger UI, set `ui`:

```dart
OpenApiConfig(registry: openApiRegistry, ui: DocsUi.swagger);
```

## Turn the docs on in production

Set `enabled: true` to show the docs in production. `enabled: false` turns them off everywhere:

```dart title="lib/config/openapi.dart"
OpenApiConfig openApi = OpenApiConfig(
  enabled: true,
  info: Info(title: 'Blog API', version: '1.0.0'),
  registry: openApiRegistry,
);
```

!!! warning
    `/docs` has no login, so anyone can see every route of your API. Do this only for a public API.

## Write the files

To get the document as files, for example for a client generator, run `dox openapi:generate`:

```bash
dox openapi:generate              # storage/openapi/openapi.json and .yaml
dox openapi:generate docs/api     # another folder
```

It runs `bin/openapi.dart` of your app. A new app does not have this file, so make it. `writeOpenApi` runs your providers and registers the routes:

```dart title="bin/openapi.dart"
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/app.dart';

Future<void> main(List<String> args) async {
  Dox().initialize(appConfig);
  await Dox().writeOpenApi(args.isEmpty ? 'storage/openapi' : args.first);
  exit(0);
}
```

## Production setup

You can also make the document at build time, put the files in the image, and serve them. The URLs stay the same. You need `lib/config/openapi.dart` (see [Setup](#setup)) and `bin/openapi.dart` (see [Write the files](#write-the-files)).

1. Make both files, if you do not have them.

2. Add a controller that serves the files. If your `pubspec.yaml` has no `dox_openapi`, run `dart pub add dox_openapi`:

    ```dart title="lib/app/http/controllers/docs.controller.dart"
    import 'dart:io';

    import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
    import 'package:dox_openapi/dox_openapi.dart'
        show OpenApiConstants, OpenApiServer;
    import 'package:my_app/config/openapi.dart';

    @Inject()
    class DocsController {
      /// The same Scalar page as the live docs. It loads `/openapi.json`.
      final String _page = OpenApiServer(
        OpenApi(info: openApi.info),
        pageTitle: openApi.pageTitle,
        ui: openApi.ui,
        scalar: openApi.scalar,
      ).docsPage().body;

      DoxResponse page() {
        return response(_page).contentType(
            ContentType.parse(OpenApiConstants.htmlContentType));
      }

      DoxResponse json() {
        return _file('openapi.json', OpenApiConstants.jsonContentType);
      }

      DoxResponse yaml() {
        return _file('openapi.yaml', OpenApiConstants.yamlContentType);
      }

      DoxResponse _file(String name, String contentType) {
        File file = File('docs/openapi/$name');
        if (!file.existsSync()) throw NotFoundHttpException();
        return response(file.readAsStringSync())
            .contentType(ContentType.parse(contentType));
      }
    }
    ```

3. Add the routes only when the live docs are off, so they do not clash in development. Import `openApi` and the controller in this file:

    ```dart title="lib/routes/web.dart"
    @override
    void register() {
      if (!openApi.isEnabled) {
        Route.get('/docs', (DocsController c) => c.page);
        Route.get('/openapi.json', (DocsController c) => c.json);
        Route.get('/openapi.yaml', (DocsController c) => c.yaml);
      }
      // ...
    }
    ```

4. Make the files in the Docker build. In the build stage, right after `RUN /root/.pub-cache/bin/dox build`, add:

    ```dockerfile title="Dockerfile"
    RUN APP_KEY=only-for-the-build-not-a-key \
        /root/.pub-cache/bin/dox openapi:generate docs/openapi
    ```

    Then, in the `RUN` step that lays out `/out`, add `/out/app/docs` to `mkdir -p` and copy the files after the `cp -r build/bundle/. /out/app/` line:

    ```dockerfile title="Dockerfile"
    RUN mkdir -p /out/app/storage /out/app/docs /out/tmp \
      && chmod 1777 /out/tmp \
      && cp -r build/bundle/. /out/app/ \
      && cp -r docs/openapi /out/app/docs/openapi \
      # ... the lines that follow stay as they are
    ```

    `bin/openapi.dart` loads your app config, so it needs an `APP_KEY`. The dummy key is only for this step. If a provider connects to a database in `setup()`, the build step must reach that database.

5. Start the image with `APP_ENV=production` and open `/docs`.

To test it on your machine, run `dox openapi:generate docs/openapi`, then start the app with `APP_ENV=production`.

!!! warning
    These routes have no login, so anyone can see every route of your API. To protect them, put a middleware on the three routes.

## Without Dox

`dox_openapi` also works on its own. Describe each route with `ApiDoc`:

```dart
import 'package:dox_openapi/dox_openapi.dart';

ApiDoc docs = ApiDoc();
Map<String, dynamic> user = docs.schema('User', userSchema); // a $ref

docs.route('GET', '/users/{id}',
    summary: 'Get one user',
    tags: <String>['users'],
    params: <String, Object>{'id': <String, dynamic>{'type': 'integer'}},
    responses: <int, ResponseDoc>{
      200: ResponseDoc(schema: user, description: 'The user'),
      404: const ResponseDoc(description: 'Not found'),
    });

OpenApi api = OpenApi(
    info: const Info(title: 'My API', version: '1.0.0'), docs: docs);
```

A schema can be a JSON Schema map, a [`dox_validation`](validation.md) schema, or any object with `toJsonSchema()`. Paths can use `{id}` or `:id`. `route` also takes `query`, `body`, `security`, `deprecated` and `operationId`. `OpenApi` also takes `servers`, `securitySchemes` and `security`.

### Reading the docs back

`docs.ref('User')` gives a `$ref` to a schema you added. `docs.has('GET', '/users/{id}')` tells you if a route has docs. `docs.add(routeDoc)` adds or replaces a `RouteDoc`.

### Getting the document

```dart
api.toJson();                              // Map
api.toJsonString();                        // pretty JSON
api.toYaml();                              // YAML
await api.writeFiles('storage/openapi');   // openapi.json + openapi.yaml
```

### Serving the docs from your own server

`OpenApiServer` gives the page and the document for a path. `docsPage()`, `json()` and `yaml()` give each one directly:

```dart
OpenApiServer server = OpenApiServer(api); // or ui: DocsUi.swagger
OpenApiResponse? page = server.handle('/docs'); // or '/openapi.json'
if (page != null) {
  // send page.body with the header Content-Type: page.contentType
}
```

### Text response keys

`responses` takes status codes as integer keys. For a text key like `default` or `2XX`, use `namedResponses`. It wins when the same key is in both:

```dart
docs.route('GET', '/users/{id}',
    responses: <int, ResponseDoc>{
      200: ResponseDoc(schema: user, description: 'The user'),
    },
    namedResponses: <String, ResponseDoc>{
      'default': const ResponseDoc(description: 'Any other error'),
    });
```

`DoxRouteAdapter().addTo(docs, routes)` adds a basic entry for each route with no docs.

- [API docs with OpenAPI](../guides/api-docs-with-openapi.md): a docs page for your API, step by step.
- [DTOs](../the-basic/dto.md): the classes that become schemas.

# Socket.IO

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/packages/socketio/

# Socket.IO

`dox_socketio` is a Socket.IO v4 server for Dart, and it is the way to do realtime in Dox.

The official clients connect to it with no changes: `socket.io-client` (JavaScript v4) and the Dart `socket_io_client` package. It has acks, rooms, namespaces, binary data and long-polling. In a Dox app, it runs on the same port as your HTTP routes, at `/socket.io/`. For a plain WebSocket with no Socket.IO protocol, use `Route.websocket` of [routing](../the-basic/routing.md#websocket-routes).

## Setup

### Install

The quick way is the CLI. It adds the package, the provider, the config and the env key (steps 1, 2, 3 and 5 below). It never overwrites a file:

```bash
dox add socketio
```

Then write a namespace (step 4) and connect a client (step 6). Add `--broadcasting` to also turn on [broadcasting](../digging-deeper/broadcasting.md). Without the CLI, do all the steps.

### 1. Add the package

```bash
dart pub add dox_socketio
```

### 2. The provider

The provider starts Socket.IO in every isolate. Put it in `lib/providers/`, so the generated container finds it:

```dart title="lib/providers/socketio_provider.dart"
import 'package:dox_socketio/dox_socketio.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/socketio.dart';

class AppSocketIoProvider extends SocketIoProvider {
  AppSocketIoProvider() : super(socketIoConfig);
}
```

### 3. The config

The config lists the namespaces to serve:

```dart title="lib/config/socketio.dart"
import 'package:dox_socketio/dox_socketio.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/socket/chat.namespace.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

SocketIoConfig socketIoConfig = SocketIoConfig(
  enabled: env.socketioEnabled,
  namespaces: <NamespaceHandler>[ChatNamespace()],
);
```

| `SocketIoConfig` option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | true | serve Socket.IO at `options.path` |
| `options` | `ServerOptions()` | see [Options](#options) |
| `namespaces` | `[]` | `NamespaceHandler` classes to register |
| `adapter` | none | makes one adapter in each isolate, see [Many isolates](#many-isolates) |

### 4. A namespace

A **namespace** handles the events of one path, like `/chat`:

```dart title="lib/app/socket/chat.namespace.dart"
import 'package:dox_socketio/dox_socketio.dart';

class ChatNamespace extends NamespaceHandler {
  @override
  String get path => '/chat';

  @override
  void onConnection(Socket socket) {
    socket.emit('welcome', <String, dynamic>{'id': socket.id});
    socket.join('lobby');
    socket.on('message', onMessage);
  }

  void onMessage(SocketEvent event) {
    // everyone in lobby but me
    event.socket.to('lobby').emit('message', event.data);
    event.ack('sent'); // answer the client callback
  }
}
```

### 5. Turn it on

Add a getter for the `SOCKETIO_ENABLED` key to `lib/config/env.dart`:

```dart title="lib/config/env.dart"
  /// serve Socket.IO on the app port
  bool get socketioEnabled => false;
```

```bash title=".env"
SOCKETIO_ENABLED=true
```

Then run `dart run build_runner build` and `dox serve`.

### 6. Connect a client

Use `transports: ['websocket']`, because long-polling does not work with many isolates. See [Many isolates](#many-isolates):

```js
import { io } from 'socket.io-client';

const socket = io('http://localhost:3000/chat', { transports: ['websocket'] });
socket.on('welcome', (data) => console.log(data.id));
socket.emit('message', 'hi', (answer) => console.log(answer)); // 'sent'
```

Requests to `/socket.io/` go to Socket.IO before the router, so route middleware does not run for them. To log users in, see [Log in a socket](#log-in-a-socket).

### Options

Give `ServerOptions` as `options` to `SocketIoConfig`, or to `SocketIoServer` without Dox:

```dart
SocketIoServer(
  options: ServerOptions(
    path: '/socket.io/',
    pingInterval: Duration(seconds: 25),
    pingTimeout: Duration(seconds: 20),
    maxHttpBufferSize: 1000000,
    transports: <String>['polling', 'websocket'],
    cors: CorsOptions(
        origins: <String>['https://my.app'], credentials: true),
  ),
);
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | `/socket.io/` | the URL path |
| `pingInterval` | 25 s | how often the server sends a ping |
| `pingTimeout` | 20 s | how long to wait for the pong before the client is gone |
| `upgradeTimeout` | 10 s | how long an upgrade from polling to websocket can take |
| `connectTimeout` | 45 s | how long the client has to join a namespace |
| `maxHttpBufferSize` | 1,000,000 bytes | the biggest message. A bigger websocket message closes the connection with code 1009 |
| `maxAttachments` | `10` | the most binary parts in one packet. More closes the client |
| `transports` | `['polling', 'websocket']` | allowed transports |
| `allowUpgrades` | true | let polling clients move to websocket |
| `cors` | none | CORS headers for polling requests. With a list of origins, it also checks the origin of websockets |
| `allowedOrigins` | none | the sites that can connect, see [Allowed origins](#allowed-origins) |
| `allowRequest` | none | accepts or refuses each request, see [Allow requests and limit sessions](#allow-requests-and-limit-sessions) |
| `maxSessions` | none | the most open sessions per isolate. Set it in production |
| `maxAttachmentBytes` | none | the most bytes of all binary parts of one packet. A bigger packet closes the client |
| `maxAuthSize` | none | the most bytes of the `auth` payload. A bigger one gets `connect_error` (`auth payload too large`) |
| `maxWriteBufferSize` | none | the most bytes kept for a client that does not read. Above it, the session closes |
| `ackTimeout` | none | the default timeout of `emitWithAck`. With none, it waits until the client answers or leaves |

On a plain `dart:io` server, the full message is read before the size check, so also set a size limit in your proxy.

## Namespaces

A namespace is a class, so its dependencies come in through the constructor:

```dart
class ChatNamespace extends NamespaceHandler {
  ChatNamespace(this.messages);

  final MessageService messages;

  @override
  String get path => '/chat';

  @override
  void onConnection(Socket socket) {
    socket.on('message', onMessage);
  }

  void onMessage(SocketEvent event) {
    event.ack(messages.save(event.data));
  }
}

// in lib/config/socketio.dart
namespaces: <NamespaceHandler>[ChatNamespace(MessageService())],
```

### Namespace middleware

A middleware checks a client before it joins. When it throws a `SocketIoException`, the client gets `connect_error` with the message and the data:

```dart
@override
List<Middleware> get middleware => <Middleware>[checkToken];

void checkToken(Socket socket) {
  if (socket.handshake.auth['token'] != 'secret') {
    throw SocketIoException('unauthorized',
        data: <String, dynamic>{'reason': 'bad token'});
  }
}
```

Any other error goes to stderr, and the client gets only `{"message": "Internal error"}`.

## Sending events

### Sending from a controller or a service

`SocketIoProvider.server` is the Socket.IO server of this isolate:

```dart
await SocketIoProvider.server?.of('/chat').to('lobby').emit('news', data);
```

From a queue job or another program, use the [emitter](#emit-from-other-programs).

### Common methods

The API follows the Node.js server. This table shows where Dart is different:

| Node.js | Dart |
| --- | --- |
| `socket.on('e', (a, cb) => ...)` | `socket.on('e', (SocketEvent e) => ...)`, then `e.data`, `e.args`, `e.ack(x)` |
| `socket.emit('e', a, b)` | `socket.emit('e', a)` or `socket.emitArgs('e', [a, b])` |
| `await socket.timeout(5000).emitWithAck('e', a)` | `await socket.emitWithAck('e', a, timeout: Duration(seconds: 5))` |
| `socket.join(r)`, `socket.leave(r)` | the same |
| `socket.to(r).emit(...)`, `socket.except(r)` | the same |
| `socket.broadcast.emit(...)` | the same |
| `io.to(r).except(x).emit(...)` | the same |
| `io.of('/chat')`, `io.use(fn)` | the same |
| `io.local.emit(...)` | the same: only sockets of this server |
| `socket.handshake` | `.headers`, `.query`, `.auth`, `.address`, `.url`, `.secure`, `.time`, `.token`, `.cookie(name)`, `.session()` |
| `socket.data` | `socket.data` (a map). Keep it JSON, because other servers get a copy |
| `await io.in(r).fetchSockets()` | `await io.to(r).fetchSockets()` (all servers) |
| `await io.timeout(5000).emitWithAck('e', a)` | `await io.timeout(Duration(seconds: 5)).emitWithAck('e', a)` |
| `io.serverSideEmit('e', a)` | `await io.serverSideEmit('e', [a])` |
| `io.on('e', (a, cb) => ...)` (from other servers) | `io.onServerSideEmit('e', (ServerSideEvent e) => ...)`, then `e.data`, `e.ack(x)` |

To send binary data, send a `Uint8List`. It can be anywhere in lists and maps. An event with many values uses `emitArgs`, `emitArgsWithAck` and `e.ackArgs([a, b])`. `e.hasAck` is true when the client waits for an answer.

### The state of a socket

```dart
socket.connected;   // true while connected
socket.transport;   // 'polling' or 'websocket'
socket.rooms;       // the rooms of the socket
socket.waitingAcks; // acks it still waits for
```

To stop a handler, call `socket.off('message', onMessage)`. With no handler, all handlers of the event go. `nsp.offServerSideEmit` does the same for server events.

### Leaving

The `disconnecting` and `disconnect` events give the reason in `event.data`, like `transport close`. To close a socket from the server, call `disconnect`. `disconnect(true)` also closes the connection under it:

```dart
socket.on('disconnect', (SocketEvent e) => print(e.data));
socket.disconnect();
```

## Log in a socket

Route middleware, like session and auth, does not run for Socket.IO. Use `SocketAuth` as a namespace middleware. Your function gets the handshake and returns the user, or null:

```dart title="lib/app/socket/chat.namespace.dart"
class ChatNamespace extends NamespaceHandler {
  @override
  String get path => '/chat';

  @override
  List<Middleware> get middleware =>
      <Middleware>[SocketAuth(findUser).handle];

  static Future<User?> findUser(Handshake handshake) async {
    String? token = handshake.token;
    if (token == null) return null;
    return User().where('api_token', token).getFirst();
  }

  @override
  void onConnection(Socket socket) {
    User user = socket.user! as User;
    socket.join('user:${user.id}');
  }
}
```

The client sends the token in `auth`, because browsers can not set headers on a websocket:

```js
const socket = io('http://localhost:3000/chat', {
  transports: ['websocket'],
  auth: { token: 'the-user-token' },
});
socket.on('connect_error', (err) => console.log(err.message)); // 'Unauthorized'
```

A returned user is kept in `socket.user`, on this server only. When the function returns null, the client gets `connect_error` with the message `Unauthorized`, and `onConnection` does not run. `SocketAuth(findUser, message: '...')` changes the message.

The handshake has these helpers:

- `handshake.token` is `auth.token` from the client, else the `Authorization: Bearer` header.
- `handshake.cookie('name')` reads a cookie and decrypts it with `APP_KEY`. Use `decrypt: false` for a plain cookie.
- `await handshake.session()` gives the Dox session of the client. It uses `AppConfig.session`, or the `SessionConfig` you give. Changes are not saved.

### With dox_auth

[dox_auth](../security/authentication.md#check-a-login-with-no-request) can check a JWT or the web login session:

```dart
static Future<User?> findUser(Handshake handshake) async {
  // an API client or a mobile app sends a JWT
  String? token = handshake.token;
  if (token != null) return Auth(guard: 'api').userFromToken(token);

  // a browser that logged in on a web page sends the session cookie
  Session session = await handshake.session();
  return Auth(guard: 'web').userFromSession(session);
}
```

A bad, expired or revoked token gives null. The session is read one time, when the socket connects, so call `socket.disconnect()` yourself after a logout. With `userCacheTtl` in `dox_auth`, a banned user can connect until the cache time ends, unless `forgetUser` runs. With the cookie session driver, an old session cookie works after logout until the `lifetime` ends.

!!! warning "Cookie login needs `allowedOrigins`"
    A browser sends its cookies on a websocket from any website. If you log users in with a cookie, set [`allowedOrigins`](#allowed-origins) to your own sites. Else another website can open a socket as your user.

## Protecting the server

### Allowed origins

`allowedOrigins` sets the websites that can open a socket. Set it when you log users in with cookies:

```dart
ServerOptions(allowedOrigins: <String>['https://app.example.com']);
```

- None (the default): no extra check. Dox logs a warning at start.
- `[]`: only pages of the same host can connect.
- A list of sites: the same host and those sites can connect.
- `['*']`: every site can connect.

Other sites get 403. A client with no `Origin` header (not a browser) can always connect. `cors` with `*` in `origins`, or no `cors`, allows websockets from any origin. `*` with `credentials: true` throws an `ArgumentError`.

### Allow requests and limit sessions

`allowRequest` runs for every handshake and every websocket upgrade. It gets an `EngineRequest` with the headers, query and address, and returns true or false. `maxSessions` is the most open sessions:

```dart title="lib/config/socketio.dart"
SocketIoConfig socketIoConfig = SocketIoConfig(
  options: ServerOptions(
    allowRequest: (EngineRequest req) => req.query['key'] == 'secret',
    maxSessions: 10000,
  ),
);
```

When `allowRequest` gives false or throws, the client gets 403. At the limit, a new handshake gets 503, and open sessions keep working. The count is per isolate, so with 4 isolates the app allows 4 times `maxSessions`.

!!! warning
    Without `maxSessions`, every GET request makes a session that lives about 45 seconds. Set it in production.

## Many isolates

Dox runs one isolate per CPU core, and each isolate has its own Socket.IO server. With many isolates, the provider uses the `IsolateAdapter`. It sends each broadcast, `socketsJoin`, `fetchSockets`, `serverSideEmit` and broadcast ack to the other isolates of the process:

| Adapter | Reaches |
|---|---|
| `InMemoryAdapter` (one isolate) | the clients of this isolate |
| `IsolateAdapter` (many isolates, the default) | the clients of every isolate of this process |
| `RedisAdapter` | the clients of every isolate of every server |

Clients must connect with websocket only. Long-polling sends many requests that can reach different isolates. It works only with `totalIsolate: 1`, or with sticky sessions in front of many single-isolate servers.

Add each namespace in the config, so every isolate adds it. A namespace that only one isolate adds with `io.of('/x')` gets no answer from the others, so `fetchSockets` and `serverSideEmitWithAck` wait 5 seconds and throw.

## Many servers: Redis adapter

With many server processes, or Dox next to Node.js servers, use the Redis adapter. A broadcast on one server then reaches the clients of all servers. Add the `ioredis` package:

```bash
dart pub add ioredis
```

Make the adapter in each isolate with a factory, because a Redis connection can not go to another isolate:

```dart title="lib/config/socketio.dart"
import 'package:dox_socketio/dox_socketio.dart';
import 'package:ioredis/ioredis.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/socket/chat.namespace.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

SocketIoConfig socketIoConfig = SocketIoConfig(
  enabled: env.socketioEnabled,
  namespaces: <NamespaceHandler>[ChatNamespace()],
  adapter: const RedisSocketAdapterFactory(),
);

/// makes the Redis adapter inside each isolate.
class RedisSocketAdapterFactory extends SocketAdapterFactory {
  const RedisSocketAdapterFactory();

  @override
  Adapter create() {
    // 127.0.0.1:6379. Or Redis(RedisOptions(host: ..., port: ...))
    Redis redis = Redis();
    return RedisAdapter(subscriber: redis.duplicate(), publisher: redis);
  }
}
```

The subscriber needs its own connection, because a connection in subscribe mode can not run other commands.

The adapter uses the format of `@socket.io/redis-adapter`, so Node.js servers with that adapter can share one Redis with Dox. If your Node.js servers use a JSON parser, set `format: RedisFormat.json`. Long-polling with this adapter also needs sticky sessions.

### Acting on all servers

With the Redis adapter, these methods work on the sockets of all servers:

```dart
// sockets of every server. Sockets of this server are `Socket`s.
List<RemoteSocket> sockets = await io.to('room1').fetchSockets();
for (RemoteSocket socket in sockets) {
  socket.emit('hello', socket.data['name']);
}

await io.to('room1').socketsJoin('room2');
await io.to('room2').socketsLeave('room1');
await io.to('banned').disconnectSockets();
```

A `RemoteSocket` also has `join`, `leave` and `disconnect`. `fetchSockets` throws a `TimeoutException` when a server does not answer in `requestsTimeout` (5 seconds by default).

To get one ack from each client on all servers, set a timeout:

```dart
List<Object?> answers = await io
    .timeout(const Duration(seconds: 5))
    .emitWithAck('ping', 'are you there?');
```

### Events between servers

`serverSideEmit` sends an event to the other servers, like "reload the config". Clients do not get it:

```dart
// on every server
io.onServerSideEmit('reload-config', (ServerSideEvent event) {
  reloadConfig(event.data);
  event.ack('done'); // only when the sender waits for an answer
});

// on one server
await io.serverSideEmit('reload-config', <Object?>['v2']);
```

To wait for one answer from each other server, use `serverSideEmitWithAck`. When a server does not answer in time, it throws an `AckTimeoutException`, and its `responses` holds the answers that came back:

```dart
List<Object?> answers =
    await io.serverSideEmitWithAck('reload-config', <Object?>['v2']);
```

## Emit from other programs

An **emitter** sends an event with no Socket.IO server, for example from a queue worker or a cron job. It writes to Redis, and every server with the Redis adapter sends the event to its clients:

```dart
import 'package:dox_socketio/dox_socketio.dart';
import 'package:ioredis/ioredis.dart';

Future<void> main() async {
  Redis redis = Redis(RedisOptions(host: '127.0.0.1', port: 6379));
  SocketIoEmitter emitter = SocketIoEmitter(redis);

  // all clients of `/`
  await emitter.emit('news', <String, dynamic>{'title': 'hello'});
  await emitter.to('room1').except('room2').emit('news', 'hi room1');
  await emitter.of('/chat').to('vip').emit('notice', 'for vip');

  await emitter.to('room1').socketsJoin('room3');
  await emitter.to('room3').socketsLeave('room1');
  await emitter.to('banned').disconnectSockets();
  await emitter.serverSideEmit('reload-config', <Object?>['v2']);

  await redis.disconnect();
}
```

The emitter does not wait for an answer. Its `key` must be the same as the adapter `key`. Both default to `socket.io`.

The emitters of other languages use the same format. For example, Node.js with [`@socket.io/redis-emitter`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@socket.io/redis-emitter):

```js
import { Emitter } from '@socket.io/redis-emitter';
import { createClient } from 'redis';

const redis = createClient({ url: 'redis://127.0.0.1:6379' });
await redis.connect();

const emitter = new Emitter(redis);
emitter.to('room1').emit('news', { title: 'hello' });
emitter.of('/chat').emit('notice', 'for everyone in /chat');
```

## Broadcasting

To send events to public, private and presence channels, see [Broadcasting](../digging-deeper/broadcasting.md).

## Without Dox

`dox_socketio` also runs with no Dox app:

```dart
import 'package:dox_socketio/dox_socketio.dart';

Future<void> main() async {
  SocketIoServer io = SocketIoServer();
  io.register(ChatNamespace());
  await io.listen(3001);
}
```

- `io.listen(port)` starts a native server on its own port. Run it in its own small program, like `bin/socket.dart`, behind the same proxy as the HTTP server.
- `io.attach(httpServer)` uses a server you already have: a `NativeHttpServer` or a `dart:io` one.
- In your own server, call `io.handle(request)` when `io.matches(request)` is true.
- `io.on('connection', (Socket socket) {...})` handles the default namespace `/` with no class. `io.sockets` is that namespace.
- `io.use(SocketAuth(findUser).handle)` logs users in on the default namespace.
- `await io.close()` disconnects everyone and stops the server.

To use the Redis adapter, give it to the server:

```dart
Redis redis = Redis(RedisOptions(host: '127.0.0.1', port: 6379));
SocketIoServer io = SocketIoServer(
  adapter: RedisAdapter(subscriber: redis.duplicate(), publisher: redis),
);
```

- [Broadcasting](../digging-deeper/broadcasting.md): send server events to channels.
- [Authentication](../security/authentication.md): log users in.
