# PDF Library

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/packages/pdf-lib/

# PDF Library

Create, load and edit PDF files in Dart with `dox_pdf_lib`, and send them from a Dox controller.

The package draws text, shapes, SVG paths and images, and it does forms, attachments, metadata, custom fonts, and PDF/A and PDF/X. It has the API of the pdf-lib JavaScript library. To fill pdfme templates, see [pdfme](pdfme.md).

## Setup

```bash
dart pub add dox_pdf_lib
```

The package uses `dart:ffi` and a small native library. It runs in Dart programs on macOS, Linux and Windows, not on the web, iOS or Android. The package downloads a ready-built library, so you do not need Rust.

On Linux, the ready-built library needs glibc 2.35 or newer, like Ubuntu 22.04 or Debian 12. On older Linux or on Alpine, build the library with cargo and set its path in your `pubspec.yaml`:

```yaml title="pubspec.yaml"
hooks:
  user_defines:
    dox_pdf_lib:
      lib_path: /path/to/libdox_pdf_lib.so
```

## Sending a PDF from a controller

Return a `DownloadableFile`, and the browser saves the file. Use `StreamFile` to show the PDF in the browser tab. See [Response](../the-basic/response.md):

```dart title="lib/app/http/controllers/report.controller.dart"
import 'dart:io';
import 'dart:typed_data';

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:dox_pdf_lib/dox_pdf_lib.dart';

@Inject()
class ReportController {
  Future<DownloadableFile> show(DoxRequest req) async {
    PDFDocument doc = await PDFDocument.create();
    PDFFont font = await doc.embedFont(StandardFonts.helvetica);
    PDFPage page = doc.addPage(PageSizes.A4);
    page.drawText('Monthly report', x: 50, y: 750, font: font, size: 24);

    Uint8List bytes = await doc.save();
    return DownloadableFile(
      ContentType('application', 'pdf'),
      Stream<List<int>>.value(bytes),
      'report.pdf',
      length: bytes.length,
    );
  }
}
```

```dart title="lib/routes/api.dart"
Route.get('/report.pdf', (ReportController c) => c.show);
```

## Creating and loading a document

Make an empty document with `create`, or read a file with `load`:

```dart
PDFDocument doc = await PDFDocument.create();

PDFDocument old = await PDFDocument.load(
    File('in.pdf').readAsBytesSync());
```

A broken file throws `PDFParsingError`. An encrypted file throws `EncryptedPDFError`.

### Loading an encrypted file

Load it with `ignoreEncryption: true`. A file with only an owner password is decrypted, and `save` writes it with no encryption. A file with a user password throws `PDFParsingError`:

```dart
PDFDocument doc = await PDFDocument.load(bytes, ignoreEncryption: true);
print(doc.isEncrypted); // true
```

### Keeping the metadata

`create` and `load` set the producer and the modification date. They also add a creator and a creation date when the file has none. To keep the metadata as it is, pass `updateMetadata: false`:

```dart
PDFDocument doc = await PDFDocument.load(bytes, updateMetadata: false);
```

### Freeing a document

A document is freed when Dart removes the object. To free it now, call `dispose`:

```dart
doc.dispose();
```

## Saving a document

`save` gives the bytes of the file:

```dart
Uint8List bytes = await doc.save();
```

It has three options, all true by default:

| Option | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `useObjectStreams` | Packs objects into object streams, for a smaller file. |
| `addDefaultPage` | Adds one page when the document has none. |
| `updateFieldAppearances` | Draws the form fields again when the form was used. |

### Saving as base64

Get a base64 string, or a data URI with `dataUri: true`:

```dart
String text = await doc.saveAsBase64(dataUri: true);
```

## Working with pages

### Adding pages

`addPage` adds a page at the end. Give a size from `PageSizes`, a width and height in points, or nothing for A4:

```dart
PDFPage page = doc.addPage(PageSizes.Letter);
doc.addPage(<double>[400, 600]);
doc.insertPage(0, PageSizes.A5);
doc.removePage(1);
```

`removePage` on a document with no pages throws `RemovePageFromEmptyDocumentError`.

### Reading pages

```dart
List<PDFPage> pages = doc.getPages();
PDFPage first = doc.getPage(0);
int count = doc.getPageCount();
List<int> indices = doc.getPageIndices(); // [0, 1, 2]
```

### Page sizes

`PageSizes` has the sizes in points, as `[width, height]`:

| Group | Names |
| --- | --- |
| A | `$4A0`, `$2A0`, `A0` to `A10` |
| B | `B0` to `B10` |
| C | `C0` to `C10` |
| RA and SRA | `RA0` to `RA4`, `SRA0` to `SRA4` |
| US and other | `Executive`, `Folio`, `Legal`, `Letter`, `Tabloid` |

### Changing the page size

```dart
print(page.getSize()); // (height: 841.89, width: 595.28)
page.setSize(420, 600);
page.setWidth(500);
page.setHeight(700);
```

`getWidth` and `getHeight` read one side. Boxes that had the size of the media box follow the new size.

### Page boxes

Each box has a get and a set method: media, crop, bleed, trim and art. A box is `(x, y, width, height)`:

```dart
page.setCropBox(10, 10, 400, 580);
PDFBox trim = page.getTrimBox();
```

The page methods are `getMediaBox`, `getCropBox`, `getBleedBox`, `getTrimBox` and `getArtBox`, and the same names with `set`. A missing crop box reads as the media box. A missing bleed, trim or art box reads as the crop box.

### Rotating a page

The angle must be a multiple of 90 degrees:

```dart
page.setRotation(degrees(90));
Degrees angle = page.getRotation();
```

| Function | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `degrees(90)`, `radians(1.57)` | A `Degrees` or `Radians` angle. |
| `toDegrees(angle)`, `toRadians(angle)` | The angle as a number. |
| `degreesToRadians(90)`, `radiansToDegrees(1.57)` | A number converted. |

### Moving and scaling the content

```dart
page.translateContent(10, 20); // moves what is on the page
page.scaleContent(0.5, 0.5);   // scales what is on the page
page.scaleAnnotations(0.5, 0.5);
page.scale(2, 2);              // page size, content and annotations
page.resetPosition();          // the text position goes back to 0, 0
```

## Copying and merging pages

`copyPages` copies pages of another document. Then add them with `addPage` or `insertPage`:

```dart
PDFDocument merged = await PDFDocument.create();
for (PDFDocument source in <PDFDocument>[a, b]) {
  List<PDFPage> pages =
      await merged.copyPages(source, source.getPageIndices());
  for (PDFPage page in pages) {
    merged.addPage(page);
  }
}
```

A page of another document that you did not copy throws `ForeignPageError`.

## Placing pages of another PDF

Use a page of another PDF as a background or a template. `embedPdf` takes bytes, a base64 string or a `PDFDocument`, and embeds the first page by default:

```dart
List<PDFEmbeddedPage> pages = await out.embedPdf(
    File('template.pdf').readAsBytesSync(), <int>[0, 1]);
PDFEmbeddedPage template = pages.first;

PDFPage page = out.addPage(<double>[template.width, template.height]);
page.drawPage(template);
page.drawText('Filled in on top', x: 50, y: 50);
```

`drawPage` takes `x`, `y`, `xScale`, `yScale`, `width`, `height`, `rotate`, `xSkew`, `ySkew`, `opacity` and `blendMode`. An embedded page has `width`, `height`, `size()` and `scale(factor)`.

### Embedding loaded pages

`embedPage` embeds one page. Give a bounding box to clip a part of it, and a matrix `[a, b, c, d, e, f]` to transform it:

```dart
PDFEmbeddedPage part = await out.embedPage(
  source.getPage(0),
  (left: 0, bottom: 400, right: 595, top: 842),
);
List<PDFEmbeddedPage> all = await out.embedPages(source.getPages());
```

All pages of `embedPages` must come from one document, or it throws `PageEmbeddingMismatchedContextError`.

## Adding text

`drawText` draws text at a point. A newline starts a new line:

```dart
page.drawText(
  'A long line of text that wraps inside 300 points.',
  x: 50,
  y: 700,
  font: bold,
  size: 14,
  color: rgb(0.1, 0.3, 0.8),
  maxWidth: 300,
  lineHeight: 18,
);
```

The options are `color`, `opacity`, `blendMode`, `font`, `size`, `rotate`, `xSkew`, `ySkew`, `x`, `y`, `lineHeight`, `maxWidth` and `wordBreaks`. With no font, the page uses Helvetica.

### Setting the text state

Set the font, size, color, line height and position one time. Then `drawText` uses them:

```dart
page.setFont(font);
page.setFontSize(12);    // default 24
page.setFontColor(grayscale(0.2));
page.setLineHeight(16);  // default 24
page.moveTo(50, 700);
page.drawText('First line');
page.moveDown(16);
page.drawText('Second line');
```

Also: `moveUp`, `moveLeft`, `moveRight`, `getPosition`, `getX` and `getY`. A font of another document throws an `ArgumentError`.

### Word breaks

With `maxWidth`, a line breaks at a space. Set other break characters for one call with `wordBreaks`, or for the document with `defaultWordBreaks`:

```dart
doc.defaultWordBreaks = <String>[' ', '-'];
page.drawText(text, maxWidth: 300, wordBreaks: <String>[' ', '/']);
```

### Word breaks in Thai, Lao, Khmer and Myanmar

These scripts have no spaces between words. `dictionaryWordBreaks` gives the index where each word starts:

```dart
List<int> breaks = dictionaryWordBreaks('ทุกสองสัปดาห์'); // [3, 6]
```

The indexes are UTF-16 indexes, like `String.substring`. The start and the end of the text are not in the list.

## Using fonts

### Standard fonts

The 14 standard PDF fonts need no font file. They have only Latin letters:

```dart
PDFFont font = await doc.embedFont(StandardFonts.timesRoman);
PDFFont same = doc.embedStandardFont(StandardFonts.timesRoman);
```

| Family | Values of `StandardFonts` |
| --- | --- |
| Courier | `courier`, `courierBold`, `courierOblique`, `courierBoldOblique` |
| Helvetica | `helvetica`, `helveticaBold`, `helveticaOblique`, `helveticaBoldOblique` |
| Times | `timesRoman`, `timesRomanBold`, `timesRomanItalic`, `timesRomanBoldItalic` |
| Symbols | `symbol`, `zapfDingbats` |

`fontName` gives the PostScript name, like `Times-Roman`. `embedFont` also takes that name as a string.

### Using other fonts

For other languages, embed a TrueType or OpenType font. `subset: true` puts only the letters you use into the file:

```dart
Uint8List bytes = File('NotoSansThai-Regular.ttf').readAsBytesSync();
PDFFont thai = await doc.embedFont(bytes, subset: true);
page.drawText('สวัสดีครับ', x: 50, y: 700, font: thai, size: 20);
```

Thai, Myanmar, Khmer, Lao, Arabic, Hebrew and Hindi text is laid out correctly. Use `subset: false` for a font in a form field that people edit, because a subset has only the letters known at save time.

`embedFont` also takes a base64 string or a data URI. Font collections (`.ttc`), WOFF files and CFF2 fonts do not work.

### Font options

`customName` replaces the font name in the file. `features` turns OpenType features on or off:

```dart
PDFFont font = await doc.embedFont(
  bytes,
  customName: 'BrandFont',
  features: <String, bool>{'liga': false},
);
```

### Measuring text

```dart
double width = font.widthOfTextAtSize('Hello', 12);
double height = font.heightAtSize(12);
double above = font.heightAtSize(12, descender: false);
double size = font.sizeAtHeight(20);
```

`getCharacterSet` gives the code points the font has. `encodeText` gives the text as a `PDFHexString` for raw operators. `name` is the PostScript name of the font.

## Colors

Each part is a number from 0 to 1:

```dart
Color red = rgb(1, 0, 0);
Color gray = grayscale(0.5);
Color black = cmyk(0, 0, 0, 1);
```

The functions give an `RGB`, `Grayscale` or `CMYK` object. A part out of range throws a `RangeError`.

## Drawing shapes

### Lines

```dart
page.drawLine(
  start: (x: 50, y: 650),
  end: (x: 350, y: 650),
  thickness: 2,
  color: grayscale(0.5),
  dashArray: <double>[4, 2],
);
```

A line also takes `opacity`, `lineCap`, `dashPhase` and `blendMode`.

### Rectangles and squares

A rectangle is 150 by 100 by default. With no color and no border color, it is filled black:

```dart
page.drawRectangle(
  x: 50,
  y: 500,
  width: 200,
  height: 100,
  color: rgb(1, 0.9, 0.9),
  borderColor: rgb(1, 0, 0),
  borderWidth: 2,
  opacity: 0.8,
);
page.drawSquare(x: 300, y: 500, size: 50);
```

### Ellipses and circles

`x` and `y` are the center. An ellipse has the radii `xScale` and `yScale`, and a circle has the radius `size`. Both are 100 by default:

```dart
page.drawEllipse(x: 200, y: 300, xScale: 80, yScale: 40);
page.drawCircle(x: 350, y: 550, size: 40, color: cmyk(0.5, 0, 0, 0));
```

### Shape options

| Option | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `color`, `opacity` | The fill. |
| `borderColor`, `borderOpacity`, `borderWidth` | The border. |
| `borderDashArray`, `borderDashPhase` | A dashed border. |
| `borderLineCap` | `LineCapStyle.butt`, `round` or `projecting`. |
| `rotate`, `xSkew`, `ySkew` | An angle, like `degrees(30)`. Ellipses and circles take only `rotate`, and circles take none. |
| `blendMode` | One of `BlendMode`, see below. |

`BlendMode` has `normal`, `multiply`, `screen`, `overlay`, `darken`, `lighten`, `colorDodge`, `colorBurn`, `hardLight`, `softLight`, `difference` and `exclusion`.

## Drawing SVG paths

`drawSvgPath` draws the `d` attribute of an SVG path. Its y axis points down, as in SVG. With no color and no border color, the border is black:

```dart
page.drawSvgPath(
  'M 0,20 L 100,160 Q 130,200 150,120 Z',
  x: 50,
  y: 450,
  scale: 0.5,
  color: rgb(0, 0.5, 0),
);
```

It takes the shape options, without `xSkew` and `ySkew`.

## Adding images

Embed a PNG or a JPEG, then draw it. The default size is the size in pixels:

```dart
PDFImage png = await doc.embedPng(File('logo.png').readAsBytesSync());
PDFImage jpg = await doc.embedJpg(File('photo.jpg').readAsBytesSync());

page.drawImage(png, x: 50, y: 700, width: 100, height: 50);
```

`drawImage` also takes `rotate`, `xSkew`, `ySkew`, `opacity` and `blendMode`. The embed methods also take a base64 string or a data URI.

### Image sizes

```dart
({double width, double height}) fit = jpg.scaleToFit(200, 200);
({double width, double height}) half = jpg.scale(0.5);
({double width, double height}) full = jpg.size();
```

`width` and `height` of a `PDFImage` are the size in pixels.

## Raw operators

`pushOperators` adds PDF operators to the page content:

```dart
page.pushOperators(<PDFOperator>[
  pushGraphicsState(),
  setFillingRgbColor(0.9, 0.1, 0.1),
  rectangle(520, 40, 50, 30),
  fill(),
  popGraphicsState(),
]);
```

| Group | Functions |
| --- | --- |
| State | `pushGraphicsState`, `popGraphicsState`, `setGraphicsState`, `setLineWidth`, `setLineCap`, `setLineJoin`, `setDashPattern`, `restoreDashPattern` |
| Transform | `concatTransformationMatrix`, `translate`, `scale`, `rotateDegrees`, `rotateRadians`, `skewDegrees`, `skewRadians` |
| Path | `moveTo`, `lineTo`, `appendBezierCurve`, `appendQuadraticCurve`, `rectangle`, `square`, `closePath` |
| Paint | `stroke`, `fill`, `fillAndStroke`, `endPath`, `clip`, `clipEvenOdd` |
| Text | `beginText`, `endText`, `setFontAndSize`, `showText`, `moveText`, `nextLine`, `setCharacterSpacing`, `setWordSpacing`, `setCharacterSqueeze`, `setLineHeight`, `setTextRise`, `setTextRenderingMode`, `setTextMatrix`, `rotateAndSkewTextDegreesAndTranslate`, `rotateAndSkewTextRadiansAndTranslate` |
| Color | `setFillingColor`, `setStrokingColor`, and the gray, RGB and CMYK forms, like `setFillingGrayscaleColor` and `setStrokingCmykColor` |
| Other | `drawObject`, `beginMarkedContent`, `endMarkedContent` |

`LineJoinStyle` has `miter`, `round` and `bevel`. `TextRenderingMode` has `fill`, `outline`, `fillAndOutline`, `invisible`, `fillAndClip`, `outlineAndClip`, `fillAndOutlineAndClip` and `clip`. To make your own operator, use `PDFOperator(name, args)`.

## Filling a form

`getForm` gives the form of the document. Get a field by its full name, then set its value:

```dart
PDFDocument doc =
    await PDFDocument.load(File('form.pdf').readAsBytesSync());
PDFForm form = doc.getForm();
form.getTextField('person.name').setText('Jane Doe');
form.getCheckBox('agree').check();
form.getRadioGroup('color').select('green');
form.getDropdown('country').select('Myanmar');
File('filled.pdf').writeAsBytesSync(await doc.save());
```

`getForm` removes XFA data. `save` draws the changed fields again.

### Finding fields

```dart
List<PDFField> fields = form.getFields();
PDFField field = form.getField('person.name');
PDFField? maybe = form.getFieldMaybe('person.age');
```

The typed getters are `getTextField`, `getCheckBox`, `getRadioGroup`, `getDropdown`, `getOptionList`, `getButton` and `getSignature`. A missing name throws `NoSuchFieldError`, and a field of another type throws `UnexpectedFieldTypeError`.

### Field flags

Every field has these methods:

| Method | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `getName()` | The full name, like `page1.address.city`. |
| `isReadOnly()`, `enableReadOnly()`, `disableReadOnly()` | Read-only flag. |
| `isRequired()`, `enableRequired()`, `disableRequired()` | Required flag. |
| `isExported()`, `enableExporting()`, `disableExporting()` | Export flag. |
| `needsAppearancesUpdate()` | True when the field must be drawn again. |
| `defaultUpdateAppearances(font)` | Draws the field again with a font. |

### Text fields

```dart
PDFTextField name = form.getTextField('name');
name.setText('Jane');
name.setAlignment(TextAlignment.center);
name.setMaxLength(40);
name.setFontSize(12);
```

| Method | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `getText()`, `setText(text)` | The text. Null or an empty string removes it. |
| `getAlignment()`, `setAlignment(a)` | `TextAlignment.left`, `center` or `right`. |
| `getMaxLength()`, `setMaxLength(n)`, `removeMaxLength()` | A longer text throws `ExceededMaxLengthError`. |
| `setImage(image)` | Shows a `PDFImage` in the field. |
| `setFontSize(size)` | The font size. |
| `updateAppearances(font)` | Draws the field again with a font. |
| `isMultiline()`, `enableMultiline()`, `disableMultiline()` | Many lines. |
| `isPassword()`, `enablePassword()`, `disablePassword()` | Hidden text. |
| `isFileSelector()`, `enableFileSelection()`, `disableFileSelection()` | A file path. |
| `isSpellChecked()`, `enableSpellChecking()`, `disableSpellChecking()` | Spell check. |
| `isScrollable()`, `enableScrolling()`, `disableScrolling()` | Scrolling. |
| `isCombed()`, `enableCombing()`, `disableCombing()` | One cell for each letter. Needs a max length. |
| `isRichFormatted()`, `enableRichFormatting()`, `disableRichFormatting()` | Rich text flag. |

### Check boxes

```dart
PDFCheckBox agree = form.getCheckBox('agree');
agree.check();
agree.uncheck();
bool on = agree.isChecked();
```

### Radio groups

```dart
PDFRadioGroup color = form.getRadioGroup('color');
List<String> options = color.getOptions();
color.select('green');
String? picked = color.getSelected();
color.clear();
```

Also: `isOffToggleable`, `enableOffToggling`, `disableOffToggling`, `isMutuallyExclusive`, `enableMutualExclusion` and `disableMutualExclusion`.

### Dropdowns and option lists

A `PDFDropdown` and a `PDFOptionList` have the same methods. `select` takes one option or a list. With `merge` true, the old selection stays:

```dart
PDFOptionList country = form.getOptionList('country');
country.setOptions(<String>['Myanmar', 'Thailand']);
country.addOptions('Laos');
country.enableMultiselect();
country.select(<String>['Myanmar', 'Laos'], true);
List<String> picked = country.getSelected();
```

A list of many options on a field with no multiselect throws `MultiSelectValueError`.

| Method | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `getOptions()`, `setOptions(list)`, `addOptions(o)` | The options. |
| `getSelected()`, `select(o, merge)`, `clear()` | The selection. |
| `setFontSize(size)`, `updateAppearances(font)` | The look. |
| `isSorted()`, `enableSorting()`, `disableSorting()` | Sorted options. |
| `isMultiselect()`, `enableMultiselect()`, `disableMultiselect()` | Many selected options. |
| `isSelectOnClick()`, `enableSelectOnClick()`, `disableSelectOnClick()` | Save the value on click. |

A dropdown also has `isEditable`, `enableEditing`, `disableEditing`, `isSpellChecked`, `enableSpellChecking` and `disableSpellChecking`.

### Buttons and signatures

A button can show an image. A signature field can only be read, flagged and removed:

```dart
PDFButton logo = form.getButton('logo');
logo.setImage(png, ImageAlignment.left);
logo.setFontSize(10);

PDFSignature sign = form.getSignature('signature');
```

### Flattening a form

`flatten` draws every field on its page and removes the fields:

```dart
form.flatten();
```

### Removing a field

```dart
form.removeField(form.getField('notes'));
```

### Drawing fields with your font

Fields use Helvetica by default (`getDefaultFont`). For other letters, draw the fields again with your font:

```dart
form.updateFieldAppearances(font);
```

### Marking fields as changed

`save` draws the changed fields again. Mark a field by its `ref`:

```dart
form.markFieldAsDirty(field.ref);
form.markFieldAsClean(field.ref);
bool dirty = form.fieldIsDirty(field.ref);
```

### XFA data

```dart
if (form.hasXFA()) {
  form.deleteXFA();
}
```

### Widgets of a field

Each field has widgets, the boxes on the pages. Read them through `acroField`:

```dart
for (PDFWidgetAnnotation w in field.acroField.getWidgets()) {
  PDFBox box = w.getRectangle();
  PDFPage? page = doc.findPageForAnnotationRef(w.ref);
}
```

A widget also has `P()` (the page ref), `getFlags()`, `getOnValue()` and `getAppearanceState()`. `acroField.getFullyQualifiedName()` gives the full name.

## Creating a form

Create a field by name, then add it to a page. A name can have parents, like `a.b.name`:

```dart
PDFForm form = doc.getForm();
PDFTextField name = form.createTextField('name');
name.setText('Jane');
name.addToPage(page, x: 50, y: 700, width: 200, height: 24);

PDFCheckBox agree = form.createCheckBox('agree');
agree.addToPage(page, x: 50, y: 650, width: 16, height: 16);
```

The create methods are `createTextField`, `createCheckBox`, `createRadioGroup`, `createDropdown`, `createOptionList` and `createButton`. A name that is already used throws `FieldAlreadyExistsError`.

### Adding widgets to a page

`addToPage` takes `x`, `y`, `width`, `height`, `textColor`, `backgroundColor`, `borderColor`, `borderWidth`, `rotate` and `hidden`. Text fields, dropdowns, option lists and buttons also take `font`. A radio group adds one button for each option, and a button takes its caption first:

```dart
PDFRadioGroup size = form.createRadioGroup('size');
size.addOptionToPage('small', page, x: 50, y: 600);
size.addOptionToPage('large', page, x: 110, y: 600);

form.createButton('send').addToPage('Send', page, x: 50, y: 500);
```

| Field | Default size |
| --- | --- |
| Text field, dropdown | 200 by 50 |
| Option list | 200 by 100 |
| Check box, radio button | 50 by 50 |
| Button | 100 by 50, gray, no border |

## Attaching files

`attach` adds a file to the document. It takes bytes, a base64 string or a data URI:

```dart
await doc.attach(
  File('data.csv').readAsBytesSync(),
  'data.csv',
  mimeType: 'text/csv',
  description: 'The raw data',
);
```

It also takes `creationDate`, `modificationDate` and `afRelationship`.

### Reading attachments

```dart
for (PDFAttachment file in doc.getAttachments()) {
  print('${file.name}: ${file.data.length} bytes');
}
```

An attachment also has `mimeType`, `description`, `creationDate`, `modificationDate` and `afRelationship`.

## Metadata

```dart
doc.setTitle('Invoice 42', showInWindowTitleBar: true);
doc.setAuthor('Jane Doe');
doc.setKeywords(<String>['invoice', 'paid']);
doc.setLanguage('en-US');
doc.setCreationDate(DateTime.now());
print(doc.getTitle());
```

| Value | Set | Get |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Title | `setTitle` | `getTitle` |
| Author | `setAuthor` | `getAuthor` |
| Subject | `setSubject` | `getSubject` |
| Keywords | `setKeywords` | `getKeywords` (one string) |
| Creator | `setCreator` | `getCreator` |
| Producer | `setProducer` | `getProducer` |
| Language | `setLanguage` | `getLanguage` |
| Creation date | `setCreationDate` | `getCreationDate` |
| Modification date | `setModificationDate` | `getModificationDate` |
| Trapped | `setTrapped(Trapped.yes)` | `getTrapped` |

`Trapped` has `yes`, `no` and `unknown`. `setTrapped(null)` removes the value.

### Custom metadata

Add your own keys to the document info. A standard key, like `Title`, throws an `ArgumentError`:

```dart
doc.setCustomMetadata('Client', 'Acme');
String? client = doc.getCustomMetadata('Client');
List<String> keys = doc.getCustomMetadataKeys();
doc.removeCustomMetadata('Client');
```

## PDF/A and PDF/X

**PDF/A** is for long-term archives, and **PDF/X** is for print. `setConformance` sets up a document for the standard you pick. You give the ICC profile:

```dart
Uint8List srgb = File('sRGB2014.icc').readAsBytesSync();

PDFDocument doc = await PDFDocument.create();
doc.setTitle('Annual report');
doc.setConformance(
  PDFStandard.pdfA2b,
  iccProfile: srgb,
  outputConditionIdentifier: 'sRGB IEC61966-2.1',
);

// PDF/A needs fonts from a font file. Standard fonts do not work.
PDFFont font = await doc.embedFont(
  File('NotoSans-Regular.ttf').readAsBytesSync(),
  subset: true,
);
doc.addPage().drawText('Kept for a long time', x: 50, y: 750, font: font);
```

`setConformance` also takes `outputCondition`, `registryName` and `info`. A bad profile, or one that does not fit the standard, throws a `PDFLibError`. After `load`, call `setConformance` again before you save.

| Standard | For | Transparency | Colors | Attachments |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pdfX1a` | print | no | CMYK, gray and spot only | no |
| `pdfX3` | print | no | must match the profile | no |
| `pdfX4` | print | yes | must match the profile | no |
| `pdfA1b` | archive | no | must match the profile | no |
| `pdfA2b`, `pdfA2u` | archive | yes | must match the profile | PDF/A files only |
| `pdfA3b`, `pdfA3u` | archive | yes | must match the profile | any file, with `afRelationship` |

The "u" levels also need Unicode text, which fonts from a font file have. RGB colors need an RGB profile, and CMYK colors need a CMYK profile. `label` gives the name, like `PDF/X-4`, and `isPDFX` is true for the print standards.

### Printing with PDF/X

PDF/X needs a title and a trim box on each page. For PDF/X-1a, give a CMYK color to every draw call:

```dart
doc.setTitle('Flyer');
doc.setConformance(
  PDFStandard.pdfX1a,
  iccProfile: coated,
  outputConditionIdentifier: 'FOGRA39',
  registryName: 'http://www.color.org',
);
PDFPage page = doc.addPage(<double>[612, 792]);
page.setTrimBox(9, 9, 594, 774);
page.drawText('Printed in CMYK', x: 50, y: 700, font: font,
    color: cmyk(0, 0, 0, 1));
```

### Attaching files to PDF/A-3

Give a relationship and a MIME type:

```dart
await doc.attach(
  File('invoice.xml').readAsBytesSync(),
  'invoice.xml',
  mimeType: 'text/xml',
  afRelationship: AFRelationship.data,
);
```

`AFRelationship` has `source`, `data`, `alternative`, `supplement`, `encryptedPayload`, `formData`, `schema` and `unspecified`.

### Checking a document

`checkConformance` lists what is still wrong, with the page and a message. It is not a full validator:

```dart
for (ConformanceIssue issue in doc.checkConformance(PDFStandard.pdfA2b)) {
  print('${issue.kind.name}: $issue');
}
```

An issue has `kind`, `pageIndex` (null for the whole document) and `message`. The kinds of `ConformanceIssueKind` are `fontNotEmbedded`, `fontNoUnicode`, `transparency`, `color`, `pageBox`, `encryption`, `embeddedFile`, `action`, `fileId`, `metadata`, `version`, `outputIntent`, `info`, `annotation` and `other`.

### Your own XMP metadata

Save makes the XMP again from the document info, so extra XMP fields of a loaded file are lost. To keep them, start from `createXmpMetadata`, add your fields, and set the result:

```dart
String xmp = doc.createXmpMetadata(standard: PDFStandard.pdfA2b);
doc.setXmpMetadata(addMyFields(xmp));
String? current = doc.getXmpMetadata();
```

### Adding an output intent

`addOutputIntent` adds only the output intent, with none of the other steps of `setConformance`:

```dart
doc.addOutputIntent(
  subtype: OutputIntentSubtype.pdfX,
  iccProfile: coated,
  outputConditionIdentifier: 'FOGRA39',
);
```

## Errors

All errors of the package extend `PDFLibError`, which has a `message`. Wrong arguments throw an `ArgumentError` or a `RangeError`.

| Error | When |
| --- | --- |
| `PDFParsingError` | The file is not a PDF that can be read. |
| `EncryptedPDFError` | `load` got an encrypted file. |
| `RemovePageFromEmptyDocumentError` | `removePage` on a document with no pages. |
| `ForeignPageError` | `addPage` or `insertPage` got a page of another document. |
| `InvalidPDFDateStringError` | A date in the file is not valid. |
| `MissingPageContentsEmbeddingError` | An embedded page has no content. |
| `PageEmbeddingMismatchedContextError` | `embedPages` got pages of two documents. |
| `NoSuchFieldError`, `UnexpectedFieldTypeError` | A field name is missing, or the field is of another type. |
| `FieldAlreadyExistsError`, `InvalidFieldNamePartError` | A new field name is used or not valid. |
| `ExceededMaxLengthError`, `InvalidMaxLengthError` | A text or max length does not fit. |
| `RichTextFieldReadError`, `CombedTextLayoutError` | A rich text or combed field can not be read or drawn. |
| `MissingDAEntryError`, `MissingTfOperatorError` | A field has no font setting. |
| `InvalidAcroFieldValueError`, `MultiSelectValueError` | A field value is not valid. |

## Without Dox

The same code works in any Dart program. Write the bytes to a file:

```dart
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_pdf_lib/dox_pdf_lib.dart';

Future<void> main() async {
  PDFDocument doc = await PDFDocument.create();
  PDFFont font = await doc.embedFont(StandardFonts.helvetica);
  PDFPage page = doc.addPage(PageSizes.A4);
  page.drawText('Hello, PDF!', x: 50, y: 750, font: font, size: 30);
  File('hello.pdf').writeAsBytesSync(await doc.save());
}
```

# pdfme

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/packages/pdfme/

# pdfme

Make PDF files from [pdfme](https://pdfme.com) templates in Dart with `dox_pdf_me`, and send them from a Dox controller.

You design the template in the pdfme designer, then fill it with data on the server. The package reads the same template JSON as pdfme, and the PDF looks the same. It is built on [PDF Library](pdf-lib.md).

## Setup

```bash
dart pub add dox_pdf_me
```

It uses the native library of `dox_pdf_lib`, so it runs in Dart programs on macOS, Linux and Windows, not on the web, iOS or Android. On Linux, the ready-built library needs glibc 2.35 or newer. For older Linux or Alpine, see [PDF Library setup](pdf-lib.md#setup).

## Filling a template

Read the template JSON with `Template.fromJson`, and give one map of inputs for each copy of the template. Return a `DownloadableFile`, or a `StreamFile` to show the PDF in the browser tab. See [Response](../the-basic/response.md):

```dart title="lib/app/http/controllers/invoice.controller.dart"
import 'dart:convert';
import 'dart:io';
import 'dart:typed_data';

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:dox_pdf_me/dox_pdf_me.dart';

@Inject()
class InvoiceController {
  Future<DownloadableFile> show(DoxRequest req) async {
    Map<String, Object?> json =
        jsonDecode(File('storage/invoice.template.json').readAsStringSync())
            as Map<String, Object?>;

    Uint8List bytes = await generate(
      template: Template.fromJson(json),
      inputs: <Map<String, String>>[
        <String, String>{'customer': 'Jane Doe', 'total': '120.00'},
      ],
      plugins: builtInPlugins,
    );
    return DownloadableFile(
      ContentType('application', 'pdf'),
      Stream<List<int>>.value(bytes),
      'invoice.pdf',
      length: bytes.length,
    );
  }
}
```

```dart title="lib/routes/api.dart"
Route.get('/invoice.pdf', (InvoiceController c) => c.show);
```

## Generating a PDF

`generate` takes a template, the inputs, the options and the plugins, and gives the bytes of the file:

```dart
Uint8List pdf = await generate(
  template: template,
  inputs: inputs,
  options: GenerateOptions(lang: 'en', title: 'Invoice'),
  plugins: builtInPlugins,
);
```

With no plugins, only `text` schemas work. Pass `builtInPlugins` for all field types.

### Inputs

Each input map makes one copy of the template. The keys are the schema names, and every value is a string:

| Schema type | Input value |
| --- | --- |
| text, select, date, time | The text, like `'Jane'` or `'2026-11-23'`. |
| table | A JSON string of rows, from `jsonEncode(rows)`. |
| multiVariableText | A JSON string of values, like `'{"name": "Ann"}'`. |
| checkbox, radioGroup, circleMark | `'true'` to turn it on. |
| image, signature | A PNG or JPEG data URL or base64. |
| svg | The SVG text. |
| barcodes | The data of the code. |

A schema with `required: true` and no value makes `generate` throw.

### Options

| Option | What it sets |
| --- | --- |
| `font` | The fonts, by name. See [Using other fonts](#using-other-fonts). |
| `colorType` | `ColorType.rgb` (default) or `ColorType.cmyk`. |
| `lang` | The PDF language and the default date locale, like `en`. |
| `title`, `author`, `subject`, `keywords`, `creator`, `producer` | The PDF metadata. |
| `creationDate`, `modificationDate` | The PDF dates. |

Read the pdfme options JSON with `GenerateOptions.fromJson`:

```dart
GenerateOptions options =
    GenerateOptions.fromJson(<String, Object?>{'lang': 'en'});
```

## Building a template

A `Template` has a base PDF and a list of schemas for each page. Sizes and positions are in millimetres, from the top left corner:

```dart
Template template = Template(
  basePdf: const BlankPdf(),
  schemas: <List<Schema>>[
    <Schema>[
      const TextSchema(
        name: 'title',
        position: Position(20, 20),
        width: 170,
        height: 15,
        fontSize: 24,
      ),
    ],
  ],
);
```

### Reading and writing JSON

`Template.fromJson` reads both pdfme formats. Each schema becomes its typed class, and a type with no plugin becomes an `UnknownSchema`. `toJson` gives the JSON back, with the keys this package does not know:

```dart
Template template = Template.fromJson(json);
Map<String, Object?> back = template.toJson();
```

Every schema, `Position` and `Sides` also has `fromJson` and `toJson`.

### Blank pages

`BlankPdf` makes blank pages. The default is A4, 210 by 297 mm, with a padding of 10 mm:

```dart
const BlankPdf(width: 148, height: 210, padding: Sides.all(5));
```

### Static schemas

Static schemas are drawn on every page of a blank base PDF, like a header. Read-only text can use `{currentPage}` and `{totalPages}`:

```dart
BlankPdf(
  staticSchema: <Schema>[
    const TextSchema(
      name: 'footer',
      position: Position(10, 285),
      readOnly: true,
      content: '{currentPage}/{totalPages}',
    ),
  ],
);
```

Read-only text also takes input names and dotted paths, like `{order.id}`, and `{date}` and `{dateTime}`.

### A PDF file as the base

With `PdfFile`, each page of the file is one page of the template. The schemas are drawn on top:

```dart
Template template = Template(
  basePdf: PdfFile(File('form.pdf').readAsBytesSync()),
  schemas: schemas,
);
```

## Common schema options

Every schema has these options:

| Option | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | The input key. |
| `position` | The top left corner, like `Position(20, 40)`. |
| `width`, `height` | The size in mm. |
| `rotate` | Degrees, clockwise. |
| `opacity` | 0 (clear) to 1 (solid). |
| `readOnly` | Shows `content` and takes no input. |
| `required` | `generate` throws when the input has no value. |
| `content` | The value of a read-only schema. |

Colors are hex strings, like `#ff0000`, `#f00` or `#ff000080` with alpha. An empty string means no color, and a bad hex value makes `generate` throw. `Sides(top: 1, right: 2, bottom: 1, left: 2)` and `Sides.all(1)` give a size for each side of a box.

## Adding text

`TextSchema` draws text in a box. Long text wraps, and Thai, Lao, Khmer and Myanmar text breaks between words:

```dart
const TextSchema(
  name: 'note',
  position: Position(20, 60),
  width: 170,
  height: 30,
  fontSize: 11,
  alignment: Alignment.justify,
  verticalAlignment: VerticalAlignment.middle,
  fontColor: '#333333',
  padding: Sides.all(2),
);
```

| Option | Default |
| --- | --- |
| `fontName` | The fallback font. |
| `fontSize` | 13 points. |
| `alignment` | `Alignment.left`. Also `center`, `right` and `justify`. |
| `verticalAlignment` | `VerticalAlignment.top`. Also `middle` and `bottom`. |
| `lineHeight` | 1, a factor of the font size. |
| `characterSpacing` | 0 points. |
| `fontColor` | `#000000`. |
| `backgroundColor` | none. |
| `borderColor`, `borderWidth` | `#000000`, no width. |
| `padding` | none. |
| `underline`, `strikethrough` | false. |
| `dynamicFontSize` | none. See below. |

`TextSchema` also has `textFormat`, `overflow`, `fontVariants` and `fontVariantFallback`. They are kept in the JSON. Inline markdown is drawn as plain text, and `TextOverflow.expand` is drawn like `visible`.

### Fitting text to the box

`DynamicFontSize` changes the font size between `min` and `max`, so the text fits:

```dart
const TextSchema(
  name: 'title',
  position: Position(20, 20),
  dynamicFontSize: DynamicFontSize(
    min: 8,
    max: 40,
    fit: DynamicFontSizeFit.horizontal,
  ),
);
```

The defaults are 4, 72 and `DynamicFontSizeFit.vertical`.

### Text with variables

`MultiVariableTextSchema` has a text with `{name}` variables. The input is a JSON string with a value for each variable:

```dart
const MultiVariableTextSchema(
  name: 'greeting',
  position: Position(20, 20),
  width: 170,
  height: 10,
  text: 'Hello {name}, welcome to {city}!',
  variables: <String>['name', 'city'],
);
// input: {'greeting': '{"name": "Ann", "city": "Paris"}'}
```

It takes all text options. When a variable is missing, nothing is drawn. For a read-only schema, `content` is a JSON string of values. With `contentSnapshot: true`, `content` is the text to draw.

### Select

`SelectSchema` is a text field with a list of `options`. It takes all text options:

```dart
const SelectSchema(
  name: 'size',
  position: Position(20, 80),
  options: <String>['Small', 'Large'],
);
```

## Adding dates and times

`DateSchema`, `TimeSchema` and `DateTimeSchema` format the input with date-fns tokens:

```dart
const DateSchema(
  name: 'date',
  position: Position(10, 150),
  format: 'MM/dd/yyyy',
);
```

They also take `locale`, `fontName`, `alignment`, `fontSize`, `characterSpacing`, `fontColor` and `backgroundColor`. Month and day names are English for every locale, and weeks start on Sunday.

## Adding images and SVG

### Images

`ImageSchema` draws a PNG or JPEG. `objectFit` is `ObjectFit.contain` (default) or `cover`:

```dart
const ImageSchema(
  name: 'photo',
  position: Position(70, 10),
  objectFit: ObjectFit.cover,
  objectPosition: ObjectPosition.centerTop,
);
```

`ObjectPosition` has `leftTop`, `centerTop`, `rightTop`, `leftCenter`, `centerCenter` (default), `rightCenter`, `leftBottom`, `centerBottom` and `rightBottom`.

### Signatures

`SignatureSchema` is drawn like an image. Its default size is 62.5 by 37.5 mm:

```dart
const SignatureSchema(name: 'sign', position: Position(20, 250));
```

### SVG

`SvgSchema` draws the SVG text of the input:

```dart
const SvgSchema(name: 'logo', position: Position(10, 10));
```

## Drawing shapes

`LineSchema`, `RectangleSchema` and `EllipseSchema` are read-only by default:

```dart
const LineSchema(
  name: 'rule',
  position: Position(10, 40),
  width: 190,
  color: '#cccccc',
);
const RectangleSchema(
  name: 'box',
  position: Position(40, 70),
  color: '#b3e5fc',
  borderColor: '#0288d1',
  borderWidth: 1,
  radius: 5,
);
const EllipseSchema(name: 'dot', position: Position(10, 70));
```

A rectangle and an ellipse take `color`, `borderColor` and `borderWidth`. A rectangle also takes `radius`.

### Circle marks

`CircleMarkSchema` draws a circle line around the box when the input is `'true'`. `borderWidth` is the line width in mm:

```dart
const CircleMarkSchema(
  name: 'yes',
  position: Position(30, 100),
  color: '#ff0000',
  borderWidth: 0.5,
);
```

## Check boxes and radio groups

Both are on when the input is `'true'`. The radio buttons of one `group` work together in the designer:

```dart
const CheckboxSchema(name: 'agree', position: Position(25, 115));
const RadioGroupSchema(
  name: 'small',
  position: Position(25, 125),
  group: 'size',
);
```

Both take `color`.

## Adding barcodes

`BarcodeSchema` draws a barcode or a QR code as vector shapes. Pick the type with `barcodeType`:

```dart
BarcodeSchema(
  name: 'link',
  barcodeType: BarcodeType.qrcode,
  position: const Position(20, 40),
  barColor: '#000000',
);
```

| Option | Default |
| --- | --- |
| `width`, `height` | The size of the type, like 30 by 30 mm for a QR code. |
| `backgroundColor` | `#ffffff`. |
| `barColor`, `textColor` | `#000000`. |
| `includetext` | true. The text under the bars. |

The types of `BarcodeType` are `qrcode`, `japanpost`, `ean13`, `ean8`, `code39`, `code128`, `nw7`, `itf14`, `upca`, `upce`, `gs1datamatrix` and `pdf417`. Each has its default `width` and `height`, and `is2D` is true for QR code, Data Matrix and PDF417. `barcodeTypes` is the list of the type names.

A value that the barcode check refuses, like a bad EAN-13 check digit, draws nothing. A value that passes the check but can not be encoded makes `generate` throw a `BarcodeInputException` with a `message`.

## Adding tables

`TableSchema` draws a table. The input is a JSON string of rows:

```dart
const TableSchema(
  name: 'items',
  position: Position(10, 170),
  head: <String>['Item', 'Qty', 'Price'],
  headWidthPercentages: <double>[50, 20, 30],
  columnStyles: ColumnStyles(
    alignment: <int, Alignment>{1: Alignment.right, 2: Alignment.right},
  ),
);
// input: {'items': jsonEncode([['Pen', '2', '3.00']])}
```

| Option | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `head` | The head text of each column. |
| `headWidthPercentages` | The width of each column, in percent. By default, each column gets the same width (30, 30, 40 for the default head). |
| `showHead` | Shows the head (true). |
| `repeatHead` | Shows the head again on each new page (false). |
| `tableStyles` | The outer border: `TableStyles(borderColor:, borderWidth:)`. |
| `headStyles`, `bodyStyles` | The cell styles: `CellStyle.head()` and `CellStyle.body()`. |
| `columnStyles` | Styles by column index, from 0. |

On a blank base PDF, a table that is taller than its box goes on over new pages. The schemas below it move down. A row with fewer cells than the head throws.

### Cell styles

`CellStyle.head()` and `CellStyle.body()` take the text options `fontName`, `alignment`, `verticalAlignment`, `fontSize`, `lineHeight`, `characterSpacing`, `fontColor` and `backgroundColor`. They also take `borderColor`, `borderWidth` and `padding`. A body style has `alternateBackgroundColor` for every second row:

```dart
const CellStyle.body(
  fontSize: 10,
  alternateBackgroundColor: '#f5f5f5',
);
```

### Image columns

A column of `TableCellType.image` shows PNG and JPEG data URLs. `ImageHeightMode.fixed` makes the image `imageHeight` mm high, 20 by default. `ImageHeightMode.auto` follows the image ratio:

```dart
const ColumnStyles(
  cellType: <int, TableCellType>{0: TableCellType.image},
  imageHeightMode: <int, ImageHeightMode>{0: ImageHeightMode.fixed},
  imageHeight: <int, double>{0: 15},
);
```

`ColumnStyles` also has `verticalAlignment`.

## Using other fonts

Text uses Roboto by default. For other languages, give your fonts in `GenerateOptions`:

```dart
Uint8List noto = File('NotoSansJP-Regular.otf').readAsBytesSync();
Uint8List pdf = await generate(
  template: template,
  inputs: inputs,
  plugins: builtInPlugins,
  options: GenerateOptions(
    font: <String, FontSource>{
      'Roboto': FontStore.defaultFont,
      'NotoSansJP': FontSource(noto),
    },
  ),
);
```

Thai, Myanmar, Khmer, Lao, Arabic, Hebrew and Hindi text is laid out correctly. A schema picks a font with `fontName`. Letters that are not in the font show as empty boxes.

### Font options

One font has `fallback: true`, and schemas with no `fontName` use it. `subset` is true by default, so only the used letters go into the file:

```dart
FontSource(noto, fallback: true, subset: false);
```

In the options JSON, the font data can also be a base64 string or a data URI. Font URLs throw an `ArgumentError`.

## Plugins

Each schema type is a plugin. `builtInPlugins` has all types, and `defaultPlugins` has only `text`. Pick only the plugins you need:

```dart
await generate(
  template: template,
  inputs: inputs,
  plugins: <String, SchemaPlugin<Schema>>{
    'Text': const TextPlugin(),
    'QR Code': const BarcodePlugin(BarcodeType.qrcode),
  },
);
```

| Plugin | Schema type |
| --- | --- |
| `TextPlugin`, `MultiVariableTextPlugin`, `SelectPlugin` | `text`, `multiVariableText`, `select` |
| `DatePlugin`, `TimePlugin`, `DateTimePlugin` | `date`, `time`, `dateTime` |
| `ImagePlugin`, `SignaturePlugin`, `SvgPlugin` | `image`, `signature`, `svg` |
| `LinePlugin`, `RectanglePlugin`, `EllipsePlugin`, `CircleMarkPlugin` | `line`, `rectangle`, `ellipse`, `circleMark` |
| `CheckboxPlugin`, `RadioGroupPlugin` | `checkbox`, `radioGroup` |
| `BarcodePlugin(type)` | the barcode types |
| `TablePlugin` | `table` |

`findPlugin(plugins, 'qrcode')` gives the plugin for a type, or null.

### Your own schema type

A schema extends `Schema`, and its `fromJson` constructor calls `Schema.fromJson`. A plugin extends `SchemaPlugin`, reads its schema from JSON and draws it in `pdf`:

```dart
class StampSchema extends Schema {
  const StampSchema({
    required super.name,
    required super.position,
    super.width = 30,
    super.height = 10,
    this.label = 'PAID',
  });

  StampSchema.fromJson(super.json)
    : label = json['label'] is String ? json['label']! as String : 'PAID',
      super.fromJson();

  final String label;

  @override
  String get type => 'stamp';

  @override
  Map<String, Object?> toJson() => <String, Object?>{
    ...super.toJson(),
    'label': label,
  };
}

class StampPlugin extends SchemaPlugin<StampSchema> {
  const StampPlugin();

  @override
  String get type => 'stamp';

  @override
  StampSchema fromJson(Map<String, Object?> json) =>
      StampSchema.fromJson(json);

  @override
  Future<void> pdf(RenderProps<StampSchema> props) async {
    PdfLayout box = PdfLayout.of(props.schema, props.page.getHeight());
    props.page.drawRectangle(
      x: box.x,
      y: box.y,
      width: box.width,
      height: box.height,
      color: rgb(1, 0, 0),
    );
  }
}
```

Give the plugin to `Template.fromJson` and to `generate`:

```dart
Map<String, SchemaPlugin<Schema>> plugins = <String, SchemaPlugin<Schema>>{
  ...builtInPlugins,
  'Stamp': const StampPlugin(),
};
Template template = Template.fromJson(json, plugins: plugins);
await generate(template: template, inputs: inputs, plugins: plugins);
```

The package exports the [PDF Library](pdf-lib.md) API, so you can use all its drawing methods on the page.

### Render props

`RenderProps` has the input `value`, the typed `schema`, the `basePdf`, the `page`, the document `doc`, the `options`, the `fonts` and a `cache`. Draw with a built-in plugin on a changed schema with `withSchema` or `copyWith`:

```dart
await const TextPlugin().pdf(
  props.withSchema(
    TextSchema(
      name: props.schema.name,
      position: props.schema.position,
      fontColor: '#ffffff',
    ),
    value: props.schema.label,
  ),
);
```

### Fonts and cache in a plugin

`fonts.resolve` gives the font name, or the fallback name for null. `fonts.embed` gives the `PDFFont`. The `cache` keeps values for the whole document:

```dart
String name = props.fonts.resolve(null);
PDFFont font = await props.fonts.embed(name);

PDFImage? logo = props.cache.get<PDFImage>('logo');
props.cache.set<PDFImage>('logo', image);
```

`fonts.sources` has all fonts, and `fonts.fallbackName` is the name of the fallback font.

### Layout in a plugin

`PdfLayout.of` turns the box of a schema into PDF points, with the origin at the bottom left. It has `x`, `y`, `width`, `height`, `rotate` and `opacity`. `rotatePoint` turns a `Point` around another one:

```dart
PdfLayout box = PdfLayout.of(props.schema, props.page.getHeight());
Point corner = rotatePoint(
    (x: box.x, y: box.y), (x: 100, y: 100), 90);
```

## Without Dox

The same code works in any Dart program. Write the bytes to a file:

```dart
import 'dart:io';
import 'dart:typed_data';

import 'package:dox_pdf_me/dox_pdf_me.dart';

Future<void> main() async {
  Uint8List pdf = await generate(
    template: Template(
      basePdf: const BlankPdf(),
      schemas: <List<Schema>>[
        <Schema>[
          const TextSchema(
              name: 'title',
              position: Position(20, 20),
              width: 170,
              height: 15),
          BarcodeSchema(
              name: 'link',
              barcodeType: BarcodeType.qrcode,
              position: const Position(20, 40)),
        ],
      ],
    ),
    inputs: <Map<String, String>>[
      <String, String>{
        'title': 'Hello, PDF!',
        'link': 'https://dartondox.dev',
      },
    ],
    plugins: builtInPlugins,
  );
  File('hello.pdf').writeAsBytesSync(pdf);
}
```

## Next steps

- [PDF Library](pdf-lib.md): draw and edit PDF files.
- [Response](../the-basic/response.md): send files from a controller.
- [`dox_pdf_me` on pub.dev](https://pub.dev/packages/dox_pdf_me): the package.
- [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/dartondox/dox-pdf-lib): the code of the package.

# MCP server

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/packages/mcp/

# MCP server

`dox_mcp` lets AI clients like Claude, ChatGPT and IDE agents call tools in your app, with the [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) (MCP).

A **tool** is an action the AI can call, like "add an expense". You write the tool in Dart and serve it from a normal Dox route. The server follows the MCP standard `2026-07-28`: each request stands alone and gets a plain JSON reply, so every isolate and every server can answer any request. Older clients work on the same route. The server has tools only, no MCP resources, prompts or streams.

## Setup

Run:

```bash
dox add mcp
```

It adds the package and writes `lib/config/mcp.dart` with an `McpServer`, and a sample tool in `lib/app/mcp/echo.tool.dart`. It never overwrites a file. To set it up by hand, run `dart pub add dox_mcp` and write those two files yourself.

`APP_KEY` must be set in `.env`, because the server signs data with it.

### Server options

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | required | the name of the server, for the client |
| `version` | required | the version of your server, for the client |
| `tools` | required | the tools. Two tools with the same name throw an `ArgumentError` |
| `title` | none | a name for people |
| `instructions` | none | text for the model about how to use the server |
| `allowedOrigins` | none | see [Checking the origin](#checking-the-origin) |
| `onToolError` | none | see [Errors in your code](#errors-in-your-code) |
| `sessions` | `SignedMcpSessions()` | sessions of older clients, see [Sessions](#sessions) |
| `requestStateTtl` | 5 minutes | how long the answers of a question work |
| `requestStateKey` | from `APP_KEY` | the key that signs the answers |

## Making a tool

A tool extends `McpTool`. It has a `name`, a `description` for the model, an `input` schema and a `call` method that does the work:

```dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:dox_mcp/dox_mcp.dart';

class AddExpense extends McpTool {
  @override
  String get name => 'add_expense';

  @override
  String get description => 'Record an expense. Amount is in dollars.';

  @override
  ObjectSchema get input => v.object(<String, Schema<Object?>>{
    'amount': v.num().positive().describe('Amount, like 12.50.'),
    'note': v.string().max(500).optional(),
  });

  @override
  Future<McpToolResult> call(
    Map<String, dynamic> args,
    McpContext context,
  ) async {
    // ... save it
    return McpToolResult.text('Recorded ${args['amount']}.');
  }
}
```

The `input` is a [validation](validation.md) schema. The client sees it as JSON Schema, and Dox checks every call before `call` runs. A tool can also have a `title` for people, and `annotations` like `{'readOnlyHint': true}`.

### Small tools

A small tool can be a function. Use `McpTool.of`:

```dart
McpTool.of(
  name: 'echo',
  description: 'Say the text back.',
  input: v.object(<String, Schema<Object?>>{'text': v.string()}),
  handler: (Map<String, dynamic> args, McpContext context) {
    return McpToolResult.text(args['text'] as String);
  },
);
```

### Tools that take a DTO

Extend `McpDtoTool<T>` to use a [`@Dto`](../the-basic/dto.md) class as the input. `handle` gets the typed object, and `@Describe` explains a field to the model:

```dart
@Dto()
class NewCategory {
  @Describe('The category name, like Food.')
  @Length(min: 1, max: 50)
  final String name;

  @Describe('A color, like #1a2b3c.')
  @HexColor()
  final String color;

  const NewCategory({required this.name, required this.color});

  static const DtoSchema<NewCategory> schema = $NewCategoryDto;
}

class CreateCategory extends McpDtoTool<NewCategory> {
  @override
  String get name => 'create_category';

  @override
  String get description => 'Add a category.';

  @override
  DtoSchema<NewCategory> get dto => NewCategory.schema;

  @override
  Future<McpToolResult> handle(
      NewCategory input, McpContext context) async {
    // ... save it
    return McpToolResult.text('Added ${input.name}.');
  }
}
```

Dox checks the arguments like a DTO in a controller, also with async rules like `@Unique` and `@Exists`.

## Tool results

A tool returns an `McpToolResult`.

### Text

`McpToolResult.text` sends one text:

```dart
return McpToolResult.text('Recorded 12.50.');
```

### JSON

`McpToolResult.json` sends a value as JSON text. A map is also sent as structured content:

```dart
return McpToolResult.json(<String, dynamic>{'id': 7, 'amount': 12.5});
```

### Images

For other content, give a list of `McpContent` items:

```dart
return McpToolResult(<McpContent>[
  McpContent.text('The chart of this month:'),
  McpContent.image(base64Png, 'image/png'),
]);
```

## Errors

### Errors the model can fix

Return `McpToolResult.error` when the model can try again, like after a bad id. The model sees the text:

```dart
return McpToolResult.error('No expense has id 7.');
```

Bad arguments work the same way, with no code. The model gets one line with each problem:

```text
Input validation error: Invalid arguments for tool create_category: name: The name is required; color: The color must be a hex color like #1a2b3c
```

### Errors in your code

If a tool throws, the client gets only `Tool failed`, because the real error can hold SQL or host names. The real error is shown only when `APP_ENV` is `development` or `local`. Set `onToolError` to log it:

```dart
McpServer(
  name: 'my-app',
  version: '1.0.0',
  tools: <McpTool>[AddExpense()],
  onToolError: (String tool, Object error, StackTrace stack) {
    Logger.danger('MCP tool $tool failed: $error');
  },
);
```

## Adding the route

Make one `McpServer` with your tools, and call `handle` from a route:

```dart
final McpServer mcp = McpServer(
  name: 'my-app',
  version: '1.0.0',
  tools: <McpTool>[AddExpense(), CreateCategory()],
  allowedOrigins: <String>['https://my.app'],
);

Route.match(<String>['GET', 'POST', 'DELETE'], '/mcp', (DoxRequest req) {
  return mcp.handle(req);
});
```

This route is open to everyone. That is fine only for a public server with no users.

### Checking who calls

The MCP route has no auth. Find the user before `handle`, then give `auth` (the user) and `scope` (a text that names the user):

```dart
Route.match(<String>['GET', 'POST', 'DELETE'], '/mcp',
    (DoxRequest req) async {
  User? user = await findUser(req.header('authorization'));
  if (user == null) return response('Invalid token').statusCode(401);
  return mcp.handle(req, auth: user, scope: 'user:${user.id}');
});
```

In a tool, read the user back:

```dart
User user = context.authAs<User>();
```

!!! warning
    An app with users must always give `scope`. The server binds the data it signs to the scope. Without it, one user can send data that was signed for another user.

Proxies write a token in the URL to their logs, so send tokens in a header. To let clients sign in by themselves, use [OAuth](#signing-in-with-oauth).

## Reading the client

### What the client can do

`context.clientCapabilities` tells what the client supports:

```dart
McpClientCapabilities? client = context.clientCapabilities;
if (client != null && client.elicitationForm) {
  // the client can show a form to the user
}
```

It has `elicitation`, `elicitationForm`, `elicitationUrl`, `sampling`, `roots` and `extensions`. For other paths, `has` checks one, like `client.has(<String>['sampling', 'tools'])`. It is null for older clients.

### Which client it is

`context.clientInfo` gives the name and version of the client, or null:

```dart
String name = context.clientInfo?.name ?? 'unknown';
```

!!! warning
    The client says this about itself. Never use it for security.

## Asking the user

A tool can stop and ask the user a question, like "Delete this expense?". The client shows it, then calls the tool again with the answer. Make the question one time, in a `static final` field. The same object asks the question and reads the answer:

```dart
class DeleteExpense extends McpTool {
  static final McpInput<bool> confirmDelete = McpInput.confirm(
    'Delete this expense?',
  );

  // name, description, input ...

  @override
  Future<McpToolResult> call(
    Map<String, dynamic> args,
    McpContext context,
  ) async {
    McpAnswer<bool>? answer = context.answer(confirmDelete);
    if (answer == null) {
      return McpToolResult.inputRequired(
          <McpInput<Object?>>[confirmDelete]);
    }
    return switch (answer) {
      McpAccepted<bool>(value: true) => _delete(args),
      McpAccepted<bool>() ||
      McpDeclined<bool>() ||
      McpCancelled<bool>() => McpToolResult.text('Cancelled'),
    };
  }
}
```

The tool runs two times: first it asks, then `context.answer` gives the answer. It works the same in `McpDtoTool.handle`. The answers are signed, work only for the same user, tool and arguments, and expire after `requestStateTtl`.

!!! warning
    The answers can be sent again until they expire. A tool that must run only one time, like a payment, must check that itself.

A question the client can not show gets an error that names the missing capability. An older client can not answer a question.

### Reading the answer

`context.answer` gives null when there is no answer yet, or the answer can not be read (like a form that fails the DTO rules). Then return `McpToolResult.inputRequired`. Else the answer is one of three classes:

- `McpAccepted<T>`: the user answered. `value` holds the answer.
- `McpDeclined<T>`: the user said no.
- `McpCancelled<T>`: the user closed the question.

### Yes or no

`McpInput.confirm` asks a yes or no question. The answer is a bool:

```dart
static final McpInput<bool> confirmDelete = McpInput.confirm(
  'Delete this expense?',
);
```

### Text

`McpInput.text` asks for one line of text. The answer is a string:

```dart
static final McpInput<String> askNote = McpInput.text('Add a note:');
```

### Number

`McpInput.number` asks for a number. The answer is a `num`:

```dart
static final McpInput<num> askAmount = McpInput.number('How much was it?');
```

### Choice

`McpInput.choice` lets the user pick one value of an enum:

```dart
enum Color { red, green, blue }

static final McpInput<Color> askColor = McpInput.choice(
  'Pick a color:',
  Color.values,
);
```

### Form

`McpInput.form` asks for many fields at once, from a `@Dto` class. The answer is the DTO object, checked by its rules:

```dart
static final McpInput<NewExpense> askExpense = McpInput.form(
  'New expense',
  NewExpense.schema,
);
```

A form has flat fields only: text, numbers, booleans, enums and lists of enum values. The DTO can not have a nested object or async rules like `@Unique`.

!!! warning
    Never ask for a password or a key in a form. Use a URL for that.

### URL

`McpInput.url` sends the user to a page, like a sign-in to another service. Use it for data that must not go through the client:

```dart
static final McpInput<void> connectBank = McpInput.url(
  'Connect your bank account.',
  'https://my.app/bank/connect',
);
```

`McpAccepted` means only that the user agreed to open the page, so check the result in your database. Never put a secret in the URL.

### Many questions

To ask many things at once, give a longer list. Read each answer with its own input. Two inputs with the same message throw an `ArgumentError`:

```dart
McpAnswer<String>? note = context.answer(askNote);
McpAnswer<num>? amount = context.answer(askAmount);
if (note == null || amount == null) {
  return McpToolResult.inputRequired(
      <McpInput<Object?>>[askNote, askAmount]);
}
```

A tool can also ask one question per round. Answers of earlier rounds are kept.

### Custom inputs

For a kind of input that `dox_mcp` does not have, extend `McpCustomInput<T>`. Give the `method`, the `capability` the client needs, the request as `toJson`, and `parse` to read the result:

```dart
class ListRoots extends McpCustomInput<List<String>> {
  @override
  String get method => 'roots/list';

  @override
  List<String> get capability => <String>['roots'];

  @override
  Map<String, Object?> toJson() {
    return <String, Object?>{};
  }

  @override
  List<String> parse(Map<String, Object?> result) {
    return <String>[
      for (Object? root in result['roots']! as List<Object?>)
        (root! as Map<String, Object?>)['uri']! as String,
    ];
  }
}
```

Use it like any other input, with `context.answer` and `McpToolResult.inputRequired`.

## Signing in with OAuth

With `McpOAuth`, you give the client only the address, like `https://my.app/mcp`. The client finds the rest and signs the user in, with OAuth 2.1 and PKCE. Your app makes the tokens and shows the consent page.

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `issuer` | required | the address of your app, like `https://my.app` |
| `tokens` | required | your `McpOAuthTokens` |
| `codes` | the default cache store | the cache store for the one-time codes |
| `mcpPath` | `/mcp` | the path of the MCP route |
| `authorizePage` | `<issuer>/oauth/authorize` | the address of the consent page |
| `codeTtl` | 1 minute | how long a code works |
| `resourceName` | none | a name for the server in the discovery file |
| `allowedClientHosts` | none | see [How clients sign in](#how-clients-sign-in) |
| `maxClientFetches` | 8 | see [How clients sign in](#how-clients-sign-in) |
| `maxClientFetchesPerHost` | 2 | see [How clients sign in](#how-clients-sign-in) |
| `clientCacheMaxAge` | 5 minutes | the longest time a client document is kept in memory |
| `clientFetcher` | `McpOAuthHttpFetcher()` | loads client documents. Tests give fake documents |

### Tokens

Implement `McpOAuthTokens`. `issue` makes a token after the user said yes, and can throw an `McpOAuthException`, like `access_denied`. `verify` gives what a token stands for, like the user, or null. Keep only a hash of the token:

```dart
class McpTokens extends McpOAuthTokens {
  @override
  Future<String> issue(McpOAuthGrant grant) async {
    String token = newRandomToken(); // your own long random text
    // ... save Hash.sha256(token) for the user grant.subject
    return token;
  }

  @override
  Future<Object?> verify(String token) async {
    // ... find the user of this token, or return null
    return null;
  }
}
```

!!! warning
    Keep MCP tokens apart from your other tokens, like in their own table. `verify` must accept only a token that `issue` made, so an API token does not work on the MCP route.

There is no refresh token. To revoke a client, delete its token.

### Routes

Make an `McpOAuth` and call `routes` in a router with no prefix, because clients look for `/.well-known/...` at the root of the host. Then check the token on the MCP route:

```dart
final McpOAuth oauth = McpOAuth(
  issuer: 'https://my.app',
  tokens: McpTokens(),
  codes: Cache().store('redis'),
);

class McpRouter extends Router {
  @override
  void register() {
    oauth.routes();
    Route.match(<String>['GET', 'POST', 'DELETE'], '/mcp', handleMcp);
  }
}

Future<DoxResponse> handleMcp(DoxRequest req) async {
  User? user = await oauth.authenticate(req) as User?;
  if (user == null) return oauth.unauthorized();
  return mcp.handle(req, auth: user, scope: 'user:${user.id}');
}
```

`authenticate` reads the `Authorization: Bearer` header and calls your `verify`. `unauthorized` answers 401 and tells the client where to sign in. All isolates must share the `codes` [cache store](../digging-deeper/cache.md), so use `file` on one server, or `redis` on many. The OAuth routes answer any origin and read no cookie.

Add a [rate limit](../security/rate-limiting.md) to the OAuth routes and the MCP route, because anyone can call `/oauth/token`, and each new `client_id` address makes the server load a file:

```dart
Route.middleware(<dynamic>[RateLimit(max: 30)], oauth.routes);
```

### The consent page

The client sends the browser to `<issuer>/oauth/authorize`. This page is yours: the person signs in there the usual way, then says yes or no. The page gets `client_id`, `redirect_uri`, `state`, `code_challenge`, `code_challenge_method` and `resource` in the query.

`verifyClient` gives the client for the page. It throws when the client or the redirect address is wrong:

```dart
McpOAuthClient client = await oauth.verifyClient(clientId, redirectUri);
// show client.name next to client.host, and the host of redirectUri
```

`client.host` is the host of the client address, like `claude.ai`. It is null for an older client that registered. `findClient` gives the client with no redirect check. The older `checkClient` and `deny` are not async: when the client document is not loaded yet, they start the load and throw `invalid_client`. Use `verifyClient` and `denyClient` in new code.

On yes, call `approve`. It gives the address to send the browser to:

```dart
String url = await oauth.approve(
  subject: '${user.id}',
  clientId: clientId,
  redirectUri: redirectUri,
  codeChallenge: codeChallenge,
  codeChallengeMethod: codeChallengeMethod,
  state: state,
  resource: resource,
);
return redirect(url);
```

On no, call `denyClient`:

```dart
String url = await oauth.denyClient(
  clientId: clientId,
  redirectUri: redirectUri,
  state: state,
);
```

The consent page decides who gets access, so keep these rules:

- Put the yes route behind your login and [CSRF protection](../security/csrf.md). Without it, another site can make a signed-in person say yes.
- Show the host of the redirect address, and the host of the `client_id` when it is an `https` address. The client chooses its own name, so the host is the part a person can trust.
- HTML-escape the client name before you print it.

A redirect address must be `https`, or `http` on `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` or `[::1]`.

### How clients sign in

A client names itself with a **client metadata document**. Its `client_id` is an `https` address of a JSON file with the name of the client and its redirect addresses. `dox_mcp` loads the file and checks it, so it stores nothing. Older clients can also register at `POST /oauth/register`.

The server loads only small files from public hosts, and follows no redirects. It keeps a document for its `Cache-Control: max-age`, at most `clientCacheMaxAge`. If the host does not answer, it uses the last document for up to 1 hour. A failed load is not tried again for 1 minute. These options limit the loads:

```dart
McpOAuth(
  issuer: 'https://my.app',
  tokens: McpTokens(),
  allowedClientHosts: <String>{'claude.ai'},
  maxClientFetches: 4,
);
```

- `allowedClientHosts`: load client documents from these hosts only. By default, any public host works. It does not block clients that register.
- `maxClientFetches`: how many documents one isolate loads at the same time. When all are busy, a new client is refused at once.
- `maxClientFetchesPerHost`: how many of these loads can go to one host.
- `McpOAuthHttpFetcher(maxFetchesPerAddress:)`: how many loads can go to one IP address. The default is 2.

## Checking the origin

A web page on another site can try to call your MCP server from the browser of a user. Set `allowedOrigins` to your own sites to stop it, also for a server on `localhost` or a private network:

```dart
McpServer(
  name: 'my-app',
  version: '1.0.0',
  tools: <McpTool>[AddExpense()],
  allowedOrigins: <String>['https://my.app'],
);
```

A request with another `Origin` header gets 403. A request with no `Origin` is not from a browser, so it can always connect. When `allowedOrigins` is not set, the server writes a warning one time at start.

## Sessions

Older clients (MCP `2025-11-25` and before) start with `initialize` and use a session. That is why the route takes GET, POST and DELETE. `SignedMcpSessions` signs each session id with a key from `APP_KEY`, so it stores nothing. A new `APP_KEY` stops all sessions, and clients start new ones.

To make DELETE end a session, give a cache store that all isolates share:

```dart
McpServer(
  name: 'my-app',
  version: '1.0.0',
  tools: <McpTool>[AddExpense()],
  sessions: SignedMcpSessions(ended: Cache().store('redis')),
);
```

For another kind of session, implement `McpSessions`. A batch from an older client can have at most 50 messages.

## Next steps

- [Authentication](../security/authentication.md): users, tokens and login in a Dox app.
- [Validation](validation.md): the schemas of tool arguments.
- [AI agents](../getting-started/ai-agents.md): help an AI agent write Dox code.
