# Testing with a database

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/guides/testing-with-database/

# Testing with a database

Run model tests against a real database: SQLite for fast local tests, or a test Postgres for the real thing.

A real database finds bugs that a mock can not find, like a wrong column name. The migrations run one time, and every test starts with empty tables.

## What you need

- A Dox app (`dox create my_app`). A new app has the `User` model, a `users` migration in `db/migration` and the `test` package.

## 1. Check the migration

The test makes its tables from your migrations. A new app has this one, with another date in the file name:

```dart title="db/migration/2026_10_22_000000_create_users_table.dart"
import 'package:dox_migration/dox_migration.dart';

class CreateUsersTable extends Migration {
  @override
  Future<void> up(Schema schema) async {
    await schema.create('users', (Table table) {
      table.id();
      table.string('name');
      table.string('email').unique();
      table.string('password');
      table.timestamps();
      table.softDeletes();
    });
  }

  @override
  Future<void> down(Schema schema) async {
    await schema.dropIfExists('users');
  }
}
```

The test imports the list of all migrations from `db/migration/migrations.dart`. `dox make:migration` updates this list.

## 2. Write the test (SQLite)

Start with SQLite, because it needs no server. The test has its own database config:

```dart title="test/user_test.dart"
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:dox_migration/dox_migration.dart';
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';
import 'package:dox_orm/testing.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/models/user/user.model.dart';
import 'package:test/test.dart';

import '../db/migration/migrations.dart';

/// One SQLite file for this test file. No server, no Postgres.
const String dbFile = 'storage/test.sqlite';

DatabaseConfig testDatabase = DatabaseConfig(
  connection: 'sqlite',
  connections: <String, ConnectionConfig>{
    'sqlite': ConnectionConfig(
      driver: Driver.sqlite,
      database: dbFile,
      debug: false,
    ),
  },
);

Future<void> deleteDbFile() async {
  for (String suffix in <String>['', '-wal', '-shm']) {
    File file = File('$dbFile$suffix');
    if (await file.exists()) await file.delete();
  }
}

void main() {
  setUpAll(() async {
    await deleteDbFile();
    await Migrator(
      migrations: migrations,
      config: testDatabase.getConnectionConfig(),
    ).migrate();
    SqlQueryBuilder.initializeWithDatabaseConfig(testDatabase);
  });

  // every test starts with empty tables
  setUp(refreshDatabase);

  tearDownAll(() async {
    await deleteDbFile();
  });

  test('saves and finds a user', () async {
    User user = User()
      ..name = 'Ann'
      ..email = 'ann@example.com'
      ..password = Hash.make('secret123');
    await user.save();

    User? found = await User().where('email', 'ann@example.com').getFirst();
    expect(found?.id, user.id);
    expect(found?.name, 'Ann');
    expect(Hash.verify('secret123', found!.password!), isTrue);
  });

  test('the tables are empty again', () async {
    expect(await User().count(), 0);
  });
}
```

`refreshDatabase()` empties every table except the migrations table, and starts the ids at 1 again.

Put `storage/test.sqlite` in `.gitignore`. Use a file, not `:memory:`, because the migrator and the ORM each open their own connection.

## 3. Run it

Run the test file:

```bash
dart test test/user_test.dart
```

## Check it

The migrations run, and then the tests pass:

```text
00:00 +0: (setUpAll)
Migrating: 2026_10_22_000000_create_users_table
Migrated: 2026_10_22_000000_create_users_table
Migrating: 2026_10_23_000000_create_queue_tables
Migrated: 2026_10_23_000000_create_queue_tables
00:00 +1: saves and finds a user
00:00 +2: the tables are empty again
00:00 +2: All tests passed!
```

## The same test on Postgres

If your app runs on Postgres in production, test on Postgres too. Use a separate database for tests, because the tests delete all rows.

Start a test database with Docker:

```bash
docker run -d --name my_app_test -p 5433:5432 \
  -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres -e POSTGRES_DB=my_app_test postgres:18
```

Change the config at the top of the test:

```dart
DatabaseConfig testDatabase = DatabaseConfig(
  connection: 'postgres',
  connections: <String, ConnectionConfig>{
    'postgres': ConnectionConfig(
      driver: Driver.postgres,
      host: 'localhost',
      port: 5433,
      user: 'postgres',
      password: 'postgres',
      database: 'my_app_test',
      debug: false,
    ),
  },
);
```

Delete `deleteDbFile()` and its two calls. The rest of the test stays the same.

## Many test files

Test files run at the same time, so two files that use the same table can break each other. Give each file its own SQLite file, or run the files one by one:

```bash
dart test --concurrency=1
```

## Test a route with the database

This test uses the `/api/users` route of the [Pagination](pagination.md) guide. `DoxTestClient` starts the app in the test, with the config in `lib/config/database.dart`:

```dart title="test/api_test.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/testing.dart';
import 'package:dox_migration/dox_migration.dart';
import 'package:dox_orm/testing.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/app.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/database.dart';
import 'package:test/test.dart';

import '../db/migration/migrations.dart';

void main() {
  late DoxTestClient client;

  setUpAll(() async {
    await Migrator(
      migrations: migrations,
      config: databaseConfig.getConnectionConfig(),
    ).migrate();
    client = await DoxTestClient.start(appConfig);
  });

  setUp(refreshDatabase);

  tearDownAll(() async {
    await client.close();
  });

  test('GET /api/users has no rows', () async {
    TestResponse res = await client.get('/api/users');
    res.expectStatus(200);
    expect(res.json['data'], isEmpty);
  });
}
```

Pick the test database with env variables:

```bash
DB_CONNECTION=sqlite DB_NAME=storage/test.sqlite \
    dart test test/api_test.dart
```

- [Migration](../database/migration.md): write migrations.
- [Database: SQLite](../database/index.md#sqlite): the SQLite settings.

# Share code with Flutter

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/guides/share-code-with-flutter/

# Share code with Flutter

Put a `@Dto` class in a shared Dart package, so the Dox server and the Flutter app check input with the same rules and error messages.

The app checks the form, so the user sees an error at once. The server checks the same input again, because it can not trust the client. The generated [DTO](../the-basic/dto.md) code is pure Dart, so it runs in Flutter and on the web.

## What you need

- A Dox app (`dox create server`). Here it is in the `server` folder.
- A Flutter app (`flutter create app`). Here it is in the `app` folder.

## The layout

The three parts live next to each other in one folder:

```text
my_blog/
  packages/
    blog_shared/     # the DTOs. Pure Dart.
  server/            # the Dox app
  app/               # the Flutter app
```

The app and the server use the same DTO:

<div class="dox-fan dox-fan--via" role="group" aria-label="The app and the server use the shared package">
  <div class="dox-fan__top"><strong>packages/blog_shared</strong><span>SaveBlog and SaveBlog.schema</span></div>
  <div class="dox-fan__cols">
    <ol><li><strong>app: Flutter</strong><span>checks the form</span></li></ol>
    <ol data-via="POST /api/blogs (JSON)"><li><strong>server: Dox</strong><span>checks the request</span></li></ol>
  </div>
</div>

## 1. The shared package

Make a plain Dart package for the DTOs:

```yaml title="packages/blog_shared/pubspec.yaml"
name: blog_shared
description: DTOs shared by the Dox server and the Flutter app.
version: 0.1.0
publish_to: none

environment:
  sdk: ^3.13.0

```

Add the packages:

```bash
cd packages/blog_shared
dart pub add dox_validation
dart pub add dev:dox_builder dev:build_runner
```

Now write the DTO. Import `dox_validation`, not `dox_core`, because `dox_core` does not run in Flutter:

```dart title="packages/blog_shared/lib/src/save_blog.dart"
import 'package:dox_validation/dox_validation.dart';

part 'save_blog.g.dart';

/// A new blog post. The server and the app check it with the same rules.
@Dto()
class SaveBlog {
  @Trim()
  @Length(min: 3, max: 255)
  final String title;

  @Trim()
  @MinLength(10)
  final String description;

  const SaveBlog({required this.title, required this.description});

  static const DtoSchema<SaveBlog> schema = $SaveBlogDto;
}
```

Export the DTOs. Also export `dox_validation`, so the app gets `ParseResult` and `ValidationException` from the same import:

```dart title="packages/blog_shared/lib/blog_shared.dart"
export 'package:dox_validation/dox_validation.dart';

export 'src/save_blog.dart';
```

Generate the code:

```bash
cd packages/blog_shared
dart pub get
dart run build_runner build
```

This writes `lib/src/save_blog.g.dart` and `lib/generated/dtos.g.dart`, the list of every DTO in the package. Commit both files, so the Flutter app does not need to run the generator.

`@Unique` and `@Exists` come from `dox_orm`, which the app can not import. Check them on the server only.

## 2. The Dox server

Add the shared package to the dependencies of the server:

```yaml title="server/pubspec.yaml"
dependencies:
  # ... the packages of the new app stay
  blog_shared:
    path: ../packages/blog_shared
```

Run `dart pub get`.

Add the DTO list of the shared package to the `dtos` list of `AppConfig`:

```dart title="server/lib/config/app.dart"
import 'package:blog_shared/generated/dtos.g.dart' as shared;
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:server/generated/dtos.g.dart';

AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  // ...
  dtos: <DtoSchema<Object>>[...dtos, ...shared.dtos],
);
```

The controller asks for `SaveBlog` like any other DTO. Bad input gets 422:

```dart title="server/lib/app/http/controllers/blog.controller.dart"
import 'package:blog_shared/blog_shared.dart' show SaveBlog;
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

@Inject()
class BlogController {
  Future<Map<String, dynamic>> store(SaveBlog body) async {
    // body.title is already trimmed and checked.
    return <String, dynamic>{'title': body.title, 'saved': true};
  }
}
```

Use `show SaveBlog` in server code, because `dox_core` and `blog_shared` both export a `ValidationException` class.

Add the route:

```dart title="server/lib/routes/api.dart"
Route.post('/blogs', (BlogController c) => c.store);
```

A bad request gets the errors as `{"key": "message"}`:

```text
POST /api/blogs  {"title": "ab", "description": "short"}
422 {"title":"The title must be between 3 and 255 characters",
     "description":"The description must be at least 10 characters"}
```

## 3. The Flutter app

Add the shared package to the app:

```yaml title="app/pubspec.yaml"
name: app
publish_to: none

environment:
  sdk: ^3.13.0

dependencies:
  flutter:
    sdk: flutter
  http: ^1.6.0
  blog_shared:
    path: ../packages/blog_shared
```

The widget checks the form with `SaveBlog.schema.safeParse()`, and sends only good input. `result.errors` has the same shape as the 422 body of the server:

```dart title="app/lib/new_blog_form.dart"
import 'dart:convert';

import 'package:blog_shared/blog_shared.dart';
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:http/http.dart' as http;

class NewBlogForm extends StatefulWidget {
  const NewBlogForm({super.key});

  @override
  State<NewBlogForm> createState() {
    return _NewBlogFormState();
  }
}

class _NewBlogFormState extends State<NewBlogForm> {
  final TextEditingController _title = TextEditingController();
  final TextEditingController _description = TextEditingController();
  Map<String, String> _errors = <String, String>{};

  Future<void> _submit() async {
    ParseResult<SaveBlog> result =
        SaveBlog.schema.safeParse(<String, dynamic>{
      'title': _title.text,
      'description': _description.text,
    });
    if (!result.success) {
      setState(() {
        _errors = result.errors;
      });
      return;
    }

    http.Response response = await http.post(
      Uri.parse('https://api.example.com/api/blogs'),
      headers: <String, String>{'Content-Type': 'application/json'},
      body: jsonEncode(SaveBlog.schema.toMap(result.value!)),
    );
    setState(() {
      _errors = response.statusCode == 422
          ? Map<String, String>.from(jsonDecode(response.body) as Map)
          : <String, String>{};
    });
  }

  @override
  void dispose() {
    _title.dispose();
    _description.dispose();
    super.dispose();
  }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return Column(
      children: <Widget>[
        TextField(
          controller: _title,
          decoration: InputDecoration(
              labelText: 'Title', errorText: _errors['title']),
        ),
        TextField(
          controller: _description,
          decoration: InputDecoration(
              labelText: 'Description',
              errorText: _errors['description']),
        ),
        ElevatedButton(onPressed: _submit, child: const Text('Save')),
      ],
    );
  }
}
```

## Other schema methods

The schema has more methods than `safeParse`:

- `parse` throws a `ValidationException` when the input is bad.
- `toMap` gives the JSON map to send.
- `toJsonSchema` gives the JSON Schema of the DTO.

If the DTO has an async `validate()` method, use `safeParseAsync` or `parseAsync`.

## Next steps

- [Validation](../the-basic/validation.md): all the rules.
- [dox_validation](../packages/validation.md): all the schema methods.

# API docs with OpenAPI

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/guides/api-docs-with-openapi/

# API docs with OpenAPI

Turn on OpenAPI docs for the blog API, open the docs page, and make the docs better with annotations.

Dox makes the docs from your code, so they stay up to date.

## What you need

- The blog API from the [tutorial](../tutorial/01-create-project.md), or any Dox app.
- `build_runner` and `dox_builder`. A new app has both, and `dox_core` has `dox_openapi`.

## 1. Write the config

`build_runner` writes `openApiRegistry` to `lib/generated/openapi.g.dart`, with your routes, DTOs and models. Pass it to an `OpenApiConfig`:

```dart title="lib/config/openapi.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:blog/generated/openapi.g.dart';

OpenApiConfig openApi = OpenApiConfig(
  info: Info(title: 'Blog API', version: '1.0.0'),
  registry: openApiRegistry,
);
```

Add it to `AppConfig`:

```dart title="lib/config/app.dart"
import 'package:blog/config/openapi.dart';

AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  // ...
  /// OpenAPI docs (config/openapi.dart)
  openApi: openApi,
);
```

## 2. Build and start

Build the code and start the server:

```bash
dart run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs
dox serve
```

The docs routes are on, because `.env` has `APP_ENV=development`.

## 3. Open the docs page

Open `http://localhost:3000/docs`. It is a [Scalar](https://github.com/scalar/scalar) page with every route and "Try it" buttons. The app now has three new routes:

| Route | What it gives |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /docs` | the Scalar docs page (HTML) |
| `GET /openapi.json` | the OpenAPI 3.1 document as JSON |
| `GET /openapi.yaml` | the same document as YAML |

## 4. Read the JSON

Get the document:

```bash
curl http://localhost:3000/openapi.json
```

This is the top level for the blog API, made shorter:

```json
{
  "openapi": "3.1.0",
  "info": {"title": "Blog API", "version": "1.0.0"},
  "paths": {
    "/api/ping": {},
    "/api/posts": {},
    "/api/posts/{id}": {},
    "/api/auth/register": {},
    "/api/auth/login": {},
    "/api/auth/user": {},
    "/ping": {}
  },
  "components": {
    "schemas": {
      "Post": {},
      "SavePost": {},
      "RegisterUser": {},
      "LoginUser": {},
      "User": {},
      "ValidationError": {}
    },
    "securitySchemes": {
      "bearerAuth": {"type": "http", "scheme": "bearer"}
    }
  }
}
```

This is `POST /api/posts`. You wrote no docs code for it:

```json
{
  "tags": ["Post"],
  "summary": "POST /api/posts",
  "operationId": "PostController.store",
  "requestBody": {
    "required": true,
    "content": {
      "application/json": {
        "schema": {"$ref": "#/components/schemas/SavePost"}
      }
    }
  },
  "responses": {
    "200": {"description": "Successful response"},
    "401": {
      "description": "Not logged in",
      "content": {
        "application/json": {
          "schema": {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
              "code": {"type": "string"},
              "message": {"type": "string"}
            }
          }
        }
      }
    },
    "422": {
      "description": "Validation failed",
      "content": {
        "application/json": {
          "schema": {"$ref": "#/components/schemas/ValidationError"}
        }
      }
    },
    "500": {"description": "Server error"}
  },
  "security": [{"bearerAuth": []}]
}
```

Each part comes from your code:

| Part | Comes from |
| --- | --- |
| `tags: ["Post"]` | the class name `PostController`, without `Controller` |
| `summary` | no `@Summary` here, so the first line of the `///` comment: `/// POST /api/posts` |
| `requestBody` | the argument `SavePost body` of `store` |
| 401 and `bearerAuth` | `AuthMiddleware` on the route |
| 422 | the route has a request class |
| 200 with no body | `store` returns `DoxResponse`, so the builder can not see the body. Step 6 fixes this |

The `Can` middleware or a `req.authorize(...)` call gives 401 and 403. `GuestMiddleware` and `ValidateSignature` give 403. A `req.validateSchema(...)` call gives 422.

## 5. See how a DTO becomes a schema

Dox turns each [DTO](../the-basic/dto.md) into a schema with the rules of every field. This is the `SavePost` DTO of the tutorial:

```dart title="lib/app/dtos/save_post/save_post.dto.dart"
@Dto()
class SavePost {
  @Trim()
  @Length(min: 3, max: 100)
  final String title;

  @Trim()
  @MinLength(10)
  final String body;

  const SavePost({required this.title, required this.body});

  static const DtoSchema<SavePost> schema = $SavePostDto;
}
```

And this is its schema in `/openapi.json`:

```json
"SavePost": {
  "type": "object",
  "title": "SavePost",
  "properties": {
    "title": {"type": "string", "minLength": 3, "maxLength": 100},
    "body": {"type": "string", "minLength": 10}
  },
  "required": ["title", "body"]
}
```

Each rule becomes a schema key:

| In the DTO | In the schema |
| --- | --- |
| `String title` (not nullable) | `"type": "string"` and `title` in `required` |
| `@Length(min: 3, max: 100)` | `"minLength": 3, "maxLength": 100` |
| `@MinLength(10)` | `"minLength": 10` |
| `@Email()` (in `RegisterUser`) | `"format": "email"` |
| `@Describe('...')` or `/// A comment` | `"description"`. `@Describe` wins over the comment |
| `@Trim()`, `@Lowercase()`, `@Unique(...)` | nothing. They change or check the value on the server only |

A model becomes a schema too. Keys in `hidden` are left out, so `User` has no `password`. When you change a rule, run `build_runner` again.

## 6. Make the docs better

Add `@Summary`, `@Description`, `@Tags` and `@Response` to a controller method. They fill the gaps that the builder can not see, like the body of a `DoxResponse`:

```dart title="lib/app/http/controllers/post.controller.dart"
@Inject()
class PostController {
  @Summary('List all posts')
  @Description('Newest posts are not first. There is no paging yet.')
  Future<List<Post>> index(DoxRequest req) async {
    return Post().all();
  }

  @Summary('Create a post')
  @Tags(<String>['Posts'])
  @Response(201, Post, description: 'The new post')
  Future<DoxResponse> store(SavePost body) async {
    Post post = Post()
      ..title = body.title
      ..body = body.body;
    await post.save();
    return response(post).statusCode(201);
  }

  // ...
}
```

Run `dart run build_runner build` again and restart the app. The result:

```json
"get": {
  "tags": ["Post"],
  "summary": "List all posts",
  "description": "Newest posts are not first. There is no paging yet.",
  "operationId": "PostController.index",
  "responses": {
    "200": {
      "description": "Successful response",
      "content": {
        "application/json": {
          "schema": {
            "type": "array",
            "items": {"$ref": "#/components/schemas/Post"}
          }
        }
      }
    },
    "500": {}
  }
},
"post": {
  "tags": ["Posts"],
  "summary": "Create a post",
  "operationId": "PostController.store",
  "responses": {
    "201": {
      "description": "The new post",
      "content": {
        "application/json": {
          "schema": {"$ref": "#/components/schemas/Post"}
        }
      }
    },
    "401": {},
    "422": {},
    "500": {}
  }
}
```

- `@Response(201, Post)` replaces the empty 200.
- `@Tags(['Posts'])` moves the route to the group "Posts" in the docs page.
- `@Summary('...')` and `@Description('...')` set the text. A `///` comment gives the same result, but the annotation wins.
- `@ApiIgnore()` leaves a method, or a whole controller, out of the docs.

See [OpenAPI: describe a route](../packages/openapi.md#describe-a-route) for all annotations.

## 7. Turn it off in production

The docs routes are on only when `APP_ENV` is development or local. With `APP_ENV=production` all three routes give 404:

```bash
# 404
curl -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://localhost:3000/docs
# 404
curl -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://localhost:3000/openapi.json
```

To turn the docs on in production, set `enabled: true`. See [OpenAPI: turn the docs on in production](../packages/openapi.md#turn-the-docs-on-in-production). To serve files made at build time, see [OpenAPI: production setup](../packages/openapi.md#production-setup).

To show the docs on staging, but never in production, set `enabled` yourself:

```dart title="lib/config/openapi.dart"
import 'package:blog/config/env.dart';

OpenApiConfig openApi = OpenApiConfig(
  enabled: env.appEnv != 'production',
  info: Info(title: 'Blog API', version: '1.0.0'),
  registry: openApiRegistry,
);
```

!!! warning
    `enabled: true` in production shows every route of your API to anyone. Do it only for a public API.

To write the document to files, run `dox openapi:generate`. See [OpenAPI: write the files](../packages/openapi.md#write-the-files).

## Check it

Read the start of the document:

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:3000/openapi.json | head -n 5
```

```text
{
  "openapi": "3.1.0",
  "info": {
    "title": "Blog API",
    "version": "1.0.0"
```

Open `http://localhost:3000/docs`, find "Create a post" under "Posts", and send a request with "Try it".

## Next steps

- [OpenAPI](../packages/openapi.md): all the options, Swagger UI and login schemes.
- [Validation rules](../the-basic/validation-rules.md): the rules and their JSON Schema keys.
- [Environments](environments.md): set `APP_ENV`.

# Docker

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/guides/docker/

# Docker

Build a small production image with `dox build`, and run it with Postgres in Docker Compose, with a health check.

The image holds only the compiled app, so it is small and starts fast.

## What you need

- A Dox app with a database.
- Docker with Compose.

## 1. Add a health route

Docker asks this route if the app works. It answers 503 when the database does not answer. Put it in `register()` of `WebRouter`:

```dart title="lib/routes/web.dart"
Route.health(
  '/health',
  checks: <String, HealthCheckFunction>{
    'database': () => QueryBuilder.query('select 1'),
  },
);
```

## 2. Add the health check binary

The final image has no shell and no `curl`, so the health check is a small Dart binary:

```dart title="bin/health.dart"
import 'dart:io';

/// Docker health check. The final image has no shell and no curl,
/// so this small binary asks the app itself. Exit 0 = healthy.
Future<void> main() async {
  String port = Platform.environment['APP_PORT'] ?? '3000';
  HttpClient client = HttpClient()
    ..connectionTimeout = const Duration(seconds: 3);
  try {
    HttpClientRequest request = await client.getUrl(
      Uri.parse('http://127.0.0.1:$port/health'),
    );
    HttpClientResponse response = await request.close();
    exit(response.statusCode == 200 ? 0 : 1);
  } catch (_) {
    exit(1);
  }
}
```

## 3. Write the Dockerfile

The first stage builds the AOT bundle. The second stage holds only the Dart runtime and the bundle, about 17 MB for the blog API:

```dockerfile title="Dockerfile"
# Stage 1: build the AOT bundle with the Dart SDK and the dox CLI.
FROM dart:stable AS build

WORKDIR /app

# Resolve dependencies first, so Docker caches this layer.
COPY pubspec.* ./
RUN dart pub get

COPY . .
RUN dart pub get --offline

# `dox build` runs build_runner, then `dart build cli`.
# The bundle is in build/bundle: bin/server, lib/, db/, .env.example
# (and bin/queue, bin/schedule when the app has them)
RUN dart pub global activate dox \
  && /root/.pub-cache/bin/dox build

# The health check binary. Plain dart:io, so `dart compile exe` is fine.
RUN dart compile exe bin/health.dart -o build/bundle/bin/health

# Lay out the final file tree. /tmp must be writable: uploads bigger
# than 1 MB are streamed to a temp file.
RUN mkdir -p /out/app/storage /out/app/public /out/tmp \
  && chmod 1777 /out/tmp \
  && cp -r build/bundle/. /out/app/ \
  && cp -r public/. /out/app/public/

# Stage 2: the Dart AOT runtime and the bundle only. No SDK, no source.
FROM scratch
COPY --from=build /runtime/ /
COPY --from=build /out/ /
WORKDIR /app

# Config comes from env variables. The image has no .env file.
EXPOSE 3000
HEALTHCHECK --interval=15s --timeout=5s --start-period=10s --retries=3 \
  CMD ["/app/bin/health"]
CMD ["/app/bin/server"]
```

Delete the `public` lines if your app has no `public` folder.

The image has no copy of `libgcc_s.so.1`. The native libraries do not need it from `dox_http_native` 3.2.4, `dox_postgres_native` 3.2.2 and `dox_mysql_native` 3.2.2. With an older version, Dox stops at start with `dox_http_native did not load`. Run `dart pub upgrade` to get the new versions.

When the container starts, the start log must end with `(native)`:

```text
[server] Server started at http://[::]:3000 with 8 isolate (native)
```

!!! warning "`dox build`, not `dart compile exe`"
    `dox_orm` bundles SQLite with a build hook. `dart compile exe` does not run build hooks and stops with an error. Build the server with `dox build`.

Keep the build context small with a `.dockerignore`:

```text title=".dockerignore"
.dart_tool/
.git/
.github/
.idea/
build/
storage/
.env
.env.*
!.env.example
Dockerfile
docker-compose.yml
pubspec_overrides.yaml
```

## 4. Write the compose file

Docker Compose runs the app and Postgres together. The lines under `environment` win over `.env`:

```yaml title="docker-compose.yml"
services:
  app:
    build: .
    # secrets and config come from .env, never from the image
    env_file: .env
    environment:
      APP_ENV: production
      APP_PORT: 3000
      DB_CONNECTION: postgres
      DB_HOST: postgres
      DB_PORT: 5432
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"
    volumes:
      # uploads survive a new image
      - uploads:/app/storage
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
    restart: unless-stopped

  postgres:
    image: postgres:18
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: ${DB_USERNAME:-postgres}
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${DB_PASSWORD:?set DB_PASSWORD in .env}
      POSTGRES_DB: ${DB_NAME:-dox}
    volumes:
      - postgres:/var/lib/postgresql
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "pg_isready", "-q", "-U", "${DB_USERNAME:-postgres}"]
      interval: 5s
      retries: 10
    restart: unless-stopped

volumes:
  postgres:
  uploads:
```

`depends_on` starts the app after Postgres answers, because the app runs the migrations at start.

## 5. Write the `.env`

Put the secrets in `.env`. It never goes into the image or into git:

```ini title=".env"
APP_NAME=my_app
APP_ENV=production
APP_KEY=<output of dox key:generate>
APP_PORT=3000

DB_CONNECTION=postgres
DB_NAME=my_app
DB_USERNAME=postgres
DB_PASSWORD=<a real password>
```

A new app skips the Postgres driver in `pubspec.yaml`. Remove the `dox_postgres_native` skip lines. See [Skip unused drivers](../database/index.md#skip-unused-drivers).

## 6. Build and run

Build the image and start both services:

```bash
docker compose up -d --build
```

## Check it

Both services are healthy:

```bash
docker compose ps
```

```text
NAME             STATUS
my_app-app-1       Up 30 seconds (healthy)
my_app-postgres-1  Up 35 seconds (healthy)
```

Ask the health route:

```bash
curl http://localhost:3000/health
```

```json
{"status":"ok","checks":{"database":"ok"}}
```

Now stop Postgres with `docker compose stop postgres`. After about 45 seconds, `docker compose ps` shows the app as unhealthy.

## HTTPS

Put Caddy or nginx in front of the app, and set `trustedProxies` in `AppConfig`. See [Deployment: HTTPS](../digging-deeper/deployment.md#https-put-a-proxy-in-front).

## Next steps

- [Deployment](../digging-deeper/deployment.md): `dox build`, the bundle and systemd.
- [Health check](../digging-deeper/health-check.md): more checks.
- [Environments](environments.md): dev, staging and production config.
- [Migration: run on server start](../database/migration.md#run-on-server-start): the migrations at start.

# Deploy to a Linux server

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/guides/deploy-vps/

# Deploy to a Linux server

Run the blog API on your own Linux server (a VPS), with systemd to keep it running and Caddy in front for HTTPS.

systemd starts the app again after a crash. Caddy gets the TLS certificate and sends the requests to the app:

<ol class="dox-flow dox-flow--labels dox-flow--plain" style="--dox-flow-gap:6rem" aria-label="Caddy in front of the app">
  <li><strong>Browser or app</strong></li>
  <li data-via="HTTPS :443"><strong>Caddy</strong><span>the TLS certificate</span></li>
  <li data-via="HTTP 127.0.0.1:3000" class="dox-flow__end" style="flex-grow:1.4"><strong>The app</strong><span>systemd runs /opt/blog/bin/server</span></li>
</ol>

## What you need

- A Linux server (Debian 12, Ubuntu 22.04 or newer) with SSH and `sudo`.
- A domain name. Its `A` (and `AAAA`) record points to the server.
- Docker on your machine, to build a Linux binary.
- The blog API from the [tutorial](../tutorial/01-create-project.md), or any Dox app.

## 1. Build the bundle for Linux

`dox build` makes a binary for the system it runs on. So build it in the `dart:stable` image, which is Debian:

```bash
docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/app -w /app dart:stable sh -c \
  'dart pub get && dart pub global activate dox &&
    /root/.pub-cache/bin/dox build'
```

The result is in `build/bundle/`:

```text
build/bundle/
  bin/server                         the AOT binary
  lib/dox_http_native-linux-*.so     the native HTTP server
  lib/dox_postgres_native-linux-*.so the native Postgres driver
  lib/dox_mysql_native-linux-*.so    the native MySQL driver
  lib/libsqlite3.so                  SQLite
  db/                                the migrations
  .env.example
```

Keep `bin/` and `lib/` together, because the binary loads the libraries from `../lib`.

!!! warning "Match the CPU of the server"
    Docker builds for the CPU of your machine. On a Mac with Apple silicon that is arm64, but most VPS plans are x86_64.
    For them, add `--platform linux/amd64` after `docker run`. Check the server with `uname -m`.

The container writes Linux paths into your `.dart_tool/`. So run `dart pub get` on your machine again before you use `dox serve`.

## 2. Make a user and the folders

Do not run the app as root. On the server, make a user `dox` that can not log in:

```bash
sudo useradd --system --no-create-home --shell /usr/sbin/nologin dox
sudo mkdir -p /opt/blog
sudo install -d -o dox -g dox /opt/blog/storage
```

The app uses these paths:

| Path | What it holds | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/opt/blog` | the bundle (`bin/`, `lib/`, `db/`) | `root` |
| `/opt/blog/storage` | files the app writes (uploads, file cache) | `dox` |
| `/var/lib/blog` | the SQLite file. systemd makes it (see step 5) | `dox` |
| `/etc/blog.env` | config and secrets | `root`, mode `600` |

## 3. Copy the bundle to the server

Copy the bundle to a temp folder, then into `/opt/blog`:

```bash
rsync -a --delete --exclude storage/ \
    build/bundle/ you@server:/tmp/blog-bundle/
ssh you@server \
    'sudo rsync -a --delete --exclude storage/ /tmp/blog-bundle/ /opt/blog/'
```

## 4. Write the env file

Put the config and the secrets in `/etc/blog.env`:

```ini title="/etc/blog.env"
APP_NAME=blog
APP_ENV=production
APP_PORT=3000
APP_KEY=<output of dox key:generate>

DB_CONNECTION=sqlite
DB_NAME=/var/lib/blog/blog.sqlite
```

Only root may read the file:

```bash
sudo chown root:root /etc/blog.env
sudo chmod 600 /etc/blog.env
```

For Postgres, set `DB_CONNECTION=postgres` and add `DB_HOST`, `DB_PORT`, `DB_USERNAME`, `DB_PASSWORD` and `DB_NAME`. Or set one [`DATABASE_URL`](../database/index.md#database_url), like `postgres://app:secret@localhost:5432/blog`. It wins over the `DB_*` keys.

Do not put a `.env` file in `/opt/blog`. Keep all values in one place.

## 5. Write the systemd unit

The systemd unit starts the app at boot and starts it again after a crash:

```ini title="/etc/systemd/system/blog.service"
[Unit]
Description=Blog API (Dox)
After=network-online.target
Wants=network-online.target

[Service]
Type=simple
User=dox
Group=dox
# the binary reads db/ and .env from this folder
WorkingDirectory=/opt/blog
EnvironmentFile=/etc/blog.env
ExecStart=/opt/blog/bin/server
# start again after a crash, and after `kill`
Restart=always
RestartSec=2
# makes /var/lib/blog, owned by the user dox
StateDirectory=blog
# small safety settings
NoNewPrivileges=true
PrivateTmp=true
ProtectSystem=full

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

Start the app:

```bash
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now blog
systemctl status blog
```

The app runs the migrations at start, before it takes requests. To change the number of isolates, set `APP_TOTAL_ISOLATE` in `/etc/blog.env`.

## 6. Close the app port

Only Caddy may talk to the app. Add this line to `/etc/blog.env`, so Dox listens on the local address only:

```ini title="/etc/blog.env"
APP_HOST=127.0.0.1
```

Also turn on a firewall, so that only SSH, HTTP and HTTPS are open:

```bash
sudo ufw default deny incoming
sudo ufw allow OpenSSH
sudo ufw allow 80/tcp
sudo ufw allow 443/tcp
sudo ufw enable
```

## 7. Put Caddy in front

Install Caddy from its [install page](https://caddyserver.com/docs/install). Then write `/etc/caddy/Caddyfile`:

```text title="/etc/caddy/Caddyfile"
api.example.com {
	encode zstd gzip

	reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:3000 {
		# while the app restarts, wait up to 10s for it instead of failing
		lb_try_duration 10s
		lb_try_interval 250ms
	}
}
```

Check the file and load it:

```bash
sudo caddy validate --config /etc/caddy/Caddyfile
sudo systemctl reload caddy
```

Caddy gets a TLS certificate for `api.example.com` by itself. Ports 80 and 443 must be open.

## 8. Trust Caddy in the app

Dox ignores the `X-Forwarded-*` headers of a proxy that is not in `trustedProxies`. List the local addresses:

```dart title="lib/config/app.dart"
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  // ...
  trustedProxies: <String>['127.0.0.1', '::1'],
);
```

Now `req.ip()` is the real client IP and `req.scheme()` is https. Build and copy again after this change (steps 1 and 3).

## Check it

Call the API over HTTPS:

```bash
curl https://api.example.com/api/ping
```

```text
pong
```

Read the logs. In production the app writes one JSON line per log:

```bash
journalctl -u blog -f                     # follow new lines
journalctl -u blog --since "1 hour ago"   # the last hour
journalctl -u blog -b                     # since the last boot
```

The first lines after the first start look like this:

```text
Migrating: 2023_07_16_131937700_create_users_table
Migrated: 2023_07_16_131937700_create_users_table
Migrating: 2026_10_22_205345_create_posts_table
Migrated: 2026_10_22_205345_create_posts_table
{"timestamp":"...","status":"info","message":"Server started at http://127.0.0.1:3000 with 2 isolate (native)","logger":{"name":"dox"},"source":"server"}
```

`(native)` means the native HTTP server loaded.

From your machine, make sure that the app port is closed:

```bash
curl -m 5 http://api.example.com:3000/api/ping   # must time out
```

## Updating the app

1. Build a new bundle (step 1).
2. Copy it to the server (step 3). Keep the old one first, so you can go back:

    ```bash
    ssh you@server \
        'sudo rm -rf /opt/blog.prev && sudo cp -a /opt/blog /opt/blog.prev'
    rsync -a --delete --exclude storage/ \
        build/bundle/ you@server:/tmp/blog-bundle/
    ssh you@server \
        'sudo rsync -a --delete --exclude storage/ /tmp/blog-bundle/ /opt/blog/'
    ```

3. Restart the app. It runs new migrations at start.

    ```bash
    ssh you@server 'sudo systemctl restart blog'
    ```

4. Read the logs (`journalctl -u blog -n 20`) and run the check.

To go back, copy `/opt/blog.prev` to `/opt/blog` and restart. A migration that already ran stays.

A restart takes about one second, and Caddy waits for the app. For an update with no downtime, run two copies on two ports and list both in Caddy. See [Deployment: many processes](../digging-deeper/deployment.md#many-processes-or-machines).

## Next steps

- [Deployment](../digging-deeper/deployment.md): `dox build`, nginx and many processes.
- [Environments](environments.md): config per environment and `APP_KEY`.
- [Docker](docker.md): the app and Postgres in Docker Compose.
- [Native server](../digging-deeper/native-server.md): the native HTTP server.

# Deploy to Fly.io

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/guides/deploy-fly/

# Deploy to Fly.io

Run the blog API on [Fly.io](https://fly.io) from the `Dockerfile` of your project, with SQLite on a volume or with Postgres.

Fly.io builds the image from your `Dockerfile` and runs it with the config in `fly.toml`.

## What you need

- A Fly.io account and the `fly` CLI (`fly auth login`).
- The blog API from the [tutorial](../tutorial/01-create-project.md), or any Dox app, with the `Dockerfile` of a new Dox app. See [Docker](docker.md).

## 1. Make the app on Fly.io

In the project folder, make the app but do not deploy it yet:

```bash
fly launch --no-deploy
```

`fly launch` asks for an app name and a region, and writes `fly.toml`.

## 2. Write `fly.toml`

Replace `fly.toml` with this file. Change `app` and `primary_region` to your values:

```toml title="fly.toml"
app = "blog-api"
primary_region = "ams"
# Dox waits up to 8 seconds for open requests on stop. Fly waits 5 by default.
kill_timeout = 10

[build]
  dockerfile = "Dockerfile"

# config that is not secret. Secrets come from `fly secrets set`.
[env]
  APP_ENV = "production"
  APP_PORT = "3000"
  DB_CONNECTION = "sqlite"
  DB_NAME = "/data/blog.sqlite"

[http_service]
  internal_port = 3000
  force_https = true
  # one machine, always on: the SQLite file is on its volume
  auto_stop_machines = "off"
  auto_start_machines = true
  min_machines_running = 1

  [[http_service.checks]]
    grace_period = "10s"
    interval = "30s"
    method = "GET"
    timeout = "5s"
    path = "/api/ping"

# the volume with the SQLite file
[mounts]
  source = "blog_data"
  destination = "/data"

[[vm]]
  memory = "256mb"
  cpu_kind = "shared"
  cpus = 1
```

- Keep `internal_port` the same as `APP_PORT`.
- Values in `[env]` must be strings, so write `"3000"`, not `3000`.
- Each `fly deploy` sets the machine to the values of `[[vm]]`.
- Keep `kill_timeout` above `shutdownTimeout` of `AppConfig`. See [Graceful shutdown](../digging-deeper/deployment.md#graceful-shutdown).

## 3. Set the secrets

`fly.toml` goes into git, so set secrets like `APP_KEY` with `fly secrets`:

```bash
fly secrets set APP_KEY=<output of dox key:generate>
```

A secret is an environment variable on every machine of the app. It wins over an `[env]` key with the same name.

## 4. Choose a database

### SQLite on a volume

For a small app, use SQLite. Make the volume that `[mounts]` asks for, in the same region:

```bash
fly volumes create blog_data --region ams --size 1
```

A volume is attached to one machine only. So with SQLite, run exactly one machine.

### Postgres

For more than one machine, use Postgres. Make a Managed Postgres cluster with `fly mpg create`, and attach it to the app:

```bash
fly mpg attach <cluster-id> --app blog-api
```

This sets the secret [`DATABASE_URL`](../database/index.md#database_url). It wins over the `DB_*` keys.

Then delete `DB_CONNECTION` and `DB_NAME` from `[env]`, and delete the `[mounts]` section. If the database asks for TLS, add `?sslmode=require` to the URL with `fly secrets set DATABASE_URL=...`.

## 5. Deploy

Build the image and start the machine. The app runs the migrations at start:

```bash
fly deploy
```

Make sure that there is one machine:

```bash
fly scale show
```

If the count is more than 1 and you use SQLite, run `fly scale count 1`.

## Check it

Call the API:

```bash
curl https://blog-api.fly.dev/api/ping
```

```text
pong
```

Look at the machines and the logs:

```bash
fly status    # the machines and their state
fly logs      # the app logs, live
```

The first log lines after the first start:

```text
Migrating: 2023_07_16_131937700_create_users_table
Migrated: 2023_07_16_131937700_create_users_table
Migrating: 2026_10_22_205345_create_posts_table
Migrated: 2026_10_22_205345_create_posts_table
{"timestamp":"...","status":"info","message":"Server started at http://[::]:3000 with 1 isolate (native)","logger":{"name":"dox"},"source":"server"}
```

## HTTPS and the client IP

Fly.io handles HTTPS and sends plain HTTP to port 3000. Set `trustedProxies`, so `req.ip()` and `req.scheme()` show the real client. Only the Fly.io proxy can reach the app port, so `['*']` is safe here:

```dart title="lib/config/app.dart"
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  // ...
  trustedProxies: <String>['*'],
);
```

## Scaling the app

Dox starts one isolate per CPU of the container:

| You want | Do this |
| --- | --- |
| more speed on one machine | raise `cpus` and `memory` in `[[vm]]`, then `fly deploy` |
| more machines | use Postgres, then `fly scale count 2`. With SQLite, stay at one machine |
| a fixed number of isolates | set `APP_TOTAL_ISOLATE` in `[env]` |

Machines do not share Socket.IO rooms or the memory cache.

## Updating the app

To send a new version, deploy again:

```bash
fly deploy
```

`fly secrets set` restarts the machines with the new value. With `--stage`, the next deploy uses the value. With one machine there is a short gap while it restarts.

## Next steps

- [Deployment](../digging-deeper/deployment.md): the bundle and HTTPS.
- [Environments](environments.md): all the env keys and `APP_KEY`.
- [Docker](docker.md): the `Dockerfile` and Docker Compose.
- [Fly.io docs](https://fly.io/docs/reference/configuration/): `fly.toml`, secrets, volumes and Managed Postgres.

# Deploy to Google Cloud Run

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/guides/deploy-cloud-run/

# Deploy to Google Cloud Run

Run the blog API on [Cloud Run](https://cloud.google.com/run) from the `Dockerfile` of your project, with Postgres on Cloud SQL and secrets in Secret Manager.

Cloud Run runs and scales the containers, and gives you an HTTPS URL.

## What you need

- A Google Cloud project with billing, and the `gcloud` CLI (`gcloud auth login`, `gcloud config set project PROJECT_ID`).
- The blog API from the [tutorial](../tutorial/01-create-project.md), or any Dox app, with the `Dockerfile` of a new Dox app. See [Docker](docker.md).
- A Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL instance with a database and a user. See step 3.

## Choosing the port

Cloud Run gives the port in the `PORT` env variable: 8080 by default, or the `--port` value. Dox listens on `PORT` when `APP_PORT` is not set. So do not set `APP_PORT`, or set it to the `--port` value.

## 1. Turn on the APIs

Turn on the APIs one time:

```bash
gcloud services enable run.googleapis.com cloudbuild.googleapis.com \
  artifactregistry.googleapis.com secretmanager.googleapis.com \
  sqladmin.googleapis.com
```

## 2. Save the secrets in Secret Manager

Anyone who can see the service can read its plain env variables. So save `APP_KEY` and the database password in Secret Manager:

```bash
openssl rand -hex 16 | tr -d '\n' \
    | gcloud secrets create blog-app-key --data-file=-
printf '%s' '<the database password>' \
    | gcloud secrets create blog-db-password --data-file=-
```

Let the Cloud Run service account read them. By default this is the Compute Engine service account, `PROJECT_NUMBER-compute@developer.gserviceaccount.com`:

```bash
for s in blog-app-key blog-db-password; do
  gcloud secrets add-iam-policy-binding "$s" \
    --member="serviceAccount:PROJECT_NUMBER-compute@developer.gserviceaccount.com" \
    --role="roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor"
done
```

## 3. Reach Cloud SQL

Cloud Run can reach Cloud SQL by a Unix socket or by a private IP. This guide uses the socket, because it needs no VPC:

1. Find the connection name of the instance: `gcloud sql instances describe INSTANCE --format='value(connectionName)'`. It looks like `PROJECT_ID:europe-west1:INSTANCE`.
2. Deploy with `--add-cloudsql-instances <connection name>` (step 4). Cloud Run then makes the socket in `/cloudsql/<connection name>`.
3. Give the service account the `roles/cloudsql.client` role.
4. Set `DB_HOST=/cloudsql/<connection name>`. A host that starts with `/` is a [Unix socket](../database/index.md#unix-socket).

The same with one URL: `DATABASE_URL=postgres://blog:<password>@/blog?host=/cloudsql/<connection name>`.

For Cloud SQL for MySQL, use the same `DB_HOST` with `DB_CONNECTION=mysql`, and no `DB_PORT`. Or use one URL: `DATABASE_URL=mysql://blog:<password>@/blog?socket=/cloudsql/<connection name>`.

For a private IP, deploy with Direct VPC egress (`--network default --subnet default --vpc-egress private-ranges-only`), and use the private IP as `DB_HOST`.

Do not use SQLite on Cloud Run. The file system of an instance is in memory, so the data is lost when the instance stops.

## 4. Deploy from source

`--source .` uploads the folder, and Cloud Build builds the image with your `Dockerfile`:

```bash
gcloud run deploy blog \
  --source . \
  --region europe-west1 \
  --port 3000 \
  --allow-unauthenticated \
  --cpu 1 --memory 512Mi \
  --min-instances 1 \
  --add-cloudsql-instances PROJECT_ID:europe-west1:INSTANCE \
  --set-env-vars APP_ENV=production,APP_TOTAL_ISOLATE=1,DB_CONNECTION=postgres,DB_HOST=/cloudsql/PROJECT_ID:europe-west1:INSTANCE,DB_PORT=5432,DB_NAME=blog,DB_USERNAME=blog \
  --set-secrets APP_KEY=blog-app-key:1,DB_PASSWORD=blog-db-password:1
```

The flags do this:

| Flag | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `--port 3000` | the port Cloud Run sends requests to. It also sets `PORT=3000`. See [Choosing the port](#choosing-the-port) |
| `--min-instances 1` | keeps one instance warm, so the first request does not wait for a cold start. An idle instance still costs money |
| `--add-cloudsql-instances` | makes the Cloud SQL Unix socket in `/cloudsql/...` |
| `--set-env-vars` | config that is not secret |
| `--set-secrets` | `ENV_NAME=SECRET:VERSION`. Pin a version number, not `latest` |
| `APP_TOTAL_ISOLATE=1` | one isolate per CPU. Set it to the `--cpu` value |

To build the image yourself, push it to Artifact Registry and deploy it with `--image`. Add the other flags from above:

```bash
docker build --platform linux/amd64 \
    -t europe-west1-docker.pkg.dev/PROJECT_ID/blog/api:1 .
docker push europe-west1-docker.pkg.dev/PROJECT_ID/blog/api:1
gcloud run deploy blog \
    --image europe-west1-docker.pkg.dev/PROJECT_ID/blog/api:1 \
    --region europe-west1 --port 3000 ...
```

## Check it

`gcloud run deploy` prints the service URL at the end. Call it:

```bash
curl https://blog-xxxxxxxx-ew.a.run.app/api/ping
```

```text
pong
```

Read the logs. The live tail needs the log-streaming component:

```bash
gcloud run services logs read blog --region europe-west1 --limit 20
gcloud beta run services logs tail blog --region europe-west1
```

The first log lines after the first start:

```text
Migrating: 2023_07_16_131937700_create_users_table
Migrated: 2023_07_16_131937700_create_users_table
Migrating: 2026_10_22_205345_create_posts_table
Migrated: 2026_10_22_205345_create_posts_table
{"timestamp":"...","status":"info","message":"Server started at http://[::]:3000 with 1 isolate (native)","logger":{"name":"dox"},"source":"server"}
```

If the deploy fails with "the container did not listen on the port", check `APP_PORT` and `--port`.

## HTTPS and the client IP

Cloud Run handles HTTPS and sends plain HTTP to the container. Set `trustedProxies`, so `req.ip()` and `req.scheme()` show the real client. Only the Cloud Run front end can reach the container port, so `['*']` is safe here:

```dart title="lib/config/app.dart"
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  // ...
  trustedProxies: <String>['*'],
);
```

## Updating the app

To send a new version, deploy again. Cloud Run keeps the flags of the last revision:

```bash
gcloud run deploy blog --source . --region europe-west1
```

- The new revision runs new migrations, and takes the traffic when it listens on the port.
- If many instances start at the same time, each one runs the migrations. So keep migrations safe to run twice, or run one instance during a deploy with a migration.
- For a new secret version, run `gcloud secrets versions add`. Then deploy with `--update-secrets APP_KEY=blog-app-key:2`.

## Next steps

- [Deployment](../digging-deeper/deployment.md): the bundle and HTTPS.
- [Environments](environments.md): all the env keys and `APP_KEY`.
- [Docker](docker.md): the `Dockerfile` and Docker Compose.
- [Cloud Run docs](https://cloud.google.com/run/docs/container-contract): the container contract.
- [Cloud SQL for Cloud Run](https://cloud.google.com/sql/docs/postgres/connect-run): connect to the database.

# Reference

# Cheat sheet

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/reference/cheat-sheet/

# Cheat sheet

This page shows the code you use each day, with a link to the full page in each section.

## Project layout

| Path | What is in it |
| --- | --- |
| `bin/server.dart` | starts the app: `Dox().initialize()`, migrations, `Dox().startServer()` |
| `bin/migrate.dart` | runs migrations for `dox migration:*` |
| `bin/seed.dart` | runs seeders for `dox db:seed` |
| `bin/queue.dart` | the queue worker for `dox queue:*` |
| `bin/schedule.dart` | the scheduler for `dox schedule:*` |
| `bin/openapi.dart` | you add it: writes the OpenAPI files for `dox openapi:generate` |
| `lib/config/` | `app.dart` (`AppConfig`), `env.dart`, `database.dart`, `cors.dart`, `cache.dart`, `storage.dart`, `logger.dart`, `queue.dart`, `schedule.dart`. You add others, like `openapi.dart`. |
| `lib/routes/` | `api.dart`, `web.dart`: one `Router` class each |
| `lib/app/http/controllers/` | `<name>.controller.dart` |
| `lib/app/dtos/<name>/` | `<name>.dto.dart` |
| `lib/app/http/middleware/` | `<name>.middleware.dart` |
| `lib/app/serializers/` | `<name>.serializer.dart` |
| `lib/app/models/<name>/` | `<name>.model.dart` |
| `lib/app/jobs/` | `<name>.job.dart` |
| `lib/providers/` | `DoxProvider` classes: ORM, storage, queue, schedule. You add others, like auth. |
| `lib/generated/` | `container.g.dart`, `openapi.g.dart`, `jobs.g.dart` and `dtos.g.dart` (an empty list when the app has no DTO). Made by `build_runner`. Do not edit. |
| `db/migration/` | migrations and `migrations.dart` (the registry) |
| `db/seeders/`, `db/factories/` | seeders (`seeders.dart` is the registry) and model factories |

See [CLI](cli.md) and [App config](app-config.md).

## CLI

```bash
dox create my_app                  # newest template
dox serve                          # dev server, hot reload, build_runner
dox build                          # AOT bundle in build/bundle
dox build_runner:build             # make .g.dart files
dox key:generate                   # APP_KEY in .env
dox env:generate                   # lib/config/env.dart from .env.example
dox env:check                      # check the env, exit 1 when bad
dox make:controller Blog [-r] [--api] [--model=Blog]
dox make:middleware Auth
dox make:dto CreateBlog
dox make:serializer Blog
dox make:model Blog -m             # model + migration
dox make:model Blog -a             # all extra files
dox make:migration create_blogs_table [--sql]
dox make:job SendWelcomeEmail
dox make:provider Cache
dox make:command send_report       # run it with dox app:send-report
dox make:mail Welcome [--no-view]
dox make:view pages/about
dox make:test Ping [--unit]
dox route:list [--json]            # no server start
dox migrate                        # migration:run
dox migrate --seed                 # then run the seeders
dox migration:rollback --step=1
dox migration:status
dox db:seed [--class=UserSeeder]
dox queue:work                     # run queued jobs
dox schedule:work                  # run scheduled tasks
dox openapi:generate [dir]
```

See [CLI](cli.md).

## Routes

```dart
class ApiRouter extends Router {
  @override
  String get prefix => 'api';

  @override
  List<dynamic> get middleware => <dynamic>[];

  @override
  void register() {
    Route.get('/ping', (DoxRequest req) => 'pong');
  }
}
```

| Code | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `Route.get('/blogs', (C c) => c.index)` | controller `C` from the container. Also `post`, `put`, `patch`, `delete`, `options` |
| `Route.get('/blogs', listBlogs)` | a plain function |
| `Route.post('/blogs', c.store, body: schema)` | `body:` is for the docs only. It checks nothing. |
| `Route.get('/blogs/{id}', c.show)` | path param. `show(int id)` |
| `Route.get('/posts/{page?}', c.list)` | optional param. `list(int? page)` |
| `Route.get('/docs/{path*}', c.page)` | rest of the path, with `/` |
| `Route.get('/me', <dynamic>[AuthMiddleware(), c.me])` | middleware first, controller last |
| `Route.match(<String>['GET', 'POST'], '/contact', handler)` | one handler for a list of methods |
| `Route.any('/webhook', handler)` | one handler for `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` and `DELETE` |
| `Route.redirect('/home', '/')` / `Route.permanentRedirect('/old', '/new')` | send a path to another URL. `302` by default, `301` for `permanentRedirect`. |
| `Route.get('/users/{id}', c.show).where('id', '[0-9]+')` | the route matches only when the param fits the regex |
| `Route.fallback((DoxRequest req) { ... })` | answers a `GET` or `HEAD` request that matches no route and no static file. Use it for a 404 page or an SPA. |
| `globalMiddleware: <dynamic>[const MethodOverride()]` | lets an HTML form reach `PUT`, `PATCH` and `DELETE` routes |
| `Route.group('/blogs', () { ... })` | prefix. Dox adds the `/` between parts. |
| `Route.middleware(<dynamic>[M()], () { ... })` | middleware for a group |
| `Route.domain('api.app.com', () { ... })` | match by `Host` |
| `Route.resource('blogs', BlogController)` | `index`, `create`, `store`, `show`, `edit`, `update`, `destroy` |
| `Route.health('/health')` | `200 {"status": "ok"}`, or `503` when a check fails. See [Health check](../digging-deeper/health-check.md). |
| `Route.staticFiles('/', 'public')` | serve a folder (CSS, JS, images) when no route matches. `maxAge:` sets `Cache-Control` |
| `Storage.route('files')` | serve a storage disk. Only signed URLs work, unless `signed: false` (`dox_storage`) |
| `Route.enabledCors(() { ... })` / `Route.disabledCors(...)` | CORS for some routes |
| `Route.websocket('echo', (WebSocket s, DoxRequest req) { ... })` | a raw WebSocket. For rooms and acks, use Socket.IO. |

Controller parameters, by type: `DoxRequest`, one `@Dto` class, a string, integer, double, num or bool for path params (by position), a `@DoxModel` (loaded by its key), an `@Inject()` class. Only positional parameters. In the examples, `c.index` is a method of a controller `C` from the container.

## Dependency injection

```dart
@Inject()                       // one instance per isolate
class PostService {
  PostService(this.posts);      // from the container, by type
  final PostRepository posts;
}

@Inject(singleton: false)       // a new instance each time
class Clock {}

// registerContainer is in lib/generated/container.g.dart
AppConfig(container: registerContainer);

Dox().ioc.get<PostService>();
Dox().ioc.override<PostRepository>(FakePostRepository()); // tests
```

Dox finds routers and providers with no `@Inject()`. Run `dart run build_runner build` after a change. See [Dependency injection](../the-basic/dependency-injection.md), [Routing](../the-basic/routing.md) and [Controller](../the-basic/controller.md).

## Middleware

```dart
class ApiKeyMiddleware implements IDoxMiddleware {
  @override
  dynamic handle(IDoxRequest req) {
    String apiKey = Env.get<String>('API_KEY');
    // Hash.equals: constant time, so the time does not leak the key
    String given = req.header('X-Api-Key') ?? '';
    if (apiKey.isEmpty || !Hash.equals(given, apiKey)) {
      return response('no').statusCode(401); // stop here
    }
    return req; // go on
  }
}
```

| Middleware | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `const RequestId()` | `X-Request-Id` header, `req.requestId` |
| `const ETag()` | `ETag` header, `304` when `If-None-Match` matches |
| `RequestTimeout(Duration(seconds: 30))` or `Route.get(...).timeout(...)` | `503` when the route is too slow |
| `const ServerTiming()` | `Server-Timing` header; `ServerTiming.add('db', d)` adds a time. Development or trusted clients only |
| `const ValidateSignature()` | `403` unless the url is from `Route.signedUrl(...)` |
| `implements IDoxNextMiddleware` | `await next()` runs the rest, then you change the response |
| `implements IDoxTerminableMiddleware` | `terminate(req, res)` runs after the answer is sent |

Middleware runs in this order: `globalMiddleware`, router `middleware`, group, route.

See [Middleware](../the-basic/middleware.md) and [Signed URLs](../security/signed-urls.md).

## Request

| Code | Gives |
| --- | --- |
| `await req.validate<CreateBlog>()` | checked DTO, or `422` |
| `req.input('name')` | one value, query or body (body wins) |
| `req.all()` / `req.only(<String>['a', 'b'])` | many values |
| `req.input('user.name', 'guest')` | dot key, with a default |
| `req.except(<String>['password'])` | all values but these |
| `req.has('name')` / `req.filled('name')` | key is there and not empty (only `filled` reads dot keys) |
| `req.exists('name')` / `req.missing('name')` | key is there (any value) / not there |
| `req.boolean('remember')` / `req.integer('page', 1)` | value as `bool` / `int` |
| `req.file('avatar')` / `req.hasFile('avatar')` | uploaded file |
| `req.bearerToken()` | token of `Authorization: Bearer` |
| `req.path()` / `req.fullUrl()` | path / full URL with query |
| `req.pathIs('admin/*')` / `req.routeIs('admin.*')` | path or route name matches |
| `req.body` / `req.query` / `req.param['id']` | one source only |
| `req.header('X-Token')` / `req.headers` | headers |
| `req.cookie('token')` | decrypted cookie |
| `req.ip()` / `req.scheme()` / `req.isSecure()` | client info. Needs `trustedProxies` behind a proxy. |
| `req.userAgent()` / `req.host()` / `req.origin()` / `req.locale` | more headers |
| `req.isJson()` / `req.isFormData()` | content type |
| `req.auth?.user<User>()` | logged in user (after `AuthMiddleware`) |
| `req.auth?.id()` / `req.auth == null` | user id, or `true` for a guest |
| `req.method` / `req.uri` | method and URI |

Files:

```dart
RequestFile file = req.input('avatar');
file.filename; file.extension; file.length;   // bytes
// save before you return (dox_storage)
String path = await file.store('avatars');
```

See [Request](../the-basic/request.md) and [Request and response](request-and-response.md).

## Response

| Return | Client gets |
| --- | --- |
| `String` | text |
| `Map`, `List`, model, `Pagination`, serializer | JSON |
| `File` | streamed file, `Range` supported |
| `Storage().stream(path)` / `Storage().download(path)` | file / download |
| `Stream<List<int>>` | streamed bytes |
| `throw NotFoundHttpException()` | `404 Not Found` |
| `abort(403)`, `abort(409, 'Taken')` | any status |
| `response(...)` | full control |

```dart
return response(<String, dynamic>{'id': 1})
    .statusCode(201)
    .header('X-Request-Id', 'abc')
    .contentType(ContentType.json)
    .cache(Duration(minutes: 5))
    .cookie(DoxCookie('theme', 'dark', httpOnly: true, secure: true));

response('ok').cookie(DoxCookie('token', ''), setExpire: true); // delete
```

| Exception | Status |
| --- | --- |
| `BadRequestException()` | `400` |
| `UnAuthorizedException()` (`dox_auth`) | `401` |
| `ForbiddenHttpException()` | `403` |
| `NotFoundHttpException()` | `404` |
| `MethodNotAllowedHttpException(['GET'])` | `405` |
| `PayloadTooLargeException()` | `413` |
| `UnsupportedMediaTypeException()` | `415` |
| `ValidationException()` | `422` |
| `InternalErrorException()` | `500` |
| `HttpStatusException(code)` | any |

See [Response](../the-basic/response.md) and [HTTP exceptions](http-exceptions.md).

## DTO validation

```dart
@Dto()
class CreateBlog {
  @Length(min: 3, max: 200)
  @Trim()
  final String title;

  final String? body;            // nullable = optional
  final Status status;           // enum = only its names

  const CreateBlog({
    required this.title,
    this.body,
    this.status = Status.draft,
  });

  static const DtoSchema<CreateBlog> schema = $CreateBlogDto;
}
```

Then `dox build_runner:build`, and `dtos: dtos` in `AppConfig`.

| Kind | Annotations |
| --- | --- |
| Text | `@Length(min:, max:)`, `@MinLength(3)`, `@MaxLength(50)`, `@Email()`, `@Url()`, `@Uuid()`, `@Ip()`, `@Regex(r'..')`, `@In([..])`, `@NotIn([..])`, `@StartsWith('a')`, `@EndsWith('b')`, `@Alpha()`, `@AlphaNumeric()`, `@AlphaDash()` |
| More text | `@Json()`, `@Digits(6)`, `@DigitsBetween(4, 6)`, `@DateFormatted('Y-m-d')`, `@Password(min: 8, mixedCase: true, numbers: true, symbols: true)` |
| Other fields | `@Confirmed()`, `@Same('email')`, `@RequiredIf('type', 'company')`, `@RequiredWith(['phone'])` |
| Change text | `@Trim()`, `@Lowercase()`, `@Uppercase()`, `@AllowEmpty()` |
| Numbers | `@Min(1)`, `@Max(9)`, `@Range(1, 9)`, `@Positive()`, `@GreaterThan(0)`, `@LessThan(9)`, `@In`, `@NotIn` |
| Lists | `@MinItems(1)`, `@MaxItems(5)`, `@UniqueItems()` |
| Dates | `@After('2000-01-01')`, `@Before('now')` |
| Files | `@MaxSize('2MB')`, `@MinSize('1KB')`, `@Mimes(['pdf'])`, `@MimeTypes(['image/png'])`, `@Image()`, `@Dimensions(minWidth: 100)` |
| Database (`dox_orm`) | `@Unique('users', column: 'email', ignoreParam: 'id')`, `@Exists('teams')` |
| Keys | `@Name('emailAddress')` |
| Docs | `@Describe('Shown in OpenAPI and MCP.')` (only the JSON Schema `description`) |
| Class | `@Dto(source: Source.query, keyCase: KeyCase.field, strict: true, messages: {...})` |

Cross field check: add `void validate(DtoErrors errors)` to the DTO. PATCH "missing or null": `Maybe<T>` with `const Maybe.missing()`.

See [DTOs](../the-basic/dto.md), [Validation](../the-basic/validation.md) and [Validation rules](../the-basic/validation-rules.md).

## Model

```dart
@DoxModel(table: 'blogs', softDelete: true)
class Blog extends BlogGenerator {
  @Column()
  String? title;

  @Column(name: 'user_id')
  int? userId;

  @BelongsTo(User)
  User? user;

  @HasMany(Comment)
  List<Comment> comments = <Comment>[];

  @override
  List<String> get hidden => <String>['secret'];
}
```

| Code | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `await Blog().find(1)` / `find('slug', 'a')` | one row or `null` |
| `await Blog().all()` | every row that matches `where` |
| `await Blog().where('status', 'live').get()` | rows that match |
| `await Blog().where('id', '>', 5).getFirst()` | first match or `null` |
| `await Blog().findOrFail(1)` / `firstOrFail()` | the row, or throws `ModelNotFoundException` |
| `await Blog().count()` | `int` |
| `await Blog().where('slug', s).hasRows()` / `hasNoRows()` | `bool` |
| `await Blog().pluck('title')` / `valueOf('title')` | one column of all rows / of the first row |
| `await Blog().sum('views')`, `avg`, `min`, `max` | one value, `null` when no row |
| `await Blog().paginate(currentPage: 1, perPage: 20)` | `Pagination<Blog>`, rows in `data` |
| `await Blog().simplePaginate(currentPage: 1, perPage: 20)` | a page without the total count |
| `await Blog().cursorPaginate(perPage: 20, cursor: c)` | a page after a cursor, `nextCursor` |
| `await Blog().create(<String, dynamic>{'title': 'a'})` | insert and return the model |
| `await Blog().firstOrCreate({...}, {...})`, `firstOrNew`, `updateOrCreate` | find, or create |
| `blog.title = 'b'; await blog.save()` | insert or update |
| `await blog.delete()` | soft delete when `softDelete: true`. Returns the deleted rows as an `int`. |
| `await blog.increment('views')` / `decrement` | change a number in one query |
| `await Blog().forceCreate({...})` | create with every key, ignore `fillable` |
| `await Model.unguarded(() async { ... })` | turn off the `fillable` check inside the callback |
| `await blog.sync('tags', <int>[1, 2])` | many to many: make the links exactly these ids |
| `await blog.attach('tags', 3)` / `await blog.detach('tags', 3)` | add / remove links |
| `await blog.forceDelete()` / `await blog.restore()` | real delete / undo soft delete |
| `Blog().withTrash()` | include soft deleted rows |
| `Blog().onlyTrashed()` | only soft deleted rows |
| `await blog.touch()` | set `updated_at` to now, `touchQuietly()` with no events |
| `blog.replicate()` | a new unsaved copy of the model |
| `Blog().preload('comments').get()` | load a relation, one query |
| `Blog().whereHas('comments').get()` / `whereDoesntHave` / `has('comments', '>=', 3)` | filter by a relation |
| `await blog.$getRelation('user')` | load a relation on one model |
| `blog.related<Comment>('comments')?.where(...).get()` | relation query |
| `blog.toJson()` / `blog.toMap()` | map, `hidden` left out of `toJson()` |
| `Blog().query()` | a new, empty query |

Relations: `@HasOne(T)`, `@HasMany(T)`, `@BelongsTo(T)`, `@ManyToMany(T)`. Polymorphic: `@MorphMany(T, 'name')`, `@MorphOne(T, 'name')`, `@MorphTo()`. Options: `foreignKey`, `localKey`, `onQuery`, `eager`.

Events: override `onCreating()`, `onCreated()`, `onSaving()`, `onUpdated()`, `onDeleting()`, ... or `Model.observe<Blog>(BlogObserver())`. `throw CancelModelEvent('why')` in a "before" event stops it. `saveQuietly()` skips events.

See [Model](../database/model/index.md), [Events](../database/model/events.md), [HasMany](../database/model/relationship/has-many.md), [Query by relations](../database/model/relation-queries.md).

## Query builder

```dart
List<Map<String, dynamic>> rows = await QueryBuilder.table('blogs')
    .select(<String>['id', 'title'])
    .where('status', 'live')
    .orWhere('views', '>', 100)
    .whereIn('id', <int>[1, 2, 3])
    .whereNull('deleted_at')
    .join('users', 'users.id', 'blogs.user_id')
    .orderBy('id', 'desc')
    .limit(10)
    .offset(20)
    .get();
```

| Code | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `whereNotIn`, `whereNotNull`, `orWhereIn`, `orWhereNull` | more filters |
| `where('a', null)`, `where('a', '!=', null)` | `IS NULL`, `IS NOT NULL` |
| `whereBetween`, `whereColumn`, `whereLike`, `whereExists` (and `Not`, `or` forms) | more filters |
| `whereDate`, `whereTime`, `whereYear`, `whereMonth`, `whereDay` | parts of a date |
| `whereJsonContains('tags', 'a')`, `whereJsonDoesntContain` | JSON values |
| `whereIn('id', QueryBuilder.table('post').select('user_id'))` | sub query |
| `whereGroup((QueryBuilder<Blog> q) { ... })`, `orWhereGroup`, `whereNot` | conditions in brackets |
| `when(condition, (QueryBuilder<Blog> q) { ... })` | add parts only when `true` |
| `whereRaw('lower(name) = @n', <String, dynamic>{'n': 'a'})` | raw SQL, bound values |
| `leftJoin`, `rightJoin`, `joinRaw` | joins |
| `joinSub(q, 'alias', 'alias.id', 'blog.id')`, `leftJoinSub`, `fromSub(q, 'alias')` | sub queries |
| `union(q)`, `unionAll(q)` | add the rows of another query |
| `groupBy('age')`, `having(...)`, `havingRaw(...)` | groups |
| `distinct()`, `selectRaw('count(*) as total')` | distinct rows, raw select |
| `latest()`, `oldest()`, `inRandomOrder()` | order |
| `chunk(100, (rows) { ... })`, `chunkById(...)` | work on a big table |
| `insert({...})`, `insertMultiple([...])` | insert |
| `upsert([...], ['email'])` | insert or update, returns an `int` |
| `insertOrIgnore([...])` | insert, skip duplicates, returns an `int` |
| `where(...).update({...})` | update, no events, no `updated_at`. Returns the changed rows as an `int`. |
| `where(...).increment('views')`, `decrement` | change a number in one query |
| `where(...).delete()`, `truncate()` | delete. `delete()` returns the deleted rows as an `int`. |
| `lockForUpdate()`, `sharedLock()` | row lock, inside a transaction |
| `QueryBuilder.query('select 1', substitutionValues: {...})` | raw query |
| `withConnection('mysql')` | another connection |
| `toSql()`, `debug(true)` | see the SQL |

See [Query builder](../database/query-builder.md).

## Migrations and schema

```dart
class CreateBlogsTable extends Migration {
  @override
  Future<void> up(Schema schema) async {
    await schema.create('blogs', (Table table) {
      table.id();
      table.foreignId('user_id').constrained('users').cascadeOnDelete();
      table.string('title');
      table.text('body').nullable();
      table.enumeration('status', <String>['draft', 'live'])
          .defaultTo('draft');
      table.timestamps();
      table.softDeletes();
    });
  }

  @override
  Future<void> down(Schema schema) async {
    await schema.dropIfExists('blogs');
  }
}
```

| Column types |
| --- |
| `id()`, `increments`, `bigIncrements`, `string(c, [255])`, `char`, `text`, `mediumText`, `longText` |
| `integer`, `bigInteger`, `smallInteger`, `tinyInteger`, `unsignedInteger` (and `Big`, `Small`, `Tiny`) |
| `float`, `double`, `decimal(c, [8], [2])`, `boolean` |
| `date`, `dateTime`, `dateTimeTz`, `time`, `timestamp`, `timestampTz` |
| `json`, `jsonb`, `uuid`, `binary`, `enumeration(c, [...])`, `foreignId`, `foreignUuid` |
| `timestamps()`, `softDeletes()`, `rememberToken()`, `morphs('owner')` |

| Modifiers |
| --- |
| `nullable()`, `defaultTo(v)`, `defaultRaw('sql')`, `useCurrent()`, `useCurrentOnUpdate()` |
| `unique()`, `index()`, `primary()`, `unsigned()`, `comment('t')`, `after('c')`, `change()` |
| keys: `constrained([table])`, `references('id').on('t')`, `onDelete('cascade')`, `cascadeOnDelete()`, `nullOnDelete()` |

Change a table: `schema.table('t', (Table table) { table.string('a').nullable().change(); table.renameColumn('b', 'c'); table.dropColumn('d'); })`.

See [Migration](../database/migration.md) and [Schema](../database/schema.md).

## Transactions

```dart
int? id = await QueryBuilder.transaction(() async {
  Blog blog = await Blog().create(<String, dynamic>{'title': 'a'});
  await QueryBuilder.table('blog_info')
      .insert(<String, dynamic>{'blog_id': blog.id});
  return blog.id;
}); // throw inside = rollback

await QueryBuilder.transaction(() async {
  // other writers wait
  Blog blog = await Blog().lockForUpdate().findOrFail(1);
  blog.title = 'b';
  await blog.save();
});
```

See [Transactions](../database/transactions.md) and [Row locks](../database/transactions.md#row-locks).

## Cache

```dart
await Cache().put('k', 'v', duration: Duration(minutes: 10));
await Cache().get('k', 'default');
await Cache().remember('posts', Duration(minutes: 5), () => Post().all());
await Cache().forget('k');
await Cache().store('redis').increment('hits');
await Cache().tag('users').flush();
CacheLock lock = Cache().store('redis')
    .lock('report', Duration(seconds: 30));
```

Values must be JSON types. `memory` is per isolate. See [Cache](../digging-deeper/cache.md).

## Storage

```dart
// path is '/avatars/<uuid>.png'
String path = await Storage().putFile('avatars', file);
await Storage().put('notes/a.txt', 'hello', exact: true); // this exact path
Uint8List? bytes = await Storage().get(path);
await Storage().exists(path);
await Storage().delete(path);
String url = await Storage().signedUrl(path,
    expiresIn: Duration(minutes: 10));
await Storage().copy(path, 'backup/a.png');
List<String> files = await Storage().files('avatars');
Uint8List report = Uint8List.fromList(<int>[1, 2, 3]);
await Storage().disk('s3').put('reports/2026.pdf', report, exact: true);
return Storage().download(path, name: 'avatar.png'); // from a controller
```

See [File storage](../digging-deeper/file-storage.md).

## JSON

```dart
String text = JSON.stringify(<String, dynamic>{
  'at': DateTime.now(),
  'user': user, // a model, has toJson()
});
List<int> bytes = JSON.bytes(<String, dynamic>{'ok': true}); // UTF-8 bytes

dynamic a = JSON.parse(text);          // from a String
dynamic b = JSON.parse(res.bodyBytes); // from bytes, from an HTTP client
```

Use `bytes` for sockets, files, queues and HTTP client bodies, not as a controller result. `parse` takes a string or bytes.

## Env

```dart
@DoxEnv()
abstract class AppEnv {
  static AppEnv load([EnvReader? reader]) => _$AppEnv.load(reader);

  String get appKey;              // APP_KEY, required
  int get appPort => 3000;        // APP_PORT, default 3000
  String? get awsBucket;          // AWS_BUCKET, optional
}

final AppEnv env = AppEnv.load();
```

A new project has this class in `lib/config/env.dart`. Use `env.appPort` in code. After you add a getter, run `dart run build_runner build`.

`Env.get<int>('APP_PORT', 3000)` reads one key by name, without the class. A real env var wins over `.env`.

See [Environment variables](../digging-deeper/env.md) and [Env reference](env.md).

## Auth

```dart
Auth.initialize(AuthConfig(
  defaultGuard: 'web',
  guards: <String, AuthGuard>{
    'web': AuthGuard(
      driver: JwtAuthDriver(
        secret: SecretKey(env.appKey),
        expiresIn: Duration(days: 7),
      ),
      provider: AuthProvider(model: () => User()),
    ),
  },
));

String? token = await Auth()
    .attempt(<String, dynamic>{'email': e, 'password': p});
String? token2 = Auth().login(user);
user.password = await Hash.makeAsync(password); // bcrypt in another isolate
bool ok = await Hash.verifyAsync(password, hash);
```

Protect a route with `AuthMiddleware()`. Client sends `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

Access tokens (`AccessTokenAuthDriver`):

```dart
Auth auth = req.auth as Auth; // after AuthMiddleware()
User user = auth.user<User>()!;
AccessToken token = await auth.createAccessToken(user,
    abilities: <String>['posts:read']);
bool ok = auth.tokenCan('posts:read');
AccessToken next = await auth.rotateAccessToken(auth.currentAccessToken!,
    grace: const Duration(seconds: 10));
// replaces the whole list
await auth.setAccessTokenAbilities(auth.currentAccessToken!,
    <String>['posts:read']);
await auth.revokeToken(req); // logout
```

`AuthMiddleware(optional: true)` lets guests through too. `GuestMiddleware(redirectTo: '/dashboard')` is for login pages.

See [Authentication](../security/authentication.md) and [Hashing](../security/hashing.md).

## Socket.IO

```dart
class ChatNamespace extends NamespaceHandler {
  @override
  String get path => '/chat';

  @override
  void onConnection(Socket socket) {
    socket.join('lobby');
    socket.on('chat', onChat);
  }

  void onChat(SocketEvent event) {
    event.socket.to('lobby').emit('chat', event.data);
    event.ack('ok');
  }
}
```

Log users in at connect time with `SocketAuth(findUser).handle` in `middleware`. The user is in `socket.user`.

Turn it on with a `SocketIoProvider` (extend it in `lib/`). With many isolates, clients must use `transports: ['websocket']`. Broadcasts reach every isolate without Redis, but many servers need the Redis adapter.

See [Socket.IO](../packages/socketio.md).

## OpenAPI

```dart
OpenApiConfig openApi = OpenApiConfig(
  info: Info(title: 'Blog API', version: '1.0.0'),
  registry: openApiRegistry, // lib/generated/openapi.g.dart
);
```

The docs are at `/docs`, `/openapi.json` and `/openapi.yaml`. They are on only in `development` or `local`, unless you set `enabled`. `@Security.bearer(format: 'API key')` above a middleware class shows its login scheme. Change one route with `@Summary`, `@Tags`, `@Request(T)`, `@Response(200, T)` or `@ApiIgnore()`.

See [OpenAPI](../packages/openapi.md).

## Testing

```dart
import 'package:dox_core/testing.dart';
import 'package:dox_orm/testing.dart';

late DoxTestClient client;
setUpAll(() async => client = await DoxTestClient.start(appConfig));
setUp(refreshDatabase); // empty every table before each test
tearDownAll(() async => client.close());

test('ping', () async {
  (await client.get('/api/ping')).expectStatus(200).expectBody('pong');
  (await client.withToken(token).post('/api/posts', body: {...}))
      .expectStatus(201);
});
```

| Fake | Code |
| --- | --- |
| cache | `Dox().cache = CacheManager(CacheConfig(defaultStore: 'memory', stores: {...}))` |
| storage | `Disk fake = Storage.manager.fake('s3');` then `Storage.manager.restore('s3')` |
| mail | `ArrayTransport mail = Mail.fake();` then `mail.assertSent()`, `mail.assertQueued()`, `mail.assertNothingSent()`, and `Mail.restore()` |
| queue | `QueueFake queue = Queue.fake();` then `queue.assertPushed<T>()`, and `Queue.restore()` |
| env | `AppEnv.load(EnvReader(environment: {...}, dotEnv: {...}))` |
| DTO | `await CreateBlog.schema.safeValidateMap(<String, dynamic>{...})` |

Run with `dart test --concurrency=1` when files share a port or tables. See [Testing](../digging-deeper/testing.md).
