# App config

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/reference/app-config/

# App config

This page lists every field of `AppConfig`, with its type, its default and what it does.

You give `AppConfig` to `Dox().initialize()` in `lib/config/app.dart`. Each field has a default except `appKey`. See the [full example](#full-example).

## Server

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `appKey` | `String` | required | Encrypts cookies and signs local storage URLs. It must be exactly 32 characters. Make one with `dox key:generate`. In production a bad key stops the app at start, see [`APP_ENV`](env.md#read-by-the-framework). |
| `previousKeys` | `List<String>` | `[]` | Old app keys. Dox can still read data that was encrypted with them. New data uses `appKey` only. See [Rotating the key](../security/encryption.md#change-the-key-key-rotation). |
| `serverPort` | `int` | `3000` | The port to listen on. When the env has no `APP_PORT` but has `PORT`, Dox uses `PORT` (Cloud Run, Fly, Render and Heroku set it). |
| `host` | `String?` | `null`: `APP_HOST`, else all interfaces | The network interface to listen on, like `127.0.0.1`. `null` reads `APP_HOST`. With neither, Dox listens on all interfaces (`::`). |
| `totalIsolate` | `int?` | the CPUs the container allows | How many isolates serve HTTP, all on the same port. The default is the number of CPUs this process can use, with the container cpuset and CPU quota. A quota rounds up (1.5 CPUs gives 2 isolates). Windows always uses one. |
| `computeWorkers` | `int` | `AppConfig.defaultComputeWorkers` (4) | How many worker isolates run `Dox().compute`, `Hash.makeAsync` and `Hash.verifyAsync`, in one pool for the process. It must be 1 or more. See [Heavy CPU work](../digging-deeper/isolate.md#heavy-cpu-work). |
| `compress` | `bool` | `false` | gzip the responses, but not streamed responses. It costs CPU on each response, so let a proxy do it if you have one. |
| `maxBodySize` | `int` | `10 * 1024 * 1024` (10 MB) | Biggest JSON or urlencoded body in bytes. Bigger gets `413`. |
| `maxMultipartSize` | `int` | `100 * 1024 * 1024` (100 MB) | Biggest `multipart/form-data` body (file uploads) in bytes. Bigger gets `413`. |
| `bodyTimeout` | `Duration` | `Duration(seconds: 120)` | A client that sends no body bytes for this long gets `408`. A slow but steady upload is fine. |
| `idleTimeout` | `Duration` | `Duration(seconds: 30)` | A keep-alive connection with no new request for this long is closed. Behind a load balancer, set it longer than the balancer's idle timeout. See [Behind a load balancer](../digging-deeper/deployment.md#behind-a-load-balancer). |
| `maxConnections` | `int?` | `null` (no limit) | The most connections one isolate holds open at once (1 or more). When it is full, new clients wait in the OS queue. The app holds up to `maxConnections * totalIsolate`, so keep that below `ulimit -n`. |
| `http2` | `bool` | `false` | The same port also speaks HTTP/2. HTTP/1.1 keeps working. Without `tls` it is HTTP/2 over plain TCP (h2c). See [HTTP/2](../digging-deeper/http2.md). |
| `maxConcurrentStreams` | `int` | `250` | The most open requests one HTTP/2 connection can have (1 or more). Used only when `http2` is `true`. |
| `tls` | `TlsOptions?` | `null` (plain HTTP) | Serve HTTPS with no proxy. `TlsOptions(certificatePath: ..., keyPath: ...)` gives the two PEM files. The port then accepts only TLS. `Dox().server.reloadCertificate()` reads the files again. See [HTTPS without a proxy](../digging-deeper/deployment.md#https-without-a-proxy). |
| `shutdownTimeout` | `Duration` | `Duration(seconds: 8)` | On `SIGTERM` or `SIGINT`, how long open requests may run before Dox closes them. Keep it below the kill timeout of your platform. See [Graceful shutdown](../digging-deeper/deployment.md#graceful-shutdown). |
| `trustedProxies` | `List<String>` | `[]` | IPs or CIDR ranges of your reverse proxies. Dox reads `X-Forwarded-For` (for `req.ip()`) and `X-Forwarded-Proto` (for `req.scheme()`) only from these. Without such a header, `req.scheme()` is `https` when `tls` is set, else `http`. `['*']` trusts any direct client, but only the last hop. Use it only when the app port is not open to the outside. |
| `isDevelopment` | `bool` (getter) | | True when `APP_ENV` is development. It reads the env at each call, so it works before the server starts. Use it in config, like a database `debug` flag. |

## Routing and request handling

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `container` | `void Function(IocContainer)?` | `null` | Pass `registerContainer` from `lib/generated/container.g.dart`. It fills the container, and also gives the routers, providers and model binders. See [Dependency injection](../the-basic/dependency-injection.md). |
| `routers` | `List<Router>` | `[]` | Routers to register first, in this order. Every other `Router` class comes from `container`. |
| `globalMiddleware` | `List<dynamic>` | `[]` | Middleware that runs on every route. A function or an `IDoxMiddleware`. |
| `dtos` | `List<DtoSchema<Object>>` | `[]` | Pass `dtos` from `lib/generated/dtos.g.dart`. Dox finds the DTOs of controllers and `req.validate<T>()` in it. |
| `validationMessages` | `MessageResolver?` | `null` (English messages) | Messages for validation errors, for example in other languages. |
| `responseHandler` | `ResponseHandlerInterface?` | `null` | A class with `DoxResponse handle(DoxResponse res)`. It sees every response before it is sent. |
| `exceptionHandler` | `ExceptionHandler` | `ExceptionHandler()` | Reports every unhandled error and turns it into a response. The default logs the error and the stack. See [Error handling](../the-basic/errors.md). |
| `htmlErrors` | `bool` | `false` | Sends an HTML error page to a request that does not want JSON. In `development` or `local` the page also shows the error and the stack. JSON clients do not change. See [An HTML error page](../the-basic/errors.md#an-html-error-page). |
| `errorPage` | `String Function(int status, Object error, StackTrace stack, bool debug)` | `defaultErrorPage` | Makes the HTML of the page. `debug` is `true` in `development` or `local`. Escape every value you put in the page. Used only with `htmlErrors`. |
| `providers` | `List<DoxProvider>` | `[]` | Providers to run first, in this order. Every other `DoxProvider` class comes from `container`. Dox runs them in every isolate at start. |
| `webSocketAllowedOrigins` | `List<String>?` | `null` (no check) | Checks the `Origin` of each `Route.websocket` route. Only the same host and the listed sites, like `https://app.example.com`, can open a socket. Others get `403`. `[]` means the same host only. With `null`, any website can open a socket with the cookies of the user. The `allowedOrigins` of a route wins. |

## Sub configs

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cors` | `CORSConfig` | `CORSConfig()` | CORS headers. See [CORSConfig](#corsconfig). |
| `logger` | `LoggerConfig` | `LoggerConfig()` | The `Logger` output. See [LoggerConfig](#loggerconfig). |
| `cache` | `CacheConfig` | `file` store in `storage/cache`, plus a `memory` store | Cache stores for `Cache()`. See [CacheConfig](#cacheconfig). |
| `session` | `SessionConfig` | `cookie` driver, cookie `dox_session`, 2 hours | Settings for `SessionMiddleware`. See [Session](../the-basic/session.md#configuration). |
| `openApi` | `OpenApiConfig` | `OpenApiConfig()` | `/docs`, `/openapi.json` and `/openapi.yaml`. See [OpenApiConfig](#openapiconfig). |
| `strict` | `StrictConfig` | `StrictConfig()` (off) | Warnings for code that blocks the server, for development. `enabled` turns it on. `blockLimit` is how long code can block an isolate before a warning, `StrictConfig.defaultBlockLimit` (50 ms) by default. See [Let Dox warn you](../digging-deeper/performance-mistakes.md#let-dox-warn-you). |
| `flags` | `CoreFlags` | `CoreFlags()` (all off) | Opt-in core behaviors. See [Core flags](#core-flags). |

## Core flags

`CoreFlags` turns on extra behaviors. Each flag is off by default:

```dart
AppConfig(
  appKey: env.appKey,
  flags: const CoreFlags(onlyPresent: true, cookieDefaults: true),
);
```

`CoreFlags.all()` turns on every flag but `isolateGroups`:

```dart
AppConfig(appKey: env.appKey, flags: const CoreFlags.all());
```

| Flag | When it is on |
| --- | --- |
| `laravelErrors` | A `422` body is `{"message": "...", "errors": {"field": ["..."]}}`, with all messages of each field. The OpenAPI docs use this shape too. Off: `{"field": "first message"}`. |
| `onlyPresent` | `req.only([...])` leaves out keys that are not in the input. So `model.update(req.only([...]))` does not write `null` for a field the client did not send. Off: a missing key is in the map with `null`. |
| `cookieDefaults` | A `DoxCookie` with no `path` gets `Path=/`, and one with no `sameSite` gets `SameSite=Lax`. A value you set wins. Off: no `Path` and no `SameSite`. |
| `hasKeyOnly` | `req.has('x')` is `true` when the key is there, with any value (also `''` or null), like `req.exists('x')`. Dot keys work. Off: `''` and null give `false`. |
| `htmlStrings` | A string from a controller is sent as `text/html`. A content type you set wins. Escape user input in the string. Off: `text/plain`. |
| `replaceHeaders` | `res.header(k, v)` replaces a value that a middleware set before. `Vary` and `Set-Cookie` still get one more value. Off: it adds a second value. Pass `replace:` to pick for one call. |
| `decryptServerError` | A `DecryptException` gives a `500` `server_error`, and the `ExceptionHandler` reports it. Off: `400` `decrypt_failed`, not reported. |
| `envExpand` | `.env` values can use `${OTHER}`, and a `"..."` value reads `\n`, `\t`, `\"`, `\\` and `\$`. Also set `Env.flags = flags;` at the top of `main()` in `bin/server.dart` and in your tests, because `.env` is read before `AppConfig` exists. See [Use one value in another](../digging-deeper/env.md#use-one-value-in-another). Off: values are read as written. |
| `rateLimitIpv6Prefix` | The default key of `RateLimit` counts an IPv6 client by its /64 prefix. One home or server gets a whole /64, so with one count per address a client gets a new count with each new address. Clients in one /64 share a count. A `key` you give is used as it is. Off: each full ip has its own count. See [Rate limiting](../security/rate-limiting.md#ipv6-clients). |
| `isolateGroups` | Each server isolate has its own heap and its own garbage collector. Each isolate runs `main()` again. See [Give each isolate its own memory](../digging-deeper/deployment.md#give-each-isolate-its-own-memory). Off: all isolates share one heap. |
| `cacheCopies` | `Cache().store('x')`, `.tag()` and `.tags()` give a new `Cache`, and the first one does not change. Off: they change the same object and give it back. |

The cache has its own flag class, `CacheFlags`, in [`CacheConfig`](#cacheconfig).

## CORSConfig

A value can be a string (`'*'` or a comma list) or a list of strings. A null value sends no header, so set at least `origin`.

| Field | Type | Default | Header |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | `bool` | `true` | Send CORS headers. A route can override it with its own `cors` setting. |
| `origin` | `dynamic` | `null` | `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`. One origin, `'*'`, or a list. With a list, Dox sends back only the request origin if it is in the list. |
| `methods` | `dynamic` | `null` | `Access-Control-Allow-Methods` |
| `headers` | `dynamic` | `null` | `Access-Control-Allow-Headers` |
| `exposeHeaders` | `dynamic` | `null` | `Access-Control-Expose-Headers` |
| `credentials` | `bool?` | `null` | `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials`. Browsers refuse it with origin `'*'`, so list your sites in `origin`. |
| `maxAge` | `num?` | `null` | `Access-Control-Max-Age` in seconds |

## LoggerConfig

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `String` | `''` | Written as `logger.name` in each JSON log line. Left out when empty. |
| `enabled` | `bool` | `false` | Turn the `Logger` on. When it is off, `LogMiddleware` logs nothing too. |
| `prettyPrint` | `bool` | `false` | `true` prints colored text. Each line starts with a tag that says where it comes from, like `[request]`, `[server]` or `[app]`. `false` prints one JSON object per line, for log services. The tag is then in the `source` field, unless your data already has a `source` key. |
| `level` | `String` | `'info'` | The lowest level to print: `debug`, `info`, `warn` or `error`. `success` counts as info, and `danger` as error. |

Your own lines get the tag `[app]`. To use another tag, give it as the third argument of `log`, `info`, `warn`, `success` or `danger`:

```dart
Logger.info('invoice sent', null, 'billing');
```

In JSON mode the tag is the `source` field. Plain warnings on stderr use the same tags.

## CacheConfig

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `defaultStore` | `String` | required | The store `Cache()` uses when no store is named. |
| `stores` | `Map<String, Map<String, dynamic>>` | required | Store name to options. Each store needs a `driver` option. |
| `flags` | `CacheFlags` | `CacheFlags()` (all off) | Opt-in cache behaviors. See below. |
| `encrypter` | `CacheEncrypter?` | `null` | Encrypts stores with `'encrypt': true`. Dox sets it. You need it only [without Dox](../digging-deeper/cache.md#encryption-without-dox). |

`CacheFlags` has one flag. `CacheFlags.all()` turns it on.

| Flag | When it is on |
| --- | --- |
| `lockThrows` | `lock.block(timeout)` with no callback throws `LockTimeoutException` when the lock was not taken in time. Off: it gives `false`. Set `lock.throwOnTimeout` to pick for one lock. |

```dart
CacheConfig(
  defaultStore: 'redis',
  stores: stores,
  flags: const CacheFlags(lockThrows: true),
);
```

Options of each driver:

| Driver | Option | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| all | `driver` | `String` | required | `file`, `memory`, `redis`, `database` or `null` |
| all | `prefix` | `String` | `dox_cache:` (`<app name>_cache:` on Redis) | Text in front of each key. |
| `file`, `redis`, `database` | `encrypt` | `bool` | `false` | Encrypt the values with the app key. |
| `file` | `path` | `String` | `storage/cache` | Folder of the cache files. |
| `file` | `prune_every` | `int` | `0` | Run `prune()` once every this many writes. `0`: a light prune at most once an hour. |
| `file` | `fsync` | `bool` | `true` | Sync each write to the disk. `false` is faster, but a power cut can lose the last writes. |
| `memory` | `max_size` | `int` | no limit | Most items in the map. |
| `redis` | `host` | `String` | `127.0.0.1` | Redis host. |
| `redis` | `port` | `int` | `6379` | Redis port. |
| `redis` | `username` | `String` | none | Redis user. |
| `redis` | `password` | `String` | none | Redis password. |
| `redis` | `db` | `int` | `0` | Redis database number. |
| `redis` | `tls` | `bool` | `false` | Use TLS. |
| `redis` | `pool_size` | `int` | `10` | Most connections per store. |
| `redis` | `max_value_bytes` | `int` | no limit | Biggest value in bytes. |
| `redis` | `options` | `RedisOptions` | none | All client options. See [Redis options](../digging-deeper/cache.md#redis-options). |
| `database` | `table`, `connection`, `prune_interval` | | | See [Database store](../digging-deeper/cache.md#database-store). |

## StorageConfig

`StorageProvider` of the `dox_storage` package takes it. See [File storage](../digging-deeper/file-storage.md).

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `defaultDisk` | `String` | `'local'` | The disk `Storage()` uses when no disk is named. |
| `disks` | `Map<String, Map<String, dynamic>>` | `{'local': {'driver': 'local', 'root': 'storage'}}` | Disk name to options. Each disk needs a `driver` option. |

Options of each driver:

| Driver | Option | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| all | `driver` | `String` | required | `local`, `s3`, `azure` or `memory` |
| `local` | `root` | `String` | `storage` | Folder of the files. |
| `local` | `url` | `String` | none | Base of the public URLs, like `http://localhost:3000/files`. |
| `local` | `app_key` | `String` | `AppConfig.appKey` | Key that signs the URLs. |
| `local` | `visibility` | `String` | `public` | `public` or `private`. |
| `local` | `atomic_writes` | `bool` | `false` | Write to a temp file, then rename it. |
| `local` | `permissions` | `bool` or `Map` | off | Visibility is the file mode. See [File storage](../digging-deeper/file-storage.md#visibility-on-a-local-disk). |
| `s3` | `bucket` | `String` | required | Bucket name. |
| `s3` | `region` | `String` | `us-east-1` | Region. |
| `s3` | `key` | `String` | required | Access key id. |
| `s3` | `secret` | `String` | required | Secret access key. |
| `s3` | `token` | `String` | none | Session token. |
| `s3` | `endpoint` | `String` | none | Custom endpoint (R2, MinIO, Spaces). |
| `s3` | `path_style` | `bool` | `false` | Use path style URLs. |
| `s3` | `url` | `String` | none | Base of the public URLs. |
| `s3` | `visibility` | `String` | `private` | `public` or `private`. |
| `s3` | `acl` | `bool` | `true` | The service supports ACLs. |
| `s3` | `batch_delete` | `bool` | `true` | The service supports batch delete. |
| `azure` | `account` | `String` | required | Name of the storage account. |
| `azure` | `key` | `String` | required | Account key (base64). |
| `azure` | `container` | `String` | required | Blob container. The driver does not create it. |
| `azure` | `endpoint` | `String` | none | URL of the blob service, without the container. For Azurite: `http://127.0.0.1:10000/devstoreaccount1`. |
| `azure` | `url` | `String` | none | Base of the public URLs. |

## OpenApiConfig

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | `bool?` | `null` | Serve the docs routes. `null` means on only in `development` or `local`. |
| `info` | `Info` | `Info(title: 'Dox API', version: '1.0.0')` | Title and version of the API. |
| `servers` | `List<Server>` | `[]` | Base URLs of the API. |
| `securitySchemes` | `Map<String, SecurityScheme>` | `{}` | Ways to log in, like `{'bearerAuth': SecurityScheme.bearer()}`. |
| `securityByMiddleware` | `Map<String, List<Map<String, List<String>>>>` | `{}` | Security for routes that use a middleware class with this name. It wins over `@Security` on the class. A middleware whose class name ends with `AuthMiddleware` gets `bearerAuth` when it has no `@Security` and no entry here. |
| `registry` | `OpenApiRegistry` | `OpenApiRegistry()` (empty) | What `dox_builder` found in the code. Pass `openApiRegistry` from `lib/generated/openapi.g.dart`. |
| `ui` | `DocsUi` | `DocsUi.scalar` | `scalar` or `swagger`. |
| `scalar` | `ScalarOptions` | `ScalarOptions()` | Options of the Scalar page. See below. |
| `pageTitle` | `String?` | `null` (uses `info.title`) | Title of the `/docs` page. |
| `include` | `List<String>` | `[]` (all routes) | Only routes with these paths are in the docs, like `['/api/*']`. A `*` at the end matches the rest of the path. |
| `exclude` | `List<String>` | `[]` | Routes with these paths are left out. Checked after `include`. |

`ScalarOptions`:

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `theme` | `ScalarTheme` | `ScalarTheme.default_` | One of `default_`, `alternate`, `moon`, `purple`, `solarized`, `bluePlanet`, `deepSpace`, `saturn`, `kepler`, `elysiajs`, `fastify`, `mars`, `laserwave`, `none`. |
| `darkMode` | `bool` | `false` | Start in dark mode. |
| `showDownloadButton` | `bool` | `true` | Show the download button for the OpenAPI document. |
| `proxyUrl` | `String?` | `null` | Send "Try it" requests through this proxy. |

## SocketIoConfig

`SocketIoProvider` of the `dox_socketio` package takes it. See [Socket.IO](../packages/socketio.md).

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | `bool` | `true` | Mount Socket.IO on the HTTP port at `/socket.io/`. |
| `options` | `ServerOptions` | `ServerOptions()` | Engine options. See below. |
| `namespaces` | `List<NamespaceHandler>` | `[]` | Namespaces to register, like `ChatNamespace()`. |
| `adapter` | `SocketAdapterFactory?` | `null` (in memory with one isolate, `IsolateAdapter` with many) | Makes the adapter in each isolate. Use a Redis adapter with many servers. |

`ServerOptions`:

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | `String` | `/socket.io/` | URL path. Must end with `/`. |
| `pingInterval` | `Duration` | 25 s | Time between two server pings. |
| `pingTimeout` | `Duration` | 20 s | Time to wait for a pong before the session is closed. |
| `upgradeTimeout` | `Duration` | 10 s | Time a websocket upgrade may take. |
| `connectTimeout` | `Duration` | 45 s | Time a client has to join a namespace after the handshake. |
| `maxHttpBufferSize` | `int` | `1000000` | Biggest message in bytes a client may send. |
| `maxAttachments` | `int` | `10` | Most binary attachments in one packet. A packet with more closes that client. |
| `transports` | `List<String>` | `['polling', 'websocket']` | Allowed transports. |
| `allowUpgrades` | `bool` | `true` | Allow upgrades from polling to websocket. |
| `cors` | `CorsOptions?` | `null` (no CORS headers) | CORS for the long-polling requests. |

`CorsOptions`:

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `origins` | `List<String>` | `['*']` | Allowed origins. |
| `credentials` | `bool` | `false` | Send `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`. |
| `methods` | `List<String>` | `['GET', 'POST']` | Allowed methods for preflight. |
| `allowedHeaders` | `List<String>?` | `null` (the requested headers) | Allowed request headers. |
| `maxAge` | `Duration?` | `null` | How long a browser may cache the preflight answer. |

## DatabaseConfig

The database is not a field of `AppConfig`. A provider calls `SqlQueryBuilder.initializeWithDatabaseConfig(databaseConfig)` in its `setup()`.

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `connection` | `String` | required | Name of the connection to use. |
| `connections` | `Map<String, ConnectionConfig>` | required | Connection name to config. |

`ConnectionConfig`:

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `driver` | `Driver` | required | `Driver.postgres`, `Driver.mysql` (also MariaDB) or `Driver.sqlite`. |
| `host` | `String` | `'localhost'` | Database host. Not used by sqlite. |
| `port` | `int` | `0` | Database port. Not used by sqlite. |
| `user` | `String` | `''` | Database user. Not used by sqlite. |
| `password` | `String` | `''` | Database password. Not used by sqlite. |
| `database` | `String` | required | Database name. For sqlite: the file path, or `:memory:`. |
| `useSSL` | `bool` | `false` | Use TLS. Postgres: mode `require` (no certificate check), set `extra['sslMode']` to change it. MySQL: the certificate is checked. |
| `debug` | `bool` | required | Print every query with `printer`. |
| `printer` | `QueryPrinter?` | `null` | `ConsoleQueryPrinter()`, `PrettyQueryPrinter()`, `FileQueryPrinter(file: File('queries.log'))` or your own. With `buffered: true`, call `await printer.flush()` before `exit()`, or the last lines are lost. |
| `logRedact` | `List<String>` | `[]` | Names of values to hide in the query log. A value shows as `***` when its key ends with one of these names. `['password', 'token']` hides `password`, `users.password` and `remember_token`. Only the log changes. |
| `slowQueryMs` | `int?` | `null` | Log each query that takes longer than this many milliseconds. `0` logs every query. `null` turns it off. It works with `debug` off. |
| `read` | `List<Map<String, dynamic>>?` | `null` | Read replica hosts. Each map can change `host`, `port`, `user`, `password`, `database` and `extra`. See [Read replicas](../database/replicas.md). |
| `write` | `Map<String, dynamic>?` | `null` | Settings of the write host, in the same form as one `read` map. Only used with `read`. |
| `sticky` | `bool` | `false` | With `read`: after a write, the reads of the same request go to the write host. |
| `extra` | `Map<String, dynamic>` | `{}` | Driver options. See below. |
| `driverFactory` | `DBDriver Function(ConnectionConfig)?` | `null` | Your own driver class. It wins over every other setting. |

Keys of `extra`:

| Driver | Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| postgres, mysql | `maxConnectionCount` | `int` | `10` | Most open connections, for the whole process. |
| postgres, mysql | `threads` | `int` | `1` | Rust threads of the native driver. Only the first pool sets it. |
| postgres, mysql | `requestTimeout` | `Duration` | 300 s | The longest wait for one request (a free connection, the connect and the query). Over it, the request fails. |
| postgres, mysql | `maxConnectionAge` | `Duration` | none on Postgres, 12 hours on MySQL | Close a connection older than this, once it has no query. |
| postgres, mysql | `idleTimeout` | `Duration` | no limit on Postgres, 12 hours on MySQL | Close a free connection that is not used for this long. |
| mysql | `serverKill` | `bool` | `true` | Stop a cancelled or timed out query on the server with `KILL`. Set `false` behind a proxy like ProxySQL. |
| mysql, sqlite | `preparedStatementCacheSize` | `int` | `100` | Prepared statements kept per connection. |
| postgres | `sslMode` | `String` | `require` with `useSSL`, else `disable` | TLS mode: `disable`, `prefer`, `require` or `verify-full`. |
| postgres | `sslRootCert` | `String` | none | Path of a PEM file with the CA certificates to trust for `verify-full`. `sslrootcert` in `DATABASE_URL`. |
| postgres | `sslWarning` | `bool` | `true` | `false` hides the warning Dox prints when TLS mode is `require`. `sslWarning=false` in `DATABASE_URL` works too. |
| postgres | `timeZone` | `String` | `UTC` | Session time zone. |
| postgres | `applicationName` | `String` | none | Name of the app in `pg_stat_activity`. |
| mysql | `verifyCertificate` | `bool` | `true` | `false` skips the TLS certificate check. Only for a self-signed certificate in development. |
| sqlite | `busyTimeout` | `int` | `5000` | `PRAGMA busy_timeout` in milliseconds. |
| sqlite | `background` | `bool` | `false` | `true` runs the queries in a helper isolate, so a slow query does not block the request isolate. `?background=true` in `DATABASE_URL` works too. See [SQLite](../database/index.md#run-queries-in-a-helper-isolate). |

A time key takes a `Duration`, or a number of seconds. See [Pool settings](../database/index.md#pool-settings).

## AuthConfig

Auth is not a field of `AppConfig`. A provider calls `Auth.initialize(AuthConfig(...))` in its `setup()`.

| Class | Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `AuthConfig` | `defaultGuard` | `String` | required | The guard `Auth()` uses when no guard is named. |
| `AuthConfig` | `guards` | `Map<String, AuthGuard>` | `{}` | Guard name to guard. |
| `AuthGuard` | `driver` | `AuthDriver` | required | How a token is made and checked, like `JwtAuthDriver(secret: SecretKey(...))`. |
| `AuthGuard` | `provider` | `AuthProvider` | required | Where users come from. |
| `AuthProvider` | `model` | `dynamic Function()` | required | Makes the user model, like `() => User()`. |
| `AuthProvider` | `identifierFields` | `List<String>` | `['email']` | Columns `attempt()` matches the login with. |
| `AuthProvider` | `passwordField` | `String` | `'password'` | Column with the bcrypt hash. |

## Full example

These are the config files of a new project. They read their values from `env`, the typed env class in `lib/config/env.dart` (see [Env reference](env.md)).

```dart title="lib/config/app.dart"
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/cache.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/cors.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/logger.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';
import 'package:my_app/generated/container.g.dart';

AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  /// Changing the key makes old cookies and encrypted data unreadable.
  appKey: env.appKey,
  serverPort: env.appPort,
  totalIsolate: env.appTotalIsolate,
  globalMiddleware: <dynamic>[
    LogMiddleware(enabled: env.appEnv != 'production'),
  ],
  container: registerContainer,

  /// Only in development. Warns when a handler blocks the isolate.
  strict: StrictConfig(enabled: env.appEnv == 'development'),
  cache: cache,
  cors: cors,
  logger: logger,
);
```

```dart title="lib/config/cache.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

CacheConfig cache = CacheConfig(
  defaultStore: env.cacheStore,
  stores: <String, Map<String, dynamic>>{
    'file': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'file', 'path': 'storage/cache'},

    /// one map per isolate, fast, not shared
    'memory': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'memory', 'max_size': 10000},
  },
);
```

```dart title="lib/config/logger.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

LoggerConfig logger = LoggerConfig(
  name: env.appName,
  enabled: true,
  level: env.logLevel,
  /// colored text is slow. JSON lines in production.
  // Env.appEnv, not appConfig.isDevelopment: appConfig is built from
  // this logger, so reading appConfig here would loop.
  prettyPrint: Env.appEnv == 'development',
);
```

```dart title="lib/config/database.dart"
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/app.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

/// Print every SQL query only in development.
bool _debug = appConfig.isDevelopment;

DatabaseConfig databaseConfig = DatabaseConfig(
  connection: env.dbConnection,

  /// Only in development. Warns about N+1 relation loads and big results.
  strict: OrmStrict(enabled: appConfig.isDevelopment),
  connections: <String, ConnectionConfig>{
    'postgres': ConnectionConfig(
      driver: Driver.postgres,
      host: env.dbHost,
      port: env.dbPort ?? 5432,
      user: env.dbUsername,
      password: env.dbPassword,
      database: env.dbName,
      extra: <String, dynamic>{
        /// One pool for all isolates.
        'maxConnectionCount': 10,
        'maxConnectionAge': Duration(hours: 1),
      },
      debug: _debug,
      printer: PrettyQueryPrinter(),
    ),

    /// MySQL and MariaDB
    'mysql': ConnectionConfig(
      driver: Driver.mysql,
      host: env.dbHost,
      port: env.dbPort ?? 3306,
      user: env.dbUsername,
      password: env.dbPassword,
      database: env.dbName,
      extra: <String, dynamic>{'collation': 'utf8mb4_general_ci'},
      debug: _debug,
      printer: PrettyQueryPrinter(),
    ),

    /// `DB_NAME` is a file path, or `:memory:`.
    'sqlite': ConnectionConfig(
      driver: Driver.sqlite,
      database: env.dbName,
      debug: _debug,
      printer: PrettyQueryPrinter(),
    ),
  },
);
```

```dart title="lib/config/cors.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

CORSConfig cors = CORSConfig(
  enabled: false,
  // a list: Dox sends back the request origin only when it is in the list
  origin: <String>['http://localhost:3000'],
  methods: <String>['GET', 'HEAD', 'POST', 'PUT', 'PATCH', 'DELETE'],
  headers: <String>[
    'accept',
    'authorization',
    'content-type',
    'x-csrf-token',
    'x-xsrf-token',
    'x-requested-with',
  ],
  exposeHeaders: <String>[
    'cache-control',
    'content-language',
    'content-type',
    'expires',
    'last-modified',
    'pragma',
  ],
  credentials: true,
  maxAge: 90,
);
```

Do not use `origin: '*'` with `credentials: true`, because the browser refuses that pair.

```dart title="lib/providers/orm_provider.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/database.dart';

/// Dox finds it by itself and runs it in every isolate.
/// No database? Delete this file.
class ORMProvider extends DoxProvider {
  @override
  Future<void> setup() async {
    SqlQueryBuilder.initializeWithDatabaseConfig(databaseConfig);
  }

  @override
  Future<void> shutdown() async {
    await SqlQueryBuilder.close();
  }
}
```

A new project also has `lib/config/storage.dart`, `queue.dart` and `schedule.dart`, with a provider for each in `lib/providers/`. See [File storage](../digging-deeper/file-storage.md), [Queue](../digging-deeper/queue.md) and [Scheduler](../digging-deeper/scheduler.md).

A new project has no `openapi.dart`, `socketio.dart` or auth provider. See [OpenAPI](../packages/openapi.md), [Socket.IO](../packages/socketio.md) and [Authentication](../security/authentication.md).

# CLI

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/reference/cli/

# CLI

This page lists every `dox` command, with its options and the files it writes.

Run `dox help` to list the commands, and `dox help <command>` to see one. These rules apply to all commands:

- A name becomes snake_case for the file and PascalCase for the class. So `BlogPost` and `blog_post` give the same result.
- A `make:*` command never overwrites a file. If the file exists, it shows `<name> already exists` and stops.
- Many `make:*` commands also have a `create:*` name, like `create:model`.
- Packages and your app can add commands. See [Package commands](#package-commands).

## Project

### `dox create`

```
dox create <project_name> [--version <version>]
```

Makes a new project from the [dox-sample](https://github.com/dartondox/dox-sample) repo.

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--version <v>` (or `--v`) | A release tag of dox-sample to clone. The default is the newest release with the same major version as the CLI. |

It clones the template into a new snake_case folder, puts your project name in the files, and makes a `.env` with a new random `APP_KEY`. It needs curl and git.

### `dox add`

```
dox add <package> [--dev] [options]
```

Adds a Dox package and runs its `<package>:install` command with your options, like `dox add orm --driver=postgres`. See [Add a package](../getting-started/add-a-package.md).

### `dox serve`

```
dox serve [--no-reload] [--ignore-build-runner]
dox s
dox server
```

Starts the dev server with hot reload and `build_runner watch`. To change the port, set `APP_PORT`, like `APP_PORT=9000 dox serve`.

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--no-reload` | Turn hot reload off. Every change restarts the server. |
| `--ignore-build-runner` | Do not start `dart run build_runner watch`. |

| Changed | Result |
| --- | --- |
| A `.dart` file in `lib/app/` (not `.g.dart`) | Hot reload, in approximately 0.1 to 0.2 seconds. A static or global value keeps its old value until a restart. |
| Routes, providers, config, `lib/generated/`, `bin/`, `db/` or a generated `.g.dart` file | The server restarts. |
| A hot reload that fails, for example a compile error | The server restarts. |

The server shows a VM service link at start. Open it for DevTools, or attach VS Code with "Dart: Attach to Dart Process".

### `dox build`

```
dox build
```

Compiles the app to a native binary for production, in `build/bundle`. It runs build_runner, then `dart build cli`. Run the app with `cd build/bundle && ./bin/server`.

| Path | What |
| --- | --- |
| `build/bundle/bin/server` | the native binary, no Dart SDK needed |
| `build/bundle/bin/queue` | the queue worker, when `bin/queue.dart` exists |
| `build/bundle/bin/schedule` | the scheduler, when `bin/schedule.dart` exists |
| `build/bundle/lib/` | native libraries from build hooks (SQLite, `dox_http_native`, ...) |
| `build/bundle/db/` | your migrations and seeders. SQLite files are not copied. |
| `build/bundle/.env.example` | copy it to `.env` or set real env vars |

Do not use `dart compile exe`, because it cannot build the native libraries.

### `dox build_runner:build` and `dox build_runner:watch`

```
dox build_runner:build
dox build_runner:watch
```

Run `dart run build_runner build` one time, or `dart run build_runner watch`. The build command shows a short output.

### `dox key:generate`

```
dox key:generate [--show] [--force]
```

Writes a random 32 character key to `APP_KEY` in the `.env` file. The file must exist.

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--show` | Print a new key and write nothing. |
| `--force` | Do not ask in production. |

A new key logs out all users. So when `APP_ENV=production`, the command asks first.

### `dox env:generate`

```
dox env:generate
```

Writes `lib/config/env.dart`, the typed env class, from `.env.example`. Run `dart run build_runner build` after it. The type of each getter comes from the example value:

| Value in `.env.example` | Getter |
| --- | --- |
| a whole number, like `3000` | `int get x => 3000;` |
| `true` or `false` | `bool get x => true;` |
| empty | `String? get x;` |
| any other text | `String get x;` (required) |

A `#` comment line above a key becomes its doc comment.

### `dox env:check`

```
dox env:check [--expand]
```

Checks the real environment and `.env` with your `AppEnv` class. It shows `The env is valid.`, or each missing or bad key and exits with code 1. It needs `lib/config/env.dart` and a `name:` in `pubspec.yaml`.

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--expand` | Check with `envExpand` on. See [Use one value in another](../digging-deeper/env.md#use-one-value-in-another). |

### `dox openapi:generate`

```
dox openapi:generate [dir]
```

Writes `openapi.json` and `openapi.yaml` into `dir` (default `storage/openapi`). It runs `bin/openapi.dart`. If that file is missing, the command shows the code for it. See [OpenAPI](../packages/openapi.md).

### `dox update`

```
dox update
```

Installs the newest CLI with the same major version. It needs curl.

### `dox version`

```
dox version
dox v
dox -v
dox --version
```

Prints the CLI version.

### `dox help`

```
dox help [command]
dox --help
dox -h
```

Without a command, it lists every command. With a command, it prints its usage, options and aliases.

## Create files

### `dox make:controller`

```
dox make:controller <name> [-r|--resource] [--api] [--model=<model>]
```

Writes `lib/app/http/controllers/<name>.controller.dart`. A `Controller` at the end of the name is removed.

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `-r` or `--resource` | A resource controller with `index`, `create`, `store`, `show`, `edit`, `update`, `destroy`. |
| `--api` | A resource controller without `create` and `edit`, the two form pages. `Route.resource` makes no route for them. |
| `--model=<model>` or `--model <model>` | A resource controller that uses the model. `index` returns all rows, and `store` creates a row from `req.body`. The other methods take the model as a parameter, so [route model binding](../the-basic/dependency-injection.md#route-model-binding) loads it. |

`--api` and `--model` each make a resource controller, also with no `-r`. Run `dart run build_runner build` after it, to add the controller to the container.

### `dox make:middleware`

```
dox make:middleware <name>
```

Writes `lib/app/http/middleware/<name>.middleware.dart`: a class `<Name>Middleware implements IDoxMiddleware` with a `handle` method that returns the request. A `Middleware` at the end of the name is removed.

### `dox make:dto`

```
dox make:dto <name>
```

Writes `lib/app/dtos/<name>/<name>.dto.dart`: a `@Dto()` class with one name field. A `Dto` at the end of the name is removed. Run `dox build_runner:build` after it. See [DTOs](../the-basic/dto.md).

### `dox make:serializer`

```
dox make:serializer <name>
```

Writes `lib/app/serializers/<name>.serializer.dart`: a class `<Name>Serializer extends Serializer<<Name>>` that imports the model. A `Serializer` at the end of the name is removed.

### `dox make:provider`

```
dox make:provider <name>
```

Writes `lib/providers/<name>_provider.dart`: a class `<Name>Provider extends DoxProvider` with an empty `setup()` and an optional `shutdown()`. A `Provider` at the end of the name is removed. Run `dox build_runner:build` after it. See [Providers](../digging-deeper/providers.md).

### `dox make:command`

```
dox make:command <name>
```

Writes `lib/app/commands/<name>_command.dart`: a class `<Name>Command extends Command`. A `Command` at the end of the name is removed. The command name is `app:<name>`, with `-` for `_`: `dox make:command send_report` makes `app:send-report`.

It adds the class to `lib/app/commands/commands.dart`, and `dox: commands:` to `pubspec.yaml`. Then run `dart pub get`. If a file has a shape that it does not know, it changes nothing and shows what to add. See [Package commands](../digging-deeper/package-commands.md#add-a-command-to-your-app).

### `dox make:mail`

```
dox make:mail <name> [--no-view]
```

| Form | Writes |
| --- | --- |
| plain | `lib/app/mail/<name>_mail.dart` and the view `resources/views/emails/<name>.dox.html` |
| `--no-view` | `lib/app/mail/<name>_mail.dart` only, with a plain text body |

The class is `<Name>Mail extends Mailable`, with the recipient `Address` in its constructor. A `Mail` at the end of the name is removed. It tells you when `pubspec.yaml` needs `dox_mailer` or `dox_view`. See [Mail](../digging-deeper/mail.md#mailables).

### `dox make:view`

```
dox make:view <name>
```

Writes `resources/views/<name>.dox.html` with a small sample. A `/` in the name makes a folder: `Pages/About` gives `resources/views/pages/about.dox.html`. See [Views](../the-basic/views.md).

### `dox make:test`

```
dox make:test <name> [--unit]
```

| Form | Writes |
| --- | --- |
| plain | `test/<name>_test.dart` that starts the app with `DoxTestClient` and checks GET `/ping`. |
| `--unit` | `test/<name>_test.dart` with a plain `package:test` test. |

A `Test` at the end of the name is removed. See [Testing](../digging-deeper/testing.md).

### `dox make:model`

```
dox make:model <name> [-m] [-c] [-r] [-f] [-s] [-a] [--api]
dox create:model <name> [-m] [-c] [-r] [-f] [-s] [-a] [--api]
```

Writes `lib/app/models/<name>/<name>.model.dart`, a `@DoxModel` class. The table name is the plural snake_case name, so `BlogPost` gives blog_posts.

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `-m` or `--migration` | Also make a `create_<table>_table` migration. |
| `-c` or `--controller` | Also make a plain controller, `<name>.controller.dart`. |
| `-r` or `--resource` | Also make a resource controller that uses the model. |
| `--api` | Also make a resource controller without `create` and `edit`, that uses the model. |
| `-f` or `--factory` | Also make a factory, `db/factories/<name>.factory.dart`. |
| `-s` or `--seed` | Also make a seeder, `db/seeders/<name>.seeder.dart`. |
| `-a` or `--all` | Also make the migration, the factory, the seeder and a resource controller. |

You can join short options: `-mcr` is the same as `-m -c -r`. Each extra file is the same as the file from its own command:

| Command | Same file as |
| --- | --- |
| `dox make:model Post -m` | `dox make:migration create_posts_table` |
| `dox make:model Post -c` | `dox make:controller Post` |
| `dox make:model Post -r` | `dox make:controller Post -r --model=Post` |
| `dox make:model Post --api` | `dox make:controller Post --api --model=Post` |
| `dox make:model Post -f` | `dox make:factory Post` |
| `dox make:model Post -s` | `dox make:seeder Post` |

If the model file exists, the command makes no file. If an extra file exists, only that file is skipped.

### `dox make:migration`

```
dox make:migration <name> [--sql]
dox create:migration <name> [--sql]
```

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--sql` | Make a `.sql` file with `-- up` and `-- down` sections in place of a Dart class. |

Writes `db/migration/<yyyy>_<mm>_<dd>_<hhmmss>_<name>.dart` (or `.sql`). Migrations run in file name order. For a Dart migration, it also updates `db/migration/migrations.dart`, and makes `bin/migrate.dart` if it is missing. The code depends on the name:

| Name | `up()` | `down()` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `create_<table>_table` | `schema.create('<table>', ...)` with `id()` and `timestamps()` | `schema.dropIfExists('<table>')` |
| `<x>_to_<table>_table` (also `from`, `in`, `on`) | `schema.table('<table>', ...)` | `schema.table('<table>', ...)` |
| anything else | a comment | a comment |

## Routes

### `dox route:list`

```
dox route:list [--json]
```

Shows each route of the app: method, path, name, handler and middleware.

```
METHOD  PATH           NAME  HANDLER             MIDDLEWARE
GET     /api/ping            ApiController.pong  LogMiddleware
GET     /ping                WebController.pong  LogMiddleware
GET     /docs                serve
GET     /openapi.json        serve
GET     /openapi.yaml        serve

5 routes
```

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--json` | Print the same data as one JSON list. |

```bash
dox route:list --json
```

```json
[{"method":"GET","path":"/api/ping","name":null,"handler":"ApiController.pong","middleware":["LogMiddleware"]}]
```

Providers do not run, so a route that a provider adds, like the Socket.IO mount, is not in the list. A function with no name shows as Closure. A fallback route has the method FALLBACK, and a mount has the method MOUNT.

## Migrations

These commands run `bin/migrate.dart` of your app, and make it if it is missing. The CLI runs `.sql` migrations itself. The database comes from `DATABASE_URL`, or from the `DB_*` keys. See [Environment variables](env.md).

| Command | Aliases | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dox migration:run` | `dox migrate` | Run the migrations that did not run yet. |
| `dox migration:rollback [--step=<count>] [--batch=<number>] [--force]` | `dox migrate:rollback` | Undo the last batch, the last `<count>` migrations, or only batch `<number>`. Give `--step` or `--batch`, not both. |
| `dox migration:reset [--force]` | `dox migrate:reset` | Undo every migration. |
| `dox migration:refresh [--seed] [--force]` | `dox migrate:refresh` | Undo every migration, then run them all again. |
| `dox migration:fresh [--seed] [--force]` | `dox migrate:fresh` | Drop every table, then run all migrations. |
| `dox migration:status` | `dox migrate:status` | Print which migrations ran, and their batch. |

`--seed` runs `dox db:seed` after the migrations. When `APP_ENV=production`, the commands that undo or drop ask first, and `--force` skips the question.

## Factories and seeders

| Command | Aliases | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dox make:factory <model>` | `dox create:factory` | Make `db/factories/<model>.factory.dart`. It imports the model with the package name of `pubspec.yaml`. |
| `dox make:seeder <name>` | `dox create:seeder` | Make `db/seeders/<name>.seeder.dart`. It updates `db/seeders/seeders.dart`, and makes `bin/seed.dart` when it is missing. |
| `dox db:seed [--class=<name>]` | | Run the seeders with `bin/seed.dart`. The default seeder is `DatabaseSeeder`. |

## Queue

These commands run `bin/queue.dart` of your app. Ctrl+C and SIGTERM go to the worker, so it can finish its job before it stops.

| Command | Runs | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dox make:job <name>` | | Make `lib/app/jobs/<name>.job.dart` with a `@Job()` class that extends `DoxJob`. It makes `bin/queue.dart` when it is missing. Run `dox build_runner:build` after it. |
| `dox queue:work [flags]` | `bin/queue.dart work [flags]` | Run the worker. |
| `dox queue:failed` | `bin/queue.dart failed` | List the failed jobs. |
| `dox queue:retry <id\|all>` | `bin/queue.dart retry <id\|all>` | Put one failed job, or all of them, back on the queue. |
| `dox queue:forget <id>` | `bin/queue.dart forget <id>` | Delete one failed job. |
| `dox queue:flush` | `bin/queue.dart flush` | Delete all failed jobs. |
| `dox queue:clear [queue]` | `bin/queue.dart clear [queue]` | Delete the jobs of a queue. The default queue is `default`. |
| `dox queue:restart` | `bin/queue.dart restart` | Make the running workers stop after their current jobs. The workers must share the cache store. |
| `dox queue:prune-failed [--hours=N]` | `bin/queue.dart prune-failed [--hours=N]` | Delete failed jobs older than N hours. The default is 24. |

Each queue command takes `--connection=NAME` for a connection of `QueueConfig.connections`. Flags of `queue:work`:

| Flag | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--queue=a,b` | `default` | The queues to read, the first one first. |
| `--concurrency=N` | `1` | How many jobs run at the same time in this process. |
| `--once` | off | Run one job, then stop. |
| `--tries=N` | `1` | How many times a job may run before it is marked as failed. A job can set its own `tries`. |
| `--timeout=S` | `60` | Seconds a job may run. |
| `--sleep=S` | `3` | Seconds to wait when the queues are empty. |
| `--stop-when-empty` | off | Stop when the queues are empty. |
| `--timeout-grace=S` | none | After a timeout, wait up to `S` seconds for the old run to end before the next try. |
| `--backoff=S[,S...]` | retry at once | Seconds to wait before a retry of a job with no backoff. One value for each retry. |
| `--max-jobs=N` | no limit | Stop after N jobs. |
| `--max-time=S` | no limit | Stop after `S` seconds. |
| `--memory=MB` | no limit | Stop when the process uses more memory. |
| `--max-sleep=S` | off | When the queues stay empty, double the sleep up to `S` seconds. |

This is the `bin/queue.dart` of a new project:

```dart
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_queue/dox_queue.dart';
import 'package:<app>/config/app.dart';

Future<void> main(List<String> args) async {
  exitCode = await QueueWorker(app: appConfig).run(args);
}
```

## Schedule

These commands run `bin/schedule.dart` of your app.

| Command | Runs | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dox schedule:work` | `bin/schedule.dart work` | Run the scheduler and keep it running. |
| `dox schedule:run` | `bin/schedule.dart run` | Run the tasks that are due now, once. |
| `dox schedule:list` | `bin/schedule.dart list` | List the scheduled tasks. |
| `dox schedule:test <name>` | `bin/schedule.dart test <name>` | Run one task now. |
| `dox schedule:clear-cache` | `bin/schedule.dart clear-cache` | Remove the `withoutOverlapping()` locks that a crash left. Do not run it while a task runs. |

Add tasks in `lib/config/schedule.dart`. These are the two files of a new project:

```dart title="lib/config/schedule.dart"
import 'package:dox_scheduler/dox_scheduler.dart';

ScheduleConfig scheduleConfig = const ScheduleConfig();

void schedule(Schedule s) {
  // s.call('cleanup', cleanup).dailyAt('02:00');
}
```

```dart title="bin/schedule.dart"
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_scheduler/dox_scheduler.dart';
import 'package:<app>/config/app.dart';
import 'package:<app>/config/schedule.dart';

Future<void> main(List<String> args) async {
  exitCode = await SchedulerRunner(
    schedule: schedule,
    app: appConfig,
    config: scheduleConfig,
  ).run(args);
}
```

See [Scheduler](../digging-deeper/scheduler.md) for the task methods, and [Queue](../digging-deeper/queue.md) for jobs.

Flags of `auth:tokens-table`:

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--uuid` | The users have uuid ids. Set `uuidIds: true` on `AccessTokenAuthDriver` too. |
| `--string-ids` | The users have text ids. Set `stringIds: true` on `AccessTokenAuthDriver` too. Do not use it with `--uuid`. |
| `--users-table=<table>` | Add a foreign key from `tokenable_id` to this table, with cascade delete. |
| `--users-key=<column>` | The column of `--users-table` for the foreign key. Default: `id`. It does nothing without `--users-table`. |

# Environment variables

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/reference/env/

# Environment variables

This page lists every env var that Dox and its packages read.

## Read by the framework

`APP_ENV` changes how strict Dox is. Set `APP_ENV=development` in your local `.env` and in CI:

- development or local: Dox shows error details in 500 answers and health checks, turns `/docs` on (when `openApi.enabled` is null), and turns the view cache off.
- development, local, test or testing: a bad `APP_KEY` or a JWT secret under 32 bytes is only a warning.
- Any other value, or no value: production. A bad key stops the app at start, `/docs` is off and error details are hidden.

| Variable | Who reads it | Default | Meaning | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `APP_ENV` | `dox_core`, `dox_auth`, `dox_view` | empty | See the list above. A bad `APP_KEY` is one that is missing, not exactly 32 characters, or a public sample key. `testing` as a real env var also loads `.env.testing`. | `APP_ENV=production` |
| `APP_NAME` | `dox_core` (`Cache`) | not set | The default `prefix` of a `redis` cache store: `My Shop` gives `my_shop_cache:`. So two apps on one Redis do not share keys. | `APP_NAME="My Shop"` |
| `APP_URL` | `dox_core` (`Route.signedUrl`) | not set | The scheme and host in front of an absolute [signed URL](../security/signed-urls.md). | `APP_URL=https://example.com` |
| `PORT` | `dox_core` (`DoxServer.portFor()`) | not set | The port to listen on, when `APP_PORT` is not set. Cloud Run, Fly, Render and Heroku set it. | `PORT=8080` |
| `APP_HOST` | `dox_core` (`DoxServer.hostFor()`) | not set (all interfaces, `::`) | The host to listen on. `127.0.0.1` keeps the app off the network, for an app behind a proxy on the same machine. `AppConfig.host` wins over it. | `APP_HOST=127.0.0.1` |
| `DATABASE_URL` | `dox_orm` (`DatabaseConfig.url`), `dox_migration` | not set | A database url. It wins over `DB_CONNECTION` and the other `DB_*` keys. The app reads it with the line `url: env.databaseUrl` in `lib/config/database.dart`. Without that line, only the shell value is read. See [Database url](../database/index.md#database_url). | `DATABASE_URL=postgres://app:secret@db:5432/blog?sslmode=require` |
| `DB_CONNECTION` | `dox_migration` (`DbConnection.config()`) | sqlite | `sqlite`, `postgres` or `mysql`. Any other value is an error. | `DB_CONNECTION=postgres` |
| `DB_HOST` | `dox_migration` | `localhost` | Database host. A path that starts with `/` is a Unix socket: the folder for Postgres, the socket file for MySQL. | `DB_HOST=127.0.0.1` |
| `DB_PORT` | `dox_migration` | `5432` (postgres), `3306` (mysql) | Database port. | `DB_PORT=5432` |
| `DB_USERNAME` | `dox_migration` | `postgres` (postgres), `root` (mysql) | Database user. | `DB_USERNAME=app` |
| `DB_PASSWORD` | `dox_migration` | `postgres` (postgres), empty (mysql) | Database password. | `DB_PASSWORD=secret` |
| `DB_DATABASE` | `dox_migration` | falls back to `DB_NAME`, then `dox` | Database name. For sqlite: the file path. | `DB_DATABASE=dox` |
| `DB_NAME` | `dox_migration` | `dox` | Same as `DB_DATABASE`. `DB_DATABASE` wins when both are set. | `DB_NAME=dox` |
| `HOME` / `USERPROFILE` | build hooks of `dox_http_native`, `dox_postgres_native`, `dox_mysql_native` | empty | Used to find `cargo` when a native library must be built from source. | set by the OS |
| `DART_VM_OPTIONS` | the Dart VM | not set | Flags for the Dart VM. The binary from `dox build` reads it. Dox never sets VM flags for you. See [Performance](../digging-deeper/performance.md#dart-vm-flags). | `DART_VM_OPTIONS=--new_gen_semi_max_size=64` |

## Read by a new project

A new project reads these keys with its typed env class in `lib/config/env.dart`. In code, use the getter, like `env.appPort`.

| Variable | Getter | Type | Default | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `APP_NAME` | `appName` | `String` | `dox` | `LoggerConfig.name`. |
| `APP_ENV` | `appEnv` | `String` | `production` | `development`, `staging` or `production`. `development` turns on colored logs and the query log. Any value except `production` turns on `LogMiddleware` (one log line per request). The framework reads it too, see above. |
| `APP_PORT` | `appPort` | `int` | `3000` | `AppConfig.serverPort`. When it is not set, Dox uses `PORT` if the env has it. |
| `APP_KEY` | `appKey` | `String` | required | `AppConfig.appKey`. Exactly 32 characters. Run `dox key:generate` to make one. |
| `APP_TOTAL_ISOLATE` | `appTotalIsolate` | `int?` | not set: one per CPU the process may use (cpuset and CPU quota) | `AppConfig.totalIsolate`. |
| `LOG_LEVEL` | `logLevel` | `String` | `info` | `LoggerConfig.level`. |
| `CACHE_STORE` | `cacheStore` | `String` | `file` | `CacheConfig.defaultStore`. A new project has the stores `file` and `memory`. Add a `redis` store in `lib/config/cache.dart` before you use it. |
| `STORAGE_DISK` | `storageDisk` | `String` | `local` | `StorageConfig.defaultDisk`. A new project has the disk `local`. Add an `s3`, `azure` or `memory` disk in `lib/config/storage.dart` before you use it. |
| `DB_CONNECTION` | `dbConnection` | `String` | `sqlite` | `DatabaseConfig.connection`: `sqlite`, `postgres` or `mysql`. |
| `DB_NAME` | `dbName` | `String` | `db/dox.sqlite` | The database name. For SQLite: the file path. |
| `DB_HOST` | `dbHost` | `String` | `localhost` | Database host. |
| `DB_PORT` | `dbPort` | `int?` | not set: `5432` for Postgres, `3306` for MySQL | Database port. |
| `DB_USERNAME` | `dbUsername` | `String` | `postgres` | Database user. |
| `DB_PASSWORD` | `dbPassword` | `String` | empty | Database password. |

To add a key, add a getter to `AppEnv` and run `dart run build_runner build`. See [Environments](../guides/environments.md#2-add-a-key).

The `.env.example` of a new project:

```ini title=".env.example"
APP_NAME=dox
APP_ENV=development
APP_PORT=3000
APP_KEY=

CACHE_STORE=file
STORAGE_DISK=local

# SQLite needs no setup. The file is created at the first start.
DB_CONNECTION=sqlite
DB_NAME=db/dox.sqlite

# Postgres or MySQL: set DB_CONNECTION=postgres or mysql and fill these in.
DB_HOST=localhost
DB_PORT=5432
DB_USERNAME=postgres
DB_PASSWORD=postgres
```

## How `.env` is parsed

A real environment variable always wins over the `.env` file. The file is read like this:

- One `KEY=value` per line. A line that starts with `#` is a comment.
- `export KEY=value` is read like `KEY=value`.
- The value is everything after the first `=`, so `DATABASE_URL=postgres://u:p@h/db?a=b` works.
- A `#` after a space starts a comment: `KEY=abc # note` gives `abc`. `KEY=abc#def` stays `abc#def`.
- Quotes (`"`, `'` or `` ` ``) keep the value as it is, also a `#`. The quotes are removed.
- An empty value (`KEY=`), only spaces, or the text `null` counts as missing. So `Env.get` gives the default.
- In tests (`dart test`, or `APP_ENV=testing` as a real env var), Dox also reads `.env.testing`. Its keys win over `.env`.
- With `CoreFlags.envExpand`, `${OTHER}` and `"..."` escapes work. See [Use one value in another](../digging-deeper/env.md#use-one-value-in-another).
- The file is read one time per isolate, from the current folder. `Platform.environment` has only the real environment.

Migrations use their own simpler parser. It does not remove `# note` comments, removes all quote characters, has no `${VAR}` expansion and does not read `.env.testing`. So keep comments on their own line.

## Next steps

- [Environment Variables](../digging-deeper/env.md): read your own keys with the typed env class.
- [Environments](../guides/environments.md): a setup for dev, test and production.
- [App config](app-config.md): the fields that the env keys fill.

# Request and response

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/reference/request-and-response/

# Request and response

This page lists the members of `DoxRequest`, `DoxResponse` and the response helpers.

## `DoxRequest`

A controller and an `IDoxNextMiddleware` get a `DoxRequest`. An `IDoxMiddleware` gets an `IDoxRequest`, with fewer members. The last column shows its members.

### Input

| Member | Returns | What it gives | On `IDoxRequest` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `validate<T>({Source? source})` | `Future<T>` | The request checked with the DTO `T`. Bad input gives `422`. Throws `StateError` when `T` is not in `AppConfig.dtos`. | no |
| `validateSchema<O>(Schema<O> schema)` | `Future<O>` | Query and body checked with a fluent `dox_validation` schema. | no |
| `all()` | `Map<String, dynamic>` | Query and body together. Body wins on the same key. | yes |
| `only(List<String> keys)` | `Map<String, dynamic>` | Only these keys from `all()`. A missing key gives `null`. | yes |
| `input(String key, [dynamic defaultValue])` | `dynamic` | One value from `all()`. A dot key like `user.name` or `items.0.id` reads inside maps and lists. You get the default when the key is not there or is null. `IDoxRequest` has no default value. | yes |
| `except(List<String> keys)` | `Map<String, dynamic>` | All values from `all()`, without these keys. | no |
| `has(String key)` | `bool` | `true` when the key is there and its text is not empty. | yes |
| `exists(String key)` | `bool` | `true` when the key is there, with any value (also `''` or null). | no |
| `missing(String key)` | `bool` | `true` when the key is not there. | no |
| `filled(String key)` | `bool` | `true` when the key is there and not empty. Dot keys work. | no |
| `boolean(String key, [bool defaultValue = false])` | `bool` | `true` for `true`, `1`, `on` and `yes`. | no |
| `integer(String key, [int defaultValue = 0])` | `int` | The value as an `int`. The default is used when the key is not there or is not a number. | no |
| `file(String key)` | `RequestFile?` | The uploaded file, or `null` when the field is not a file. | no |
| `hasFile(String key)` | `bool` | `true` when the field holds a file or a list of files. | no |
| `add(String key, dynamic value)` | `void` | Adds a value to `all()` and `body`. | yes |
| `merge(Map<String, dynamic> values)` | `void` | Adds many values to `all()` and `body`. | yes |
| `body` | `Map<String, dynamic>` | The parsed body (JSON or form fields). Files are `RequestFile`. | no |
| `query` | `Map<String, dynamic>` | The query string. | no |
| `param` | `Map<String, dynamic>` | The route params, like `{'id': '5'}`. | no |
| `pathParams` | `Map<String, String>` | The route params as text. `null` values are left out. | no |
| `bound<T>(String param)` | `T` | The value that `Route.bind` made for this route param. Throws `StateError` when there is none. | no |
| `requestBody` | `RequestBody` | The body as it was read, for DTOs. | no |
| `isJson()` | `bool` | The content type is JSON. | yes |
| `isFormData()` | `bool` | The content type is form data (`multipart/form-data` or urlencoded). | yes |
| `toJson()` | `Map<String, dynamic>` | `all()` with files replaced by their file name. Lets `jsonEncode(req)` work. | yes |

### Headers, cookies and client

| Member | Returns | What it gives | On `IDoxRequest` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `header(String key)` | `String?` | One header. `null` when it is not there. | yes |
| `headers` | `Map<String, dynamic>` | Every header. Many values of one name are joined. | yes |
| `httpHeaders` | `HttpHeaders` | The `dart:io` headers object. | no |
| `contentType` | `ContentType?` | The parsed `Content-Type`. | yes |
| `bearerToken()` | `String?` | The token of `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, or `null`. | no |
| `cookie(String key, {bool decrypt = true})` | `String?` | One cookie. Decrypted with `appKey` unless `decrypt: false`. | yes |
| `ip()` | `String` | The client IP, or `unknown`. From `X-Forwarded-For` only behind a trusted proxy. | yes |
| `scheme()` | `String` | `http` or `https`. It is `https` when `AppConfig.tls` is set. Behind a trusted proxy, it comes from `X-Forwarded-Proto`. | no |
| `isSecure()` | `bool` | `scheme()` is `https`. | no |
| `clientIp` | `String?` | The client IP, or `null`. | no |
| `userAgent()` | `String` | The `User-Agent` header, or `unknown`. | yes |
| `host()` | `String` | The `Host` header, or `unknown`. | yes |
| `origin()` | `String?` | The `Origin` header. | yes |
| `referer()` | `String?` | The `Referer` header. | yes |
| `locale` | `String?` | The first language of `Accept-Language`, like `th`. `null` when there is none or it is `*`. | no |
| `auth` | `IAuth?` | The auth object set by `AuthMiddleware`. `req.auth?.id()` gives the user id. It is `null` for a guest. | yes |
| `expectsJson()` | `bool` | The client wants JSON: an `Accept` header with json, a JSON body, or `X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest`. An Inertia request is not. | no |
| `DoxRequest.expectsJsonFor(HttpHeaders headers)` | `bool` | The same check as `expectsJson()`, for raw headers. A static method. | no |
| `requestId` | `String?` | The id that the `RequestId` middleware set, or null. | no |
| `protocolVersion` | `String` | The HTTP version: `1.0`, `1.1` or `2.0`. | no |

### Session

| Member | Returns | What it gives | On `IDoxRequest` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `session` | `Session` | The session of the request. Needs `SessionMiddleware`. Throws `StateError` without it. | no |
| `hasSession` | `bool` | `true` when the request has a session. | no |

### Route and raw request

| Member | Returns | What it gives | On `IDoxRequest` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `method` | `String` | The HTTP method in upper case. | yes |
| `uri` | `Uri` | The request URI. | yes |
| `route` | `RouteData` | The matched route. | no |
| `getRouteData()` | `RouteData` | Same as `route`. | yes |
| `path()` | `String` | The request path, like `/admin/users/5`. | no |
| `fullUrl()` | `String` | The full URL with the query string. | no |
| `pathIs(String pattern)` | `bool` | `true` when the path matches. `*` matches any text. | no |
| `routeIs(String pattern)` | `bool` | `true` when the route name matches. It is `false` for a route with no name. | no |
| `getRouteIdentifier()` | `String` | A key for the route (base64 of `<method>|<domain><path>`). Useful for a cache or rate limit key. | yes |
| `httpRequest` | `HttpRequest` | The `dart:io` request. Use it for raw access. | yes |
| `takeOverResponse()` | `void` | Your handler sends the response itself on `httpRequest.response`, and Dox sends nothing more. Your code must close the response. | no |
| `responseTakenOver` | `bool` | True after `takeOverResponse()`. | no |

## `DoxResponse`

Each setter returns the same `DoxResponse`, so you can chain the calls.

| Member | Returns | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DoxResponse(dynamic content)` | `DoxResponse` | The constructor. `content` can be a `String`, number, `Map`, `List`, a JSON serializable object, a `Stream<List<int>>`, a `File`, a `StreamFile` or a `DownloadableFile`. |
| `statusCode(int code)` | `DoxResponse` | Sets the status. Default `200`. |
| `status` | `int?` | The status set with `statusCode()`, or `null` (which means `200`). |
| `content(dynamic content)` | `DoxResponse` | Replaces the content. |
| `getContent()` | `dynamic` | The content as it was given. |
| `stream(Stream<List<int>> stream)` | `DoxResponse` | Sets a byte stream as content. |
| `contentType(ContentType type)` | `DoxResponse` | Sets `Content-Type`. A `File` without it gets the type from its extension. |
| `header(String key, dynamic value, {bool? replace})` | `DoxResponse` | Sets one header. A second call with the same key, in any case, replaces the value. A value that a middleware already put on the response stays, unless `replace` is true. When `replace` is null, `CoreFlags.replaceHeaders` decides. |
| `headers` | `Map<String, dynamic>` | The headers set so far, by name. |
| `withHeaders(Map<String, dynamic> values)` | `DoxResponse` | Adds these headers. A key replaces the header with the same name, in any case. Other headers stay. |
| `cookie(DoxCookie cookie, {bool setExpire = false})` | `DoxResponse` | Adds a `Set-Cookie` header. `setExpire: true` sends the cookie as expired, which removes it. |
| `cache(Duration duration)` | `DoxResponse` | Sets `Cache-Control: max-age=<seconds>`. |

## Response helpers

These top level functions give a `DoxResponse`.

| Function | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `response([dynamic content])` | Same as `DoxResponse(content)`. |
| `redirect(String url, {int status = 302})` | A redirect to `url`. It sets the `Location` header. |
| `back(DoxRequest req, {String fallback = '/'})` | A `302` redirect to the `Referer` header, or to `fallback` when there is none. |

## How the content is sent

A controller can return a plain value or a `DoxResponse`:

| Content | Sent as |
| --- | --- |
| `null` | an empty body |
| `String` | text, as it is |
| `Map`, `List`, number, `bool`, object with `toJson()` | JSON, `Content-Type: application/json` |
| `DateTime` | its ISO 8601 text |
| `File` | streamed, with `Content-Length`, `Accept-Ranges` and one `Range` supported |
| `StreamFile` | streamed with its content type. An HTML, XML or JavaScript type is sent as a download, in a sandbox. |
| `DownloadableFile` | streamed with `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="<name>"` |
| `Stream<List<int>>` | streamed chunk by chunk |
| `IHttpException` | its status and `toResponse()`, see [HTTP exceptions](http-exceptions.md) |
| other `Exception` or `Error` | `500` with `{"code": "server_error", "message": "Server Error"}`. In development or local, the body is the error text. |

## Next steps

- [Request](../the-basic/request.md): read the input of a request, with examples.
- [Response](../the-basic/response.md): send a response, with examples.
- [HTTP exceptions](http-exceptions.md): the error classes and their status codes.

# HTTP exceptions

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/reference/http-exceptions/

# HTTP exceptions

An HTTP exception stops a request and sends an error answer with the right status code, like `404` or `403`.

Each HTTP exception extends `IHttpException`, with three fields: the status `code`, a short `errorCode` and a `message`. Throw it, or return it from a middleware or a controller.

## Throwing an exception

Throw one of the classes below when a request cannot continue:

```dart
throw NotFoundHttpException(message: 'Blog not found');
```

The client gets a JSON body with the error code and the message:

```
HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
content-type: application/json

{"code":"not_found","message":"Blog not found"}
```

## The classes

Most classes take the named parameters `message`, `errorCode` and `code`. The table shows the defaults.

| Class | Package | `code` | `errorCode` | Default `message` | Dox throws it when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `BadRequestException` | `dox_core` | `400` | `bad_request` | `Bad Request` | the body can not be read, like JSON that is not valid |
| `UnAuthorizedException` | `dox_auth` | `401` | `unauthorized` | `Authentication failed` | `AuthMiddleware` finds no valid token |
| `ForbiddenHttpException` | `dox_core` | `403` | `forbidden` | `Forbidden` | never; it is for your own use |
| `NotFoundHttpException` | `dox_core` | `404` | `not_found` | `Not Found` | no route fits (message `<METHOD> <path> not found`), a typed path param does not fit (`{id}` is not an `int`), or route model binding finds no row |
| `MethodNotAllowedHttpException` | `dox_core` | `405` | `method_not_allowed` | `Method Not Allowed` | the path has routes, but not for this method. The `Allow` header lists the methods, like `Allow: GET, POST, HEAD`. |
| `PayloadTooLargeException` | `dox_core` | `413` | `payload_too_large` | `Payload Too Large` | the body is bigger than `maxBodySize` or `maxMultipartSize` |
| `UnsupportedMediaTypeException` | `dox_core` | `415` | `unsupported_media_type` | `Unsupported Media Type` | a DTO reads a body that is not JSON and not form data |
| `TokenMismatchException` | `dox_core` | `419` | `csrf_token_mismatch` | `CSRF token mismatch` | `CsrfMiddleware` finds no CSRF token, or a wrong one |
| `ValidationException` | `dox_core` | `422` | `validation_failed` | `{}` (a `Map`) | a DTO, `req.validate()` or `schema.parse()` of `dox_validation` finds bad input |
| `TooManyRequestsException` | `dox_core` | `429` | `too_many_requests` | `Too Many Requests` | a `RateLimit` middleware sees too many requests |
| `InternalErrorException` | `dox_core` | `500` | `server_error` | `Server Error` | never; it is for your own use |
| `QueryException` | `dox_core` | `500` | `sql_query_error` | `Error in sql query` | never; it is for your own use |

## Any status: `abort` and `HttpStatusException`

For a status with no class, use `abort(code)`:

```dart
if (post.userId != req.auth?.id()) abort(403);
```

You can also pass a message:

```dart
abort(404, 'No post with this id');
```

`abort` throws an `HttpStatusException`. Throw it yourself to send headers too:

```dart
throw HttpStatusException(503,
    headers: <String, String>{'retry-after': '60'});
```

Common codes get a default `errorCode` and `message`, like `forbidden` and `Forbidden` for `403`:

```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
content-type: application/json

{"code":"forbidden","message":"Forbidden"}
```

Other codes get `http_error` and `Error`.

## What the client gets

The status is the code of the exception, and the body is JSON. A text message gives `{"code": "<errorCode>", "message": "<message>"}`. For your own JSON shape, give a map as the message:

```dart
throw NotFoundHttpException(
    message: <String, String>{'error': 'not_found'});
// 404 {"error":"not_found"}
```

A `ValidationException` always has a map, with one entry per field:

```
HTTP/1.1 422 Unprocessable Entity
content-type: application/json

{"email":"The email is not a valid email","name":"The name is required"}
```

A form post with a session gets a redirect back, with the errors and the old input in the session. See [Session](../the-basic/session.md#validation-errors-and-old-input).

### Other errors

Any other error gives 500 with `{"code": "server_error", "message": "Server Error"}`. When `APP_ENV` is development or local, the body is the error text.

These errors go to the `report` method of the [exception handler](../the-basic/errors.md). An HTTP exception with a 5xx code also goes there.

## Making your own exception

Extend `IHttpException` and set the three fields in the constructor:

```dart
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

class PaymentRequiredException extends IHttpException {
  PaymentRequiredException({
    dynamic message = 'Please pay',
    String errorCode = 'payment_required',
    int code = HttpStatus.paymentRequired,
  }) {
    super.code = code;
    super.errorCode = errorCode;
    super.message = message;
  }
}
```

To give each error the same JSON shape, override `toResponse()`. It returns the body.

## Next steps

- [Error handling](../the-basic/errors.md): report and render errors.
- [Response](../the-basic/response.md#errors): more error examples.
- [Error index](errors.md): each message that Dox shows or throws.
